participation. Teach the undergraduate Freshman Orientation 1-credit course each semester and
any other undergraduate course as needed to support academic success initiatives including but
not limited to guidance, counseling. Address all areas of academic concerns with students,
including tutoring, study skills, and time management, and connect student-athletes with
appropriate academic support resources within the athletic department and broader university.
Make referrals to other points of service such as counseling, financial aid, career services,
student life, and disability services, collaborating closely with athletic department staff as
needed. Participate in professional development opportunities, staying current on best practices
in athletic advising and NAIA regulations. Remain current in high impact practices as related to
academic advising, student success, and higher education. Contribute to the success of the
department by completing all other duties as needed to promote the vision, fulfill the mission,
and abide by the values of the College.

Education and Experience Requirements: Master’s degree or foreign equivalent in
Kinesiology with a concentration in Exercise and Sport Psychology or related field with 2 years
of experience as an Academic Advisor for Athletic Student Retention, ___, or similar duties under
a different job title.

student athletes and developing personalized degree plans; working with NAIA, NCAA or
NJCAA regulations and ensuring student athletes meet requirements; working with FERPA and
HIPAA laws; and working with first generation at-risk students. Demonstrated ability to teach
as shown by a seminar presentation or teaching experience.

curriculum vitae, copies of all transcripts, and names, addresses, titles, phone numbers, and e-
mail addresses of at least 5 professional references to hr@Talladega College, 627

title: Shingle Roofing Superintendent
description:
Baker Roofing Company – Shingle Roofing Superintendent

Baker Roofing Company is 100% Employee Owned and invests in our team members by empowering success through structured growth plans and intensive training courses. We value our employees by providing competitive benefits, prioritizing safety, and promoting work-life balance.

Benefits to Joining the Baker Team:

Apply today and start building your future with Baker Roofing Company!

Summary
The Shingle Roofing Superintendent will oversee Shingle Reroof projects on commercial buildings. The Superintendent will manage crews, enforce safety compliance, track weekly progress, track material usage, document roadblocks, provide training and support to crews, enforce quality control, and keep the project on schedule and on budget.
Requirements
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The lists below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.
Minimum Qualifications
  • Education: Minimum high school graduate, bachelor's degree preferred.
  • Experience: 5+ years of hands-on shingle roofing experience, project management experience in residential or commercial roofing preferred.
  • Driver's License: Required.
  • Certifications: OSHA10, First Aid, and CPR Training preferred.
  • Languages: Must be fluent in English, and Spanish is a plus.
  • Travel: Must have the ability to travel 30% across North Carolina, South Carolina, and Virginia. The average project requiring travel will be 2 days at a time during the work week.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
  • Extensive knowledge of residential and commercial steep slope roofing systems including slate, tile, synthetic slate, asphalt shingles, and copper & zinc standing seam.
  • Knowledge and experience with soldering copper and stainless steel.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and Scheduling Software.
  • Experience with a CRM and estimating software is a plus.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Possess a motivated, professional, and self-starter attitude.
  • Ability to work independently in the field and manage multiple priorities and calendars.
What You'll Do
  • Ensure a safe working environment for all crews, subcontractors, and other contractors on the project.
  • Maintain and improve quality control, job site cleanliness, and daily housekeeping.
  • Communicate job progress, field concerns, and technical questions with supervisor on a daily basis.
  • Complete all paperwork related to the project including time sheets, safety huddles/toolbox talks, material and sheet metal shop requisitions, and job reports.
  • Install and replace roofs and exterior walls with metal, slate, single-ply systems, asphalt, aluminum, wood, gravel, gypsum, and related materials.
  • Conduct trim/panel measurements and clip spacing plans.
  • Repair cracks, defects, and damages to the roofing systems using appropriate materials.
  • Apply adhesives, caulking, sealants, and coatings to roofing systems as needed.
  • Operate company-owned and rented vehicles, mechanized devices, and heavy equipment.
  • Inspect equipment, structures, and materials before each use.
  • Coordinate punch list and job close-out before the crew completes the job and leaves the site.
Physical Demands & Work Environment
  • Requires the ability to lift and carry items weighing 50 pounds.
  • Requires the ability to stand, walk, and balance for long periods of time.
  • Requires use of abdominal and lower back muscles to support part of the body repeatedly or continuously over time without giving out or fatiguing.
  • Requires seeing details at close range.
  • Requires repetitive movement, bending, twisting, kneeling, crouching, stooping, or crawling.
  • Working in temperatures above 90°F or below 32°F.
  • Working at heights and in other potentially dangerous conditions.
  • Exposure to extremely bright or inadequate lighting.
  • Exposure to loud, distracting, or uncomfortable noise levels.
  • Exposure to contaminants, hazardous materials, and potentially hazardous equipment.
  • Exposure to minor injuries such as burns, cuts, bites, or stings.
  • Performing work where errors may have significant consequences. Strict adherence to all safety policies, procedures, and regulations is required.

They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. All personnel may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed.

If you need special assistance or accommodation in applying for employment at Baker Roofing Company, please contact our Recruiting department at 919-828-2975 or recruiting@bakerroofing.com.

EOE Minorities/Females/Disability/Veterans; VEVRAA Federal Contractor

title: IT Infrastructure Support Specialist
description:
Founded in 1978, CAMP Facility Services offers a vibrant work environment and a strong commitment to quality, accessible support, and holistic project management. We prioritize relationships with clients and staff alike, treating everyone like family.

Specializing in commercial construction and building maintenance, we serve construction managers, property managers, and building owners across diverse sectors. Our mission emphasizes partnership, continuous improvement through teamwork and education, and exceeding expectations to build lasting relationships based on respect and professionalism.

Why join our CAMP?

Our employees are encouraged to take advantage of an array of benefits and opportunities, including:

  • Health Benefits - Medical, Dental & Vision
  • 401K and Company Match Benefits
  • Paid Holidays, Vacation, and Personal Time Off
  • 1 Paid Day Off for Community Service
  • Employee Referral Bonuses
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Advancement Opportunities

Position Summary

The IT Infrastructure Support Specialist serves as a primary point of contact for IT support while also supporting the organization’s network and cloud infrastructure. This role is responsible for diagnosing, resolving, and escalating hardware, software, network, and system issues while ensuring a high level of customer service. In addition to supporting end-user devices and the Microsoft 365 environment, the specialist monitors and troubleshoots Fortinet network equipment and assists with the day-to-day administration of Azure networking services, enterprise print management, the RingCentral phone system, and account provisioning across a wide range of business applications. This position includes periodic travel to company offices across the United States to resolve issues that require an on-site presence.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide support to team members by responding to incidents and service requests remotely and in person.
  • Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve hardware, software, and application issues in a Windows and Microsoft 365 environment.
  • Configure, deploy, and maintain end-user devices including laptops, desktops, mobile devices, and peripherals, using Microsoft Intune and Windows Autopilot for enrollment, provisioning, and ongoing management.
  • Support new hire onboarding and offboarding by preparing equipment, provisioning user accounts, and ensuring appropriate system access.
  • Accurately document incidents, requests, assets, and user information in the Service Desk and Asset Management systems.
  • Monitor and respond to alerts related to connectivity, applications, and device performance, escalating issues when necessary.
  • Assist with user administration in Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Azure AD (Entra ID).
  • Monitor and perform basic troubleshooting of Fortinet network equipment, including FortiGate firewalls, FortiSwitch, and FortiAP wireless access points, escalating configuration changes and complex issues to the company's third-party network provider.
  • Support Azure networking components such as virtual networks, subnets, VPN gateways, network security groups, and site-to-site connectivity, escalating complex changes as needed.
  • Administer enterprise print management through PrinterLogic, including printer deployment, driver management, and resolution of print-related issues.
  • Administer the RingCentral phone system, including user and extension provisioning, call queues and routing, auto-attendant/IVR configuration, device setup, and troubleshooting of call quality and connectivity issues.
  • Provision, modify, and deprovision user accounts and access across a wide variety of business applications, following established approval and least-privilege practices.
  • Create, update, and maintain IT documentation such as procedures, standards, and how-to guides.
  • Follow IT policies, security standards, and best practices to help maintain a secure and reliable computing environment.
  • Work closely with the company's third-party network provider on escalated issues and planned changes, supplying site detail and diagnostics, acting as the on-site presence when physical work is required, and tracking items through to resolution.
  • Collaborate with other IT team members and vendors to resolve complex technical issues.
  • Travel to company offices across the United States as needed to resolve complex network, connectivity, and other office technology issues on site.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities & Qualifications

Technical Knowledge & Skills — Required

  • 3–5+ years of experience in a Service Desk, Help Desk, or technical support role supporting end users, including hands-on exposure to network or infrastructure support.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Windows desktop and laptop operating systems.
  • Experience supporting Microsoft 365 applications (Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint).
  • Basic to intermediate understanding of networking concepts (IP addressing, DNS, DHCP, VPN).
  • Knowledge of computer hardware, peripherals, and mobile devices.
  • Familiarity with IT service management (ITSM) principles and ticketing systems.
  • Experience with endpoint provisioning and lifecycle management using traditional imaging and/or modern cloud-based methods (such as Intune or Autopilot), along with software deployment and user account provisioning.
  • Experience provisioning and administering user accounts and access across a wide variety of business applications and SaaS platforms.

Technical Knowledge & Skills — Preferred

  • 1–3 years of hands-on experience in a Fortinet environment, including FortiGate firewalls, FortiSwitch, and FortiAP wireless access points.
  • Working knowledge of Azure networking, including virtual networks, subnets, network security groups, VPN gateways, and hybrid connectivity.
  • Experience administering Microsoft Intune, including device enrollment, compliance and configuration policies, application deployment, and endpoint security baselines.
  • Experience administering PrinterLogic or a comparable enterprise print management platform.
  • Experience administering RingCentral or a comparable cloud VoIP/UCaaS phone platform, including user provisioning, call routing, and call quality troubleshooting.

Professional Skills

  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent customer service orientation with clear verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to explain technical issues in simple terms to non-technical users.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple tickets and priorities.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities in a fast-paced support environment.

Education & Experience

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Associate degree or higher in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field preferred.
  • Equivalent work experience and/or certifications may be considered in place of a degree.

Certifications (Preferred)

  • CompTIA A+
  • CompTIA Network+
  • Microsoft 365 Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate (MD-102)
  • Fortinet NSE 4 (or other Fortinet Network Security certifications)
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Network Engineer Associate (AZ-700) or Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104)
  • Other relevant Microsoft, Fortinet, or IT support certifications

Travel Requirements

  • Travel up to 25% to company offices across the United States to resolve complex network, internet connectivity, and other site-level technical issues that cannot be addressed remotely.
  • Act as on-site hands during these visits in coordination with the company's third-party network provider, performing physical installation, replacement, and cabling of network equipment, verifying connectivity, and confirming that remotely applied changes are working as intended.
  • Perform additional on-site work as needed, including basic wireless and connectivity troubleshooting, site surveys, equipment inventory, and support for office moves, expansions, and closures.
  • Occasional overnight and weekend travel is required, including scheduled after-hours maintenance windows and cutovers.
  • Occasional travel on short notice may be required to respond to site outages or other business-critical incidents.
  • Must be able to travel by air and maintain valid identification acceptable for domestic air travel.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift and transport computer equipment weighing up to approximately 50 lbs.

title: DEXA Licensed - Mobile Health Technician
description:
Licensed DEXA Technician

Are you tired of your DEXA certification sitting underused in a clinic shift or a sales-driven screening job? As a Licensed DEXA Technician at BodySpec, you'll put your California BDEO certification to work the way it's meant to be used — one-on-one scans that actually help people understand their bodies, with no cold-calling, no client book to build, and no quotas. You'll be at the heart of numerous health journeys, celebrating successes and offering support in a role that's as rewarding as it is dynamic.

First-year Licensed DEXA Technicians in the South Bay can expect to earn up to $77,086 in total cash compensation, plus equity.

You'll Love This Job If You Have:

  • Passion for Preventive Health: You believe health is about more than treating illness — you want to help people understand their bodies and reach their goals.
  • Customer Service Instincts: You love one-on-one interaction and creating great experiences. You're warm, professional, and can make anyone feel comfortable — without the pressure of building your own book of business.
  • Startup Energy: You're energized by variety and building something new. Traditional healthcare feels slow and bureaucratic to you. You want to be part of a small, dynamic team where your work actually matters.
  • Grit and Flexibility: You don't mind early mornings or getting your hands dirty. You're resourceful — when something's broken, you fix it or propose solutions instead of waiting for someone else.
  • Ready to Work, Not Ready to Wait: You're already BDEO-certified and want to put that license into practice immediately — not spend months in a training pipeline before you start making an impact.

What Will You Do?

  • Work in our storefronts or directly in the community, driving our mobile scan vans to community centers, gyms, workplaces, health fairs, clinics, and other locations.
  • Perform DEXA scans from day one using your existing BDEO certification, backed by a hands-on BodySpec onboarding — including a team immersion week in Austin, TX — to get you fluent in our scan protocols, equipment, and customer experience standards.
  • Take ownership of your events from setup to tear down, exemplifying excellence in service delivery and customer service — all while making a genuinely positive impact on dozens of people each day.
  • Handle general administrative and maintenance-related duties related to our storefront, machines, vans, and equipment.
  • Assist with other duties as assigned by the Leadership Team.

Requirements

  • Must currently hold an active California BDEO (Bone Densitometry Equipment Operator) certification issued by the California Department of Public Health, Radiologic Health Branch.
  • This is a standing role with rolling start dates — no fixed cohort or class to wait for.
  • Available to work one of the following consistent schedules: Sunday–Thursday (Friday & Saturday off). Event times typically run 7am–8pm depending on location; earlier start times may be required to accommodate drive time so you're on-site and ready for clients at 7am.
  • Based in Mountain View, Sunnyvale, Cupertino, or the surrounding area.
  • If you've taken standardized tests such as the SAT, ACT, ASVAB, or others, we ask you to share your scores. This isn't required and won't be a sole factor in hiring, but it helps us learn more about candidates since we don't run pre-employment testing.
  • Valid driver's license and a driving record in good standing.
  • Able to lift/carry up to 50 lbs.
  • Ability to thrive with direct, unfiltered feedback — we'll tell you exactly what you need to improve.

Compensation

  • Base Salary: $33.02/hour ($68,682 annualized at 40 hrs/week)
  • Performance Bonus: Up to 7% of base annually ($4,808) — half paid in cash ($2,404), half in stock options
  • Team Revenue Bonus: $500/month when we hit monthly goals ($6,000 annually — we hit our goals 9 out of 12 months in 2025)
  • Total Cash Compensation: Up to $77,086
  • Equity: Stock options through performance bonus and additional grants based on performance

All team members regardless of position are eligible for additional stock option grants and profit sharing based on performance. We expect both cash and equity compensation to grow as the company scales.

Benefits

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k)
  • Paid time off
  • Sick leave
  • $75/month commute reimbursement
  • $10/shift meal stipend
  • Company-wide peer bonus program for recognizing excellent teamwork
  • Employee assistance program
  • Regular team events (both virtual and in-person)

BodySpec is transforming how people understand and improve their health through accessible DEXA scanning. As a Licensed DEXA Technician, you'll bring that insight directly into the communities we serve, from day one. If you're ready to put your certification to work immediately, deliver an exceptional scan experience every time, and join a team that moves fast, we want to hear from you.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

title: Job Coach
description:
Job Coach / Employment Specialist – Part-Time

Location: Germantown, Maryland
Service Area: Germantown and surrounding Montgomery County communities

Hours: Up to 29 hours per week, with the potential to transition to full-time
Schedule: Predominantly daytime hours, Monday through Friday
Work Setting: Community-based with regular local travel
Mileage: Reimbursement for approved work-related travel

Help People Build Careers and Greater Independence

RISE Services is hiring a compassionate, dependable, and resourceful Job Coach / Employment Specialist to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain meaningful employment.

In this community-based role, you will meet participants at employer worksites and other locations throughout Germantown and surrounding Montgomery County communities. You will help participants explore career interests, search and apply for jobs, prepare for interviews, learn workplace responsibilities, communicate with employers, and develop the skills needed for long-term employment success.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. We welcome applicants with relevant experience in disability services, human services, education, behavioral health, workforce development, direct support, career coaching, case management, retail supervision, customer service, or other positions involving teaching, mentoring, or helping others succeed.

Training is provided.

Schedule and Hours

This position offers up to 29 hours per week. Most services in the Germantown area are provided during daytime hours, Monday through Friday.

Weekend work is occasionally needed to provide coverage when another employee is unavailable, but this is not a regularly scheduled weekend position.

Weekly schedules may include:

  • On-site job coaching

  • Job searching and completing applications

  • Resume and interview preparation

  • Employer outreach

  • Employment-readiness activities

  • Community-based participant meetings

  • Progress notes and required documentation

When a participant is not working their full number of authorized service hours, the Job Coach may provide other approved employment services, including job searching, completing applications, developing resumes, preparing for interviews, contacting employers, and teaching workplace-readiness skills.

Employees who want additional hours may have the opportunity to transition to full-time as caseloads and service needs grow. Full-time hours are not guaranteed and depend on participant referrals, scheduling needs, employee availability, and satisfactory job performance.

What You’ll Do

Job Coaching and Workplace Support

  • Provide individualized coaching at employer worksites and in community settings.

  • Help participants learn job duties, workplace routines, safety procedures, and employer expectations.

  • Teach workplace communication, professional behavior, time management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Help participants communicate effectively with supervisors and coworkers.

  • Develop natural workplace supports that promote greater independence.

  • Monitor participant progress and adjust coaching strategies as participants develop new skills.

  • Provide ongoing support to promote successful employment retention.

Job Search and Career Preparation

  • Help participants identify their strengths, interests, abilities, support needs, and employment goals.

  • Assist participants with resumes, applications, job searches, and interview preparation.

  • Conduct mock interviews and employment-readiness activities.

  • Identify opportunities that match each participant’s interests, abilities, experience, and goals.

  • Coordinate interviews, hiring activities, and onboarding support.

  • Help participants understand workplace expectations and identify reasonable accommodations when appropriate.

Employer and Community Engagement

  • Build professional relationships with employers throughout Germantown and Montgomery County.

  • Contact businesses to identify potential employment opportunities.

  • Educate employers about inclusive hiring and available workplace supports.

  • Communicate with participants, families, employers, vocational rehabilitation counselors, schools, and community partners.

  • Attend hiring events, team meetings, training, and other scheduled activities.

Documentation and Service Coordination

  • Complete accurate progress notes and service documentation within required deadlines.

  • Maintain participant records according to funding-source and organizational requirements.

  • Track job searches, applications, interviews, placements, wages, scheduled hours, and employment retention.

  • Communicate participant progress, concerns, scheduling changes, and service needs to the appropriate supervisor.

  • Participate in service-planning and team-coordination activities.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree is not required.

  • Relevant experience supporting individuals with disabilities or others who experience barriers to employment is preferred.

  • Experience in teaching, coaching, mentoring, customer service, supervision, human services, behavioral health, workforce development, or a related field may also be considered.

  • Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

  • Ability to work independently and make responsible decisions in community settings.

  • Ability to maintain a consistent schedule and complete documentation on time.

  • Basic computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.

  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

  • Ability and willingness to travel locally and transport participants when required.

  • Ability to satisfy applicable background-screening and employment requirements.

Preferred but Not Required

  • Supported Employment, job-coaching, or job-development experience.

  • Experience supporting individuals with intellectual, developmental, behavioral, or other disabilities.

  • Knowledge of vocational rehabilitation or disability-employment services.

  • Understanding of the Americans with Disabilities Act and reasonable workplace accommodations.

  • Experience working with employers, schools, rehabilitation counselors, or community organizations.

  • CESP, ACRE, DSP, or another employment-support credential.

Who Will Succeed in This Position?

You may be a strong fit if you are:

  • Compassionate, patient, dependable, and encouraging.

  • Comfortable working at employer locations and throughout the community.

  • Able to teach and motivate participants while promoting independence.

  • Professional and confident when communicating with employers and community partners.

  • Resourceful and willing to find solutions when challenges arise.

  • Organized and able to manage appointments, follow-ups, and documentation.

  • Flexible when participant or employer schedules change.

  • Comfortable working independently without constant direct supervision.

Why Join RISE Services?

  • Make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals with disabilities.

  • Help people build careers, confidence, and greater independence.

  • Work predominantly during weekday daytime hours.

  • Receive mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel.

  • Participate in paid training and professional development.

  • Build experience in human services, disability services, workforce development, and career coaching.

  • Access potential opportunities for additional hours and advancement.

  • Join a collaborative, growing, and mission-driven organization.

Benefits

Part-time employees may be eligible for:

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Employee Tenure Bonus Program

  • Mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel

  • Paid training and professional development

Employees who transition to an eligible full-time position may also receive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays

  • Short-term disability insurance

  • Life insurance

  • Long-term care option

Benefit eligibility requirements apply.

Important Work-Setting Information

This is a community-based position, not a remote or traditional office-based role. Services are provided at employer worksites and other community locations throughout Germantown and surrounding Montgomery County communities.

Applicants must have reliable transportation and be comfortable driving between community locations. Transporting participants may be required as part of the position.

Equal Opportunity Employer

RISE Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We recruit, hire, train, compensate, and promote employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Apply Today

If you enjoy teaching, encouraging others, solving problems, and helping people accomplish meaningful goals, apply for the Part-Time Job Coach / Employment Specialist position with RISE Services.

A bachelor’s degree and previous job-coaching experience are not required. Relevant experience, dependability, professionalism, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to helping others succeed are strongly valued.

title: Financial Audit Intern - Health Provider Review- Summer 2027
description:
Financial Audit Intern - Health Provider Review
Summer 2027: June 1 - August 6

About Our Program
The Comptroller of the Treasury's Audit Internship Program is a 10-week paid educational and experiential learning opportunity offering undergraduate students a chance to witness and participate in the audit operations of the office. Interns will spend the summer building skills through their assignment to an active audit, audit-specific training, and professional development training. Interns will also have opportunities to build relationships with each other through shared experiences.

Health Provider Review Financial Audit Intern responsibilities may include performing examinations in accordance with attestation standards established by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants and conducting desk reviews, which involve obtaining financial and statistical data from providers and determining the accuracy and reasonableness of the information submitted to our office. Responsibilities may include examining, analyzing, and reviewing records, financial statements, claims data, and cost reports for providers participating in the TennCare Program.

Our summer internship program is designed to be both professionally and academically beneficial. Interns gain hands‑on experience while participating in meaningful professional development activities such as Business Etiquette Day, a full‑day session focused on professionalism, emotional intelligence, and understanding one’s professional brand, complete with an etiquette lunch led by staff. Interns also enjoy engaging activities like speed networking with full‑time employees, a guided tour of the Tennessee Capitol to explore the state’s history, and weekly cohort check‑ins to foster connection and collaboration. The cohort experience culminates in a final presentation showcasing what interns have learned and contributed during their time with the Office.

Location
Financial Audit internship opportunities are based out of Nashville, Tennessee. Depending on the audit assignment, interns may have the opportunity for limited travel during the summer. Typical travel opportunities are in the Nashville area; however, some may allow for travel to other parts of Tennessee.

Who We're Looking For
We are seeking students who are rising juniors, seniors, or enrolled in graduate accounting programs and are interested in applying their classroom knowledge to governmental auditing. To qualify for the internship program, applicants should have successfully completed at least 6 credit hours of accounting coursework. Preference will be given to students who have completed intermediate or advanced accounting classes.

Successful interns are those who are adaptable, able to think critically, work well both individually and as part of a team, and are willing to learn and grow. Candidates should exhibit strong interpersonal, verbal communication, organizational, and writing skills. Interns are expected to apply their classroom knowledge to meaningful audit work.

About Our Office
The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury is responsible for the audit of state and local governmental entities and participates in the general financial and administrative management and oversight of state government. In the Comptroller’s Office, we strive to deliver on our mission to make government work better. Through dedicated hard work and commitment, every Comptroller’s Office employee accepts personal responsibility to accomplish our mission and uphold it.

Compensation
Interns are paid $24 per hour via a third-party company. This position may require in-state day travel to audit sites. Audit-related travel will be reimbursed.

Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Quality Assurance Inspector
description:
Quality Assurance Inspector

Carlsbad, CA | $24–$29/hour DOE

At Means Engineering, we don’t just manufacture parts — we create high-impact solutions across multiple industries. As a vertically integrated contract manufacturer, everything happens under one roof: design, prototyping, machining, build, testing and delivery.

What you’ll get to do:

  • Plan and perform detailed inspections of materials, parts and assemblies using precision measuring equipment such as calipers, micrometers, dial indicators, depth gages, optical comparators, height gages, surface plate, and digital/automated inspection devices.
  • Document all inspection results per company policies and requirements in the ERP system. Follow all requirements of company quality management system including ISO9001, AS9100, and ISO13485 requirements
  • Perform receiving inspection, in-process inspection, final inspection, and shipping inspection to ensure quality and conformance to customer specifications
  • Perform First Article Inspections and generates First Article Inspection reports in accordance with AS 9102 (SAE Aerospace Standard for the First Article Inspection).
  • May participate in the Material Review Board; inspects material being reviewed; transacts Non-Conforming Material Reports; completes and scans Defective Material Reports (DMR)
  • Transports material and parts to and from various work centers to perform quality inspection

The Interventional Cardiologist / Endovascular Medicine Specialist provides physician-level cardiovascular, vascular, venous, and structural heart consultation services for patients through Oyate Health Center. The position emphasizes timely outpatient specialty access, diagnostic interpretation, procedural planning, care coordination, clinical quality, and collaboration with primary care, referrals, PRC, diagnostic services, emergency services, and external procedural partners to deliver safe, culturally grounded care close to home.

The following functions are fundamental to the position and are required of all incumbents, with or without reasonable accommodation. These functions define the role and are not an exhaustive list of all duties.

Provides physician-level cardiovascular assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, and follow-up for patients with coronary artery disease, PFO/ASD concerns, peripheral vascular disease, venous disease, hypertension, and related cardiovascular or vascular conditions within scope of licensure, credentialing, privileges, and available service capabilities.

title: Powder Paint Helper
description:
Job Title: Powder Paint Helper

Position Title: Powder Paint Helper (Full-time)
Department: Operations/Onsite Los Angeles
Reports To: Production Manager

Job Summary

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented Powder Paint Helper to join our manufacturing and finishing team. You will support lead powder coaters by preparing metal parts, operating industrial wash stages, loading/unloading conveyor lines, and ensuring parts are cured flawlessly. This role is perfect for individuals wanting to master industrial coating and surface preparation technologies. Hours are Monday-Friday from 7 am until 3:30 pm. Pay range of $19-20/hour.

Duties and Responsibilities

Part Preparation & Masking

  • Apply masking plugs, caps, and high-temperature tape to threads, holes, and surfaces that must remain free of powder.
  • Wipe down parts using chemical solvents or degreasers to remove oils, rust, and manufacturing debris.
  • Operate pretreatment systems such as chemical wash stations, phosphate baths, or blast cabinets to ensure proper powder adhesion.

Production Line Operations

  • Hang parts securely onto overhead conveyor racks or rolling carts using hooks and fixtures.
  • Unload finished parts carefully from the line after they emerge from the curing oven and have cooled completely.
  • Inspect quality of coated items for defects like light coverage, runs, bubbles, or contamination before final packaging.

Equipment & Shop Maintenance

  • Clean powder booths and fluidizing hoppers thoroughly between color changes to prevent cross-contamination.
  • Monitor oven temperatures and line speeds under the direction of the lead coater.
  • Maintain inventory by stocking powder boxes, masking supplies, hooks, and personal protective equipment.

Safety & Environmental Compliance

  • Wear mandatory PPE including air-purifying respirators, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, and protective suits.
  • Handle powder safely to manage dust accumulation and maintain a safe, explosion-free workspace.
  • Follow safety protocols for handling hazardous pre-treatment chemicals and working around high-heat curing ovens.

Requirements and Qualifications

Skills & Experience

  • Experience: Previous experience in a manufacturing, warehouse, or auto-body shop environment is a plus; we will train the right candidate to Powder Coat.
  • Education: High School Diploma or GED.
  • Detail-Oriented: Ability to spot minor surface imperfections and apply precise masking.
  • Pace: Able to work efficiently in a fast-paced, high-volume production environment.
  • Communications: Must be bi-lingual (English/Spanish)

Physical Requirements

  • Stamina: Ability to stand for 8–10 hours per day and perform repetitive reaching, lifting, and hanging motions.
  • Strength: Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly.
  • Environment: Comfortable working in an industrial environment that can be hot (near curing ovens) and dusty.

We are beginning with a small Rhode Island caseload. The position will start part-time, with hours expected to increase as additional referrals are received and services expand.

As the program grows, the successful candidate may have the opportunity to take on increased responsibility for new staff, referral relationships, service coordination, and regional program operations.

What You'll Do

Initially, your primary responsibility will be providing direct employment services to individuals with disabilities, including:

  • Career exploration and employment preparation

  • Job searching and job development

  • Connecting with local employers

  • Job placement

  • Job coaching and workplace support

  • Employment-retention services

  • Helping clients identify employment goals and overcome barriers to employment

  • Communicating with clients, families, employers, and referral partners

  • Completing accurate and timely service documentation

You'll provide services in community settings such as client homes, workplaces, employer locations, and other locations throughout the East Bay region.

An Opportunity to Grow With the Program

This is not simply a traditional Job Coach position.

RISE Services is actively developing its Rhode Island program, and we are looking for someone who would like the opportunity to grow with us.

As referrals and staffing increase, responsibilities may expand to include:

  • Helping coordinate services and client coverage

  • Supporting and mentoring newly hired Employment Specialists

  • Developing relationships with Rhode Island ORS and other referral partners

  • Building relationships with local employers

  • Participating in community and transition meetings

  • Helping monitor documentation and service quality

  • Assisting with the continued development of RISE Services' Rhode Island employment program

There are currently no employees reporting to this position. Supervisory responsibilities would be added as the Rhode Island team grows.

Who We're Looking For

This could be an excellent next step for an experienced:

Job Coach • Employment Specialist • Supported Employment Specialist • Vocational Specialist • Vocational Rehabilitation Professional

We are looking for someone who:

  • Works independently and follows through on responsibilities

  • Enjoys helping individuals with disabilities achieve employment goals

  • Is comfortable providing services in the community

  • Is organized, dependable, and responsive

  • Can solve routine problems independently

  • Communicates professionally with clients, families, employers, and referral partners

  • Is interested in professional growth and future leadership opportunities

  • Understands the importance of accurate and timely service documentation

Experience with Rhode Island ORS, vocational rehabilitation, supported employment, transition services, or Rhode Island disability services is especially valuable.

Qualifications

Applicants must meet one of the following:

Bachelor's degree in human services, social work, counseling, rehabilitation, psychology, education, or a related field plus at least three years of relevant experience;

OR

High school diploma or equivalent plus at least five years of relevant experience.

Relevant experience may include supported employment, vocational rehabilitation, disability services, employment services, job coaching, transition services, or a related field.

Additional Requirements

Candidates must have:

  • A valid driver's license

  • Reliable personal transportation

  • Required automobile insurance

  • Ability to travel throughout the East Bay region

  • Ability to transport clients when required

  • Ability to complete required background checks, screenings, and training

  • Basic proficiency with computers and web-based documentation systems

Mileage reimbursement is provided according to company policy.

About RISE Services

RISE Services helps individuals with disabilities obtain and maintain competitive, integrated employment through individualized, community-based services.

We're looking for someone who wants to do meaningful direct-service work today while having the opportunity to help build and eventually lead a growing employment-services program in Rhode Island.

Equal Employment Opportunity

RISE Services provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, country of ancestral origin, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, Rhode Island, or local law.

title: Senior Counsel, Digital Justice Initiative
company: Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law
description:
The Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law is one of the nation’s leading national racial justice legal organizations. Formed in 1963 at the request of President John F. Kennedy, the Lawyers’ Committee uses legal advocacy to achieve racial justice, fighting inside and outside the courts to ensure that Black people and other people of color have the voice, opportunity, and power to make the promises of our democracy real.

The Lawyers’ Committee has litigation, public policy, and advocacy programs in the substantive areas of Voting Rights, Election Protection, Digital Justice, Economic Justice, Criminal Justice, Economic Opportunities, and Fair Housing. The organization advances its mission as the premier organization marshaling the resources of the private bar alongside our own talented staff, with over 1 million pro bono hours billed to our cases and matters over the past decade.

Job Title: Senior Counsel, Digital Justice Initiative
Location: Washington, DC
Job Type: Full-Time
Union Affiliation: Union
Accountable to: Director, Digital Justice Initiative

About the Role:
Are you ready to shape the legal fight for civil rights in the digital age? The Digital Justice Initiative (DJI) is looking for a Senior Counsel to help lead high-impact litigation and advocacy at the intersection of technology, equity and justice.
This is a rare opportunity for an experienced litigator to make a real mark: you’ll develop and prosecute cutting-edge cases, shape legal strategy across DJI’s full portfolio, and drive the advocacy work that defines the field. Reporting to the Director of DJI, you’ll operate with significant autonomy – owning complex, high-stakes matters from strategy through execution and delivering the kind of work that sets the standard for the team.
If you’re a skilled litigator who wants your expertise to directly advance digital rights and justice, this role offers the platform, trust, and the mission to do exactly that.



What You’ll be Doing:
Essential responsibilities of the Senior Counsel include, but are not limited to, the following:
  • Litigate in federal and/or state courts.
  • Independently develop and execute litigation and advocacy strategies for complex, high-impact matters from investigation through resolution.
  • Lead complex legal workstreams and case teams, establish priorities and timelines, assess legal and strategic risk, and ensure high-quality, timely deliverables.
  • Conduct legal research and write legal memoranda, briefs, and other documents.
  • Produce final-quality legal analysis, pleadings, briefs, discovery, and other written work that reflects advanced legal judgment, accuracy, and strategic insight.
  • Lead investigations, identify plaintiffs for impact lawsuits, and develop new cases.
  • Conduct in-depth research of potentially highly offensive subject matters.
  • Effectively work and manage relationships with law firms and non-profit co-counsel.
  • Work in close collaboration with organizational and individual clients.
  • Engage in public speaking and write public-facing articles, reports, and other materials.
  • Demonstrate a commitment to diversity within and outside the office and an ability to implement an impact-driven approach to the work.
  • Monitor key developments and stay abreast of new technologies and data practices that impact civil rights and equal opportunity.
  • Serve as a senior subject-matter resource on digital justice, discriminatory data practices, algorithmic systems, emerging technologies, and their civil rights implications.
  • Advise colleagues and organizational leadership on complex legal questions, litigation risk, advocacy strategy, and developments affecting the Digital Justice Initiative portfolio.
  • Identify and implement improvements to legal processes, case-management practices, research tools, and quality standards.
  • Mentor and provide substantive guidance to less-experienced attorneys, fellows, paralegals, and other team members.
  • Work closely with colleagues across Lawyers’ Committee units to help identify and pursue shared advocacy objectives and in support other legal advocacy as needed.


Minimum Requirements and Competencies:
  • Deep commitment to the advancement of civil rights and racial justice.
  • Graduation from an accredited law school.
  • A minimum of 9 years post-JD legal experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex litigation matters or legal workstreams and exercise sound judgment with limited supervision.
  • Active membership in the District of Columbia bar or the ability to waive in.
  • Significant experience litigating complex civil matters, ideally including trials, fact and expert discovery, motion practice, and witness examinations.
  • At least some familiarity with technology and civil rights issues such as data privacy, algorithmic bias, online harassment, content moderation, anti-discrimination laws, Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, unfair and deceptive practices laws, or other similar issues.
  • Excellent legal research and writing skills.
  • Advanced ability to analyze novel and complex legal issues and consistently produce accurate, well-reasoned, final-quality work product.
  • Demonstrated strength in strategic judgment, creative problem solving, risk assessment, and decision-making.
  • Strong project and matter-management skills, including the ability to set priorities, manage competing deadlines, coordinate contributors, and move complex work forward.
  • Demonstrated ability to advise colleagues, provide constructive feedback, share expertise, and support the development of less-experienced team members;
  • Sound judgment and discretion in handling confidential, privileged, sensitive, and high-risk information.
  • Strong, creative, and curious intellect and ability to analyze issues, develop novel legal strategies, and apply traditional civil rights laws in a new environment.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the capacity to build trust and credibility and collaborate with multiple partners, internal and external.
  • Demonstrated stakeholder-management skills and the ability to build effective relationships with clients, impacted communities, co-counsel, experts, advocates, organizational leaders, and other partners.
  • Demonstrated experience working with and for communities of color and/or low-income communities.
  • Willingness and ability to travel on a regular basis for client matters and other meetings.



Ready to Make an Impact? If you are passionate about civil rights, racial justice, and promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion, we want to hear from you. Join our mission to drive positive change and contribute to our dynamic team!

Apply Today: Be part of the force for civil rights and make a lasting impact. Submit your application to help us create a more equitable and inclusive world.

Benefits: The Lawyers' Committee offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes healthcare coverage (medical, dental & vision), parental leave, 403(b) contribution with employer match contributions, voluntary short- and long-term disability and an employer paid monthly cell phone stipend.

Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: The Lawyers’ Committee embraces diversity and inclusion in our workplace. We strongly encourage candidates of color and candidates from underrepresented communities to apply. The Lawyers’ Committee does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race, religion, color, creed, national origin, ancestry, disability, medical condition, marital status, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression, pregnancy, parental status, family responsibility, personal appearance, genetic information, matriculation, immigration status, union activities, political affiliation, military veteran status, credit information or any other status protected under law.
This position is part of a bargaining unit represented by the Nonprofit Professional Employees Union. Employment terms, including wages and benefits, are subject to collective bargaining agreements.

Reasonable Accommodation: The Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and applicable state and local laws. If you require an accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact Human Resources at humanresources@lawyerscommittee.org.

This position is part of a bargaining unit represented by the Nonprofit Professional Employees Union. Employment terms, including wages and benefits, are subject to collective bargaining agreements.

The Lawyers’ Committee offers competitive compensation for our exempt attorney positions, with salaries ranging from $76,000 to $165,000. The specific salary within this range is determined based on the candidate’s experience, including the timing of their law degree attainment. Generally, candidates who obtained their law degree more recently will start at the lower end of the scale. Candidates with more extensive experience or those who obtained their law degree earlier may be eligible for salaries towards the higher end of the scale. We are committed to providing a fair and transparent compensation structure that reflects the value and experience of our attorneys.

title: Financial Audit Intern- Summer 2027
description:
Financial Audit Intern
Summer 2027: June 1 - August 6

About Our Program
The Comptroller of the Treasury's Audit Internship Program is a 10-week paid educational and experiential learning opportunity offering undergraduate students a chance to witness and participate in the audit operations of the office. Interns will spend the summer building skills through their assignment to an active audit, audit-specific training, and professional development training. Interns will also have opportunities to build relationships with each other through shared experiences.

Intern responsibilities may include learning to examine and review records, reports, financial statements, and management practices for state and local government entities and other organizations receiving public funds. Interns may have the opportunity to evaluate the following: fairness of financial statement presentation, the adequacy of internal controls, the efficiency and effectiveness of an entity's operations and systems, and compliance with laws, regulations, contracts, and grant agreements.

Our summer internship program is designed to be both professionally and academically beneficial. Interns gain hands‑on experience while participating in meaningful professional development activities such as Business Etiquette Day, a full‑day session focused on professionalism, emotional intelligence, and understanding one’s professional brand, complete with an etiquette lunch led by staff. Interns also enjoy engaging activities like speed networking with full‑time employees, a guided tour of the Tennessee Capitol to explore the state’s history, and weekly cohort check‑ins to foster connection and collaboration. The cohort experience culminates in a final presentation showcasing what interns have learned and contributed during their time with the Office.


Location
Financial audit internship opportunities are based out of Nashville, Tennessee. Depending on the audit assignment, interns may have the opportunity for limited travel during the summer. Typical travel opportunities are in the Nashville area; however, some may allow for travel to other parts of Tennessee.

Who We're Looking For
We are seeking students who are rising juniors, seniors, or enrolled in graduate accounting programs and are interested in applying their classroom knowledge to governmental auditing. To qualify for the internship program, applicants should have successfully completed at least 6 credit hours of accounting coursework. Preference will be given to students who have completed intermediate or advanced accounting classes.

Successful interns are those who are adaptable, able to think critically, work well both individually and as part of a team, and are willing to learn and grow. Candidates should exhibit strong interpersonal, verbal communication, organizational, and writing skills. Interns are expected to apply their classroom knowledge to meaningful audit work.

About Our Office
The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury is responsible for the audit of state and local governmental entities and participates in the general financial and administrative management and oversight of state government. In the Comptroller’s Office, we strive to deliver on our mission to make government work better. Through dedicated hard work and commitment, every Comptroller’s Office employee accepts personal responsibility to accomplish our mission and uphold it.

Compensation
Interns are paid $24 per hour via a third-party company. This position may require in-state day travel to audit sites. Audit-related travel will be reimbursed.

Equal Opportunity Employer

It is the Comptroller’s policy to provide an environment free of discrimination and harassment of an individual because of that person’s race, color, national origin, age (40 and over), sex, sexual orientation, transgender and gender identity status, pregnancy, religion, creed, disability, veteran’s status, or any other category protected by state and/or federal civil rights laws.

title: Analytics Engineer
description:
TITLE

Analytics Engineer III

WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE

You will take ownership of how Addgene's data is structured, documented, and maintained, and establish the standards and practices that define how the organization works with data. Your work will build a data warehouse that earns trust by deploying engineering best practices where they are currently missing, validating the datasets that drive decisions, and enabling anyone on the team to understand how any result was produced.

POSITION REPORTS TO

Director of Data Science

APPROXIMATE START DATE

October 2026

SALARY

$117,000 - $120,000 annually + our amazing benefits (see below)!

LOCATION & POLICY ON REMOTE WORK

This is a hybrid position that requires at least two days a week onsite at our Watertown, Massachusetts Headquarters. Our beautiful office space has free, ample parking with a complimentary shuttle from Harvard Square and is on multiple bus lines, with the cost of public transit covered by Addgene for those onsite at least twice a week.

The Role:

Our data team functions as an internal core facility, serving partners across scientific, commercial, and business development functions. We are looking for an Analytics Engineer who will take ownership of the infrastructure that powers our data, bringing engineering discipline, sound judgment and responsibility for the systems they build and maintain.

This is a role for someone who finds satisfaction in making messy things reliable. You will inherit a complex data environment, and your job will be to understand it thoroughly, and implement deliberate improvements. The work is technical at its core, but requires deep analytical thinking that catches problems before they surface and ability to push tasks forward to completion.

To succeed in this role, your work will span three areas:

Data warehouse ownership

  • Take end-to-end ownership of our BigQuery data warehouse, including organization, documentation, and maintenance
  • Apply software engineering best practices for data transformation and modeling, bringing consistency and version control to how tables and views are built and updated
  • Assess internal data sources not yet represented in the warehouse and design pipelines to ingest, validate, and integrate them
  • Build and support reliable datasets as the foundation for dashboards and reporting
  • Manage tasks, assess priority and scope, and set realistic expectations

Data quality and validation

  • Create and maintain data quality checks that catch problems before they reach downstream users
  • Develop and operationalize a shared data lexicon to establish consistent definitions that can be applied across tables, dashboards, and reports
  • Expand instructions for BigQuery tables and views to improve the reliability and usefulness of AI-assisted data access
  • Write reliable, readable Python for wrangling, transformation, and reporting tasks

Pipeline development and maintenance

  • Build and maintain robust data pipelines that bring critical internal data sources into the warehouse reliably and on schedule
  • Improve the coverage and resilience of existing pipelines, reducing fragility and increasing the value of our data
  • Contribute to code review, applying and upholding engineering standards across the team's codebase
  • Identify opportunities to automate manual or repetitive processes, freeing team capacity for higher-value work

Skills and Competencies

  • 5+ years of experience in an analytics engineering role
  • A Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field is preferred; a Bachelor's degree with equivalent professional experience is also acceptable
  • Hands-on experience owning and managing a data warehouse, such as BigQuery or comparable platform, with track record of not just maintaining what exists, but making decisions about how it should be structured and rationale behind it
  • Experience with dbt for data transformation and warehouse management is highly preferred
  • Strong proficiency with SQL, including complex queries, joins and aggregations
  • Proficient with Python for data engineering tasks (pipeline development, scripting, automation)
  • Experience with data validation, quality assurance, and documentation practices
  • Familiarity with AI tools or agents in data engineering context
  • Interest in the life sciences and a willingness to develop working knowledge of the science behind the data related to your work
  • Demonstrated ability to identify problems proactively, and follow through without close supervision
  • Experience in a small, cross-functional team where priorities shift and individual judgment matters

Benefits

At Addgene, we prioritize our people with comprehensive benefits that support both your work and your life.

Full-time employees receive:

  • 85% company-paid healthcare premiums including dental (extending to family members) and 100% company-paid deductible
  • Life, short-term, and long-term disability insurance.
  • 22 days of PTO on top of our winter break closure and company holidays. ‌
  • A 403(b) retirement account with a company match of 4% after 2 years of employment. ‌
  • Annual professional development stipend
  • Annual lifestyle stipend
  • Fully paid public transportation for employees who work onsite four or more days per week. ‌
  • Onsite yoga classes & wellness reimbursement
  • Pet insurance
  • Annual financial planning one-on-ones with our plan administrator

The Organization:

Addgene is a self-sustaining, thriving nonprofit life sciences organization that was created to help scientists share DNA-based research materials called plasmids. ‌Our mission is to accelerate research and discovery by improving access to useful research materials and information. Since its founding in 2004, Addgene has grown and innovated in order to assist the research community by archiving and sharing useful DNA-based research materials and resources (such as plasmids, viral vectors, and recombinant antibodies) with scientists worldwide. Broad availability of these unique research materials promotes the advancement of research in a wide variety of disciplines, including cancer, heart disease, and neurodegenerative disorders, while increasing collaboration within the scientific community. Learn more here from our President & Executive Director, Chonnettia Jones.

As an “Addgenie”, you will work collaboratively with internal teams to help fulfill this mission, including scientists, software engineers and product developers, renowned customer support teams, scientific content creators, and business development professionals. Together, Addgenies create and enhance opportunities for research scientists to deposit their materials, find products and resources easily on our website, and receive unparalleled support in receiving and expertly using our materials in their own experiments.

Life at Addgene:

Addgene is a truly special place to work. We are an inclusive and welcoming group of people from many backgrounds and perspectives. We believe in flexibility, actively supporting professional development, and a strong work/life balance. We value sharing ideas and feedback with each other and the company. Learn more about Life at Addgene

title: Senior Database Administrator (DB2 z/OS + Oracle + SQL Server)
description:
We are looking for a Senior Database Administrator (DB2 z/OS + Oracle + SQL Server) to support our client based in Tallahassee, FL.

US BASED CANDIDATES ONLY.

Candidates must be located in Tallahassee, FL or the surrounding area.

*No third parties and no sponsorship*

Who we are

Founded in 2009 and headquartered in beautiful Miami, FL, TECKpert is a tech consulting and staff augmentation firm. At TECKpert, we offer a contingent workforce built for any size digital transformation project. Experts in design, development, IT, analytics and marketing, provide innovative digital solutions to achieve success in our new economy. Our leaders identify the technical talent best suited to bolster our client's capabilities, across all industries, including, healthcare, government, finance, legal, real estate, and startups.

The Opportunity

TECKpert is seeking a Senior Database Administrator to support our client, a state transportation agency in Tallahassee, FL, on the database layer feeding a multi-year financial management modernization program. This role supports critical database platforms across DB2 for z/OS, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server, ensuring the application and processing architectures, data dictionaries, and database schemas meet the agency's data standards.

The DBA will assist in the design, development, amendments, and optimization of the database schemas to meet system requirements. This includes performance monitoring and tuning, database maintenance, disaster recovery, and support for the agency's integrated application environment. Work is 5 days per week onsite at the agency's Tallahassee IT office with flexible hours between 7:00 AM and 7:00 PM plus Saturday and on-call coverage as needed.

Job duties include, but are not limited to:

  • Perform daily operational and database administration activities across DB2 for z/OS, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server platforms
  • Plan, design, implement, and support database structures for application and reporting workloads
  • Conduct database performance monitoring and tuning using z/OS and cross-platform monitoring tools
  • Develop and maintain database administration procedures, runbooks, and technical documentation
  • Perform SQL code reviews and query optimization for application teams
  • Assist with training and mentoring of other technical staff on DBA best practices
  • Support disaster recovery planning, point-in-time recovery, and verification testing for infrastructure change management
  • Perform DB2 for z/OS catalog maintenance, sub-system point-in-time recovery, and DB2 upgrades
  • Coordinate with application, security, and infrastructure teams to maintain a stable and performant database environment
  • Support other database or infrastructure activities as requested by the agency

Compensation and Term

This opportunity is for a full-time, contract position with possible extensions and pay commensurate with experience up to $65 per hour or $130,000 per year. The contract runs October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, with possible renewal. The role is 40 hours per week onsite in Tallahassee, FL, with flexible hours between 7:00 AM and 7:00 PM and possible Saturday or on-call coverage.

Qualifications you need

A successful candidate has the following experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience
  • Minimum 15 years combined database administration experience across DB2 for z/OS, Microsoft SQL Server, and Oracle
  • Advanced knowledge of DB2 for z/OS application integration, performance management, and database administration
  • Advanced knowledge of upgrading DB2 for z/OS, DB2 catalog maintenance, and DB2 sub-system point-in-time recovery
  • Advanced knowledge of JCL for building and troubleshooting mainframe job streams
  • In-depth knowledge of the Z/OS integrated platform, ISPF, COBOL, CA GEN model management, and ASG Scheduler
  • In-depth knowledge of DB2 for z/OS database monitoring tools and z/OS software monitoring tools
  • In-depth knowledge of technical infrastructure implementation planning and coordination
  • Solid working knowledge of Oracle 10g and above application integration, performance management, and database administration
  • Solid working knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2008R2 / 2012 application integration, performance management, and database administration
  • Solid working knowledge of z/OS started task creation and management, RACF, CICS, IOF, and Disaster Recovery
  • Working knowledge of SSMS, SSRS, SSIS, Windows Servers, and Microsoft Azure
  • Excellent communication, customer service, and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to work 5 days per week onsite in Tallahassee, FL, plus flexible hours and on-call coverage
  • Authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship
  • Ability to pass an FBI Level II background check

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience with FDOT integrated database infrastructure
  • Knowledge of FDOT Financial Management applications
  • Knowledge of the FDOT integrated application environment
  • Prior experience supporting the Florida PALM (Planning, Accounting, and Ledger Management) program or a comparable statewide accounting modernization initiative
  • Working knowledge of z/OS EXITs and BJS
  • IBM Certified Database Administrator (DB2 for z/OS), Oracle Certified Professional DBA, or Microsoft Certified: Azure Database Administrator Associate

Working with us

Working with TECKpert means more options. As new opportunities arise, you tell us what you think is a good fit for you. What industries interest you most? Do you prefer an on-location, 9-5? Or would you want a flexible schedule and remote work? We proudly offer a wide variety of roles. Many of our TECKperts enjoy coworking and skills training coupled with the stability of full-time employment. We believe TECKpert gives today's digital professionals an agile path to start and advance their career. All of our opportunities require at least 20 hours per week and can be one to twelve months in length. Choose the opportunity that matches your interest and desired cadence.

Next Steps

Thank you for applying. If you are selected, we will reach out for a skills assessment and to schedule a short prescreen video call to get to know you better. We will also be in touch for any future roles your profile will match with.

Important Application Notice:

To ensure the integrity of our recruitment process, please note the following requirements:

  • Resume Formatting: Ensure your resume is clearly formatted and includes all relevant details. Applications with poorly formatted resumes or missing critical information will be rejected without review.
  • Verification Information: To help verify your identity, please include a link to your LinkedIn profile, GitHub repository (for technical roles), or other professional profiles that can substantiate your experience and verify your identity.
  • Fraudulent Submissions: We take candidate verification seriously. Submitting fraudulent information, fake resumes, or any attempt to deceive will result in immediate disqualification from the process. Fraudulent applications may also be referred to the appropriate authorities for further action.

Recruiting Safety Notice: To protect job seekers from scam listings, please note that all official communications from our hiring team will come exclusively from a @teckpert.com email address. TECKpert will never ask for sensitive personal information or financial details during the initial interview phase. If you are ever unsure about the authenticity of a outreach, please reach out to us directly through our official website.

Thank you for your cooperation
