title: Director of Retail Banking
company: First Federal Bank of Kansas City
description:
First Federal Bank of Kansas City (FFBKC) is one of the largest mutually owned banks in the Midwest with a 90-year history of serving the Kansas City metropolitan area. We exist to help people build a better financial future and as a mutual institution, every dollar we earn is reinvested in our customers, our communities, and our people. We are in an intentional period of growth and transformation, expanding our small business, commercial banking, and FinTech capabilities while strengthening our retail foundation and relationships.

At First Federal, you’ll be supported by diverse, talented, energetic individuals moving toward a common vision of prosperity and a home for all. You’ll have boundless opportunities for growth – whether it’s personal or professional development to reach your career goals, company events to strengthen your connections, or volunteer work to champion our community partners.

Your success is our success. When our employees feel valued, our customers feel valued, and our community grows.

Hear what our team members have to say:

SUMMARY

The Director of Retail Banking is a visible, coaching-first leader responsible for the performance, culture, development, and training of FFBKC's nine banking centers. This is not a desk role. It is a presence role built on consistent, meaningful engagement with every banker and Banking Center Manager in the network.

This leader plays a key role on the retail leadership team and is the primary advocate for retail banking within the organization. They carry a clear vision for what retail banking looks like at its best, communicate that vision with conviction, and translate it into daily direction, coaching, and accountability for their teams. They show up with an agenda and follow through on issues quickly and escalate appropriately. They know their people by name and aspiration and every person on the team feels it.

Critically, this leader is the primary developer and deliverer of the sales, leadership, and customer experience (CX) training program for the retail network. Operational training is managed separately by other departments; this role owns the sales, service and leadership development function for retail exclusively.

The Director of Retail Banking reports to the Chief Operating Officer and operates with a high degree of autonomy, accountability and self-direction. They are expected to bring strategic thinking, retail expertise, training capability, and execution discipline that makes the retail division run efficiently and productively. They communicate proactively, clearly, and candidly with leadership at every level.


WHAT THE TEAM WILL SAY ABOUT YOU

The feedback we received from our banking center staff describes this person precisely:
  • An advocate for retail banking and the people who do it every day.
  • Present, visiting every banking center every two to three weeks, spending time with every team member, not just the manager and providing feedback to the Executive Leadership Team on ways to improve.
  • Make people feel seen and heard.
  • When there is an issue, you tackle it and follow through and your team never wonders if their concern was received.
  • Balance risk and maximize opportunity within the bank's established risk appetite.
  • Not afraid to change and bring your team along with you.
  • Show up to every visit with a clear agenda providing education, direction, coaching, and recognition.
  • Communicate a vision for retail that every team member can articulate.
  • Proactive, not reactive.
  • Feel like a part of the team, not above it.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Presence & Advocacy:

  • Conducts regular, structured banking center visits on a minimum bi-weekly cadence, with a prepared agenda that includes education, coaching, direction, and recognition and spending time with every team member.
  • Serves as the primary advocate for retail banking within the organization, ensuring the needs, wins, and voices of banking center teams are heard and acted upon at the leadership level.
  • Responds to banking center concerns and issues with urgency; follows through with timely resolution and communication so teams always know where things stand.
  • Builds genuine relationships with banking center staff at every level, knowing their professional goals, strengths, and development areas.
Training Design & Delivery:
  • Develops, owns, facilitates, and continuously improves the retail team's sales training curriculum, customer experience (CX) training materials, and banking center manager leadership development content.
  • Ensures all training content reflects current bank strategy, products, service standard, and the Hungry, Humble, Smart performance framework.
  • Leads the completion and full rollout of consumer loan training across the retail network (with HELOC training to be completed within 90 days of hire).
  • Partners with operational departments where training intersects with operational processes; but owns the sales, service, and leadership development curriculum exclusively.
  • Measures training effectiveness through branch performance outcomes, scorecard results, and observed behavior change - revising content and delivery accordingly, ensuring that the learning is being put into action and achieving the desired results.
Vision & Direction:
  • Establishes, communicates, and continuously reinforces a clear vision, budget, and scorecard for retail banking that every team member can understand and connect to their daily work.
  • Translates organizational strategy into branch-level priorities and expectations; ensures teams know what they are working toward and why it matters.
  • Leads change with clarity and conviction - bringing teams along through transitions rather than around them.
  • Operates within and reinforces the bank's Entrepreneurial Operating System (EOS) rhythm: clear rocks, scorecards, structured rhythm meetings, and accountable follow-through.
Coaching & Development:
  • Coaches Banking Center Managers and their teams to develop capability, not just correct behavior, by asking questions before offering solutions.
  • Uses the Banking Center Team Challenge scorecard (Hungry, Humble, Smart) as the primary framework for performance conversations, development planning, and recognition.
  • Develops Banking Center Managers into leaders who operate with confidence and accountability; identifies and accelerates high potential individuals.
  • Builds a sales culture grounded in relationship depth and household primary, not product pushing.
Performance & Accountability:
  • Drives deposit growth, net new account production, partner referrals, and consumer loan volume across all nine banking center locations.
  • Owns performance against Banking Center Team Challenge targets and communicates results transparently with banking center teams and leadership.
  • Manages direct reports with clear expectations, defined deadlines, and structured performance conversations.
  • Monitors key retail metrics including deposit mix, household primacy, product penetration, attrition, and customer satisfaction scores.
  • Executes the retail customer acquisition strategy developed in partnership with leadership, using data to inform targeting, channel allocation, and branch-level priorities.
Strategy & Partnerships:
  • Partners actively in the bank's retail strategy development and the annual retail recommendation to the board.
  • Partners with Commercial Banking and Treasury Management to identify and convert commercial client employees and referral opportunities into retail banking relationships.
  • Collaborates with Marketing to develop targeted campaigns supporting new customer acquisition, customer retention, checking account growth, deposit growth, HELOC production, and overall relationship deepening.
  • Identifies and proposes new products, services, and approaches to advance retail banking goals; stays current on internal and external market trends, competitor activity, and customer behavior.
  • Uses internal and external data to analyze and recommend opportunities for growth and improved revenue.
Community & Culture:
  • Maintains active community presence in the bank's markets, representing FFBKC with professionalism and purpose.
  • Promotes and model's the bank's mission - helping people build a better financial future - in every customer and team interaction.
  • Participates in community development activities and encourages banking center teams to do the same.
  • Complies with all applicable banking laws and regulations, including, but not limited to, the Bank Secrecy Act, USA Patriot Act, and related anti-money laundering statutes; and federal consumer protection legislation and regulations.
SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
Direct reports include Banking Center Managers across all nine locations. May include additional retail support roles as the organization evolves. Responsible for hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and development of all direct reports in accordance with bank policies, practices, and applicable law.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
The right candidate will bring a combination of retail banking expertise, genuine people leadership, training design and facilitation skills, and the character to lead a team that is already performing well- someone to take it further, not start over.
  • Humble, hungry, and smart - the Ideal Team Player standard applied across our organization.
  • Kind, not just nice, and willing to deliver honest feedback and have hard conversations in service of a person's growth.
  • Presence as a discipline.
  • A builder, not a fixer - someone who coaches people rather than solves problems for them.
  • Minimum 5 years of retail banking leadership experience with direct responsibility for multiple branch locations and their teams.
  • Demonstrated track record of developing Banking Center Managers and frontline staff - not just managing to results.
  • Demonstrated experience developing sales, CX, and leadership training curriculum - not just delivering programs created by others; must be able to design from scratch.
  • Proven experience facilitating training for varied audiences, from frontline tellers to Banking Center Managers, with measurable outcomes.
  • Proven experience building and executing sales and service cultures, with measurable results in deposit growth, household acquisition, and customer satisfaction.
  • Consumer lending experience required; HELOC experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience operating within a structured performance management or business operating system (EOS or equivalent) preferred.
  • Familiarity with data-driven retail strategy and the ability to translate analytics into branch-level action.
Education:
  • Bachelor's degree (B.A./B.S.) in business or related field, or equivalent professional experience.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS
National Mortgage Licensing System & Registry (NMLS) registration; Notary Public License; Signature Guarantee Certification

Note: The purpose of this document is to provide a general summary of essential responsibilities and requirements for the position and is not meant as an exhaustive list.

First Federal actively seeks to recruit and hire protected veterans.

First Federal Bank is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all people without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, citizenship status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other legally protected category.

title: Job Coach
description:
Job Coach / Employment Specialist – Part-Time

Location: Springfield, Virginia
Service Area: Springfield and surrounding Fairfax County communities
Pay: $21.00–$22.00 per hour, based on experience
Hours: Up to 29 hours per week, with the potential to transition to full-time
Schedule: Predominantly daytime hours, Monday through Friday
Work Setting: Community-based with regular local travel
Mileage: Reimbursement for approved work-related travel

Help People Build Careers and Greater Independence

RISE Services is hiring a compassionate, dependable, and resourceful Job Coach / Employment Specialist to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain meaningful employment.

In this community-based role, you will meet participants at employer worksites and other locations throughout Springfield and surrounding Fairfax County communities. You will help participants explore career interests, search and apply for jobs, prepare for interviews, learn workplace responsibilities, communicate with employers, and develop the skills needed for long-term employment success.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. We welcome applicants with relevant experience in disability services, human services, education, behavioral health, workforce development, direct support, career coaching, case management, retail supervision, customer service, or other positions involving teaching, mentoring, or helping others succeed.

Training is provided.

Schedule and Hours

This position offers up to 29 hours per week. Most services in the Springfield area are provided during daytime hours, Monday through Friday.

Weekend work is occasionally needed to provide coverage when another employee is unavailable, but this is not a regularly scheduled weekend position.

Weekly schedules may include:

  • On-site job coaching

  • Job searching and completing applications

  • Resume and interview preparation

  • Employer outreach

  • Employment-readiness activities

  • Community-based participant meetings

  • Progress notes and required documentation

When a participant is not working their full number of authorized service hours, the Job Coach may provide other approved employment services, including job searching, completing applications, developing resumes, preparing for interviews, contacting employers, and teaching workplace-readiness skills.

Employees who want additional hours may have the opportunity to transition to full-time as caseloads and service needs grow. Full-time hours are not guaranteed and depend on participant referrals, scheduling needs, employee availability, and satisfactory job performance.

What You’ll Do

Job Coaching and Workplace Support

  • Provide individualized coaching at employer worksites and in community settings.

  • Help participants learn job duties, workplace routines, safety procedures, and employer expectations.

  • Teach workplace communication, professional behavior, time management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Help participants communicate effectively with supervisors and coworkers.

  • Develop natural workplace supports that promote greater independence.

  • Monitor participant progress and adjust coaching strategies as participants develop new skills.

  • Provide ongoing support to promote successful employment retention.

Job Search and Career Preparation

  • Help participants identify their strengths, interests, abilities, support needs, and employment goals.

  • Assist with resumes, applications, job searches, and interview preparation.

  • Conduct mock interviews and employment-readiness activities.

  • Identify employment opportunities that match each participant’s interests, abilities, experience, and goals.

  • Coordinate interviews, hiring activities, and onboarding support.

  • Help participants understand workplace expectations and identify reasonable accommodations when appropriate.

Employer and Community Engagement

  • Build professional relationships with employers throughout Springfield and Fairfax County.

  • Contact businesses to identify potential employment opportunities.

  • Educate employers about inclusive hiring and available workplace supports.

  • Communicate with participants, families, employers, vocational rehabilitation counselors, support coordinators, schools, and community partners.

  • Attend hiring events, team meetings, training, and other scheduled activities.

Documentation and Service Coordination

  • Complete accurate progress notes and service documentation within required deadlines.

  • Maintain participant records according to funding-source and organizational requirements.

  • Track job searches, applications, interviews, placements, wages, scheduled hours, and employment retention.

  • Communicate participant progress, concerns, scheduling changes, and service needs to the appropriate supervisor.

  • Participate in service-planning and team-coordination activities.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree is not required.

  • Relevant experience supporting individuals with disabilities or others who experience barriers to employment is preferred.

  • Experience in teaching, coaching, mentoring, customer service, supervision, human services, behavioral health, workforce development, or a related field may also be considered.

  • Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

  • Ability to work independently and make responsible decisions in community settings.

  • Ability to maintain a consistent schedule and complete documentation on time.

  • Basic computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.

  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

  • Ability and willingness to travel locally and transport participants when required.

  • Ability to satisfy applicable background-screening and employment requirements.

Preferred but Not Required

  • Supported Employment, Individual Supported Employment, job-coaching, or job-development experience.

  • Experience supporting individuals with intellectual, developmental, behavioral, or other disabilities.

  • Knowledge of Medicaid Waiver, vocational rehabilitation, or disability-employment services.

  • Understanding of the Americans with Disabilities Act and reasonable workplace accommodations.

  • Experience working with employers, schools, support coordinators, vocational rehabilitation agencies, or community organizations.

  • CESP, ACRE, DSP, or another employment-support credential.

Who Will Succeed in This Position?

You may be a strong fit if you are:

  • Compassionate, patient, dependable, and encouraging.

  • Comfortable working at employer locations and throughout the community.

  • Able to teach and motivate participants while promoting independence.

  • Professional and confident when communicating with employers and community partners.

  • Resourceful and willing to find solutions when challenges arise.

  • Organized and able to manage appointments, follow-ups, and documentation.

  • Flexible when participant or employer schedules change.

  • Comfortable working independently without constant direct supervision.

Why Join RISE Services?

  • Make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals with disabilities.

  • Help people build careers, confidence, and greater independence.

  • Work predominantly during weekday daytime hours.

  • Receive mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel.

  • Participate in paid training and professional development.

  • Build experience in human services, disability services, workforce development, and career coaching.

  • Access potential opportunities for additional hours and advancement.

  • Join a collaborative, growing, and mission-driven organization.

Benefits

Part-time employees may be eligible for:

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Employee Tenure Bonus Program

  • Mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel

  • Paid training and professional development

Employees who transition to an eligible full-time position may also receive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays

  • Short-term disability insurance

  • Life insurance

  • Long-term care option

Benefit eligibility requirements apply.

Important Work-Setting Information

This is a community-based position, not a remote or traditional office-based role. Services are provided at employer worksites and other community locations throughout Springfield and surrounding Fairfax County communities.

Applicants must have reliable transportation and be comfortable driving between community locations. Transporting participants may be required as part of the position.

Equal Opportunity Employer

RISE Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We recruit, hire, train, compensate, and promote employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Apply Today

If you enjoy teaching, encouraging others, solving problems, and helping people accomplish meaningful goals, apply for the Part-Time Job Coach / Employment Specialist position with RISE Services.

A bachelor’s degree and previous job-coaching experience are not required. Relevant experience, dependability, professionalism, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to helping others succeed are strongly valued.

title: Simulator Technician II-Security Clearance Eligibility Required
description:
Job Summary


The Simulator Technician II is responsible for building, maintaining, repairing, and operating various types of simulators used in training programs for the military, aviation, and other industries. The technician will be responsible for ensuring that the simulators are in good working condition and will work with other team members to ensure that the training programs and equipment run smoothly. This position will support maintenance services for Crew Training Aids, Devices, Simulators and Simulations (TADSS), Ground Maintenance Driver Trainers (GMDT). The position is located at Ft. Benning, GA, USA

Responsibilities/Duties/Functions/Tasks

  • Perform routine maintenance on simulators, including cleaning, calibration, and component replacement In Accordance With (IAW) the documented Scheduled Maintenance/Preventative Maintenance Checks and Services.
  • Troubleshoot and diagnose issues with simulators and work with other team members to resolve problems quickly.
  • Maintain TADSS and Government Furnished Property (FGFP) in Fully Mission Capable (FMC) condition.
  • Maintenance performed IAW technical data; if technical data/checklist is not provided for any single item, maintenance IAW the best commercial standards. Maintain all the documentation (Operator & Maintainer Manual, Instructor/Operator Manual, Commercial Off- The-Shelf Manual, Technical Data Package Schematics and Cold Start Procedures) spares and tools.
  • Conduct safety checks and inspections of simulators prior to use.
  • Review/report facility issues that cause Non-Fair Wear and Tear (NFWT) to simulator devices.
  • Keep detailed records of all maintenance and repairs performed on simulators.
  • Ensure that all simulators are in compliance with industry standards and regulations.
  • Work with the engineering team to improve simulator design, functionality and manufacturability.
  • Assist in the setup and breakdown of training equipment, including setting up equipment and preparing simulators for use.
  • Provide technical support to users of simulators during training sessions.
  • Coordinate with other departments to ensure that simulators are available for use when needed.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for the job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent, technical degree or certification preferred.
  • 3 - 6 years of experience in maintaining and operating simulators.
  • Understanding of computer systems and software, including programming and troubleshooting.
  • Familiarity with electrical and mechanical systems and ability to troubleshoot and repair them.
  • Ability to work effectively in a team environment and communicate clearly with other team members.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to keep accurate records.
  • Ability to work independently and prioritize tasks effectively.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

Essential Mental Requirements

  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Excellent decision-making skills.

title: Critical Environment Technician (Night Shift)
description:
Overview

As a Critical Environment Technician (NightShift) (CET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, recognizing safe versus unsafe work environment, having a hands-on understanding of how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.

Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.



Responsibilities

Critical Environment Culture

  • Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
  • Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
  • Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
  • Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
  • Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
  • Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Equipment and Systems Operations
  • Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
  • Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.
  • Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometime minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
  • Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Physical Requirements
  • Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working Conditions
  • Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
  • As indicated, above, this role has a travel requirement of up to 25% which means you may be required to travel, from time to time, as part of this role.
  • As indicated above, have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.

Other

  • Embody our culture and values


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.

Background Check Requirements:

Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
  • Citizenship Verification: This position requires verification of citizenship due to citizenship-based legal restrictions. Specifically, this position supports United States federal, state, and/or local government agency customers and is subject to certain citizenship-based restrictions where required or permitted by applicable law. To meet this legal requirement, and as a condition of employment, the successful candidate’s citizenship will be verified with a valid passport.
  • This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 1+ year(s) technical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical) OR equivalent experience.


Critical Environment Ops ATR-B - The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is USD $23.65 - $37.07 per hour. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $31.54 - $40.91 per hour.

Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here:

Critical Environment Ops ATR-C - The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is USD $27.45 - $48.03 per hour. title: SVP Growth & Development (Non-profit, Cleantech Incubator)
description:
About LACI

The Los Angeles Cleantech Incubator (LACI) is a nonprofit organization creating an inclusive green economy. We create impact in Los Angeles and nationwide by working with startups to accelerate the commercialization of clean technologies; transforming markets through catalytic partnerships with policymakers, innovators, and market leaders in zero emission transportation, clean energy, and sustainable cities; and enhancing communities through workforce development, pilots, and other programs. Originally founded as an economic development initiative by the City of Los Angeles and its Department of Water & Power (LADWP), LACI is recognized as one of the most innovative business incubators in the world. Since 2011, LACI has helped 500+ portfolio companies raise over $1.5 billion in funding, generate $477 million in revenue, deploy $60M+ in pilot funding, and create more than 3,000 direct and indirect jobs, with a long-term economic impact of more than $733 million. Learn more at .

Position Summary:

The Senior Vice President (SVP) of Growth and Development is a critical leadership role responsible for driving and executing LACI’s development and fundraising strategy to support the organization’s growth. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer (COO) and partnering closely with the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the SVP will align development initiatives across the organization as we work to scale our impact throughout the Los Angeles region and beyond via our growing national programming (BATWorks in NYC, City Climate Innovation Challenge, LACI Cleantech Debt Fund, National Coalition of Clean Energy Incubators).

The ideal candidate is a sophisticated strategist who has successfully led organizations through similar inflection points. Leveraging our strong financial health (current $25M–$30M budget) and existing funding base, you will optimize current institutional models and build sustainable corporate partnerships, unlock high-net-worth individual donors, and diversify and expand our reach. As a member of the Leadership Team, you will oversee the Development Team and serve as a vital external ambassador.

What You’ll Do:

  • Fundraising Strategy and Execution: Collaborate with the CEO and COO to establish annual and multi-year fundraising goals, related strategies, and assignment of responsibilities for targets, follow up, etc. Design and implement comprehensive strategies to increase funding to support growth and diversify revenue streams, including government grants, corporate sponsorships, philanthropic foundations, and high-net-worth individual support.
  • Relationship Management and Campaigns/Events: Develop a dynamic donor cultivation system, including a relationship management system to enhance organizational alignment and ensure effective engagement with current and prospective supporters. Support and coordinate investment-oriented capital for LACI funds and financing initiatives. Lead annual and multi-year fundraising campaigns, events, and special initiatives. Partner with the Marketing and Communications Team to ensure cohesive messaging that highlights fundraising goals and organizational impact.
  • Leadership and Collaboration: Work closely with the CEO and COO on fundraising progress, strategic opportunities, and challenges, along with regular reporting. Work across LACI’s matrixed organizational structure and strategy by coordinating with Leadership Team members to align funding opportunities with LACI’s strategic organizational priorities. Create and manage the Development Team budget and resources. Supervise, mentor, and support Development Team staff, establishing clear performance metrics and professional development paths. Manage external consultants as required.
  • Grant Management and Development: Collaborate with the Senior Director, Grants Development to oversee the full lifecycle of grant applications—from identification and proposal writing to submission and reporting—ensuring full compliance with city, state, and federal requirements. Cultivate and maintain strategic relationships with grant officers and government funding agencies.
  • Data Management and Reporting: Oversee the maintenance of accurate donor records and fundraising activities using donor management software. Monitor, analyze, and report on fundraising outcomes, including grant performance, donation trends, and financial impact. Ensure all fundraising and reporting activities adhere to the highest legal and ethical standards.

Why You’re Right for the Job:

  • You are a strategic thinker: You have a proven ability to analyze complex situations, set goals, solve problems, and lead with clarity through changing variables.
  • You're a strong communicator. You know how to craft clear and compelling messages and are excited to apply that skill to story-telling that advances an inclusive green economy.
  • You're collaborative and relationship-focused. You enjoy working alongside colleagues and contribute to a positive team environment.
  • You take ownership of your work. Whether managing complex projects or routine tasks, you approach your work with care and accountability. You're comfortable working independently while also knowing when to seek input or support.
  • People trust you. You are honest, trustworthy and have the ability to maintain discretion in handling sensitive information.
  • You are adaptable: You are comfortable navigating ambiguity and working in agile environments to achieve project goals.

Requirements:

Basically, we want to know you can get the job done. This means you have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Strategic, results-oriented relationship builder with a deep commitment to LACI’s mission.
  • Minimum of 10 years of nonprofit fundraising experience, with at least 5 years in a leadership role overseeing growth and development strategies at the regional and national levels.
  • Fluency in corporate, government and philanthropic fundraising, including complex giving vehicles.
  • Ability to understand how market and policy shifts affect funding, and adapt strategies.
  • Expert interpersonal and communication skills (verbal, writing, editing), with an ability to thrive in a highly collaborative, cross-functional environment.
  • Robust existing network within the philanthropic, corporate, donor-advised fund, and investor communities.
  • Strong understanding of competitive grant development and ability to guide high-quality proposals, donor materials, and investment/funder communications.
  • Proven track record developing and securing significant institutional, philanthropic, public-sector, and/or investment-oriented funding commitments.
  • Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple competing priorities.
  • Experience advancing equity & inclusion in diverse work environments.
  • Proven success managing a high-performing Development team.
  • Proficiency with donor management systems (e.g., Salesforce).
Preferred Qualifications
  • Master’s degree in a related field.
  • Experience working in the fields of climate, environment, energy, and/or cleantech startups.
  • Experience and understanding of capital formation for blended finance tools, with an understanding of the fund capitalization and investor cultivation process.

Work Requirements

  • This role is hybrid, working onsite at our downtown Los Angeles office at least 3 days per week. Additional days onsite may be required depending on work responsibilities, events, and other factors.
  • Availability to work occasional weekends and/or evening hours or events related to funder cultivation and relationship building.
  • Some travel may be required, including local and national.

Position Details:

This is a full-time position, starting immediately. LACI operates out of the La Kretz Innovation Campus, in the bustling Downtown LA Arts District. Since we are rapidly growing, you will be getting in on the ground floor at LACI, with the opportunity to evolve with us and shape your future here.

Salary Range: SVP Range $180-215k commensurate with experience, education, skills, etc and total compensation package including health benefits, 401k match, professional development, commuter benefits and more.

In addition to working on a campus with other innovators, we offer industry competitive benefits including: paid holidays, vacation/sick time, health benefits, 401(k) plan, professional development, and paid parking. We also support alternative transportation with a metro pass for every employee.

title: Graphic Design Specialist

We're looking for a Graphic Design Specialist to join the Marketing team at H-FARM College: someone curious, dynamic and hands-on, ready to take ownership of the design area and help shape the evolution of our visual identity.

There's plenty of space to bring ideas, share references and challenge what we do. We believe in discussion: we talk it through, decide on a direction together, then work together to make it real. We care about quality, and just as much about getting good work done, on time and with purpose.

YOUR PLACE IN THE TEAM

You report directly to the Marketing Director and Marketing Manager and work closely with the other specialists on the team (Social Media, Photo/Video, Content). You're the main point of reference for design, with full ownership of your area, in a collaborative structure where everyone has clear responsibilities and we support each other.

80% — Design & Creative

  • Brochures, flyers, folders and marketing materials
  • Website, digital assets, social content and creatives

title: Associate
description:

Location: New York, NY (hybrid)

_______________________________________________________________________________

Company Description
Simon Quick Advisors is an independent, employee-owned RIA that offers holistic financial planning solutions for affluent families, business owners and executives. We offer sophisticated strategies built around individual needs, preferences, risk tolerances, objectives, and tax considerations.

Our purpose is to give our clients and our team the freedom to pursue what matters. We give our clients the peace of mind in knowing that they have a trusted partner in Simon Quick. Mission of the Position
The Client Advisory Associate plays a vital role in delivering a high-touch, personalized client experience by supporting Client Advisors in the design and execution of comprehensive wealth management strategies. This includes contributions across key planning areas such as investments, tax, estate, insurance, and cash flow. The Associate ensures operational excellence, strengthens client relationships, and supports the creation of thoughtful, data-driven financial plans that align with each client’s unique goals. This role is intentionally structured as a developmental path toward becoming a lead advisor and obtaining the CFP® designation, offering exposure to all facets of holistic financial planning and client service.

Top Accountabilities

    • KPI: Proactive identification of planning opportunities and quality of recommendations across multiple planning domains (e.g., tax, estate, insurance)

  • Accountability 2: Deliver High-Quality Client Service and Daily Communication Support: Serve as a key point of contact for clients to support ongoing service needs, clarify planning strategies, and coordinate implementation across internal and external stakeholders.
    • KPI: High client satisfaction scores
    • KPI: Timely and professional response to client inquiries
  • Accountability 3: Execute and Monitor Investment and Financial Plan Implementation: Manage the operational execution of investment changes and financial planning recommendations, ensuring seamless coordination and documentation.
    • KPI: Zero data inconsistencies across internal systems
    • KPI: Timely execution and follow-through on client decisions
  • Accountability 4: Maintain and Review Client Performance and Planning Reports: Support the preparation and quality control of performance reports and planning updates, ensuring that they reflect current client objectives and financial conditions.
    • KPI: On-time and error-free delivery of client performance and planning reports
    • KPI: Accuracy in reflecting portfolio and planning changes
  • Accountability 5: Ensure Adherence to Fiduciary, Compliance, and Procedural Standards: Monitor and document client activity to ensure alignment with firm policies, fiduciary obligations, and best practices in client care.
    • KPI: 100% compliance with documentation and procedural standards
    • KPI: Timeliness of implementation and reporting

Other Duties & Responsibilities
  • Engage directly with clients to support a variety of service needs while helping to foster trusted, long-term relationships.
  • Coordinate with third-party providers, including custodians, investment managers, estate attorneys, and tax professionals, to facilitate timely and accurate execution of client strategies.
  • Interface with external investment managers to gather information, track investment activity, and support the alignment of client portfolios with overall planning goals.
  • Prepare meeting materials such as financial plans, performance reports, and investment summaries; participate in client meetings and capture next steps and follow-ups.
  • Uphold strict client confidentiality and remain vigilant in monitoring accounts for unusual or potentially fraudulent activity.
  • Collaborate with the Client Service Associate and other team members to ensure seamless execution of operational and administrative tasks.

Key Criteria/Requirements
  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 4-8 years of financial services experience
  • Experience with Fidelity and Schwab
  • Experience using DocuSign, Orion, Salesforce, and eMoney
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word)
  • Experience with tax and estate planning concepts (trust structures, estate/gift tax planning, Roth conversions, charitable giving strategies, etc.) preferred
  • While the CFP® certification is not required upon hire, candidates are expected to pursue and obtain the CFP® designation as part of their long-term professional development once approved by management.

Key Competencies

Description:

Rail Maintenance Associate
The Rail Maintenance Associate plays a key role in supporting Phillips 66's rail fleet maintenance operations, serving as the primary point of contact between rail repair shops, lessors, and internal Rail Coordinators. This position is responsible for managing the full lifecycle of rail car shop trips, including submitting shop requests, tracking repair estimates and invoices, managing diversion data, and maintaining accurate records of mandatory compliance test dates. The Rail Maintenance Associate ensures data integrity within the Rail Transportation Management System (TMS) and actively supports off-lease car management, fuel surcharge updates, and regular reporting to key stakeholders across the organization.
Responsibilities may include:
  • Serve as data steward for repair estimates, ensuring accuracy and preventing duplicate entries within the TMS
  • Manually load estimate files (.txt or .dat) into the system and verify that correct data files are loaded when estimates are absent
  • Ensure shop information is accurate and up to date to support the approval and rejection of Billing Repair Cards (BRCs)
  • Act as liaison between rail repair shops and the internal Rail Maintenance team for all communications and follow-up on Estimate approvals
  • Submit daily shop requests through applicable platforms (MyGatx, LinkNet, etc.)
  • Send inbound notifications when P66 bills cars to shop and manage Outbound (OB) disposition in system and between shops, lessors, and Rail Coordinators when cars are complete. Process shop diversions and coordinate to obtain Bills of Lading (BOLs) and diversion documentation
  • Support Annual Compliance Shop Program and update system as cars are sent to shop for cars due testing throughout the year and obtain Projected Outbound Dates (PODs) for assigned rail cars
  • Ensure mandatory test date updates received when shops request outbound (OB) disposition and input that data in the system. Activity ensures the master list of mandatory test dates are accurate in the system for tank tests, valve tests, stub sill, thickness, Rule 88.B2, service equipment, and linings.
  • Identify rail cars operating under OTMA, manage associated data within the system, and submit OTMA information to the leasing company at the time of shop request entry
  • Communicate invoices to appropriate parties and file accordingly
  • Manage trip diversion data, including origin changes, car status (cleaned), and comments authorized by the Rail Coordinator.
  • Communicate new route codes to relevant stakeholders for diversions and shop trips
  • Run daily reports to track off-lease car departures from shop; request off-lease dates from lessors upon car release and coordinate with the Rail Fleet & Maintenance Analyst to update car status; ensure trips are closed with appropriate comments
  • Balance time commitments, deliverables, and strategic versus tactical priorities across assigned rail maintenance functions

Basic/Required Qualifications:
  • Legally authorized to work in the job posting country
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; associate's degree in Supply Chain, Transportation, Business, or a related field preferred
  • 2 or more years of experience in rail logistics, fleet management, or transportation operations
  • Working knowledge of Transportation Management Systems (TMS)
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook)
  • Attention to detail and strong organizational skills
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and shift priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to interact effectively with stakeholders across multiple functional areas, including rail repair shops, lessors, and internal logistics teams
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, ensuring common understanding
  • Self-starter with the ability to identify and recommend process improvements for greater efficiency
  • Ability to adapt to varying and/or unexpected changing conditions with minimal direction
  • Demonstrate a high level of personal initiative and sense of urgency to get the job done, with the potential and desire to advance to a higher level of responsibility

Preferred Qualifications:
  • Familiarity with rail maintenance platforms such as MyGatx or LinkNet
  • Experience with Rail transportation management systems
  • Experience with SAP or other ERP systems in a logistics or supply chain environment
  • 2 or more years of direct experience in the oil and gas industry, particularly in bulk liquid transportation
  • Basic understanding of rail car equipment
  • Experience processing and managing repair estimates, Billing Repair Cards (BRCs), and OTMA compliance requirements
  • Knowledge of rail car mandatory inspection and testing requirements (tank test, valve test, stub sill, thickness, 88b2, service equipment, linings
  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Transportation, Business, or a related field preferred

title: Postdoctoral Researcher / Research Scientist - Yurkovich Lab
description:
Synthetic Biology & AI Opportunity
Remote or hybrid (if in the San Francisco Bay Area)

POSITION SUMMARY
Are you ready to architect the future of longevity by turning biological complexity into actionable AI?

Recent advancements in biomedical technologies are generating vast amounts of multimodal data, paving the way for a deeper, systems-level understanding of human health. We are seeking a highly skilled Postdoc Scholar or Research Scientist to join the Yurkovich Lab for Applied Systems BioAI. Our research harnesses artificial intelligence and systems science to drive health innovation.

We are looking for a candidate with a strong background in synthetic and computational biology who is excited to translate complex biology into actionable AI. In this role, you will be instrumental in annotating, organizing, and democratizing multimodal biological data using knowledge graphs to pioneer new technologies. This position uniquely bridges academia and industry, as your work will leverage knowledge graphs and AI technologies to support both applied research efforts and the development of new commercial initiatives.

If you are a highly motivated individual with a passion for scientific discovery, a strong computational background, and a desire to make a significant impact on human healthspan, we encourage you to apply.

Responsibilities
  • Translate synthetic biology data and complex biological mechanisms into frameworks optimized for artificial intelligence and machine learning models.
  • Design, build, and implement advanced knowledge graphs and network models to integrate and analyze complex, multimodal biological data.
  • Leverage machine learning, AI, and large language models to extract actionable insights from large-scale biomedical datasets.
  • Spearhead the technical transition of biological research into viable commercial AI products and solutions.
  • Collaborate closely with AI scientists and domain experts to translate complex biological questions into quantitative network and mathematical models.
  • Design, develop, and test software applications and data pipelines using object-oriented programming languages and software engineering best practices.
  • Stay up-to-date with the latest advancements in artificial intelligence, graph theory, computational modeling, and systems biology.
Qualifications
  • PhD in Biotechnology, Synthetic Biology, Systems Biology, Bioengineering, or a related field.
  • Strong foundation and demonstrated expertise in synthetic biology and computational biology.
  • Experience building, querying, or analyzing knowledge graphs and complex networks
  • Proficiency in machine learning and AI techniques
  • Experience in Python
  • Experience in software engineering
  • Familiarity with biological data, biomedicine, and/or longevity research is highly preferred
  • Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and critical thinking skills
  • Strong communication, writing, and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to work both independently and as a highly collaborative part of a team
Compensation & Benefits
  • $75,000 to $110,000 annual salary depending on skills and experience.
  • Generous benefits including health insurance, paid parental leave, vacation/sick leave, a 401(k) with 5% employer match, and student loan repayment.
About the Buck Institute for Research on Aging
Our success will ultimately change healthcare. The Buck Institute aims to end the threat of age-related diseases for current and future generations by bringing together highly capable and passionate scientists from a broad range of disciplines to identify and impede the mechanisms of aging.

Located in Marin County, California, the Buck is an independent nonprofit institution dedicated to increasing human healthspan—the healthy years of life. Globally recognized as a pioneer and leader in targeting aging, the number one risk factor for diseases including Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, cancer, macular degeneration, heart disease, and diabetes, the Buck seeks to help people live better, longer.

We are an equal-opportunity employer. We strive to create an atmosphere where diversity of identity, experience, and background is welcomed, valued, and supported. Candidates who contribute to this diversity are strongly encouraged to apply.

To Apply
To be considered, please apply online and submit your CV plus a PDF document that includes a summary of your research interests and the names, email, and phone numbers of 3 references.

title: Youth Job Coach – Career & Transition Services
description:
Youth Job Coach – Career & Transition Services

Organization: RISE Services
Pay: $21.00 per hour, plus mileage reimbursement
Status: Full-time, benefits eligible
Schedule: Flexible schedule with significant afternoon, evening, and weekend availability
Work Setting: Community-based with regular local travel

Help Students Prepare for Employment and Life After High School

RISE Services is hiring a Youth Job Coach to help students with disabilities explore careers, develop workplace skills, and prepare for employment and life after high school.

This is a great opportunity for someone with experience in job coaching, education, special education, behavioral support, mentoring, workforce development, human services, or working with teenagers and young adults.

You do not need previous experience with Pre-Employment Transition Services, commonly called Pre-ETS. We will provide training on the program requirements and documentation.

What You Will Do

As a Youth Job Coach, you will work individually and in small groups with students, generally ages 14–21, who have disabilities, IEPs, or Section 504 Plans.

You will help students:

  • Explore careers that match their interests and strengths.

  • Learn how to search and apply for jobs.

  • Create resumes and practice interviewing.

  • Develop communication, teamwork, punctuality, and problem-solving skills.

  • Understand workplace expectations and professional behavior.

  • Build confidence, independence, and self-advocacy skills.

  • Explore college, vocational training, and other postsecondary options.

  • Participate in workplace tours, job shadowing, informational interviews, and approved work experiences.

  • Obtain work permits and complete other employment-related steps when needed.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide engaging, individualized career-readiness and employment activities.

  • Teach practical job-readiness and independent-living skills.

  • Adapt instruction to each student’s abilities, communication style, interests, and support needs.

  • Help students identify career goals, strengths, preferences, and potential barriers.

  • Prepare students for work-based learning experiences and provide support throughout the experience.

  • Communicate professionally with students, families, schools, employers, and vocational rehabilitation counselors.

  • Coordinate activities around school schedules and student availability.

  • Complete progress notes, service documentation, timesheets, and reports accurately and on time.

  • Follow RISE Services policies, confidentiality requirements, and vocational rehabilitation program guidelines.

  • Participate in required meetings, training, supervision, and quality-assurance activities.

Schedule

Because most students attend school during the day, candidates must have meaningful availability during:

  • Afternoons

  • Evenings

  • Weekends

  • School breaks and holidays

Some daytime hours may be used for school meetings, training, documentation, employer outreach, program coordination, and other approved responsibilities.

Applicants must be able to maintain a dependable and reasonably consistent weekly schedule. The exact schedule will vary based on student availability, authorized services, work experiences, and program needs.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience working with teenagers, young adults, individuals with disabilities, or other populations requiring support.

  • Ability to engage, motivate, and build positive relationships with young people.

  • Strong communication, organization, and time-management skills.

  • Ability to work independently in schools, workplaces, and community settings.

  • Ability to complete electronic documentation accurately and on time.

  • Availability during afternoons, evenings, and weekends.

  • Valid driver’s license and reliable personal transportation.

  • Willingness to travel throughout the assigned service area.

  • Basic computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.

  • Ability to meet applicable background-check and employment requirements.

A bachelor’s degree is not required.

Preferred Experience

Experience in any of the following areas is helpful but not required:

  • Job coaching or employment services

  • Teaching, tutoring, mentoring, or youth programming

  • Special education or behavioral support

  • Career counseling or workforce development

  • Human services, social work, psychology, or rehabilitation

  • Working with students who have IEPs or Section 504 Plans

  • Coordinating workplace experiences or employer partnerships

  • Virginia DARS or Maryland DORS services

Who Will Succeed in This Position?

The ideal candidate is:

  • Patient, encouraging, creative, and dependable.

  • Comfortable working with teenagers and young adults.

  • Able to make career-development activities practical and engaging.

  • Comfortable traveling between schools, workplaces, and community locations.

  • Professional when communicating with families, schools, counselors, and employers.

  • Able to manage a flexible schedule and work independently.

  • Organized and committed to completing documentation on time.

  • Passionate about helping young people become more confident and independent.

Benefits

Eligible full-time employees may receive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off and holiday accrual

  • Short-term disability insurance

  • Life insurance

  • Long-term care option

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Employee Tenure Bonus Program

  • Mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel

  • Paid training and professional development

Eligibility requirements may apply.

About RISE Services

RISE Services helps individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain competitive employment. Our person-centered services help people build skills, increase independence, access opportunities, and achieve meaningful employment and community outcomes.

This position provides youth transition and employment-readiness services through state vocational rehabilitation programs, including the Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services and/or the Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services.

Equal Opportunity Employer

RISE Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and equal access to employment. Employment decisions are made without regard to any status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Apply Today

If you enjoy helping young people recognize their strengths, develop real-world skills, and prepare for employment, we encourage you to apply. Join RISE Services and help students take meaningful steps toward successful careers and greater independence.

title: Director of Renewals
description:
Help us build the next generation of renewals at Sembi.

Sembi is the parent company behind leading software quality and DevOps brands including TestRail, Xray, Testmo, Ranorex, PreEmptive, and Kiuwan. Our products help development, QA, and security teams build, test, secure, and ship better software with confidence.

We’re bringing these businesses together to create a stronger, more connected customer experience while preserving the unique strengths of each brand. As we continue to grow, we’re investing in the capabilities that will help us build lasting customer relationships, and renewals is at the heart of that mission.

The Role

We’re looking for a Director of Renewals to lead our global renewals organization across the Sembi portfolio.

This is an opportunity to build and lead a world-class renewals function spanning six established software brands and thousands of customers around the world. You’ll own the strategy, operating model, forecasting, performance, and team responsible for protecting Sembi’s recurring revenue and strengthening customer retention.

This isn’t a role focused simply on processing renewals. We’re looking for someone who can transform renewals into a predictable, data driven, customer centric revenue engine.

You’ll report to the VP of Customer Experience and work closely with Customer Success, Support, Sales, Finance, Operations, Product, and Marketing leaders across Sembi.

What You'll Own

  • Lead Sembi’s global renewals strategy across TestRail, Xray, Testmo, Ranorex, PreEmptive, and Kiuwan, owning retention performance, renewal bookings, churn, contraction, and overall renewal outcomes.
  • Build a predictable renewals engine with consistent methodologies, processes, playbooks, and operating rhythms across brands and customer segments.
  • Own the renewals pipeline and CRM discipline, establishing clear standards for opportunity management, renewal stages, close dates, risk identification, and data quality.
  • Drive forecasting and executive visibility, building reliable renewal forecasts, dashboards, and reporting that clearly communicate pipeline health, risks, trends, and expected outcomes.
  • Identify and mitigate renewal risk early, partnering with Customer Success and other teams to develop proactive strategies for at-risk customers and prevent avoidable churn.
  • Use data and customer insights to improve retention, analyzing churn, contraction, renewal performance, and customer trends across products, segments, and geographies to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a high performing global renewals team, establishing clear goals, accountability, performance expectations, and career development.
  • Partner across the business with Customer Success, Support, Sales, Finance, Operations, Product, and Marketing to create a connected customer lifecycle and seamless renewal experience.
  • Improve systems, automation, and operational efficiency, partnering with Operations and Finance to strengthen CRM data, system integrations, workflows, and reporting.
  • Evolve the renewals function into a strategic revenue discipline, continuously raising the bar on predictability, productivity, customer retention, and scalable growth.

What You Bring

  • Significant experience leading SaaS renewals, customer success, account management, or another recurring revenue function.
  • Proven success improving retention and reducing churn at scale.
  • Experience managing a substantial recurring revenue portfolio and renewal forecast.
  • Strong understanding of SaaS metrics including GRR, NRR, churn, contraction, ARR, and forecast accuracy.
  • Experience building or transforming renewal processes and operating models.
  • Strong analytical, strategic, and operational skills.
  • Exceptional cross functional leadership and communication abilities.
  • A track record of building and developing high performing teams.
  • Comfort working across multiple products, customer segments, and geographies.
  • A builder's mindset: you see ambiguity as an opportunity to create something better.

Why This Role?

This is a chance to have portfolio level impact.

You won’t be responsible for renewals for just one product. You’ll help define how six established Sembi brands retain and grow their customer relationships. You’ll have the visibility and influence to shape strategy, improve how we operate, develop a global team, and directly impact one of the most important drivers of our business.

If you’re an experienced renewals leader who loves building teams, creating predictability, solving complex problems, and turning customer retention into a competitive advantage, we’d love to meet you.

title: Operations Delivery Manager
description:
LOCATION: Our office is located in Minnetonka, MN. Candidates must reside in the Twin Cities area and will be required to be in-office 5 days per week.

A job at B is like no other. We are on a mission to Be Relevant - make a meaningful difference in the lives of others. This talented team lives our values every day. These values have made RAZR what it is for years, and today, they are more critical than ever. They keep us connected. They make us a team. They allow us to thrive.

The RAZR Core Values You Live

Be Intentional

  • You take action and pursue the ultimate best outcome for RAZR and our clients

  • You dig in and understand the details of how the business works

  • You run towards, and you don’t run away

  • You understand that “whatever it takes” is just that

  • You have a plan, and you execute it even when you don’t feel like it

Embrace the Attitude of How

  • You understand that problems are simply opportunities to solve them

  • You view commitments as promises to be kept...regardless

  • You can’t stand not knowing; you have an unquenchable thirst to understand why

  • You are an active participant, never a spectator
