Enjoy the Ride

  • You are grateful for both life’s challenges and opportunities

  • You passionately pursue excellence in everything you do

  • You laugh often and don’t take yourself too seriously

  • You love change, and living in the gray is energizing to you

  • You can't wait to get out of bed in the morning & get on with your day

Overview

The Operations Delivery Manager is responsible for the operational delivery, configuration, and ongoing support of client loyalty programs at RAZR.

This role translates approved client requirements and business rules into accurate platform configurations, validates that programs function as intended, and supports testing, launch readiness, and transition into ongoing operations.

The Operations Delivery Manager also serves as a key operational contact for assigned client programs, coordinating configuration changes, campaigns and promotions, issue resolution, and operational support with clients and internal teams.

The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, operationally minded, comfortable working with technology, and able to translate complex business requirements into accurate platform configurations and scalable operational processes.


Responsibilities

Program Implementation & Configuration

  • Own the operational setup and configuration of new client loyalty programs within the RAZR platform.

  • Translate approved requirements, business rules, and program designs into accurate platform configurations.

  • Develop and execute validation procedures and test scenarios to confirm configured programs and processed data produce expected results.

  • Validate member/customer records, transactions, balances, rewards, and other program outcomes during implementation.

  • Investigate configuration, data, or processing discrepancies and coordinate resolution with the appropriate internal teams.

  • Support QA, user acceptance testing, launch readiness, and go-live activities.

  • Partner with the Program Manager to ensure configuration, testing, dependencies, risks, and operational requirements are reflected in implementation plans.

  • Transition newly launched programs into ongoing operational support.

Client Operations & Service Management

  • Serve as a key operational contact for assigned client programs during implementation and ongoing operations.

  • Provide guidance on program configuration, platform functionality, campaigns, promotions, and operational processes.

  • Manage ongoing configuration changes and ensure updates are appropriately reviewed, tested, and validated.

  • Own initial triage of client-escalated operational, customer service, and technical issues.

  • Coordinate issue resolution with Support, Technology, Product, Account Management, and other teams as needed.

  • Maintain clear client communication and follow-up on outstanding issues, changes, and operational needs.

  • Support a high-quality client experience by proactively identifying and addressing operational challenges or service gaps.

Operational & Financial Coordination

  • Coordinate operational requirements related to client contracts, compliance activities, vendors, and other administrative needs.

  • Partner with Account Management and internal teams on billing, invoicing, collections, forecasting, and related client activities.

  • Track outstanding operational and administrative items through resolution.

Process Improvement & Operational Excellence

  • Develop, refine, and maintain operational processes, workflows, procedures, and documentation.

  • Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency, scalability, accuracy, and consistency of program implementation and operations.

  • Identify recurring configuration or operational issues and partner with the appropriate teams to address root causes.

  • Support automation and process improvements that reduce manual effort and improve service quality.

  • Contribute operational insights and client feedback to Product and process improvement initiatives.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with Program Management, Product, Support, Technical Services, and other internal teams.

  • Work alongside the Program Manager – Implementations to ensure operational and configuration activities are appropriately incorporated into implementation efforts.

  • Provide subject matter expertise on program configuration and operational requirements.

  • Communicate configuration decisions, requirements, risks, and issues clearly to Program Manager and internal stakeholders.

  • Escalate operational issues and blockers when additional support or decision-making is required.

  • Help ensure effective handoffs and communication between client-facing, operational, and technical teams.


Qualifications & Experience

  • 3-5 years of experience in SaaS implementation, client operations, platform operations, customer success, technical support, program operations, or related fields.

  • Experience working with SaaS platforms and configuring technology solutions based on client or business requirements.

  • Strong attention to detail and demonstrated accuracy in configuration and operational execution.

  • Strong problem-solving, troubleshooting, and issue-triage skills.

  • Ability to understand business requirements and translate them into platform configurations and operational processes.

  • Comfortable working with technology platforms, integrations, data workflows, and technical teams.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple operational priorities.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Experience with financial institutions, banking, credit unions, fintech, or financial services is preferred.

  • Experience with loyalty, rewards, promotions, CRM, or customer engagement platforms is a plus.


What Success Looks Like

  • Success in this role means client programs are configured accurately, validated thoroughly, and operationally ready for launch.

  • The Operations Delivery Manager brings together platform expertise, attention to detail, operational judgment, and client focus to ensure programs work as intended from implementation through ongoing operations. They provide the operational expertise required by the Program Manager and broader implementation team while becoming a trusted operational partner to assigned clients.


About Us

RAZR is a fast-growing marketing technology company headquartered in the Twin Cities, and we count some of the world’s most recognized brands among our clients. Working across various industries, including healthcare, medical technology, financial services, and retail, we help our clients acquire, retain, and grow consumers by leveraging our proprietary technology platform, Fibonacci™. The RAZR approach is rooted in behavioral science and combines strategy with visual design to create sustainable behavior change within consumer audiences.

With our Clients, Colleagues, and in our Communities, we live our Mission - Be Relevant – “Make a meaningful difference in the lives of others.” At the foundation of our Culture, you’ll find the Core Values of “Be Intentional”, “Embrace the Attitude of How”, and “Enjoy the Ride”, this is a mindset and a commitment to how we show up every day. The RAZR team is driven to pursue the ultimate best outcome for our key constituents. There are no jobs here, just opportunities to serve and make a material impact in the world.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, and our employees have unique strengths, experiences, and backgrounds who share a passion for improving people's lives.

title: DEXAS Licensed - Mobile Health Technician
description:
Are you tired of your DEXA certification sitting underused in a clinic shift or a sales-driven screening job? As a Licensed DEXA Technician at BodySpec, you'll put your California BDEO certification to work the way it's meant to be used — one-on-one scans that actually help people understand their bodies, with no cold-calling, no client book to build, and no quotas. You'll be at the heart of numerous health journeys, celebrating successes and offering support in a role that's as rewarding as it is dynamic.

First-year Licensed DEXA Technicians in the Los Angeles area can expect to earn up to $72,069 in total cash compensation, plus equity.

You'll Love This Job If you Have:

  • Passion for Preventive Health: You believe health is about more than treating illness — you want to help people understand their bodies and reach their goals.
  • Customer Service Instincts: You love one-on-one interaction and creating great experiences. You're warm, professional, and can make anyone feel comfortable — without the pressure of building your own book of business.
  • Startup Energy: You're energized by variety and building something new. Traditional healthcare feels slow and bureaucratic to you. You want to be part of a small, dynamic team where your work actually matters.
  • Grit and Flexibility: You don't mind early mornings or getting your hands dirty. You're resourceful — when something's broken, you fix it or propose solutions instead of waiting for someone else.
  • Ready to Work, Not Ready to Wait: You're already BDEO-certified and want to put that license into practice immediately — not spend months in a training pipeline before you start making an impact.

What Will You Do?

  • Work in our storefronts or directly in the community, driving our mobile scan vans to community centers, gyms, workplaces, health fairs, clinics, and other locations.
  • Perform DEXA scans from day one using your existing BDEO certification, backed by a hands-on BodySpec onboarding — including a team immersion week in Austin, TX — to get you fluent in our scan protocols, equipment, and customer experience standards.
  • Take ownership of your events from setup to tear down, exemplifying excellence in service delivery and customer service — all while making a genuinely positive impact on dozens of people each day.
  • Handle general administrative and maintenance-related duties related to our storefront, machines, vans, and equipment.
  • Assist with other duties as assigned by the Leadership Team.

Requirements

  • Must currently hold an active California BDEO (Bone Densitometry Equipment Operator) certification issued by the California Department of Public Health, Radiologic Health Branch.
  • This is a standing role with rolling start dates — no fixed cohort or class to wait for.
  • This role requires regular weekend work (both Saturday and Sunday). Available to work one of the following consistent schedules: Wednesday–Sunday (Monday & Tuesday off) or Sunday–Thursday (Friday & Saturday off). Event times typically run 7am–8pm depending on location; earlier start times may be required to accommodate drive time so you're on-site and ready for clients at 7am.
  • Able to live in, and travel to, the Santa Monica, Hollywood, Culver City, Pasadena, Glendale, and Burbank areas.
  • If you've taken standardized tests such as the SAT, ACT, ASVAB, or others, we ask you to share your scores. This isn't required and won't be a sole factor in hiring, but it helps us learn more about candidates since we don't run pre-employment testing.
  • Valid driver's license and a driving record in good standing.
  • Able to lift/carry up to 50 lbs.
  • Ability to thrive with direct, unfiltered feedback — we'll tell you exactly what you need to improve.

Compensation

  • Base Salary: $30.69/hour ($63,835 annualized at 40 hrs/week)
  • Performance Bonus: Up to 7% of base annually ($4,468) — half paid in cash ($2,234), half in stock options
  • Team Revenue Bonus: $500/month when we hit monthly goals ($6,000 annually — we hit our goals 9 out of 12 months in 2025)
  • Total Cash Compensation: Up to $72,069
  • Equity: Stock options through performance bonus and additional grants based on performance

All team members regardless of position are eligible for additional stock option grants and profit sharing based on performance. We expect both cash and equity compensation to grow as the company scales.

Benefits

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k)
  • Paid time off
  • Sick leave
  • $75/month commute reimbursement
  • $10/shift meal stipend
  • Company-wide peer bonus program for recognizing excellent teamwork
  • Employee assistance program
  • Regular team events (both virtual and in-person)

BodySpec is transforming how people understand and improve their health through accessible DEXA scanning. As a Licensed DEXA Technician, you'll bring that insight directly into the communities we serve, from day one. If you're ready to put your certification to work immediately, deliver an exceptional scan experience every time, and join a team that moves fast, we want to hear from you.

title: License Owner / Operator, Northern Virginia
description:
Build the Future of Football in Northern Virginia

What if your passion for football could become something you lead, grow, and make your own?

Stranger Soccer is expanding into new cities around the world and is looking for a License Owner / Operator to bring the Stranger Soccer experience to Northern Virginia.

This isn't a traditional management position. It's an opportunity to build, own, and grow a local football operation while becoming part of an established international brand. We're looking for entrepreneurial individuals who are passionate about football and driven to create a meaningful impact in their local community.

Imagine Being the Person Who...

  • Brings football players together through a seamless mobile platform
  • Builds a vibrant football community in Northern Virginia
  • Creates memorable playing experiences week after week
  • Leads a growing local operation backed by proven technology and global expertise

What You'll Do

As the License Owner / Operator, you'll oversee every aspect of Stranger Soccer, including:

  • Growing the local player community
  • Securing football venues and partnerships
  • Recruiting and managing Official Hosts
  • Leading marketing and community-building initiatives
  • Delivering consistently outstanding game experiences

You'll have the independence to grow your local operation while receiving ongoing support, technology, and operational guidance from our Singapore headquarters.

Why Stranger Soccer?

Stranger Soccer makes playing football as simple as booking a gym session. Through our mobile app, players can discover games, reserve a spot, and simply turn up to play.

Founded in Singapore, Stranger Soccer now operates in 10+ cities worldwide and has delivered more than 100,000 games. Our proven model is built for growth—and we're ready to bring it to Northern Virginia.

Who We're Looking For

  • A football enthusiast with strong local insight
  • An entrepreneurial self-starter who enjoys taking ownership
  • A leader who can build relationships and grow a local community
  • Someone looking for more than a job—someone who wants to create lasting impact

Ready to Take the Lead?

Visit and explore "Bring Stranger Soccer to Your City" to learn more and express your interest.

Help shape the future of football in Northern Virginia—and build something you'll be proud of.

title: Executive III
description:
Office of the Illinois Secretary of State
Alexi Giannoulias

Job Title: Executive III
Division: Property Management
Union: N/A

Salary: Range $5,909 to $11,209 monthly – commensurate with experience

Overview:

Directs and supervises Property Managers; plans, assigns, and monitors workflow, evaluating employee performance and reporting problems to upper management; directs management research studies relative to the Property Management (Leases); drafts contract language for each lease with language required by Illinois Comptroller’s Office and state statute; take daily phone calls from facility managers on any issues at the facilities and work with the landlords or janitorial staff to resolve any issues; prepares complex administrative reports on division activities.

Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Directs and supervises property managers including training employees; plans, assigns, and monitors workflow, evaluating employee performance, providing positive feedback, and reporting problems with recommendations of discipline to upper management when necessary; ensures adherence to program policies and procedures; determines established and implements operational procedures and workflow; recommends actions affecting subordinate staff; approves work standards and authorizes time off; supports the organizing and coordinating of office procedures to ensure organizational effectiveness and productivity; prepares holdover letters; manages vendor and contractor relationships and reviews service contracts to ensure facility management needs are being met; prioritizes and manages multiple projects simultaneously and follows through on issues in a timely manner; assist in the resolution of any administrative problems that may arise in the day-to-day operations.
  • Directs management research studies relative to the Property Management (Leases); drafts contract language for each lease with language required by Illinois Comptroller’s Office (IOC) and state statue, including financial disclosures; processes any change of ownership documentation to be filed with IOC; manages all leases to track lease expirations, holdovers, and other time sensitive tasks; submit Contract Obligation Document (COD) with each lease; required when filing lease with the IOC compiles and submits compiled administrative reports for such to the Chief of Staff for review and approval; directs the effectuation of new/revised/current program policies and practices; assists the Chief of Staff in policy development and needed program changes.
  • Negotiates with landlords to determine what expenses can and cannot be reimbursed, i.e., plumbing repairs, matters caused by the SOS employees or customers; take daily phone calls from facility managers on any issues at the facilities and work with the landlords or janitorial to resolve any issues; take regular phone calls from utility companies i.e., whether excessive usage is the fault of SOS or if there is a plumbing or electrical issue to be resolved by the landlord; serves as liaison to outside brokerage firm on administrative and operational task.
  • Prepares complex administrative reports on division activities for submittal to the Chief of Staff; processes any end of year reconciliations that come in from the landlords on property taxes and utilities; processes all vouchers for monthly lease payments, monthly janitorial costs and utilities where necessary.
  • Performs other related duties as required or assigned.

Education and Experience:

Requires knowledge, skill and mental development equivalent to completion of four years college, preferably with courses in business or public administration and three years of managerial experience in a public or business organization.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
  • Requires thorough knowledge of the principles and practices of public and business administration.
  • Requires extensive knowledge of functions and organization of State Government
  • Requires working knowledge of the principles of business accounting, program budgeting, personnel management and statistics.
  • Requires elementary knowledge of data processing business applications.
  • Requires ability to develop and manage a statewide program.
  • Requires ability to analyze administrative problems and adopt an effective course of action.
  • Requires ability to develop, install and evaluate new and revised methods, procedures and performance standards.
  • Requires ability to exercise judgment and discretion in implementing and interpreting departmental policies and procedures.
  • Requires ability to estimate and budget for future needs and cost for personnel, space, equipment, supplies and services.
  • Requires ability to develop and maintain cooperative managerial working relationships.
  • Requires willingness to travel and possession of a valid Illinois driver’s license as required by individual positions within the class.
Application Process:
  • Please visit to apply by completing the online application; you may also upload a resume or other attachments as needed.
  • Preference will be given to Illinois residents in the hiring and selection process, in accordance with the Illinois Secretary of State Merit Employment Code.
  • Questions regarding this posting or Illinois Secretary of State employment practices may be directed to Job Counselors at our Personnel offices in Chicago (312-793-5515) or Springfield (217-782-4783).
Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Applicants must be lawfully authorized to work in the United States.
Applicants are considered for all positions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital or veteran status, or the presence of a non-job-related medical condition or disability.

title: Inventory Associate
description:

Location: Lumberton, NC

title: DevOps Developer
description:
Job Summary
Join OVHcloud and be part of creating the cloud of tomorrow. We empower people who want to grow, make their work stand out, and take ownership of dynamic, meaningful projects. You’ll enjoy autonomy in your work, strong support from management, and the freedom to explore new challenges—helping you make a tangible impact and shape the future of our cloud infrastructure alongside passionate, collaborative peers.

The Automation and Tooling Developer is responsible for the design, development, and maintenance of cutting-edge automation solutions that enhance business efficiency. This position collaborates with key stakeholders to understand business needs and create innovative tools and automation scripts to streamline operations. This role is instrumental in advancing OVHcloud DevOps practices, fostering technical excellence, and ensuring robust documentation across all automation processes.

Base pay range: $120,000 - $145,000 (based on relevant experience).

Essential Duties & Responsibilities
  • Design, develop, test, and maintain robust automation tools and scripts using programming languages such as Python, Go, PowerShell, or similar.
  • Work closely with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver tailored automation solutions aligned with business goals.
  • Integrate automation tools with existing systems, including APIs, databases, and enterprise software, ensuring seamless interoperability.
  • Ensure the accuracy, performance, and reliability of automation tools through rigorous testing and debugging processes.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive documentation for tools, scripts, workflows, and processes, ensuring clarity, usability, and accessibility for all stakeholders.
  • Diagnose and resolve issues with automation systems promptly and efficiently.
  • Stay abreast of industry trends and emerging technologies to incorporate best practices and innovative solutions into the automation strategy.
  • Advance the adoption of DevOps principles by implementing CI/CD pipelines and automating infrastructure provisioning using tools like Jenkins, Ansible, or Terraform.
  • Provide technical guidance and professional development opportunities to cross-functional teams, fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement.
  • Apply AI-assisted tooling to daily work and help the team define where it helps and where it doesn't.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field; equivalent experience considered in lieu of degree.
  • 5+ years in software development and automation.
  • Strong knowledge of programming languages, such as Python, Go, PowerShell, or Perl.
  • Proven experience with automation frameworks, such as Ansible, Puppet, or Terraform.
  • Working knowledge of current AI/LLM capabilities and limitations, gained through hands-on use (not just headlines), or curiosity about AI and a track record of getting up to speed on new tooling quickly.
  • Expertise in cloud-native programming languages such as Go, Python, Ruby on Rails, or Java.
  • Strong understanding of DevOps tools and practices, including CI/CD pipelines (e.g., Jenkins, Git).
  • Full stack development experience (front and back end).
  • Experience with container orchestration systems like Kubernetes and containerization tools like Docker.
  • Solid knowledge of REST APIs, HTTP, and JSON integration.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages (i.e., Bash).
  • Familiarity with data integration and processing via APIs, databases, and data warehousing.
  • Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality documentation that supports development, operations, and stakeholder communication.
  • Exceptional analytical and debugging skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex ideas clearly and effectively.
  • Experience managing tasks, projects, and teams in a dynamic environment.

Our Culture

title: Sustainable Operations Program Manager
description:
The NBCUniversal Team is looking for a Sustainable Operations Program Manager to join our Sustainability team.

In this role, you will champion the execution of NBCU’s ambitious carbon reduction plan. You will work with a wide range of internal, corporate, and external stakeholders to define our approach to decarbonization and foster programs and pilots to implement initiatives across the global enterprise. You will report progress on our environmental goals to senior leadership, working groups, and the Sustainability Council.

You will report to the Director of Sustainability Strategy, to coordinate NBCU’s efforts and ensure alignment with broader enterprise goals. You will partner with the NBCU Sustainability Data Solutions Team as they provide real-time data that accurately measures NBCU’s carbon emissions and progress against its reduction targets. Finally, you will own and manage the Sustainability Project Tracker and emissions Long Range Plan as a key component of our sustainability strategy approach.

What You’ll Do

  • Manage our Sustainable Operations strategy, including end-to-end management of programs focused on: renewable energy, green building, fleet electrification, and facility decarbonization (boiler electrification & energy efficiency projects).
  • Research emerging sustainability trends, net-zero targets and methodology updates, low carbon technologies, market landscape, rebate/incentive programs, and big ideas
  • Pilot new programs and clean technologies that improve sustainability performance and reduce carbon emissions
  • Manage NBCU’s Sustainability Long Range Plan and emissions forecasts including:
    • Maintain a robust project tracker that includes financial, carbon and energy data on an ongoing basis
    • Support development of dashboards and reporting to track progress towards our goals for both the enterprise and individual business units
    • Sustainability capital planning: tied to the Sustainability Long Range Plan, annual sustainability budgeting, and initiative-specific funding requests.
    • Roll up and prioritize these initiatives to maximize reduction and minimize cost and business disruption impact
  • Support the Sustainability team, including cross-disciplinary projects and tracking applicable and forthcoming environmental laws and regulations.

Let’s Talk About You…

  • Results-oriented and Organized Project Manager – You are experienced with balancing a diverse set of projects and a broad cross-section of internal and external stakeholders
  • Passionate About Our Mission – You are purpose-driven to embed sustainability in a large enterprise
  • Detail-oriented and Spreadsheet Pro – You are experienced at presenting analytics and auditing data (with expertise in leveraging advanced functions within MS Excel)
  • Growth Leader and Innovative – You are a proven leader known to challenge the status quo, introduce new and better ways of delivering results, and make difficult decisions and lead through change

What You Have…

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field such as: Environmental Sciences/Studies, Sustainability, Engineering, or equivalent professional experience
  • 4+ years of sustainability-related work experience
  • Proven expertise in environmental sustainability and relevant technical skills, such as: greenhouse gas accounting, emission reduction target setting, renewable energy tracking, carbon accounting, and data collection
  • Experience participating in sustainability program roll outs from end-to-end
  • A documented track-record of delivering sustainability pilots and projects, across geographies and balancing priorities and stakeholders
  • 1+ year(s) of proficiently delivering in financial analysis, carbon reduction project vetting, emission forecasting, and building dynamic program trackers

What Would Make You a Stand-out:

  • Master’s Degree in Sustainability, Management, Energy, or any relevant program
  • Familiarity with film/TV, theme parks, broadcast, data centers, or studio business segments
  • Experience supporting large, multi-site portfolios that rely heavily on external providers to deliver high-quality and timely work product
  • Experience working in Finance, Accounting, Sourcing, or similar departments

Additional Requirements:

This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website.

title: Job Coach
description:
Job Coach / Employment Specialist – Part-Time

Location: Winchester, Virginia
Service Area: Winchester and surrounding Frederick County communities
Pay: $21.00–$22.00 per hour, based on experience
Hours: Up to 29 hours per week, with the potential to transition to full-time
Schedule: Predominantly daytime hours, Monday through Friday
Work Setting: Community-based with regular local travel
Mileage: Reimbursement for approved work-related travel

Help People Build Careers and Greater Independence

RISE Services is hiring a compassionate, dependable, and resourceful Job Coach / Employment Specialist to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain meaningful employment.

In this community-based role, you will meet participants at employer worksites and other locations throughout Winchester and surrounding Frederick County communities. You will help participants explore career interests, search and apply for jobs, prepare for interviews, learn workplace responsibilities, communicate with employers, and develop the skills needed for long-term employment success.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. We welcome applicants with relevant experience in disability services, human services, education, behavioral health, workforce development, direct support, career coaching, case management, retail supervision, customer service, or other positions involving teaching, mentoring, or helping others succeed.

Training is provided.

Schedule and Hours

This position offers up to 29 hours per week. Most services in the Winchester area are provided during daytime hours, Monday through Friday.

Weekend work is occasionally needed to provide coverage when another employee is unavailable, but this is not a regularly scheduled weekend position.

Weekly schedules may include:

  • On-site job coaching

  • Job searching and completing applications

  • Resume and interview preparation

  • Employer outreach

  • Employment-readiness activities

  • Community-based participant meetings

  • Progress notes and required documentation

When a participant is not working their full number of authorized service hours, the Job Coach may provide other approved employment services, including job searching, completing applications, developing resumes, preparing for interviews, contacting employers, and teaching workplace-readiness skills.

Employees who want additional hours may have the opportunity to transition to full-time as caseloads and service needs grow. Full-time hours are not guaranteed and depend on participant referrals, scheduling needs, employee availability, and satisfactory job performance.

What You’ll Do

Job Coaching and Workplace Support

  • Provide individualized coaching at employer worksites and in community settings.

  • Help participants learn job duties, workplace routines, safety procedures, and employer expectations.

  • Teach workplace communication, professional behavior, time management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Help participants communicate effectively with supervisors and coworkers.

  • Develop natural workplace supports that promote greater independence.

  • Monitor participant progress and adjust coaching strategies as participants develop new skills.

  • Provide ongoing support to promote successful employment retention.

Job Search and Career Preparation

  • Help participants identify their strengths, interests, abilities, support needs, and employment goals.

  • Assist participants with resumes, applications, job searches, and interview preparation.

  • Conduct mock interviews and employment-readiness activities.

  • Identify opportunities that match each participant’s interests, abilities, experience, and goals.

  • Coordinate interviews, hiring activities, and onboarding support.

  • Help participants understand workplace expectations and identify reasonable accommodations when appropriate.

Employer and Community Engagement

  • Build professional relationships with employers throughout Winchester and Frederick County.

  • Contact businesses to identify potential employment opportunities.

  • Educate employers about inclusive hiring and available workplace supports.

  • Communicate with participants, families, employers, vocational rehabilitation counselors, support coordinators, schools, and community partners.

  • Attend hiring events, team meetings, training, and other scheduled activities.

Documentation and Service Coordination

  • Complete accurate progress notes and service documentation within required deadlines.

  • Maintain participant records according to funding-source and organizational requirements.

  • Track job searches, applications, interviews, placements, wages, scheduled hours, and employment retention.

  • Communicate participant progress, concerns, scheduling changes, and service needs to the appropriate supervisor.

  • Participate in service-planning and team-coordination activities.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree is not required.

  • Relevant experience supporting individuals with disabilities or others who experience barriers to employment is preferred.

  • Experience in teaching, coaching, mentoring, customer service, supervision, human services, behavioral health, workforce development, or a related field may also be considered.

  • Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

  • Ability to work independently and make responsible decisions in community settings.

  • Ability to maintain a consistent schedule and complete documentation on time.

  • Basic computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.

  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

  • Ability and willingness to travel locally and transport participants when required.

  • Ability to satisfy applicable background-screening and employment requirements.

Preferred but Not Required

  • Supported Employment, Individual Supported Employment, job-coaching, or job-development experience.

  • Experience supporting individuals with intellectual, developmental, behavioral, or other disabilities.

  • Knowledge of Medicaid Waiver, vocational rehabilitation, or disability-employment services.

  • Understanding of the Americans with Disabilities Act and reasonable workplace accommodations.

  • Experience working with employers, schools, support coordinators, vocational rehabilitation agencies, or community organizations.

  • CESP, ACRE, DSP, or another employment-support credential.

Who Will Succeed in This Position?

You may be a strong fit if you are:

  • Compassionate, patient, dependable, and encouraging.

  • Comfortable working at employer locations and throughout the community.

  • Able to teach and motivate participants while promoting independence.

  • Professional and confident when communicating with employers and community partners.

  • Resourceful and willing to find solutions when challenges arise.

  • Organized and able to manage appointments, follow-ups, and documentation.

  • Flexible when participant or employer schedules change.

  • Comfortable working independently without constant direct supervision.

Why Join RISE Services?

  • Make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals with disabilities.

  • Help people build careers, confidence, and greater independence.

  • Work predominantly during weekday daytime hours.

  • Receive mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel.

  • Participate in paid training and professional development.

  • Build experience in human services, disability services, workforce development, and career coaching.

  • Access potential opportunities for additional hours and advancement.

  • Join a collaborative, growing, and mission-driven organization.

Benefits

Part-time employees may be eligible for:

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Employee Tenure Bonus Program

  • Mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel

  • Paid training and professional development

Employees who transition to an eligible full-time position may also receive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays

  • Short-term disability insurance

  • Life insurance

  • Long-term care option

Benefit eligibility requirements apply.

Important Work-Setting Information

This is a community-based position, not a remote or traditional office-based role. Services are provided at employer worksites and other community locations throughout Winchester and surrounding Frederick County communities.

Applicants must have reliable transportation and be comfortable driving between community locations. Transporting participants may be required as part of the position.

Equal Opportunity Employer

RISE Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We recruit, hire, train, compensate, and promote employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Apply Today

If you enjoy teaching, encouraging others, solving problems, and helping people accomplish meaningful goals, apply for the Part-Time Job Coach / Employment Specialist position with RISE Services.

A bachelor’s degree and previous job-coaching experience are not required. Relevant experience, dependability, professionalism, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to helping others succeed are strongly valued.

title: Fiber Network Locator
description:
IQ Fiber was built to do internet differently. We're a 100% fiber-optic internet provider with a simple mission: To engineer a smarter internet experience. That means internet that's fast, reliable, and simply priced, backed by real humans who answer when you call and solve problems before you know they exist.

We bring that same thinking to how we build our company. Our teammates are a big part of what makes IQ Fiber different, and we believe how we work matters just as much as what we deliver. We're looking for good humans who bring great ideas, raise the bar with every task, and want to be part of a bigger story. Your work matters here.


Position Summary

The Fiber Network Locator performs skilled, technical field work requiring the accurate and efficient locating of existing underground fiber optic cables. Locating facilities may require the use of shovels and post-hole diggers to dig and expose the facilities. May be called upon to assist Construction Technicians in cabinet certifications, and other related duties.

Key Responsibilities

  • Utilizes various electronic equipment to find and mark the location of underground fiber.
  • Utilizes probe rods, shovel, posthole diggers, and other excavation equipment as necessary to locate and/or verify location of underground utilities.
  • Communicates directly with customers, other departments, employees, regulatory agencies, governmental agencies, and the general public verbally or in writing, as needed.
  • Provides accurate locations of underground utilities, in a safe and efficient manner.
  • Operates with a high degree of efficiency various job-related equipment to provide accurate and efficient locates as requested.
  • Works closely with the design team to review and update "as-built" records.
  • Prepares accurate time and material records and "as-built" reports and diagrams to provide accurate updates to key maps.
  • Participates in announced or unannounced overtime work and responds to callouts during non-working hours or emergencies, as required.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.
  • All other duties as assigned.


Job Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent and two (2) years of experience in the operation of utility locating equipment, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Possession of a valid Delaware Driver’s License.
  • Knowledge of underground utility systems.
  • Knowledge of the Delaware Department of Transportation’s (DelDOT’s) Maintenance of Traffic (MOT).
  • Knowledge of the occupational hazards and the proper safety precautions of working in the electric utility field, primarily working near energized electrical equipment, as well as the water and sewer.
  • Knowledge of overhead and underground utilities.
  • Ability to use considerable judgment.
  • Ability to accurately read and interpret as-builts, blueprints, diagrams, sketches, construction plans, and key maps of underground utilities systems.
  • Ability to understand and follow quickly and accurately brief oral and written instructions on moderately complex matters.
  • Ability to efficiently handle emergencies and multiple tasks simultaneously.
  • Ability to operate personal computer and laptop.
  • Ability to accurately prepare reports and keep records.
  • Ability to understand the operation and functions of various electronic locating equipment.
  • Ability to learn and apply policies and procedures, including safety rules and regulations.
  • Ability to drive a company vehicle.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, orally and in writing.
  • Ability to compose written correspondence.
  • Ability to follow written and oral instructions.
  • Ability to establish effective working relationships with employees, officials, and the general public.
  • Ability to pass a driving record and background check screening. Must have clear driving records for the past two years.

Physical Requirements
  • Ability to exert up to 50 pounds of force occasionally while using probe rods, shovels, and posthole diggers to locate and expose underground infrastructure.
  • Ability to balance, crouch, and stoop repeatedly while locating and marking underground utilities in the field.
  • Ability to walk and stand for extended periods while conducting locates across active job sites.
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions with exposure to dirt, noise, and odors.
  • Ability to push and pull excavation tools to expose and verify underground fiber infrastructure.

Work Environment & Schedule Requirements

Work is performed outside in varying weather conditions, with exposure to dirt, noise, odors, and fumes, at ground level. This is a safety sensitive role.

Benefits Available:

  • Fun environment.
  • Fast-growing company.

  • Voluntary Benefits: Medical (HSA & FSA options), Dental, Vision, Voluntary Life, Hospital Indemnity Insurance, Accident Insurance, Critical Illness.

Wilder Systems builds robots that do precision work across aerospace manufacturing and MRO — drilling, fastening, sanding, and inspection — on systems deployed to factory floors and flight lines worldwide. As a Senior Test Engineer, you own the test strategy for a system: how we prove it works before it ships and keep it working in the field. You define test requirements across components, design the fixtures and instrumentation that expose failures, drive mechanical and electromechanical issues to root cause, and mentor the test engineers around you — working across the robotics mechanical, electrical, and hardware teams on real hardware.

What You'll Do

  • Test strategy & requirements — own the test strategy and requirements for a system, across its mechanical and electromechanical components.

  • A track record owning test strategy for a mechanical or electromechanical system or product end-to-end.

  • Deep experience with functional, structural/fatigue, tolerance, and environmental testing of complex hardware.
  • Hands-on debugging of mechanical and electromechanical integration issues on real hardware.
  • Solid fundamentals in measurement and data acquisition: instrumentation, sensors, calibration, and interpreting test data.

Preferred Experience

The Neck Sander completes all stages of the Neck Manufacturing process, ensuring each guitar neck is ready to proceed to the next step of the manufacturing process.   • Sand the perimeter of the neck, removing tear out and machining marks.
  • Drill out truss rod holes on the top and bottom of the neck and install truss rods into the neck back.
  • Identify the fingerboard type and size and pair it with a neck shaft.
  • Glue fingerboards to the front of the neck.

title: Program Counsel
description:
This position will be based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, or Washington, D.C. FIRE operates on a hybrid work schedule that allows for a mix of in-the-office and remote work days for eligible employees. Fully remote work will not be considered for this position.

About FIRE

The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression’s mission is to defend and sustain the individual rights of all Americans to free speech and free thought — the most essential qualities of liberty. FIRE educates Americans about the importance of these inalienable rights, promotes a culture of respect for these rights, and provides the means to preserve them.

Position Description

This position is open for an attorney (Program Counsel) or non-attorney advocate (Program Officer) who will assist with the day-to-day operations of FIRE’s Campus Rights Advocacy (CRA) team and work closely with the department’s Director, Senior Program Counsel, and staff. The duties for this position include but are not limited to:

  • Reviewing, responding to, and managing individual case submissions from students, student organizations, and faculty members and providing input on future action/referral.
  • Collecting and reviewing relevant documentation, including university materials and policies, to construct narratives of incidents of First Amendment, due process, or other rights being violated.
  • Determining an advocacy plan for designated cases, including devising creative advocacy options and collaborating among internal departments on execution.
  • Authoring and reviewing letters to universities and accrediting agencies on behalf of students, student organizations, and faculty.
  • Authoring and reviewing other types of public advocacy for designated cases, including (but not limited to) blogs, social media posts, and statements to reporters.
  • Serving as primary press contact on designated cases, including conducting interviews for television, radio, and print media as needed or assigned.
  • Authoring, filing, and tracking Freedom of Information Act requests as necessary for evaluating cases.
  • Identifying candidates for litigation in coordination with FIRE’s CRA and litigation departments.

The Program Counsel or Officer may also contribute articles and columns to outside publications, contribute features to FIRE Newsdesk, and attend conferences on behalf of the organization.

This position involves a moderate amount of travel. Occasional work on weekends and evenings should be expected.

The expected start date for this position is as soon as possible.

Qualifications

A successful candidate must demonstrate knowledge of and passion for FIRE’s mission and an ability to articulate that passion in a way that will make others enthusiastic about our cause. A candidate must also be able to demonstrate:

  • Proficiency in general First Amendment law and familiarity with its underlying principles. Knowledge of campus speech law is highly desired.
  • Familiarity with general principles of due process.
  • Familiarity with either FOIA/state public records laws or with principles of written discovery, privileges, and document review preferred.
  • Familiarity with general principles underlying university conduct codes and the administrative structure of universities.
  • Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment.
  • Excellent legal research, writing, and public speaking skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Exceptional conscientiousness.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills.

Grit, charisma, and a sense of humor are a plus.

Candidates for Program Counsel must have a J.D. from an ABA-accredited law school. Candidates who possess a J.D. and are not already a member of the Pennsylvania or D.C. bar must be willing to obtain licensure in Pennsylvania or D.C. Candidates for Program Officer must have a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and excellent legal research skills. Paralegal or legal assistant experience preferred.

Salary and Compensation

For candidates with a J.D., the projected salary range for this position is $65,000-$75,000. For candidates with a Bachelor’s degree, the projected salary range for this position is $57,000-$65,000. FIRE conducts periodic evaluations where employees may receive raises or bonuses for outstanding and excellent work. FIRE also offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes employer-paid comprehensive health, dental, and life insurance for employees; a Section 125 Flexible Spending Account option; matching retirement contributions; and a generous paid time-off plan.

Applications

Applicants should provide a resume, cover letter, writing sample or other demonstration of work (portfolio, for example), salary requirements, and contact information for at least two professional references. All applications are confidential. Please address applications to Cait Scanlan, Chief People Officer.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States.

FIRE is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

As part of FIRE's hiring process, all candidates receiving a conditional offer of employment will be required to undergo a background check as permitted by and in compliance with federal, state, and local law.

title: Fence Crew Foreman
description:
Centralia / Tumwater, WA
Full Time | $30–$60+ Per Hour, Depending on Ability

Lead Great Projects. Build a Career You’re Proud Of.

Cascade Fence & Deck is looking for an experienced builder who is ready to lead a fence crew and take ownership of their projects.

We’ve been building high-quality outdoor projects since 1997, and our Tumwater location is entering its next stage of growth. We need ambitious, capable people who want to help us build something great—not just show up, put in their hours, and go home.

You don’t need to know every detail of our system on day one. You do need construction experience, strong leadership instincts, pride in your work, and the ability to keep a crew moving.

Our mission is to create a company we all like to work for, and every employee plays a role in making that happen. We work hard, hold each other accountable, and still make room for family, hunting, fishing, sports, and life outside of work.

The Role

As a Fence Crew Foreman, you will lead a two- to three-person crew building high-quality residential fence projects throughout the Olympia, and surrounding areas.

You will be responsible for:

  • Leading and developing your crew
  • Reviewing project plans and preparing for each job
  • Communicating with the project manager and homeowner
  • Keeping projects productive, organized, and on schedule
  • Solving jobsite challenges without needing constant direction
  • Making sure the customer is happy with the finished product

We provide the trucks, trailers, tools, equipment, and support you need to succeed.

What We’re Looking For

The right person will:

  • Have solid construction OR fence-building experience
  • Know how to lead people and set the pace on a jobsite
  • Take pride in quality, efficiency, and clean jobsites
  • Communicate professionally with customers and coworkers
  • Be dependable and accountable
  • Be comfortable working outdoors year-round
  • Have a valid driver’s license and a good driving record (needs to be insurable)
  • Want to continue learning and increasing their value

Specific fence experience is preferred, but we’re open to strong construction leaders from related trades who are willing to learn our systems.

This Role Might Not Be for You If:

  • You need someone constantly telling you what to do next
  • You blame the plans, customer, crew, or weather when something goes wrong
  • You sacrifice quality to finish faster—or productivity in the name of perfection
  • You don’t enjoy leading and developing other people
  • You aren’t comfortable communicating with homeowners
  • You’re looking for an easy, low-accountability construction job

The work is physical and fast-paced. You’ll lift heavy materials, dig holes, solve problems, and work outside in Washington weather. We work hard, but we also make sure good performance is recognized and rewarded.

Compensation and Benefits

  • $30–$60+ per hour, depending on demonstrated ability and value
  • Clear opportunities to increase your pay as your skills and responsibilities grow
  • Approximately 45–50 hours per week
  • Overtime pay for all hours over 40
  • Optional Saturday work when available—never mandatory
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance fully paid for you and your family
  • Two to three weeks of paid time off per year, earned on an accrual basis
  • Company-paid phone plan for qualifying positions
  • Company trucks, tools, and equipment provided
  • Home every night
  • Opportunities to advance into project management, training, operations, or other leadership roles

Why Cascade Fence & Deck?

We’ve been in business since 1997, and we’re still growing. We offer the stability of an established company with the opportunity to make a meaningful impact at a growing location.

If you’re a capable builder who feels underpaid, underappreciated, or limited in your current position, we’d like to talk with you.

We review every application we receive.

Want to learn more about our company, culture, and hiring process? Visit our careers page:

Work Doesn’t Have to Suck

title: Counselor OTP
description:
Cornerstone Family Healthcare is actively recruiting for an OTP Counselor to join our growing team in Newburgh, NY.

RATE OF PAY/SALARY: $30.00-$34.06

WORK LOCATION(S): Newburgh, NY

STATUS: Full-time


CORNERSTONE’S MISSION:

Cornerstone Family Healthcare is a non-profit Federally Qualified Health Center with a mission to provide high quality, comprehensive, primary and preventative health care services in an environment of caring, dignity and respect to all people regardless of their ability to pay. For more than fifty years, Cornerstone has been responsive to meeting the needs of the communities in which we serve with a continued emphasis on the underserved and those without access to health care regardless of race, economic status, age, sex, sexual orientation or disability.


CORNERSTONE BENEFITS:

Competitive salaries I Health Benefits I Retirement plan I Paid Time Off I Sick Time I Flexible Spending I Dependent Care I Paid Holidays


General Purpose:

The purpose of the counselor is to provide case management, substance use counseling, and advocacy services to an assigned caseload. This counselor will participate as a member of an interdisciplinary treatment team to facilitate the client recovery and rehabilitation processes. These goals are accomplished by providing individual and group counseling, developing interventions as needed and contributing to the healthy integrity of the program’s therapeutic environment.


Description of Duties:

  • Provide case management and advocacy services to an assigned caseload.
  • Participate in monitoring the therapeutic environment to ensure that the behavioral guidelines are followed, a therapeutic milieu is maintained and professional relationships remain positive.
  • Provides psycho-education and counseling relevant to chemical dependency and relapse prevention.
  • Participate in assessment screenings to determine client needs/preferences; formulates and implements treatment, transition and discharge /continuing care planning collaboratively with individual clients.
  • Facilitates the re-socialization process of clients by serving as a role model.
  • Conducts facility safety checks as assigned to visually assess clients for the use of alcohol/drugs or the environment of care for unsafe conditions.
  • Ensures the maintenance of accurate, complete, timely and high-quality client records that comply with external regulatory standards and agency policy and procedure.
  • Complies with 42 CFR confidentiality and HIPPAA privacy and security regulations.
  • Works cooperatively with other staff as a member of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Functions as a liaison/advocate to client’s families and other agencies as needed.
  • Provides outreach, education and prevention services to the local community, schools, groups and agencies as necessary and as provided by management staff.
  • Provides crisis intervention and management, generating referrals to agency or external mental health providers or other service providers, as indicated.
  • Attend and participate in monthly department, All Staff and other required meetings.
  • Be familiar with and adhere to all clinical, administrative, and general policies and procedures as outlined in the Cornerstone Policy and Procedure Manual and Employee Handbook.
  • Maintain confidentiality of all aspects of Cornerstone including, but not limited to, patient confidentiality, financials, and employee relations.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

title: Physical Therapist (PT) – Mobile/Home-Based Care
description:
Overview

We are seeking a skilled, compassionate, and dependable Physical Therapist (PT) to provide high-quality physical therapy services to patients in their homes throughout the San Diego region.

The Physical Therapist will travel to patients' homes to perform comprehensive evaluations, develop individualized plans of care, provide skilled therapeutic interventions, monitor patient progress, and educate patients and caregivers on strategies to improve mobility, function, safety, and independence.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working independently in a home-based environment, has strong clinical judgment and communication skills, and is passionate about delivering patient-centered care.

This is a 1099 independent contractor position.

Duties and Responsibilities

· Travel to patients' homes throughout the assigned service area to provide physical therapy services.

· Perform comprehensive physical therapy evaluations in the patient's home environment.

· Assess strength, range of motion, balance, gait, mobility, coordination, endurance, pain, functional limitations, and ability to safely perform activities of daily living.

· Evaluate the patient's home environment and identify potential safety and fall risks that may impact mobility and independence.

· Develop individualized plans of care based on evaluation findings, physician orders/referrals, patient needs, clinical judgment, and functional goals.

· Establish measurable short-term and long-term functional goals.

· Provide skilled physical therapy interventions appropriate to the patient's diagnosis and functional limitations, including:

o Therapeutic exercises

o Therapeutic activities

o Neuromuscular re-education

o Gait and mobility training

o Balance and coordination training

o Functional strengthening

o Manual therapy when clinically appropriate

o Transfer training

o Fall prevention and safety training

· Train patients in the safe use of assistive devices such as walkers, canes, and other mobility equipment.

· Develop and instruct patients in individualized home exercise programs.

· Educate patients and caregivers regarding diagnosis, treatment, exercises, mobility, safety, fall prevention, and strategies to promote independence.

· Monitor patient response to treatment and make appropriate clinical modifications to the plan of care.

· Perform reassessments and communicate changes in patient condition or functional status as appropriate.

· Coordinate care with physicians, nurses, caregivers, physical therapist assistants, occupational therapists, and other healthcare professionals.

· Communicate effectively with referring providers regarding patient progress, concerns, and recommendations.

· Complete accurate, timely, and thorough documentation for evaluations, daily treatment visits, reassessments, progress reports, and discharge summaries.

· Maintain compliance with applicable federal and state regulations, professional standards, payer requirements, and company policies.

· Recognize changes in patient condition that may require physician notification, additional medical evaluation, or modification of treatment.

· Maintain patient confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries at all times.

· Provide compassionate, respectful, and professional care to patients and their families in the home setting.

Requirements

· Current and valid Texas Physical Therapist license in good standing.

· Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapy program.

· Strong knowledge of anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, and rehabilitation principles.

· Strong clinical reasoning and patient assessment skills.

· Ability to independently perform comprehensive PT evaluations and develop appropriate plans of care.

· Experience treating patients with orthopedic, musculoskeletal, neurological, balance, gait, weakness, mobility, and/or functional limitations preferred.

· Strong knowledge of therapeutic exercise, gait training, balance training, functional mobility, neuromuscular re-education, and fall prevention.

· Excellent patient assessment and acute/chronic pain management skills.

· Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

· Ability to work independently and effectively manage a mobile patient caseload.

· Must be punctual, dependable, organized, and professional.

· Comfortable entering and providing care in patients' homes and working with patients and caregivers in a home-based environment.

· Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required.

· Ability to travel throughout the assigned service area.

· CPR/BLS certification preferred or required according to company policy.

· Previous home health, mobile therapy, outpatient, orthopedic, neurological, geriatric, or community-based experience is preferred.

Mobile/Home-Based Care Expectations

Because this position involves providing care in patients' homes, the Physical Therapist must be able to:

· Arrive at scheduled visits within the expected timeframe.

· Manage travel time and maintain an efficient daily schedule.

· Carry and transport necessary clinical equipment and supplies.

· Adapt treatment approaches to different home environments and available space.

· Maintain a safe and professional environment during every patient visit.

· Communicate promptly regarding cancellations, scheduling changes, or patient concerns.

· Respect patients' homes, privacy, routines, and individual preferences.

· Demonstrate sound clinical judgment when working independently in the community.

Documentation and Compliance

The Physical Therapist is responsible for completing all required clinical documentation accurately and within established timeframes, including:

· Initial evaluations

· Treatment notes

· Reassessments

· Progress reports

· Recertifications, when applicable

· Discharge documentation

· Home exercise programs

· Communication with referring providers

· Other documentation required by the organization, payer, or applicable regulations

Job Type

Full-time – 1099 Independent Contractor

Pay Structure (1099)

· Guaranteed base pay: $1,080 per week

· Base compensation is calculated at $45 per patient visit, based on a minimum of 6 patient visits per day.

· $45 per additional patient visit for visits beyond the daily base of 6.

· Compensation is subject to the terms of the independent contractor agreement.

Schedule

4/10 Schedule

· Four 10-hour workdays per week

· Typical start time: 7:30 AM–8:30 AM, depending on patient scheduling and geographic coverage.

· Daily schedule may vary based on patient locations, visit duration, and patient needs.

Work Location

Mobile/Home-Based – San Diego Region

The Physical Therapist will travel to assigned patients' homes throughout the designated service area.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a clinically confident, compassionate, and self-motivated Physical Therapist who enjoys working one-on-one with patients and families. The successful candidate will be comfortable making clinical decisions independently, adapting treatment to the patient's home environment, and providing high-quality care while maintaining excellent documentation and communication.

This position is an excellent opportunity for a Physical Therapist who values autonomy, flexibility, meaningful patient relationships, and community-based care

description:

For more information, please visit our website: .

MMR is seeking HSE Project Technician candidates looking to work full time out of our site in Mesa, AZ. The responsibilities would include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Report to the Project Safety Coordinator, and/or Branch Office Safety Coordinator.

  • Other duties to include additional HS&E related support not listed as requested by the Project Safety Coordinator and Site Management.

  • Must comply with all safety and company rules and regulations
Education and Certifications required: OSHA 30, HS Diploma or equivalent, 2-5 years of experience as an HSE technician in Electrical. OSHA 500/510 preferred.

Employee must possess proper forms of identification such as valid Driver’s License or State identification, and a Social Security Card. State and/or local license/certifications may be required.
Certification which may be a plus: Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Occupational Health and Safety Technician (OHST), Construction Site Safety Technician (CSST), NFPA 70E knowledge

**Bilingual in Spanish and English preferred but not required.

58-hour workweek

title: Dietitian
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

As an integral member of the interdisciplinary care team, the Dietitian is responsible for the planning, monitoring, and approving of menu foods. The Dietitian provides therapeutic services to individual Residents. The Dietitian works in collaboration and consults with the Food Services Manager to ensure food services meet all legislative standards, Park Place policy and Resident satisfaction. Treats Residents with dignity and demonstrates an attitude of caring. The Dietitian ensures a commitment to Resident safety and to our “culture of safety” as per Park Place Strategic Directions. Current availability for 15 hours per week.

TYPICAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

1. In collaboration with the interdisciplinary care team and the Resident and/or family, assesses all Residents upon Move-In and annually to complete a documented, in-depth nutritional assessment, based on the Resident’s needs, abilities, and goals.

2. Provides consultation to the Food Services Manager in planning the menu and textured diets, and other dietary matters as they arise. Approves the rotating menu.

3. Performs swallowing assessments and makes recommendations on diet textures, feeding techniques and safety precautions.

4. Counsels Residents and family members on therapeutic diets, and other nutritional concerns.

5. Prescribes dietary supplements as appropriate (e.g., Resident with weight loss, wounds) and monitors their effectiveness and use.

6. Monitors quality of food served to Residents and Resident’s acceptability of items served.

7. Provides employees in-service education on nutrition related topics (e.g., dysphagia, therapeutic diets).

8. Responsible for routinely reviewing Resident weight data and following up with an in-depth nutritional assessment and plan revision as appropriate.

9. Coordinates and participates in MDS data entry by communicating with and observing the Resident and communicating with interdisciplinary team members and family.

10. Responsible for both the Minimum Data Set (MDS) and the Resident Assessment Protocols (RAPs) as it pertains to nutrition, which includes but is not limited to care plans, progress notes, assessments, profiles and/or tracking.

11. Documents complete, accurate and relevant data for every Resident according to Park Place’s policies.

12. Acts as a role model by demonstrating professionalism, empathy, trust, and respect in all interpersonal relationships, and recognizes personal impact on team dynamics.

13. Takes the Dietitian lead in the Park Place Home’s quality improvement/ performance measurement initiatives and processes including follow-up with summary and action plan implementation to meet or exceed best practice and Accreditation Standards.

14. Focuses on quality of care and safety assurance and improvement by taking a leadership role in Park Place site committees (e.g., Site Leadership, Resident Council).

15. Performs other related duties as needed.

HEALTH AND SAFETY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Responsible to read, understand and comply with Park Place’s and provincially mandated Occupational Health and Safety policies and safe work practices.

• Involved in all aspects of the Health and Safety Program including:

• Uses safe work procedures,

• Promotes health and safety policy and awareness,

• Makes safety suggestions.

• Reads OHS minutes posted.

• Responsible to take every reasonable precaution to protect the safety of Residents, self, other staff, and the public.

• Reports any good catch (near miss), injury, accident, or equipment damage to supervisor immediately and completes required reports.

• Corrects and/or reports unsafe conditions.

• Sets a good example.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Must have a university degree in Food and Nutrition or related field of study. Two (2) years recent related experience an asset.

SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

• Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing.

• Ability to organize work.

• Ability to operate related equipment.

• Ability to work in teams collaboratively and communicate with others in a respectful manner.

• Physical ability to carry out the duties of the position.

description:

Choice isn’t optional. It’s everything.
In life. In health. In how we fight for our future. But somewhere along the way, medicine forgot that. Today’s system runs on one-size-fits-all answers and a cold “just take this” mentality. It’s efficient. It’s easy. It’s wrong.

EVEXIAS exists to blow that model wide open.
We’re pioneering a new way of doing things, and it starts by handing the decision back to the people who matter... you and your provider. TOGETHER, you choose treatments tailored to your whole self: mind, body, and spirit—including advanced, personalized hormone therapies designed to restore balance and vitality.
We go beyond surface symptoms to uncover the root cause, using today’s breakthroughs to ignite a transition of modern medicine…where insight runs deeper, care is pro-active, and connection is everything. We dig deeper. Treat smarter. And restore something even more powerful than health—your Freedom. This isn’t just healthcare. It’s your comeback story, and that story starts with a choice.

Get Well. Live Well.

Position Summary
The Quality Assurance Technician provides on-the-floor support for the cGMP production of implantable hormone pellets. This role acts as a Quality presence during receiving, manufacturing, and packaging by performing incoming inspections, line clearances, and in-process verifications. The technician documents observations, identifies discrepancies, and escalates concerns to ensure only compliant materials and processes are utilized.
Incoming Material and Component Inspection
  • Verify that active pharmaceutical ingredients, excipients, and packaging materials are received into appropriate status.
  • Perform visual inspections for damage, cleanliness, and container-closure integrity.
  • Compare items against purchase orders, packing slips, and specifications including lot numbers and expiration dates.
  • Verify labeling, Certificates of Analysis, and Safety Data Sheets.
  • Maintain material status labels and ensure inventory records reflect current disposition.
  • Coordinate with Supply Chain, QC, and Warehouse for sampling, testing, or returns.
In-Process QA Oversight and Line Clearance
  • Perform and document line clearance before start-up, after changeovers, and at operation completion.
  • Verify room and equipment readiness, including cleaning status and calibration records.
  • Conduct independent checks on material identity, quantities, equipment settings, and yield data.
  • Provide floor oversight during weighing, pellet compression, and packaging operations.
  • Review documentation in real-time for compliance with Good Documentation Practices.
  • Ensure proper identification and segregation of all product, components, and waste.
Quality Documentation and Support
  • Complete checklists, logs, and electronic records accurately and contemporaneously.
  • Initiate or assist with quality event and nonconformance documentation.
  • Maintain records in an audit-ready condition for regulatory or customer inspections.
  • Communicate recurring errors or process signals to Quality management.
  • Collaborate across departments while maintaining independent quality judgment.
Qualifications
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • At least two years of experience in quality, inspection, manufacturing, or a regulated environment.
  • Ability to read and follow written procedures, specifications, and batch records.
  • Strong attention to detail with proficiency in Microsoft Office.
  • Ability to complete all required cGMP, data integrity, and safety training.
  • Preferred: Associate degree or experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing or 503B facilities.
