title: Program Access & Intake Coordinator
description:
Position Summary


The Program Access & Intake Coordinator serves as Oliver Gospel's mission-wide coordination point for clear, respectful, timely, and consistent access to applicable programs. Building on the former Connections Intake Coordinator function, the role connects people in need to appropriate Oliver Gospel services or, when Oliver Gospel is not the appropriate or available resource, to community, social-service, healthcare, behavioral-health, housing, or ministry resources.

The Coordinator manages assigned inquiries, referrals, pre-screening, applications, intake processes, eligibility documentation, admission coordination, HMIS and other required access data, and warm handoffs to receiving program disciplines. The role helps replace facility-specific intake practices with one coordinated access approach while preserving approved program-specific eligibility and admission requirements.

The Coordinator is not the ongoing Case Manager, Residential Support supervisor, Pastor/Biblical Counselor, or behavioral-health clinician. The role gathers and communicates information necessary for access and safe handoff, recognizes needs requiring another discipline, and routes those needs through established decision, referral, and escalation pathways.

Position Qualifications


For Employment with Oliver Gospel

A believer in Jesus Christ. Affirm without reservation Oliver Gospel’s Statement of Faith. Fully support Oliver Gospel’s Mission and Vision Statements. Demonstrate the ability and desire to work in harmony with other Oliver Gospel employees. Be on time and ready to work at the assigned work location on every scheduled workday. Due to the potential impact on Oliver Gospel’s Program Participants, the use of tobacco and/or vaping products is not permitted during scheduled work hours or at any Oliver Gospel event. Possess a valid South Carolina driver’s license.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in social work, human services, psychology, sociology, public health, ministry, or a closely related field; an equivalent combination of relevant education and substantial directly related experience may be considered with HR and program leadership approval.
  • Minimum two (2) years of relevant experience in intake, admissions, social services, homelessness services, residential services, recovery services, community referral, case-management support, or a closely related human-services setting.
  • Working knowledge of homelessness, poverty, addiction/recovery, mental and behavioral health needs, shelters/residential programs, and community-resource systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to engage people from varied backgrounds with dignity, maintain appropriate boundaries, de-escalate difficult interactions, and communicate clearly in person, by telephone, virtually, and in writing.
  • Strong administrative, organizational, research, problem-solving, critical-thinking, data-quality, and follow-through skills.
  • Ability to apply established criteria consistently, recognize urgent concerns, and follow escalation/referral procedures without practicing outside assigned scope.
  • Ability to work independently while remaining aligned with the Director of Programs, organizational structure, and interdisciplinary team.
  • Proficiency with common office technology and ability to learn and accurately use HMIS and other organizational systems.
  • Ability to travel to Oliver Gospel Mission facilities and approved off-site intake/community locations as required, subject to HR verification of applicable driving requirements.

Preferred

  • Direct experience with HMIS, coordinated entry, shelter intake, residential admissions, recovery-program admissions, or centralized access systems.
  • Working knowledge of Midlands-area homelessness, housing, behavioral-health, healthcare, benefits, family-support, and ministry/community-resource systems.
  • Experience with referral tracking, waitlist/capacity management, quality assurance, data integrity, or process improvement.

Mission-Wide Program Access & Connections

  • Serve as a primary coordination point for individuals seeking services, referral sources, and internal teams seeking access to assigned Oliver Gospel programs.
  • Respond to telephone, voicemail, email, virtual, in-person, and approved off-site access inquiries in a timely and professional manner.
  • Clearly explain Oliver Gospel's Mission, applicable program offerings, eligibility requirements, expectations, application/intake steps, available pathways, and next actions.
  • Apply approved access and eligibility criteria consistently across facilities and programs while recognizing approved program-specific differences.
  • Maintain the approved access/intake standards, tools, and guidance used by trained Residential Support personnel when they execute defined front-desk, emergency-shelter, or after-hours admission procedures.
  • Help reduce unnecessary barriers, duplicate questioning, inconsistent messaging, and siloed facility-based access practices.
  • Maintain current knowledge of Oliver Gospel programs, capacity considerations, referral pathways, community resources, and changes affecting access.

Pre-Screening, Intake & Admission Coordination

  • Complete assigned pre-assessments/pre-screening, applications, intake interviews, consent and information-sharing processes, orientation steps, and required access documentation.
  • Gather information necessary to support eligibility, placement, immediate-needs recognition, and safe handoff without conducting clinical assessments or assuming another discipline's professional responsibilities.
  • Coordinate approved admissions with the appropriate receiving program and disciplines based on established criteria, capacity, safety requirements, and decision rights.
  • For admissions executed by Residential Support, provide the standards, forms, data requirements, training support, and follow-up needed for consistent implementation; the Coordinator does not replace 24/7 Residential Support coverage.
  • Communicate relevant immediate needs and intake information to authorized Case Management, Residential Support, Spiritual Formation, and other receiving personnel so services can begin without unnecessary repetition.
  • Escalate unclear eligibility, exceptions, placement, capacity, safety, medical, behavioral-health, withdrawal/substance-use, family, accessibility, or other concerns through established protocols.
  • Support transitions between Oliver Gospel programs when a new access, eligibility, or intake process is required.
  • Reconcile next-business-day documentation, HMIS, referral, or eligibility follow-up for after-hours admissions when assigned by procedure.

Referral, Resource Navigation & Warm Handoffs

  • Collaborate with approved social-service, healthcare, behavioral-health, housing, government/community, church, and ministry referral sources to support appropriate program access.
  • Identify appropriate alternatives for people whom Oliver Gospel cannot serve, cannot immediately accommodate, or whose needs fall outside Oliver Gospel's service scope.
  • Provide referral information and warm handoffs when feasible rather than ending the interaction at an unavailable service, ineligibility determination, or lack of capacity.
  • Maintain current, usable community-resource information related to homelessness, housing, addiction/recovery, mental and behavioral health, poverty, family needs, healthcare, benefits, and other common access needs.
  • Identify recurring referral gaps, misinformation, unmet needs, discharge-planning issues, or system barriers and communicate trends to the Director of Programs.
  • Build productive referral-source relationships within delegated authority; formal organizational partnerships, commitments, or resource obligations require approval through established organizational channels.

HMIS, Documentation & Data Integrity

  • Enter and maintain required resident and intake information in HMIS and other approved organizational systems according to role permissions, program requirements, and established timelines.
  • Perform assigned quality assurance and data-integrity activities related to HMIS and access/intake records; identify and correct errors within authority and elevate systemic issues.
  • Maintain timely, accurate, objective, confidential, and complete records of inquiries, referrals, screening, eligibility, admission decisions, waitlists/capacity status, handoffs, and external referrals as required.
  • Track and report agreed access indicators, which may include referral source, inquiry volume, eligibility outcomes, admissions, waitlists, declined/ineligible referrals, time to disposition, handoff completion, and access barriers.
  • Collaborate with authorized organizational teams by providing approved aggregate program/access data and information as requested while protecting confidential information.
  • Use access data to identify bottlenecks, inconsistent practices, avoidable delays, referral trends, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Person-Centered, Trauma-Responsive & Rights-Respecting Access

  • Treat every prospective and entering resident with dignity, clarity, compassion, respect, and appropriate choice.
  • Provide information in a clear and understandable manner so individuals can make informed decisions regarding available services and next steps.
  • Use trauma-responsive communication and avoid unnecessary repetition, humiliation, adversarial screening, coercive interactions, or promises that cannot be kept.
  • Respect privacy, confidentiality, informed consent/refusal, and approved information-sharing requirements throughout access and intake processes.
  • Seek assistance when disability, language, family composition, communication needs, or other circumstances require accommodation or additional support.
  • Recognize that access and intake are often a person's first experience of Oliver Gospel and consistently demonstrate Christ-centered hospitality and the organizational performance framework.

Care Team, Continuity & Role Boundaries

  • Residential Support retains responsibility for front-desk coverage, facility supervision, bed/space execution, belongings procedures, distribution of basic essentials, security rounds, operational rule enforcement, and other 24/7 residential functions unless an approved policy assigns otherwise.
  • The Program Access & Intake Coordinator does not own routine front-desk reception or around-the-clock shelter coverage; the role owns the mission-wide access framework, assigned screening/intake processes, data integrity, and coordinated handoff.
  • Practice the principle: One Mission. One Resident. One Coordinated Plan. Distinct Roles. Shared Outcomes.
  • Ensure intake information follows the resident to the appropriate receiving team so continuity begins at admission rather than requiring the resident to restart the process with each discipline.
  • Clarify the handoff point after intake and avoid retaining ongoing Case Management, pastoral, residential-supervision, or clinical responsibilities that belong to another discipline.
  • Participate in Care Team or program coordination discussions when access, referral, admission, transition, or intake information is relevant.
  • Recognize and route needs to Case Management, Spiritual Formation, Residential Support, or qualified external Mental & Behavioral Health providers according to established scope and referral pathways.
  • Do not create a separate intake silo or independently direct the work of another discipline.

Strategic Alignment & Community Impact

  • Support Oliver Gospel's strategic movement from fragmented service delivery toward consistent, measurable, Christ-centered transformation by creating reliable access and handoff processes across programs.
  • Contribute access and referral data that help leadership understand demand, service gaps, community needs, capacity constraints, and progress toward measurable program outcomes.
  • Support the organization's role as a connector in the community by maintaining accurate referral pathways and identifying opportunities for better coordination, while remaining within delegated authority.
  • Coordinate appropriately with Spiritual Formation and other designated leaders when church or ministry partners are part of approved access, referral, mentoring, discipleship, or community-support pathways.
  • Support phased pilots and process improvements approved by the Director of Programs rather than independently expanding the scope of Program Access & Intake.

Competency, Communication & Continuous Improvement

  • Demonstrate and maintain competencies required for access, screening, intake, eligibility processes, trauma-responsive communication, HMIS/data quality, confidentiality, referral, risk recognition, de-escalation, and interdisciplinary handoff.
  • Participate in supervision, competency assessment, training, coaching, and performance development.
  • Initiate strong, consistent communication with the Director of Programs and peers; participate actively in assigned meetings and complete follow-up responsibilities on time.
  • Work independently within established authority while staying aligned with organizational priorities, approved workflows, and leadership direction.
  • Navigate changing priorities and a high-volume workload with sound judgment, organization, accuracy, and appropriate escalation.
  • Receive feedback and correction with humility and contribute recommendations that improve access, resident experience, coordination, data quality, and program consistency.

Core Competencies

Program Access & Intake • Screening & Eligibility Processes • HMIS & Data Integrity • Resource Navigation & Referral • Trauma-Responsive Communication • Person-Centered Service • Rights, Confidentiality & Consent • Risk Recognition & Escalation • Warm Handoff & Continuity • Interdisciplinary Coordination • De-escalation • Organization & Prioritization • Sound Judgment • Relationship Building • Teachability • Organizational Accountability

Organizational Performance & Accountability

At Oliver Gospel, successful performance is measured by both what an employee accomplishes and how the employee accomplishes it. Every employee is accountable for fulfilling the responsibilities, competencies, and expected outcomes of the position while consistently advancing Oliver Gospel's Mission and Vision and demonstrating the Core Values, How We Work practices, and the integrated Ideal Team Player virtues of Humble, Hungry, and Smart. These expectations are integral to recruitment and selection, onboarding, supervision and coaching, professional development, performance evaluation, promotion and advancement, recognition, retention, and corrective action.

Organizational Framework: Mission • Vision • Core Values: Faith, Love, Integrity, Servant Mindset, Initiative • How We Work: We Pray, We Step Out, We Breathe, We Build, We Press On, We Receive, We Love, We Release, We Speak Truth, We Imagine • Ideal Team Player: Humble, Hungry, Smart.

Physical & Work Demands

  • Ability to work effectively in a changing, growth-oriented environment.
  • Ability to concentrate, apply sound judgment, and manage complex information.
  • Ability to work effectively amid disruptions, critical issues, and interactions with emotionally distressed individuals.
  • Ability to maintain a positive, professional, and mission-focused approach.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, responsibilities, interruptions, and competing demands.
  • Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while performing computer-based and administrative work.
  • Ability to operate a computer and other office equipment for extended periods.
  • Ability to move throughout Oliver Gospel Mission facilities to engage with residents, employees, and program teams.
  • Ability to travel between Oliver Gospel Mission facilities and participate in community and professional meetings as needed.
  • Ability to participate in meetings and work evening or weekend hours as organizational needs require.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, and through electronic communication.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and composure when handling sensitive, emotional, or difficult situations.
  • Ability to adapt to changing technology, systems, procedures, and organizational priorities.

Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by the Director of Programs that are consistent with the purpose and level of the position and evolving organizational needs.

  • The Bible inspired Word of God, a revelation of Himself to humanity and is the instrument through which God speaks to us.

  • Salvation is only by grace, a free gift of God, through faith in the Lord Jesus, who died for our sins. Those who receive Christ by faith have their sins forgiven and are made new creatures in Christ.

title: Data Architect
description:
Job Title: Data Architect

Experience: 9+ Years
Industry: Banking / Financial Services

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced Data Architect with a strong background in AI/ML and Big Data architectures to design, implement, and govern enterprise-wide data solutions. The ideal candidate will play a critical role in enabling data-driven decision-making, advanced analytics, and AI capabilities within a banking environment while ensuring compliance with regulatory and security standards.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and implement enterprise data architecture across traditional systems, Big Data platforms, and cloud ecosystems.
  • Architect scalable data lakes, data warehouses, and lakehouse solutions supporting structured and unstructured data.

  • Ensure compliance with banking regulations, data privacy laws, and security standards.
  • Evaluate and recommend emerging technologies to enhance the organization’s data capabilities.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, or related field.
  • 9+ years of experience in data architecture, data engineering, or related roles, preferably in the banking or financial services industry.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms: AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.

  • Strong understanding of AI/ML data pipelines and frameworks (Python, TensorFlow, PyTorch).
  • Expertise in ETL/ELT tools and data pipeline orchestration.
  • Knowledge of data governance, metadata management, and data quality frameworks.
  • Familiarity with banking data domains (risk, compliance, fraud, customer analytics).
  • Excellent problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certifications in Cloud Platforms (AWS/Azure/GCP) or Data Architecture.
  • Experience with real-time streaming architectures.
  • Knowledge of regulatory frameworks such as Basel III, GDPR, or local banking compliance standards.
  • Exposure to Data Mesh or Data Fabric architectures.
  • Experience with API-based data integration and microservices architecture.

Key Competencies

  • Strategic Thinking
  • Data Governance & Compliance
  • Solution Architecture
  • Stakeholder Management
  • Innovation & Continuous Improvement

Site Identification & Land Acquisition

  • Represent Provident within the data center industry and build a network of relationships across the ecosystem, including brokers, utilities, capital partners, general contractors, and hyperscale customers.

  • Bachelor's degree in Real Estate, Business, Finance, or a related field preferred.

  • Background in data centers preferred; experience with hyperscale or mission-critical development strongly preferred.

  • Proven track record developing relationships with capital partners, brokers, utilities, and end customers.
  • Willingness to learn and adapt in a fast-moving, rapidly evolving industry.

Since its inception in 1991, Provident has developed over $6 Billion of real estate projects. We are disciplined and focused on executing deals that offer the best strategy for Provident and our investor partners. With over three decades of experience with opportunistic land development and vertical development in various key U.S. markets, our company thrives on an entrepreneurial spirit and an excellent track record of success.

Knowledge/Skills:

  1. Strong expertise in major social media platforms.

  5. Deep understanding of storytelling, with the ability to interpret and deploy an established brand positioning.

  6. Familiarity with analyzing social media data and insights.

title: Vil du skape gode arbeidsplasser gjennom mat, service og trivsel i Molde
description:
Er du glad i mennesker, mat og god service?
I Toma tror vi at de små tingene kan gjøre en stor forskjell i arbeidsdagen. En hyggelig lunsjpause, et rent og innbydende arbeidsmiljø og et smil i hverdagen bidrar til trivsel for alle.
Nå søker vi en servicemedarbeider til en spennende 60 % stilling i et nytt kontorbygg i Molde, hvor vår kunde nylig har flyttet inn. Her får du en viktig rolle i å skape gode opplevelser for rundt 50 ansatte gjennom både kantinedrift og renhold.
Dette er en selvstendig stilling for deg som liker å ta ansvar, yte service og bidra til at andre får en bedre arbeidsdag.
Hva skal du gjøre?
Arbeidshverdagen består av en kombinasjon av kantineoppgaver og renhold.
I kantinen vil du blant annet:
  • Tilberede og servere enkel og smakfull lunsj
  • Lage en varmrett et par dager i uken
  • Bidra med idéer til menyer og tilbud
  • Bestille varer og følge opp innkjøp
  • Sørge for at kantinen fremstår hyggelig og innbydende
Innen renhold vil du:
  • Utføre daglig renhold av kontorlokaler og fellesområder
  • Bidra til et rent, ryddig og trivelig arbeidsmiljø
  • Følge etablerte rutiner for kvalitet og hygiene
Du vil få god opplæring og støtte fra oss, både når det gjelder mattilbud, menyplanlegging, innkjøp og rutiner. Målet er at du skal føle deg trygg og lykkes i rollen.

Hvem ser vi etter?
Du trenger ikke være utdannet kokk eller ha lang erfaring fra kantine eller renhold. Det viktigste for oss er at du er serviceinnstilt, positiv og trives med mennesker og i en fysisk jobb.
Vi tror du:
  • liker å skape gode opplevelser for andre
  • er selvstendig og tar ansvar
  • har interesse for mat og har lyst å lære mer
  • er strukturert og pålitelig
  • trives med varierte arbeidsoppgaver
  • har øye for orden og kvalitet
Derfor vil du trives hos oss
Hos Toma blir du en del av et selskap som hver dag jobber for å gi mennesker en bedre arbeidsdag.
Vi tilbyr:
  • God opplæring og støtte i oppstarten
  • En variert og selvstendig arbeidshverdag
  • Mulighet til å sette ditt eget preg på kantinetilbudet
  • Lønn, pensjon og forsikringer etter tariff
  • Et inkluderende arbeidsmiljø med dyktige kollegaer
Praktisk informasjon
  • Arbeidssted: Molde
  • Stilling: 60 %
  • Arbeidstid: Mandag til fredag på dagtid (ca. 4,5 timer per dag)
  • Oppstart: medio. oktober 2026
Klar for å skape gode arbeidsdager?
Hvis du kjenner deg igjen i beskrivelsen, vil vi gjerne høre fra deg.
Send oss din søknad og fortell litt om hvorfor denne rollen passer for deg.

Har du spørsmål til stillingen? Ta gjerne uformell kontakt med avdelingsleder Rita Ramberg på mobil 400 19 181
Søknadsfristen er søndag 20. september. Ikke nøl med å søke, vi behandler søknader fortløpende
Vi er opptatt av ditt personvern og har derfor kun har mulighet til å ta imot CV og søknader ved å søke via annonsen.

title: SMS Data Collector - English (Kenya)
description:
SMS Data Collection Participant - English (Kenya)

Location: Remote: Participants must be based in Kenya

Schedule: Flexible

Project type: Short-term/project-based

Device requirement(s): You must use your own mobile phone and Kenya phone number

The Project

Productive Playhouse is seeking English-speaking participants for a mobile messaging data collection project. Participants will submit authentic scam and spam SMS messages received on their personal mobile phones to help improve technology designed to identify fraudulent and unwanted communications.

This is a flexible, remote opportunity. Participants may submit eligible messages whenever they receive them, provided all submissions meet project requirements..

Your contributions will support the development of tools designed to make mobile messaging safer for users around the world.

Why Participate?

  • Earn $1.25 USD for each qualified message you submit
  • Participate remotely on a flexible schedule
  • Help improve scam-detection technology by showing how real messages appear in English.

Duties

  • Submit authentic SMS messages that meet project guidelines
  • Identify each message as either Scam or Spam
  • Categorize submissions according to the appropriate message type
  • Ensure all submissions are complete, accurate, and meet quality standards
  • Follow all project instructions and submission requirements

Please note: Messages collected from email or other platforms are not eligible. Submissions must be SMS messages received directly on your mobile phone.

Only submissions that meet requirements will be eligible for payment

Project Requirements

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Are a native or expert-level fluency in English, as spoken in Kenya
  • Currently located in Kenya
  • Have access to your own mobile device
  • You must have access to your own Kenya phone number
  • Can follow project guidelines and quality standards

Why PPH?

  • Your language skills are the whole point — and this project pays for them
  • Apply once, get contacted directly when a spot opens — no chasing
  • Work from anywhere, on your own schedule, alongside any other work you do
  • Clear task specs, no ongoing oversight, no micromanagement
    Real project experience with a global data and language services company
  • Work that actually improves how AI understands your language

About Productive Playhouse

We started by teaching kids through award-winning programming. We grew into a global data and language services company trusted by clients worldwide. But the mission never changed: keep language alive.

Transcription, translation, localization, linguistic analysis, AI evaluation — it all comes back to preserving languages and the cultures they carry.

All engagements are contingent upon successful completion of identity verification. Productive Playhouse is an equal opportunity organization headquartered in California and committed to diversity and inclusion across our global workforce. title: Practicum Advisor
description:
Who we are

At Yorkville University and Toronto Film School, we believe education is more than the pursuit of knowledge – it is a catalyst for transformation. Our mission, grounded in democratizing education, is to create access for learners from every background and empower them to achieve their aspirations and advance their careers.

We are committed to delivering rigorous, flexible programs that are both personally fulfilling and professionally rewarding, while contributing to the betterment of society. Since 2004, Yorkville has been among Canada’s few private, for-profit, fully accredited degree-granting universities, with campuses in Ontario, British Columbia, and New Brunswick. Together with Toronto Film School, we offer creative and academic pathways at both the college and university levels, cultivating a multidisciplinary environment where innovation and the arts converge.

Our community is vibrant and diverse. Many of our learners are adults balancing education with careers and personal commitments. Every member of our team – whether in teaching, operations, or technology – is dedicated to removing barriers and expanding access. Together, we deliver flexible, industry-informed learning that leads to meaningful opportunities.

At our core is human connection – guiding people to reimagine their futures in a community defined by opportunity, creativity, and growth.

Who we need

Reporting to the Manager of Practicum Applications, we are hiring a Practicum Advisor to support students in the Master of Arts in Counselling Psychology program as they prepare for practicum. As our new Practicum Advisor, you will guide students through pre-practicum requirements, helping them understand what they need to complete and supporting their progression through each stage of the process. You will review applications and documentation, track student progress, and collaborate with university teams to help ensure students are prepared to move forward with their placements in accordance with university requirements.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates across Canada.

What's in it for you

Impact on a critical stage of the student journey. Practicum is an important milestone for Master of Arts in Counselling Psychology students as they move from academic learning toward applied professional experience. You will help students navigate the requirements leading up to this stage, providing the clarity, guidance, and follow-through they need to feel prepared and confident as they progress toward practicum.

Influence on student readiness and progression. You will play an important role in helping students successfully move through the pre-practicum process. By reviewing applications and documentation, clarifying requirements, tracking progress, and coordinating with students, potential supervisors, practicum sites, faculty, and university teams, you will help identify and resolve issues that could otherwise delay a student's progression. Your work will contribute to a well-coordinated experience and help ensure students are ready to move forward with their placements.

Specialized knowledge and career growth. You will build expertise in practicum processes, graduate education, student advising, and the requirements involved in preparing counselling psychology students for field training. Working across student services, faculty, practicum sites, and supervisors will give you broad exposure to the academic and administrative processes behind experiential learning while strengthening skills you can continue to build on within student services and post-secondary education.

How you will make an impact

  • Guide students through the pre-practicum process. You will provide clear, responsive support to Master of Arts in Counselling Psychology students as they prepare for practicum. You will answer questions, clarify requirements, and provide direction on the documentation and steps students need to complete.
  • Review and coordinate practicum applications. You will review practicum applications and supporting documentation for completeness and accuracy, following established university requirements and processes. You will communicate with students when additional information or action is needed and help keep applications moving forward.
  • Track student progress. You will monitor students as they move through the different stages of the pre-practicum process, maintaining accurate and confidential electronic records. You will manage a high volume of information and follow up on outstanding requirements to help students stay on track.
  • Communicate and collaborate. You will correspond with students and work with practicum sites, potential supervisors, faculty, and university colleagues to support a well-coordinated practicum process. You will communicate professionally and thoughtfully, helping ensure everyone has the information they need.
  • Support continuous improvement. You will help maintain and update pre-practicum documents, resources, and presentations as requirements and processes evolve. You will contribute to the day-to-day effectiveness of the team and take on additional activities that support students and the practicum application process.

What you bring

  • The education. You have a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Social Sciences, or a related field, providing you with a strong foundation for understanding and supporting the needs of a diverse graduate student population.
  • The organizational skills. You are highly organized and comfortable managing a large volume of detailed and confidential information. You can work independently, prioritize competing needs, maintain accurate records, and contribute as a collaborative member of a team.
  • The technical skills. You are proficient with Microsoft Office, Adobe, and data management tools, and you are comfortable learning new systems and software. You can use technology effectively to organize information, maintain documentation, and support day-to-day processes.
  • The communication and relationship-building skills. You can build trusting relationships and communicate professionally with graduate students, prospective students, faculty, university staff, and other professionals. You know how to adapt your communication to different audiences, provide clear information, and navigate challenging conversations with diplomacy and sound judgment.
  • The ability to navigate complex situations. You bring strong conflict resolution and crisis management skills and can remain thoughtful and professional when situations are sensitive or challenging. You approach barriers with empathy, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the diverse experiences and needs of graduate students.

Why work at Yorkville University?

At Yorkville University and Toronto Film School, we are united by a shared purpose: placing the student experience at the heart of everything we do. Whether you are teaching, designing curriculum, advising students, advancing technology, or supporting operations, your work directly fuels learning potential, strengthens inclusive communities, and fosters purposeful curiosity.

Here, professional growth is part of our culture. In your role, you will have opportunities to help the launch of career-relevant programs, expand your expertise, and access tuition-free courses across our institutions - from certificates to master’s degrees. Curiosity, initiative, and innovation are encouraged, and your ideas can move from vision to reality.

Our scale offers the best of both worlds: the reach and stability of a national institution combined with the agility of a mid-sized organization, where contributions are visible and valued. You will be part of a diverse and inclusive community where authenticity is celebrated, collaboration is expected, and impact is shared - on students, colleagues, and your own professional journey.

At Yorkville and Toronto Film School, your work does more than make a difference. It empowers others to achieve their possible, while giving you the opportunity to realize yours.

Compensation philosophy

At Yorkville University and Toronto Film School, we believe compensation should be fair, straightforward, and supportive of your growth. Our salary ranges reflect progression from learning in the role to excelling, with each offer based on skills, experience, and role complexity.

This position offers a minimum annual salary of $50,000, a midpoint of $53,500 and a maximum of $55,000. Established hires typically start near the midpoint, while the upper range is reserved for those with deep expertise and sustained contributions. Offers below the midpoint recognize strong potential with room to grow.

We strive for equitable, consistent pay, though rates may vary within the same role based on performance, specialized knowledge, and impact.

Base salary is one part of a broader package that includes paid time away, retirement savings matching, and extended health coverage with 80% of premiums paid. After 12 months of full-time employment, there is also tuition-free access to all our education programs.

We welcome conversations about compensation throughout the hiring process.

Join us

We welcome and appreciate candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. If you have 70% of the qualifications we seek, express your interest.

What you can expect from our hiring process:

  • A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Yorkville University and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
  • A virtual interview with the Manager of Practicum Applications and Team Lead, Practicum Applications to discuss your experience and approach to supporting students, managing detailed administrative processes, and collaborating as part of a team.

Diversity, equity, and inclusion are critical components of life at Yorkville University and Toronto Film School, and we are committed to making these values an integral part of our culture. We encourage applications from all qualified applicants, including women, persons with disabilities, Black, Indigenous and People of Colour (BIPOC), people from the Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Transsexual, Queer, Questioning, Two-Spirit, Intersex, Asexual + (LGBTQ2SIA+) community and other equity-seeking groups.

Yorkville University is committed to providing accessible employment practices that comply with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). If you require accommodation for disability, please notify Human Resources at 1-877-429-4029.

  • Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal and communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated knowledge of regulatory compliance standards

GPTLHB Clinical Rotation Program

To be eligible for participation in the GPTLHB Clinical Rotation Program, applicants must have a confirmed preceptor, sponsoring department, academic program, or designated staff sponsor. Applications submitted without an identified placement sponsor will be deemed ineligible and will not proceed through the review process.


The Great Plains Tribal Leaders Health Board (GPTLHB) Clinical Rotation Program provides undergraduate, graduate, and professional students with meaningful clinical learning opportunities in a variety of healthcare disciplines. Participants gain hands-on experience while working alongside healthcare professionals dedicated to serving the Tribal Nations of the Great Plains. Through these experiences, students develop practical skills, expand their professional knowledge, and gain exposure to culturally responsive healthcare delivery.

Equal Opportunity Statement

GPTLHB is committed to providing equal educational and training opportunities for all qualified applicants and participants. GPTLHB does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, tribal, or local law. Individuals who require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the Clinical Rotation Program may request accommodation in accordance with applicable laws and organizational procedures.

Eligibility Requirements

  • Maintain a cumulative grade point average (GPA) of 2.5 or higher.
  • Demonstrate effective verbal and written communication skills appropriate for a clinical learning environment.
  • Comply with all program requirements and GPTLHB policies, procedures, confidentiality standards, and professional conduct expectations.
  • Demonstrate basic proficiency in technology necessary to complete educational and clinical activities, including:
    • Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook);
    • Email communication and file attachments; and

Additional Requirements

  • Background screening;
  • Drug screening;
  • Required immunization and health clearance documentation; including most recent COVID-19

title: Vice President, Power Development (Data Centers)
description:
📍 Location: Dallas, TX
🏢 Asset Class: Data Centers
🕒 Employment Type: Full-Time | In-Office + Travel)


Position Overview:
Provident Data Centers is seeking a VP, Power Development to build out and lead behind-the-meter power development in support of Provident's hyperscale data center platform.

This role will report to the Managing Partner and will work closely with Provident's Hyperscale Data Center Development and land acquisition teams to identify and develop behind-the-meter power solutions, secure sites with strong power fundamentals, and build relationships with independent power producers (IPPs), utilities, and other participants across the power ecosystem.

This is a highly visible role for a success-driven power industry executive who thrives in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment and is excited to help build a new behind-the-meter power platform from the ground up.


Key Responsibilities:
Hyperscale & Site Collaboration
  • Partner with Provident's Hyperscale Data Center Development team to identify and develop behind-the-meter power solutions for hyperscale sites.
  • Work with Provident's land acquisition team to evaluate and help secure sites with favorable power fundamentals, including generation potential, fuel access, interconnection feasibility, and proximity to transmission.
  • Assess power generation options, including natural gas, renewables, and battery storage, for individual sites and across Provident's site portfolio.
IPP & Ecosystem Relationships
  • Develop and manage relationships with independent power producers (IPPs), utilities, EPCs, fuel suppliers, and other participants across the power generation ecosystem.
  • Build a broad network of executive relationships across the IPP and power industry to source and advance behind-the-meter power opportunities.
  • Represent Provident within the power and energy industry, including at industry conferences, forums, and other relationship-building venues.
Power Procurement & Deal Structuring
  • Lead the procurement of natural gas and other fuel supply (“molecules”) required to support behind-the-meter generation.
  • Structure and negotiate power generation agreements, including power purchase agreements (PPAs), tolling agreements, and fuel supply contracts, in partnership with legal counsel.
  • Evaluate deal structure and economics, including capital costs, generation technology selection, and financing structure, to optimize project returns.
Business Development
  • Lead business development efforts for Provident's behind-the-meter power business, including sourcing new opportunities and cultivating relationships with prospective partners.
  • Collaborate with the Hyperscale Data Center Development team to position behind-the-meter power solutions for prospective hyperscale customers.
  • Track market trends, generation technology developments, and regulatory changes affecting behind-the-meter power development, and share insights with executive leadership.

Qualifications & Experience:
Education & Technical Foundation
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related field preferred.
  • 10+ years of experience in power development, including generation, utility, or IPP experience.
  • Broad network of executive relationships across the IPP and power industry.
  • Knowledge of and background in the latest power generation technologies, including natural gas, renewables, and battery storage.
  • Experience structuring power generation deals, with a broad understanding of deal structure and associated economics.
  • Background in data centers or behind-the-meter power development preferred.
  • Willingness to learn and adapt in a fast-moving, rapidly evolving industry.
Skills & Competencies
  • Success-driven individual with a strong desire to build a new platform in a dynamic, entrepreneurial setting.
  • Broad understanding of deal structure and associated economics.
  • Ability to work effectively across a broad virtual team in an entrepreneurial setting.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills across technical, financial, and executive stakeholders.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present effectively to executive leadership and external partners.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with sound judgment in evaluating power generation opportunities and partners.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
Company Overview:
Since its inception in 1991, Provident has developed over $6 Billion of real estate projects. We are disciplined and focused on executing deals that offer the best strategy for Provident and our investor partners. With over three decades of experience with opportunistic land development and vertical development in various key U.S. markets, our company thrives on an entrepreneurial spirit and an excellent track record of success.

Over the past 30+ years, Provident has executed a diversified real estate investment and development platform. Currently, the $7.5 billion portfolio includes product types such as multi-family, industrial, master-planned communities, hospitality, retail, office, mixed-use, and data centers across the United States.

Under the leadership of Leon Backes and Jay Hawes, Provident is a respected, well-capitalized investment firm that has thrived through three decades and multiple market cycles with foresight, depth of experience, and a unique ability to adapt to shifting demands, market trends, and challenging economic cycles. Provident is in constant pursuit of flexibility, innovation, and professionalism in its operations and investments. By maintaining a streamlined decision-making process, Provident is able to capitalize on fast-moving opportunities and rapidly adjust to dynamic market forces.

Benefits:

  • Company-Provided Life Insurance and Long-Term Disability Insurance

title: Dispensary Associate - GrowHealthy (Tamarac)
description:
At iAnthus, we are not just in the business of cannabis; we’re in the business of empowering individuals to lead healthier, happier lives through access to premium-quality medicinal and adult-use cannabis products. We believe in the potential of cannabis to enhance wellness and redefine the future of self-care. As a trailblazer in the cannabis industry, we’re committed to providing a holistic approach to well-being, fostering a community where every patient and customer can thrive and find relief.

Who We Are:

iAnthus Capital Management is a multi-state operator, encompassing the full spectrum of cannabis enterprises, from cultivation to processing to retailing. Cannabis will be the next great transformative industry - not just because it has the power to change people’s lives (especially those suffering from chronic ailments) – but also because it will impact many other industries, from agriculture to pharmaceuticals to alcoholic beverages. Our mission is to create the most valuable cannabis brands and network of cannabis operations and distribution nationally. At iAnthus, you will be given opportunities for career development, a flexible work environment, excellent benefits, a wellness program and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the cannabis industry.

Who You Are:

You have a strong desire to learn and to contribute to a team. You are passionate about making an inclusive, positive, and compliant workforce. You can effectively manage your time and focus on ensuring data integrity and accuracy for your projects. If you would like to work in a fast-paced environment and are interested in building something meaningful with the rest of the iAnthus team, we would love to hear from you!

Benefits:

  • Paid Sick Leave
  • Wellness Program
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Product Discounts
  • Ability to work in a growing company where your talents and skills can have a positive impact

Summary:

As a Dispensary Associate, you’ll be a vital force in the evolving world of cannabis. Acting as a trusted advisor, you’ll be at the forefront of patient acquisition for medicinal cannabis and welcoming adult-use use customers, fostering an environment where education, exploration, and satisfaction intersect. Your primary responsibility is to offer comprehensive education on strains, effects, and various methods of cannabis use, ensuring everyone receives tailored information to make informed decisions. Beyond education, you’ll be the face of our dispensary, delivering warm and informed service, recording transactions in the POS system, and collaborating closely with dispensary managers to maintain a clean and organized dispensary environment.

Essential Functions:

The Dispensary Associate elevates the dispensary experience for our patients and customers. This role is the heartbeat of our interactions, where you’ll be a vital part of shaping a positive, informative, and seamless journey for prospective, new, and returning customers. Your key responsibilities include, but is not limited to the following:

  • Welcome everyone with a friendly attitude, creating a positive dispensary experience.
  • Guide and educate patients and customers in choosing the right medicine and products, providing personalized insights into strains and effects.
  • Proactively interact with customers, guide them through our product offerings, and highlight exclusive specials to increase sales opportunities.
  • Enter and access patient records accurately, confirming identities and eligibility to purchase in line with legal and company standards.
  • Represent the company’s brand well as a brand ambassador.
  • Follows and uphold the company’s core values, including respect, diversity, sustainability, research, and service.
  • Adheres to iAnthus' cultural principles of collaboration, innovation, and accountability.
  • Accurately handle transactions, receiving payments with a smile, and recording purchases in our Dispensary Management System.
  • Provide patients and customers with informative printed materials, helping them make well-informed decisions.
  • Bring a sales-focused attitude to every shift, always looking for chances to increase sales and grow business.
  • Work with Dispensary Managers to check product inventory, making sure we have a diverse and fresh selection that meets our patients' and customers’ needs.
  • Maintain a clean and organized dispensary area.
  • Additional duties and responsibilities as assigned.

This job description is not intended to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities. This description reflects managements’ assignment of essential functions, and it does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Duties and responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice.

Your willingness to contribute to the evolving needs of our team is highly valued.


Qualifications + Education:

  • Must be twenty-one (21) years of age or older
  • High School diploma or equivalent is required.
  • Must consent to a criminal background check.
  • Employment offers are contingent upon successful completion of the criminal background check.
  • Must have a valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills with a passion for delivering top-notch customer service.
  • Ability to work independently, coordinate multiple tasks, and prioritize work effectively.
  • Reliability is a must.
  • Meticulous organizational skills with acute attention to detail.
  • Computer-savvy, with a knack for quickly mastering new software.
  • Knowledge of or willingness to learn state-specific cannabis laws and regulatory compliance is non-negotiable.
  • Comfortable teaching customers about the medicinal and adult-use aspects of cannabis and conducting workshops or info sessions to boost their understanding and confidence in choosing products.
  • Ganjier Certification preferred

Starting Pay Rate: $15/hr


Working Conditions:

The employee works in a medical dispensary environment and uses a computer, telephone, and other office equipment to perform duties. This is a hands-on, customer-facing position. The position will regularly interact with the public and needs to engage patients and customers in a friendly and helpful manner. The employee must be able to function effectively in a high-paced, fast-moving retail environment. The employee may be subjected to work in environments that include exposure to, but not limited to, fumes, dust, odors, heights, indoor A/C, no A/C, motion and noise.

The position also requires a high level of scheduling flexibility and will occasionally include evening, weekend, and holiday work hours. The employee will encounter frequent interruptions throughout the workday and must have a high regard for self-management, time management, and scheduling of activities.


Physical Requirements:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to remain in a stationary position 80% of the time, move around, and clearly communicate. The employee must constantly position oneself to move freely around the store. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds with assistance. The employee will often need to use a ladder, with up to a 12’ extension and general hardware tools.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

Equal Employment Opportunity:
iAnthus Capital Management provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

title: Construction Management Representative
description:

Position/Project Overview:

Project Solutions Inc. is seeking a Construction Management Representative to provide tto provide construction management oversight, inspection, coordination, reporting, and contract administration services for the NERI 326119 Remove Historic Structures project at New River Gorge National Park and Preserve, West Virginia.

This role is contingent upon award of project.

Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Monitor construction, demolition, and site restoration activities to verify compliance with contract requirements, plans, specifications, and applicable standards
  • Perform field observations and inspections of contractor work at project sites located throughout New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
  • Prepare and maintain daily reports, project documentation, records, and correspondence related to construction progress and project activities
  • Review contractor schedules, submittals, cost proposals, change requests, and payment applications, and provide recommendations to the Government
  • Coordinate and communicate with contractors, National Park Service personnel, and other project stakeholders regarding project status, progress, and issues

  • Provide oversight of demolition and hazardous materials (HAZMAT) abatement activities associated with the removal of historic structures

​​Experience:

  • Experience reviewing and interpreting construction drawings, specifications, contract documents, and project requirements
  • Experience monitoring contractor performance and verifying compliance with contract requirements, safety regulations, and construction standards
  • Experience preparing and maintaining project documentation, inspection records, progress reports, and construction correspondence
  • Experience evaluating or reviewing project schedules, cost proposals, change requests, and contractor payment applications
  • Experience coordinating and communicating with contractors, project stakeholders, and Government representatives during project execution

  • Knowledge of and experience with demolition and hazardous materials (HAZMAT) abatement activities
  • Ability to safely navigate active construction sites, including areas with steep slopes, stairs, ladders, and uneven terrain encountered throughout the project sites

title: Contract Analyst
description:
Are you looking for limitless career opportunities with a company that values growth, innovation, and teamwork? At Ntiva, we’re more than a Managed Services Provider, we’re a community dedicated to helping each other, our clients, and their businesses thrive both personally and professionally. Ntiva is a culture of people who are passionate about the work…and each other.

Our clients view us as an essential part of their teams, relying on us for strategic guidance, fast solutions to complex challenges, and proactive support. With strategic locations across the U.S. and leadership from our founder, Steven Freidkin, we’re on the front lines of a fast-paced industry, facing cybersecurity threats and rapid technology changes together.

If you thrive in a dynamic, supportive environment and enjoy going above and beyond, we’d love to meet you. Come explore one of our many opportunities and grow with us!

How You'll Make an Impact
As a Contract Analyst, you will play a critical role in ensuring the accuracy and successful execution of client agreements and sales orders. You will own the contract fulfillment process from contract award through agreement setup, billing readiness, and operational handoff. Your attention to detail and ability to interpret contractual requirements will directly impact revenue accuracy, client satisfaction, operational efficiency, and successful service delivery. You will collaborate with Sales, Finance, Procurement, Service Delivery, and Project teams to ensure all contractual obligations are accurately translated into our systems and processes.

Location and Work Expectations

  • This is a remote position; however, team members should be willing and able to travel if the need arises, though such travel is expected to be infrequent. Candidates with proximity to one of our Centers of Excellence are preferred (Lombard, IL; McLean, VA; Shreveport, LA; Overland Park, KS).

What You Will Be Doing:

  • Monitor and manage the sales order pipeline to ensure timely processing.
  • Review signed agreements, quotes, and supporting documentation for completeness and accuracy.
  • Convert product and labor items from sales orders to the appropriate operational teams for execution.
  • Create and maintain recurring client agreements within ConnectWise and related systems.
  • Configure agreement billing, contract start dates, renewal dates, and cancellation dates.
  • Process agreement additions, removals, and modifications while ensuring compliance with contract terms.
  • Validate service changes against vendor portals, client records, and internal documentation before processing.
  • Maintain accurate customer records and system configurations.
  • Partner with Finance to ensure billing accuracy and prevent revenue leakage.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to resolve contract discrepancies and operational issues.
  • Identify process improvement opportunities and assist with automation initiatives.
  • Create and maintain documentation, procedures, and training materials.
  • Support special projects and other duties as assigned.

You'll Be Successful in This Role If You Have:

  • 2+ years of experience in contract administration, contract analysis, billing operations, finance operations, or a related field.
  • Experience working with CRM systems.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel and Office 365 skills.
  • Ability to analyze data, identify discrepancies, and recommend solutions.
  • Experience documenting processes and maintaining procedural documentation.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across departments.
  • A proactive mindset focused on continuous improvement and process efficiency.

Bonus Points For:

  • Experience working in a Managed Service Provider (MSP) environment.
  • Experience supporting recurring revenue or subscription-based services.
  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Operations, or a related field.
  • Experience with process automation or workflow improvement initiatives.

Required Language Skills:

  • Ability to communicate professionally, in English, both written and orally
  • Ability to write business correspondence and process procedures
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, and the general public

The base pay range for this position is expected to be between $65,000 and $75,000 per year. The base pay offered may vary depending on multiple non-discriminatory factors including, but not limited to, market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position also includes medical benefits, 401(k) eligibility, and PTO. Additional details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

FLSA Status: Salaried, Exempt

Work Authorization Criteria

Team members must establish a dedicated safe workspace that is free from distractions, hazards, and that is secure from unauthorized access. This includes following Ntiva’s IT User and Security Policies that include but are not limited to password-protecting all equipment, keeping confidential and proprietary documents secure, refraining from using public Wi-Fi, having adequate arrangements in place to avoid significant interruptions from caregiving responsibilities during work hours (except in emergency situations with manager approval). Any remote work away from a team member’s normal expected dedicated safe workspace must be requested by team member, is subject to review by management, and must adhere to Ntiva policies and procedures.

Our Commitment to a Diverse Workforce
At Ntiva, we are committed to creating and maintaining a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming work environment for all employees and job applicants. We firmly believe that a diverse workforce fosters a wider range of perspectives, experiences, and ideas that lead to increased creativity, innovation, and problem-solving capabilities. As an equal opportunity employer, we actively seek to recruit and retain a diverse workforce that reflects the communities we serve.
