title: Associate Director, Product Safety & Compliance
description:
The Opportunity

Caraway Home is looking for an experienced Associate Director, Product Safety & Compliance to build our product compliance function from the ground up and own what we call the Caraway Promise, a testing-obsessed, transparency-first approach to product safety that sets the bar for the industry. The Caraway Promise exists because we believe in transparency, not because the industry requires transparency.

This is a foundational role, the first dedicated compliance hire at Caraway, responsible for building the frameworks, lab relationships, testing strategy, supply chain diligence, claims substantiation, and regulatory sequencing across a diverse and growing product portfolio. You will own the full compliance lifecycle across Caraway's product categories (cookware, bakeware, electrical items, food contact materials, textiles, and packaging), always meeting or exceeding the most stringent applicable global standard to establish industry-leading Caraway protocols and procedures. You will be US-based, work closely with Asia-based suppliers and third-party labs (particularly in China), and build the internal systems and processes that let Caraway scale compliantly, credibly, and with confidence.

Additionally, an important responsibility of this role is disseminating key information, labels, and results to support marketing initiatives. You need to be a strong communicator, working collaboratively with cross functional teams, to broadcast and showcase the diligence Caraway is taking across its entire product portfolio in regards to compliance, being able to assist with crafting accurate, transparent, educational and understandable language and messaging that resonates with our consumer.

This position reports to our Director, Product Development.

Who You Are

You have ten or more years of product safety and regulatory compliance experience in consumer goods, ideally grounded in chemistry, materials science, or applied laboratory research, with deep expertise in food contact materials, cookware, kitchen appliances, or an adjacent hard goods category. You know FDA, LFGB, EU Framework Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, REACH, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, NSF, FSC, and CPSC requirements not as acronyms on a checklist, but as frameworks you've navigated hands-on, including where global standards diverge. You’ll use this fluency to scale the Caraway Promise internationally: building a testing and compliance framework that anticipates global standards.

You are a builder and a scientist at heart, ready to own a compliance program entirely: selecting labs, building testing matrices, writing material certification requirements, establishing supplier audit cadences, and designing the studies needed to substantiate product claims. You operate comfortably across cultures and time zones, with direct experience working with labs and manufacturers in Asia, particularly China. You communicate complex science and regulatory requirements clearly to internal teams (Product, Marketing, Legal, Supply Chain) and external partners alike, and you see internal education as core to the job.

Responsibilities

  • Own and pioneer the Caraway Promise: define and champion a testing-obsessed, transparency-first approach to product safety that goes beyond what regulation requires, because we believe our customers deserve it.
  • Build Caraway's product safety and compliance program, defining frameworks, documentation standards, testing protocols, regulatory calendars, and governance processes across all product categories (cookware, bakeware, small appliances, food contact materials, textiles, and packaging); integrate compliance across the full product lifecycle, from development and supplier onboarding through market placement, ongoing monitoring, and end-of-life.
  • Own and continuously monitor regulatory compliance across US federal and state requirements (FDA food contact, CPSC, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, Colorado PFAS Act, and emerging state chemical legislation) and international standards (EU LFGB, EC No 1935/2004, REACH, RoHS, UK REACH post-Brexit), always applying the most stringent applicable standard; lead regulatory change management as a distinct workstream, assessing impact and briefing stakeholders ahead of deadlines.
  • Lead product component mapping and material disclosure, maintaining a complete picture of every material, coating, pigment, and component across Caraway's supply chain, including Declarations of Compliance, material safety data sheets, and test reports.
  • Design and manage Caraway's testing strategy, selecting and managing third-party labs (particularly in Asia, including NRTLs for small appliances), defining testing scope and frequency by product type and risk level, and sequencing testing within development timelines to avoid launch delays or costly late-stage findings.
  • Own claims substantiation: design and commission the clinical, laboratory, and comparative studies (for example migration testing, coating durability, comparative non-stick performance) needed to support our non-toxic, food-safe, and sustainability claims. Partner with Marketing and Customer Research on which claims to make and how to communicate them, and ensure all claims are legally defensible and compliant with FTC guidelines and retailer requirements (Target, Crate & Barrel, Bloomingdale's, etc.), including CA AB 1200 disclosure obligations.
  • Conduct supply chain compliance diligence, including BSCI and Sedex (SMETA) social compliance audits and material certifications (OEKO-TEX, FSC, GRS, GOTS); embed Caraway's material and safety standards directly into manufacturing quality plans in China so factory teams implement them consistently on the production line, not just on paper; manage supplier CAPA processes and produce performance reporting to inform sourcing decisions.
  • Serve as Caraway's internal subject matter expert on product safety and science, building internal education that embeds our standards into onboarding and cross-functional fluency by year one; act as the primary point of contact for retailers, certifying bodies, and regulatory agencies on compliance matters.
  • Own product incident management, leading investigations into consumer complaints and non-conformances, conducting root cause analysis, implementing CAPAs, and coordinating with Legal, Customer Experience, and Operations on any product withdrawal or CPSC recall process; maintaining documentation and reporting readiness for regulatory inquiries.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • 10+ years of product safety, regulatory compliance, or quality assurance experience in consumer goods, with at least 5 years focused on food contact materials, cookware, kitchen appliances, or closely adjacent hard-goods categories; demonstrated ownership across the full compliance lifecycle, from concept and supplier qualification through launch and incident response. No junior or generalist profiles.
  • Deep, working knowledge of food contact material regulations including FDA 21 CFR, LFGB (Chapters 30/31), EU Framework Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, REACH, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, FSC, NSF, and the Colorado PFAS Chemicals Consumer Protection Act; familiarity with UK REACH and other international frameworks is a strong plus.
  • Background in chemistry, materials science, or applied laboratory and clinical research, with direct experience designing and running studies used to substantiate product safety or performance claims.
  • Demonstrated experience managing third-party lab relationships in Asia (China in particular), including test plan scoping, report interpretation, and navigating discrepancies between lab results and supplier-provided data.
  • Hands-on experience with social compliance and supply chain auditing programs, including BSCI and Sedex/SMETA (2- and 4-pillar); familiarity with material certification schemes (OEKO-TEX Standard 100, FSC, GRS, GOTS); skilled at managing CAPA processes and building supplier performance scorecards.
  • Proven ability to develop and manage product testing strategies, including migration testing, heavy metals (lead, cadmium), PFAS/PFOA screening, sensory evaluation, and applicable electrical safety standards (UL, ETL, IEC 60335) for small appliances.
  • Familiarity with FTC Green Guides and CPSC Section 15(b) reporting obligations, product recall mechanics, and the CPSC Fast Track Recall Program.
  • Ability to build and maintain product component maps and material traceability documentation across a multi-supplier, multi-category portfolio, including Declarations of Compliance, mill certificates, glaze and coating specifications, and batch-level test records.
  • Strong cross-functional communication and risk management skills; able to translate scientific and regulatory findings into clear, prioritized guidance for Product, Marketing, Legal, Sourcing, and Supply Chain, and to present compliance risk and status to senior leadership.
  • Demonstrated experience building compliance programs or functions in an environment with limited existing infrastructure; entrepreneurial by nature, with the ability to prioritize and execute without relying on inherited playbooks.
  • Ability to travel internationally to visit manufacturing partners and labs in Asia, up to 35 to 40% annually; experience working with facilities in China required, with additional familiarity across Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia) a plus.
  • Proficiency in Mandarin (spoken and/or written) is a bonus; at minimum, demonstrated effectiveness working through translation with Mandarin-speaking suppliers, factories, and lab contacts.
  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Food Science, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field, with hands-on laboratory or clinical research experience a strong plus; advanced degree or professional certification (for example RAPS, ISO Lead Auditor) a plus.
  • Experience with small appliance safety standards (UL 60335-1, IEC 60335-2 series, ETL) preferred; experience managing certification processes with Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratories (NRTLs) a plus.
  • Familiarity with retailer compliance and vendor onboarding requirements (Target, Crate & Barrel, Bloomingdale's, Costco, Amazon) and the documentation standards they require from suppliers.

Please note that the duties and responsibilities outlined in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employees assigned to this position. It is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required for the role. Additional tasks and responsibilities may be assigned as needed to meet business needs.

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $140,000 to $160,000. Final compensation will depend on a variety of factors determining base pay at offer, including but not limited to skills, qualifications, and experience. This range provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within the role.

Who We Are

Caraway is a home goods brand on a mission to craft well-designed, non-toxic essentials that thoughtfully raise the standards of what you cook with. We're passionate about creating elevated products, made without forever chemicals, that are better for you, your family, and the planet. We prioritize a holistic approach to the creation of Caraway products. We partner with ethical manufacturers where their employees are safe, paid fairly, given benefits, and work regulated hours. Our eco-friendly manufacturing process emits less CO2 than traditional non-stick coatings, and we use sustainable packaging practices and ship in packaging made from recycled materials. We pride ourselves on continuously striving to do and be better, for you and the planet, in every step of the process.

Since launching in November 2019, we've become one of the fastest growing digitally native brands of the last decade and are now sold in retailers including Target, Bloomingdale's, Crate & Barrel, The Container Store, Costco, Zola, and many more.

We've amassed over 200,000+ five-star reviews from more than 2.5M+ happy customers and thousands of press hits from the likes of Vogue, Domino, Good Housekeeping, Food & Wine, Architectural Digest, PureWow, Fortune, and CNN.

Caraway is a fully remote company filled with motivated and hardworking innovators and doers. We're continually developing programs to support our distributed team to ensure a successful remote experience. If you're looking to join a brand that folks love, read on and apply!

Life at Caraway

Team: You will be joining a passionate and collaborative fully remote crew that prides itself on high-quality work, supporting one another, sharing our successes, and building a brand we truly love, together.

Culture: At Caraway, we value continuous learning and career growth. We strive to continually optimize our processes, ensuring that we're thoughtful in everything we do, both internally and externally. We listen to our employees, celebrate our wins, and constantly look for ways to be better for our crew, and the world.

Workplace: Being a fully remote company, we have no headquarters and are truly distributed across the US and internationally. Our leadership team sits in the US. We offer a monthly stipend towards co-working space should folks need to switch up their working environment every now and then.

Benefits: We value you and your family. With this in mind, full-time eligible employees are provided:

  • Equity: We believe in our product and that the sky's the limit for where our business is going. You are an asset to Caraway's success, and we think you should be rewarded for it.
  • 401k: A 3% company match to help you plan for your future.
  • Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage options with generous employer contributions, plus access to FSA/HSA/Dependent Care FSAs.
  • Parental Leave: Up to 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, depending on tenure, and access to additional fertility care services via KindBody.
  • A Setup That Works for You: From MacBook to PC, we've got you covered. Let us know what you prefer and we'll get your at-home setup stocked.
  • Elevate Your Workspace: Annual reimbursements for you to elevate your workspace, from standing desks to desktop succulents.
  • Fully Remote: Need to pick up the kids? No problem. Have a doctor's appointment? Enjoy. Flexibility when you need it most.
  • Coworking Reimbursement: Need a break from the home setting? Monthly reimbursements for you to get out of the house and work from anywhere, from day passes to monthly memberships.
  • Events and Swag: Connection is top of mind, even in our completely remote environment. We have monthly virtual events, company-wide offsites, and plenty of new Caraway swag.
  • Leveling Up with Caraway: In addition to exciting opportunities and exposure in your day-to-day work, we offer annual reimbursements to full-time employees to support their professional development.
  • #AwayFromCaraway: We believe healthy, happy humans do better work. We offer unlimited PTO in addition to our 11+ paid annual holidays and quarterly wellness days.
  • Wellness Reimbursement: Monthly reimbursements for you to stay well, from meal services to gym memberships to monthly massages.
  • Employee Discount: We provide an employee discount on all Caraway Home products so you can continue to level up your kitchen and home life, too.
  • Home Upgrade(s): Complimentary product as a new hire, plus continuous opportunities to expand your Caraway Home collection.

Caraway is an Equal Opportunity & Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

title: Volunteer Projects Assistant
description:
Partnerships for Parks (PfP) is a public-private partnership of NYC Parks and City Parks Foundation (CPF) that supports and champions a diverse network of partners caring and advocating for neighborhood parks and green spaces. We equip people, organizations, and government with resources and opportunities to ensure these spaces are dynamic community assets.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support and lead citywide It’s My Park (IMP) volunteer projects, in collaboration with other PfP staff and under the direction of the Corporate Program Manager
  • Provide motivation, supervision, and hands-on guidance to volunteers in an outdoor environment at beautification projects, including clean-ups, horticulture, and painting
  • Liaise with NYC Parks Maintenance & Operations and PfP staff to ensure supply deliveries and returns
  • Manage supply inventory for borough storehouses, including organizing and compiling tool orders and conduct site visits
  • Support special events, workshops, and other PfP initiatives as needed
  • Follow best safety practices for leading volunteers, as determined by PfP

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

  • High school graduation or equivalent and three years of experience in community work, volunteer management, or stewardship efforts related to duties described above

PREFERRED SKILLS/QUALIFICATIONS

  • Excellent organizational and customer service skills
  • Reliable and able to work a flexible schedule (early morning events and possibly a few weekends)
  • Ability to work outdoors in all weather and carry supplies within a park
  • Experience working with volunteers, especially in parks or gardens and/or environmental education
  • Ability to work effectively within a team, and independently, and with diverse constituencies
  • College degree and related community experience as described above
  • Computer literacy, especially in Google Suite

ABOUT CITY PARKS FOUNDATION

At City Parks Foundation (CPF), we are dedicated to invigorating and transforming New York City parks into dynamic, vibrant centers of urban life through arts, environmental education, sports, and community building programs for all New Yorkers. Our ethos is simple: we believe thriving parks mean thriving communities.

Community engagement includes Partnerships for Parks, a public-private program of City Parks Foundation and NYC Parks, which supports and champions a growing network of community leaders who care and advocate for the transformation of our neighborhood parks and the Parks and Open Space Partners-NYC coalition of conservancies and alliances. We also administer the NYC Green Fund, a regranting program for parks and open space nonprofits and grassroots organizations.

We produce SummerStage, the iconic free, outdoor performing arts festival in NYC, presenting world-class artists from across the globe and our own neighborhoods on our mainstage in Central Park and in local parks in all five boroughs, and our Swedish Cottage Marionette Theatre and roving PuppetMobile present marionette puppet theater throughout New York City.

We connect youngsters to nature in the urban environment through progressive, experiential teaching. Using parks as classrooms, we provide learning experiences and hands-on activities in urban forests, coastal areas, and gardens.

Free golf, tennis, track & field, soccer, and fitness programs bring high-quality instruction and equipment into areas where few organized athletic opportunities exist. We offer leveled training, year-round scholarship coaching, and special pro events.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. City Parks Foundation does not offer visa sponsorship.

title: Head of Product Operations
description:
About Digital Green

Digital Green is a global non-profit that has spent nearly two decades helping smallholder farmers build more prosperous, resilient livelihoods—reaching over 10 million farmers to date. Our flagship product, FarmerChat, is a multilingual AI-powered advisory platform that gives farmers timely, locally relevant guidance—from climate-resilient practices to pest management, input use, and market access—in the language and format that works for them. Today FarmerChat reaches farmers across India, Kenya, Ethiopia, Nigeria, and Brazil, with millions of questions asked and answered in over 15 local languages. We combine deep, on-the-ground agricultural extension experience with modern AI to meet farmers where they are, and help them make better decisions, faster.

About the Role

We are looking for a senior Product Operations leader to build and run the operating system that keeps FarmerChat product work moving from early ideas through development, beta, production, and learning.

This role sits at the center of a fast-moving Product organization. You will create clarity across priorities, decisions, stakeholders, dependencies, and timelines; make sure the right people are involved at the right moments; and help Product and Engineering leaders turn decisions into coordinated execution.

You will not own the product vision or make product decisions on behalf of Product leaders. You will own the process that helps those decisions happen with the right information, clear accountability, and strong follow-through.

You will work particularly closely with Product and Engineering leadership, helping establish clear handoffs and shared ways of working as initiatives move from product definition into technical delivery. You will also serve as a key stakeholder partner for the Product organization, building trusted relationships across functions and leadership teams, creating clear channels for input and feedback, and helping ensure Product decisions are well understood across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Run Product Operations

  • Build and maintain clear, lightweight ways of working across Product, Engineering, Tech/AI, Design, Research, Growth, and other teams.
  • Run the core operating cadence, including planning, stage reviews, decision forums, and cross-functional meetings.
  • Maintain a reliable source of truth for priorities, roadmap status, key decisions, risks, dependencies, and open questions.
  • Track progress proactively, surface blockers early, and ensure decisions and follow-ups move to closure.
  • Improve ways of working over time, introducing enough structure to create clarity and predictability without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.

Bring the Right Inputs into Product Decisions

  • Coordinate the process for bringing together signals from Product, Research, Growth and Data, Design, Country Teams, Strategy, Legal, and other relevant functions.
  • Ensure the right stakeholder perspectives are brought into the process at the appropriate points.
  • Prepare clear, decision-ready materials that synthesize inputs, trade-offs, evidence, and open questions for Product leadership.
  • Make priorities, assumptions, and decision rationale visible and understandable across the organization.

Coordinate the Product Lifecycle

  • Help move work from early signals and prototypes through product definition, engineering, beta, and production.
  • Coordinate required stakeholder input and review at the appropriate stages, ensuring decisions, risks, dependencies, and open questions are clear before work advances.
  • Ensure product requirements, design, success measures, dependencies, and risks are sufficiently clear before work enters Engineering.
  • Establish clear handoffs and ways of working with Engineering as initiatives move from product definition into build, testing, beta, and release.
  • Work closely with the Engineering delivery counterpart to maintain a shared view of scope, readiness, dependencies, timelines, and unresolved issues.
  • Track feedback and decisions so teams understand what was included, deferred, or changed and why.
  • Coordinate beta and production-readiness processes and ensure learning feeds back into future product work.

Strengthen Stakeholder Alignment and Communication

  • Build trusted relationships with leaders and key stakeholder groups across the organization so Product can work effectively across functions and surface issues early.
  • Create a predictable rhythm of clear product updates for leadership and the broader organization.
  • Translate complex Product and Engineering work into language that different teams can understand and act on.
  • Ensure key decisions, changes, and trade-offs are communicated clearly, and close the loop with stakeholders after important decisions.
  • Reduce the amount of time teams spend reconstructing past decisions, chasing information, or working from different versions of the truth.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in Product Operations, product/program management, product delivery, Chief of Staff, or a comparable operating role in a technology environment.
  • Strong experience working with senior Product and Engineering leaders.
  • Demonstrated ability to build practical processes and improve ways of working in fast-changing organizations.
  • Strong judgment about when structure is useful and when it becomes unnecessary process.
  • Excellent stakeholder-management and facilitation skills, with the ability to move work forward through influence rather than formal authority.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and the ability to synthesize complex information clearly.
  • Strong ownership, organization, and follow-through.
  • Familiarity with product roadmaps, OKRs, user research, experimentation, and modern Product/Engineering workflows.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in AI/ML, data-intensive, or rapidly scaling digital products.
  • Experience working across multiple countries, cultures, or operating environments.
  • Exposure to agriculture, global development, or products designed for underserved users.

What Success Looks Like

  • Product work moves through a clear and predictable process without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
  • Decision ownership is clear and decisions are documented and followed through.
  • Stakeholders are engaged at the right points rather than late in the process.
  • Product and Engineering have clear handoffs, shared visibility into readiness, and a consistent understanding of dependencies and risks.
  • The wider organization has a clear view of what Product is working on, what has changed, and why.
  • Product requirements, design, and key decisions are sufficiently resolved before major Engineering work begins.
  • The CPO and Product leaders spend less time coordinating, chasing follow-ups, and reconstructing decisions and more time on product and strategy.

title: Planner – Air Quality
description:
About Houston-Galveston Area Council

The Houston-Galveston Area Council (H-GAC) is one of the largest regional planning commissions in the country, serving a diverse 13-county region with more than 7 million people. We are the pulse of our region, addressing issues that cross city limits and county lines every day.
We make decisions that affect our transportation system, support the safety and well-being of our residents, connect people to jobs, help communities recover from natural disasters, protect water quality, and much more. We work to make the Houston-Galveston region a great place to live, work, and thrive.


What Will I Be Doing?

H-GAC is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Air Quality Planner to join the Air Quality Team within the Metropolitan Planning & Analysis Division. This position is ideal for a professional interested in environmental policy, sustainability, transportation planning, regional air quality management, and climate action.

Under the direction of the Air Quality Program Manager, the Air Quality Planner will support the development and implementation of regional air quality and climate initiatives designed to reduce emissions and improve air quality throughout the Houston-Galveston region.

The position will contribute to H-GAC’s air quality planning activities, including the development and implementation of regional air quality plans, including the Clean Air Action Plan, emissions reduction strategies, clean transportation planning including zero-emission vehicle initiatives, data analysis, program evaluation, stakeholder engagement, and regional coordination.

The Air Quality Planner will work collaboratively with local governments, transportation agencies, state and federal partners, community organizations, businesses, universities, and other regional stakeholders to advance practical strategies that improve air quality and support a healthier, more sustainable region.


Key Qualifications
  • Knowledge of regional air quality, climate, sustainability, transportation, or environmental planning.
  • Familiarity with air quality improvement strategies, emissions reduction approaches, and climate action planning.
  • Understanding of federal, state, and local air quality regulations and policy frameworks.
  • Experience working with emissions inventories, air quality monitoring data, greenhouse gas data, or related environmental datasets.
  • Experience with GIS, data visualization, dashboards, or other analytical tools.
  • Knowledge of zero-emission vehicles, clean transportation strategies, and transportation electrification.
  • Experience supporting grant-funded programs, including grant administration, reporting, or compliance.
  • Experience coordinating projects involving multiple agencies, jurisdictions, or stakeholder groups.
  • Experience with community outreach, stakeholder engagement, environmental education, or public communications.
  • Experience working with local governments, metropolitan planning organizations, councils of governments, or other regional planning organizations.

What You’ll Gain
  • The opportunity to work on regional air quality and climate initiatives affecting more than 7 million residents.
  • Hands-on experience supporting implementation of air quality planning activities, including the Clean Air Action Plan and regional emissions reduction strategies.
  • Exposure to air quality data analysis, emissions inventories, transportation planning, and environmental policy.
  • Opportunities to work directly with local governments, transportation agencies, community organizations, businesses, universities, and other regional partners.
  • Experience developing and tracking projects, performance measures, and implementation strategies.
  • Opportunities to represent H-GAC at regional and professional meetings, conferences, and stakeholder events.
  • Professional development and mentorship from experienced planners, policy analysts, and environmental professionals.

Do you have...
  • Bachelor’s degree in an applicable academic discipline or related field of study
  • Three (3) years of experience working with local government, nonprofit programs, school or in job related duties

Salary Range: $65,000.00 to 75,000.00

All employees of H-GAC are required to reside within the agency’s region of service to support our commitment to excellence in service of our region.

H-GAC is an equal opportunity/ADA employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, or protected veteran status.

title: Houseman
description:
Houseman- The Westin Michigan Avenue


The Westin Michigan Avenue is looking for a Houseman to join the team!

Vinayaka Hospitality was founded in 2008 on a foundation of innovation, intelligence, and compassion. Our team takes pride in combining a passion for hospitality with practical hotel management. By collaborating with renowned brands like Hilton, Marriott, and Hyatt, we efficiently manage 11 properties across diverse locations. Committed to ongoing growth, we actively seek opportunities and are dedicated to helping both our team and hotels thrive. We remain responsive and proactive in our strategies for sales, marketing, and revenue, ensuring swift adaptability to market changes. Beyond Management, we cultivate strong partnerships with major industry players, showcasing our dedication to success in the ever-evolving world of hospitality

Join the team at The Westin Michigan Avenue Chicago — a landmark downtown hotel where elevated comfort meets iconic luxury. At The Westin, you’ll be part of a culture that champions well-being, innovation and extraordinary experiences for both guests and associates. Nestled on Chicago’s Magnificent Mile, you’ll work in a dynamic setting offering inspiring views, modern amenities and a commitment to “doing well, and doing good.” If you’re passionate about hospitality and ready to elevate your career in a role where your purpose matters, let’s create unforgettable moments together.

Job Summary

The Houseperson supports the housekeeping team by maintaining cleanliness and organization throughout the facility. This role is responsible for ensuring that common areas, hallways, restrooms, and designated workspaces remain clean, safe, and well-stocked. The Houseman assists with cleaning tasks, responding to housekeeping needs, transporting linens, and supporting special projects as assigned.

Physical Demands

  • Ability to push and pull housekeeping carts and equipment.
  • Occasional climbing of ladders or step stools.
  • Ability to be on feet for extended periods.

title: Technical Analyst
description:
Job Title: Technical Analyst
Company: Celerity
Location: U.S. (Remote/ work from home eligible) Travel as Required
Industry: Utilities Consulting / Digital Transformation / FSM Implementations
Experience Required: 7+ Years
Company Overview: Celerity is a consulting firm specializing in utilities and energy sectors. We empower organizations by converting complex data into actionable intelligence to mitigate risk, optimize assets, and maximize project outcomes. Our background and expertise enable us to drive and deliver transformation and operational excellence for our clients.
Position Overview: We are seeking an experienced Technical Analyst to support the delivery of a complex Field Service Management (FSM) platform implementation for a utilities client. This role bridges business requirements and technical execution — translating functional needs into technical specifications, supporting solution configuration, and ensuring the platform is implemented correctly, tested thoroughly, and delivered successfully. The ideal candidate will bring strong analytical and technical skills, hands-on FSM platform experience, implementation project experience, and the ability to collaborate effectively across a cross-functional delivery team including the Technical Project Manager, Solution Architect, Product Developers, and Product Solution Architects.
Key Responsibilities:
Requirements & Technical Analysis:
  • Analyze and document detailed technical and functional requirements for the FSM platform implementation, working closely with business stakeholders and the Solution Architect.
  • Translate business requirements into technical specifications, configuration workbooks, user stories, and functional design documents.
  • Conduct gap analysis between out-of-the-box FSM platform capabilities and client-specific business requirements.
  • Support development of solution design documents, data mapping specifications, and integration requirements.
Solution Configuration & Implementation Support:
  • Support configuration of the FSM platform (e.g., scheduling rules, work order types, service territories, mobile workflows, dispatch logic) based on approved designs.
  • Partner with Product Developers and Product Solution Architects to validate that technical builds align with documented requirements and architecture standards.
  • Assist in designing and validating system integrations with adjacent platforms (GIS, OMS, ERP, CRM, IoT/telemetry).
  • Support data migration activities including data mapping, cleansing, validation, and reconciliation.
Testing & Quality Assurance:
  • Develop test plans, test cases, and test scripts to validate FSM platform functionality against business requirements.
  • Lead or support System Integration Testing (SIT), User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and regression testing cycles.
  • Log, track, and manage defects through resolution, working with Product Developers to prioritize and validate fixes.
  • Ensure traceability between requirements, configuration/build, and test coverage.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Work closely with the Technical Project Manager to provide status updates, flag risks/issues, and support project planning and reporting.
  • Collaborate with the Solution Architect and Product Solution Architects to ensure technical solutions align with overall architecture and scalability requirements.
  • Partner with Product Developers to clarify requirements, review technical builds, and troubleshoot implementation issues.
  • Support business analysts and end users during design workshops, walkthroughs, and training sessions as needed.
Documentation & Knowledge Transfer
  • Maintain up-to-date technical documentation, configuration guides, and runbooks throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Support development of training materials and knowledge transfer documentation for client teams.
  • Contribute to lessons-learned sessions and continuous improvement of implementation methodology and reusable assets.
Deployment & Hypercare Support
  • Support cutover planning, deployment activities, and go-live readiness assessments.
  • Provide hypercare support post go-live, triaging and resolving technical issues in collaboration with the delivery team.
Educational Qualifications:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field or equivalent experience.
  • Advanced degree (MBA or Master’s) is preferred.
Required Skills and Experience:
  • 7+ years of experience in a Technical Analyst, Systems Analyst, or similar technical delivery role within enterprise software implementations.
  • Hands-on experience implementing or supporting Field Service Management (FSM) or workforce management platforms (e.g., Salesforce Field Service, ServiceMax, IFS Field Service Management, Oracle Field Service Cloud, ClickSoftware).
  • Experience within the utilities industry (electric, gas, water) is strongly preferred, particularly with field operations, mobile workforce, or asset management systems.
  • Proven experience working on full implementation lifecycles: requirements gathering, design, configuration/build, testing, deployment, and hypercare.
  • Experience working in a consulting or systems integrator environment supporting client-facing delivery engagements.
  • Strong technical analysis and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex business needs into technical solutions.
  • Solid understanding of system integration concepts (APIs, middleware, data mapping/ETL) relevant to utilities technology ecosystems.
  • Working knowledge of relational databases and SQL for data analysis, validation, and troubleshooting.
  • Familiarity with Agile and traditional project delivery methodologies (Scrum, SAFe, Waterfall).
  • Experience with requirements management and defect tracking tools (Jira, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, or similar).
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and business stakeholders.
  • Detail-oriented with strong documentation discipline and testing rigor.
  • Ability to travel to client site (domestic and(or) international) as required and defined per project requirements.
Certifications:
  • Relevant FSM platform certifications (e.g., Salesforce Field Service Consultant/Administrator, ServiceMax certification).
  • Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP) or similar business/technical analysis certification.
  • Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) or Agile certification.
  • ITIL Foundation certification (a plus, given field service and incident/change management overlap).

The salary range for this position is provided in good faith and is subject to variation based on geographic location, candidate experience, and market conditions. Final compensation will be determined after a comprehensive evaluation of the candidate’s qualifications and alignment with the role.

In accordance with applicable pay transparency laws—including but not limited to those in California, Colorado, New York, Washington, and other jurisdictions—we disclose salary ranges to promote equity and transparency. Where required by law, compensation and benefits information will be included in job postings or made available upon request.

title: President (RH-ISAC)
description:
President

Retail & Hospitality Information Sharing and Analysis Center (RH-ISAC)

Remote | Full-Time, Exempt

The Opportunity

The Retail & Hospitality Information Sharing and Analysis Center (RH-ISAC) seeks a strategic, relationship-driven President to lead the organization into its next chapter of growth and impact.

RH-ISAC is the trusted cybersecurity community for retail, hospitality, and other consumer-facing organizations. Its members include leading retailers, restaurants, hotels, gaming organizations, travel companies, food retailers, and consumer products companies. RH-ISAC connects information security teams at the strategic, operational, and tactical levels to exchange intelligence, address emerging threats, share leading practices, and build stronger, more resilient organizations.

The next President will inherit a highly respected organization, an engaged member community, a talented team, and a collaborative, high-trust culture. Reporting to the Board of Directors, this executive will build upon RH-ISAC’s strong foundation while bringing strategic vision, innovation, operational discipline, and a willingness to take thoughtful, calculated risks.

Key opportunities include expanding membership and international reach, strengthening member engagement and value, advancing RH-ISAC’s intelligence-sharing capabilities, and helping the organization and its members navigate the increasing impact of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy, Growth, and Member Value

  • Partner with the Board and leadership team to establish and execute RH-ISAC’s strategic direction and three-year roadmap.
  • Drive sustainable membership growth, engagement, retention, and international expansion.
  • Advance the organization’s intelligence-sharing capabilities, educational offerings, research, communications, and brand visibility.
  • Anticipate emerging cybersecurity and technology trends and translate them into relevant strategies and services.
  • Serve as a visible, accessible, and credible ambassador for RH-ISAC and its mission.

Board, Team, and Culture Leadership

  • Build a transparent, productive, and trusted relationship with the Board of Directors.
  • Keep the Board informed of organizational performance, strategic progress, finances, risks, and opportunities.
  • Lead and develop a talented team while preserving RH-ISAC’s collaborative, high-accountability, and high-trust culture.
  • Establish clear priorities, expectations, and performance measures while empowering staff to lead within their areas of expertise.
  • Model humility, authenticity, transparency, sound judgment, and respect.

Financial and Organizational Stewardship

  • Ensure RH-ISAC’s long-term financial strength, operational effectiveness, and regulatory compliance.
  • Oversee the annual budget, financial reporting, organizational policies, talent practices, and succession planning.
  • Align staffing, resources, and investments with the organization’s strategic priorities.
  • Cultivate productive relationships with government agencies, industry leaders, trade associations, service providers, and other strategic partners.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be an accomplished executive who combines strategic vision with strong operational leadership and a genuine passion for serving members. This individual will understand that RH-ISAC’s success is built on trust and will take time to listen, learn, and understand the organization before implementing significant change.

Competitive candidates will bring:

  • Senior leadership experience within a membership association, non-profit, cybersecurity or technology organization, professional network, or similarly complex environment.
  • A record of driving membership growth, business development, revenue diversification, partnerships, or market expansion.
  • Experience developing and executing strategic plans that produced measurable results.
  • Demonstrated success leading and developing high-performing teams.
  • Experience working effectively with a governing Board.
  • Strong financial, operational, and organizational management capabilities.
  • Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Experience engaging members, clients, partners, vendors, government agencies, and other influential stakeholders.
  • Cybersecurity, information security, intelligence-sharing, or related industry experience is highly desirable.
  • International growth or global market experience is a plus.

Leadership Profile

RH-ISAC seeks a leader who is:

  • Strategic, innovative, and forward-looking.
  • Authentic, transparent, and grounded in integrity.
  • An attentive listener who builds credibility and trust.
  • Collaborative while remaining decisive and accountable.
  • Comfortable balancing executive leadership with hands-on engagement.
  • Adaptable and effective in a fast-moving, matrixed environment.
  • Passionate about member service and RH-ISAC’s mission.

First-Year Priorities

During the first year, the President will be expected to:

  • Establish trusted relationships with staff, the leadership team, Board members, key member organizations, and strategic partners.
  • Develop a deep understanding of RH-ISAC’s culture, operations, membership, and strategic priorities.
  • Maintain strong staff engagement and retention through the leadership transition.
  • Demonstrate meaningful progress against the strategic roadmap.
  • Strengthen member engagement, value delivery, and organizational visibility.
  • Assess opportunities for sustainable growth, international expansion, and innovation.
  • Success will be reflected in an engaged staff, increased member value and participation, measurable strategic progress, and continued confidence from the Board and membership.

Location, Compensation, and Benefits

This is a remote position requiring regular virtual collaboration across multiple time zones and occasional travel for Board meetings, member events, conferences, staff gatherings, and strategic partnerships.

The anticipated salary range is $250,000-$350,000k annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

RH-ISAC offers medical, dental, and vision insurance; FSA and HSA options; short-term disability coverage; and a 401(k) plan with an employer matching contribution.

To Apply

RH-ISAC is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

RH-ISAC has retained OneDigital Executive Search to lead this national search on the organization’s behalf, including reviewing applications, assessing qualifications, and presenting qualified candidates for consideration.

To fully realize our goal, we prioritize our understanding of the complexities of DEI within our workforce to inform our approach to talent management. We believe that this guides how we do our work, advise our clients to operationalize DEI and position our content and educational opportunities help strengthen the talent management capacity of the social impact sector.

title: Data Analyst
description:
Data Ideology
At DI, we provide Data & Analytics expertise to drive measurable business outcomes, often solving complex business problems for our clients. Our data analytics advisory services enable our customers to transform data into insights by driving a culture of empowerment and ownership of results. Our team consists of highly motivated individuals passionate about learning, understanding, collaborating, and intellectually curious. For more information about Data Ideology, visit

Data Analyst– Contract

title: Senior Programmer (Artificial Intelligence Support)
description:
Requisition ID

2026-4632

Job Summary

We are seeking a Senior Programmer – Artificial Intelligence Support to join our team supporting the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Testosterone Screening and Treatment Expansion Program. In this role, you will design, develop, and maintain AI-informed web-based and client-server applications that support clinical screening and treatment workflows across VA healthcare systems. Your work will directly contribute to expanding access to evidence-based testosterone screening and treatment for Veterans nationwide. The ideal candidate is a technically versatile and proactive developer who thrives in complex federal healthcare environments, is comfortable bridging the gap between clinical end users and technical teams, and brings a disciplined, methodology-driven approach to software development and system integration.

Primary Responsibilities

Design, develop, modify, test, and implement web-based applications, client-server applications, and OS-level automation scripts in support of VA clinical program workflows related to testosterone screening and treatment expansion. Integrate and implement Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) software solutions into existing VA IT architecture, ensuring compatibility, security compliance, and alignment with VA enterprise standards. Develop and maintain SQL queries, stored procedures, and data models within Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS) to support application functionality, reporting, and clinical data analysis. Collaborate closely with clinical users, program stakeholders, and project managers to define system requirements, write program specifications, and translate business needs into technical solutions using an established Systems Development Methodology (SDM). Document test conditions, create test data sets, execute test plans, and analyze results to validate application performance; coordinate system testing activities and assist clinical end users with User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Research and evaluate emerging technologies and AI-driven approaches relevant to clinical decision support and healthcare data processing; develop and maintain work plans, project documentation, and data and process models throughout the software development lifecycle.

Minimum Qualifications

8+ years of professional experience in software development, including hands-on experience with web-based applications, client-server architecture, and process automation scripting. Bachelor's degree (BA/BS) in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a closely related technical field required. Prior experience supporting federal agency IT programs, preferably within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) or another federal healthcare environment, is strongly desired. Must be able to obtain and maintain a VA network access credential (PIV/CAC) and successfully complete a VA background investigation (MBI or equivalent) prior to onboarding. Must be authorized to work in the United States; this position does not offer visa sponsorship. Demonstrated proficiency in SQL and RDBMS application development, COTS software integration, and use of a formal Systems Development Methodology (SDM) for planning, coding, and deploying enterprise applications.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with VA electronic health record systems, including VistA, CPRS, and/or Cerner/Oracle Health, is strongly preferred. • Familiarity with VA IT security frameworks, including experience navigating the VA's Authority to Operate (ATO) process or completing VA Privacy and Information Security training. • Exposure to AI/ML concepts or tools applied in a clinical or healthcare data context, such as predictive modeling, clinical decision support, or natural language processing of EHR data. • Knowledge of HL7, FHIR, or other healthcare interoperability standards relevant to integrating clinical data systems. • Experience developing data and process models in support of federal health program reporting, analytics, or quality improvement initiatives.

title: Information Technology Associate
description:
Information Technology Associate

The Information Technology Associate provides tier-1 technical support and technology services that enable staff to effectively advance the Center for Health Care Strategies’ (CHCS) mission. This role serves as a primary resource for resolving technology issues, managing IT assets, supporting Microsoft 365 and business applications, maintaining documentation, and assisting with technology initiatives across the organization.

This position is ideal for an early-career IT professional who enjoys problem solving, helping others, learning new technologies, and contributing to a mission-driven collaborative organization. For the initial month of employment, the incumbent will be required to report to the office on a daily-basis, Monday through Friday, for training purposes. Thereafter, the incumbent will be required to be onsite three days/week, with the ability to work remotely the other two days.

Technical Support

  • Tier 1 Support - Provide tier 1 technical support to users via Zoom, email, and in-person for hardware, software, and technology-related issues. Deliver timely, professional, and customer-focused support while maintaining a positive user experience.
  • Software Troubleshooting - Diagnose and resolve software issues across Windows 11, Microsoft 365 applications, SharePoint, Zoom, Salesforce, iOS, Android and other approved business applications. Perform basic account administration and user support as needed.
  • Hardware Support - Address hardware issues involving laptops, monitors, printers, docking stations, and other computer accessories. Perform setup, troubleshooting, upgrades, replacements, and basic maintenance.
  • Support Tracking - Document all support requests, resolutions, and recurring issues in the IT support system. Monitor trends and recommend improvements to enhance service delivery and user satisfaction.
  • User Training & Technology Adoption – Support staff in adopting technology by providing training, troubleshooting assistance, best-practice guidance, and maintaining user-facing instructional materials.

Asset Management

  • Asset Tracking - Maintain accurate records of IT assets including laptops, monitors, docking stations, and related equipment. Track assignments, inventory levels, and lifecycle replacements.
  • Vendor Coordination - Coordinate repairs, replacements, and maintenance of hardware with external vendors. Assist with obtaining quotes and managing purchasing requests. Maintain positive vendor relationships and ensure timely follow-up on open issues.
  • Shipping - Manage the packing, shipping, receiving, and distribution of computer equipment and technology assets. Serve as primary contact for organizational UPS account administration and related shipping activities.
  • Audio-Visual (AV) Support - Manage, maintain, and support AV technology used in conference rooms, meetings, presentations, events, and external engagements, including displays, webcams, microphones, computers, and related equipment.
  • Onboarding & Offboarding - Assist with employee onboarding and offboarding processes, including equipment assignments, account setup, access management, recovery of assets, and related documentation.

Systems Administration Support

  • Operating Systems & Application Maintenance - Install, configure, update, and maintain Windows 11 operating systems and approved software applications.
  • Network Troubleshooting - Assist with basic network troubleshooting, connectivity issues, printer support, wireless access issues, and related infrastructure troubleshooting.
  • Documentation & Training Resources – Create, maintain, and update IT documentation, system procedures, user guides, quick-reference materials, and training resources to support staff and technology operations.
  • Microsoft 365 & SharePoint Administration - Assist with administration and support of Microsoft 365 services, including user accounts, licensing, groups, SharePoint sites, permissions, document libraries, and troubleshooting.
  • Salesforce Support - Assist with Salesforce administration, interface updates, user support, reporting assistance, and troubleshooting.
  • Policy & Process Support – Assist in the development, maintenance, and communication of IT policies, procedures, standards, and best practices. Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and service quality.


Core Competencies/ Requirements

  • Associate’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. One to three years of experience providing technical support in a professional environment is preferred.
  • Experience supporting Microsoft Windows and Microsoft 365 environments.
  • Familiarity with SharePoint, Salesforce, and cloud-based collaboration tools preferred.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills with ability to research issues, identify root causes, and recommend solutions.
  • Excellent communications skills: ability to write effectively and communicate tactfully both internally and externally.
  • Superior organizational skills, meticulous attention to detail, follow-through and the ability to multi-task and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to adapt to changing technologies and organizational needs.
  • Demonstrated curiosity and commitment to continuous learning.
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively with other team members.
  • Maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information.
  • Ability to exercise a high degree of judgement and prioritize work accordingly in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to interact effectively with internal team members and able to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

Physical Requirements/Working Conditions

CHCS operates a hybrid environment. The employee will perform job duties in a business office or business home office environment. Minimum Internet speed required for home office environment is 25 Mbps download speed and 25 Mbps upload speed. Tasks are generally carried out with no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands. This role requires the ability to operate a computer for extended periods of time with standard office equipment. This role requires the ability to occasionally lift and move technology equipment up to 30 pounds. The position may be required to attend meetings, both on- and off-site, via phone, videoconference or in person. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace and will consider reasonable accommodation to assist qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this job.

Salary and Compensation

At CHCS, our employees are at the heart of everything we do. Our market-competitive offerings include comprehensive benefits and resources to support our employees’ physical, emotional, financial, personal, career, and community wellbeing. These benefits and resources include, but are not limited to:

  • Paid Time Off including Vacation, Holidays, and Sick Time
  • Retirement Plan
  • Medical and Prescription Drug Insurance
  • Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Disability and Life Insurance
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Community and Volunteer Opportunities
  • Employer Assistance Program
  • ….and more!


Salary Range: $58,691 - $82,167. The final salary offer will be determined based on various factors, including the candidate’s relevant experience, specialized skills, and responsibilities. We typically hire new team members at the introductory portion of this range to allow for future growth and progression within the role.


To Apply

Interested candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, and salary requirements to CHCS’ Career Center with. No telephone inquiries please. The cover letter should include the following elements:


  • Why you are interested in the IT Associate position.
  • Any additional professional and/or personal experience that informs your qualifications for the position that otherwise is not obvious from your resume.
  • Your salary requirements for the position.


If you require a reasonable accommodation for a disability to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview, or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please contact CHCS’ Human Resources Team at hr@chcs.org or 609-528-8400 (voice)/711 for TTY.

title: Program Director
description:
Program Director – Behavioral Health

Perimeter Behavioral of the Ozarks | Springdale, Arkansas

Lead the Team. Strengthen the Program. Make an Impact.

Are you a behavioral health leader who enjoys being where the work happens?

Perimeter Behavioral of the Ozarks is seeking an experienced and energetic Program Director to provide leadership to our residential treatment program in Springdale, Arkansas. This is a highly visible, hands-on leadership role for someone who can develop strong teams, create structure and accountability, and help maintain a safe, therapeutic environment for the youth we serve.

As Program Director, you will oversee the day-to-day operations of the therapeutic milieu and provide leadership to our Mental Health Technicians, Mental Health Technician Coordinators, and Program Coordinators. You will work closely with nursing, clinical, case management, activities, and facility leadership to ensure our teams are aligned and our youth receive consistent, high-quality care.

This position is ideal for a leader who can balance people, programming, safety, and operations while remaining actively engaged with staff and youth throughout the facility.

What You'll Do

As Program Director, you will:

  • Provide leadership and oversight for the daily operations of the residential treatment milieu.

  • Lead, coach, mentor, and develop Mental Health Technicians, MHT Coordinators, Program Coordinators, and other assigned staff.

  • Create a culture of accountability, teamwork, professionalism, and therapeutic engagement.

  • Maintain a visible leadership presence on the units and provide real-time coaching, guidance, and problem-solving.

  • Oversee staffing schedules, daily assignments, shift coverage, and required patient-to-staff ratios.

  • Monitor census, patient acuity, staffing needs, and unit activity and make operational adjustments when needed.

  • Partner with nursing, clinical services, case management, activities therapy, and other departments to promote coordinated patient care.

  • Support the development and implementation of structured residential behavioral programming that aligns with individualized treatment goals.

  • Oversee activity programming and special events in collaboration with the Program Coordinator.

  • Participate in recruiting, interviewing, onboarding, training, performance management, and professional development of milieu staff.

  • Review MHT and MHT Coordinator documentation for accuracy, timeliness, quality, and regulatory compliance.

  • Identify performance and documentation trends and develop coaching or corrective action strategies when improvement is needed.

  • Support crisis prevention and intervention by helping staff anticipate escalating behaviors and utilize effective de-escalation strategies.

  • Promote patient rights, employee safety, patient safety, and a trauma-informed treatment environment.

  • Assist with regulatory readiness and compliance with facility policies, state requirements, and accreditation standards.

  • Review program data and operational trends and recommend opportunities to strengthen services and outcomes.

  • Participate in the Administrator-On-Call rotation and serve as a leadership resource when operational, staffing, or patient-care needs arise.

  • Step into unit operations when necessary to support patient safety, staffing ratios, and continuity of services.

What We're Looking For

We are looking for a leader who is comfortable leading from the floor—not just from an office.

The successful candidate will be able to build relationships with frontline staff while maintaining clear expectations and accountability. You should be comfortable making decisions in a fast-paced behavioral health environment, responding to changing priorities, coaching staff in real time, and collaborating across departments.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Must be at least 21 years of age.

  • Bachelor's degree in a human services-related field required.

  • Minimum of two years of supervisory experience in a medical or behavioral health setting.

  • Valid driver's license.

  • Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and respond effectively to changing operational needs.

  • Ability to work collaboratively with clinical, nursing, administrative, and direct-care teams.

  • Flexibility in scheduling based on facility and program needs.

Preferred Experience

Candidates with experience in one or more of the following areas are strongly encouraged to apply:

  • Residential behavioral health

  • Psychiatric residential treatment

  • Child and adolescent behavioral health

  • Therapeutic milieu management

  • Mental Health Technician or direct-care leadership

  • Staff development and performance management

  • Trauma-informed care

  • Crisis prevention and de-escalation

  • Behavioral health regulatory or accreditation compliance

Why This Role Matters

Our Mental Health Technicians and frontline teams spend more time with our youth than almost anyone else in the organization. The leadership, structure, coaching, and support they receive directly influence the quality of the treatment environment.

The Program Director plays a critical role in ensuring staff have clear expectations, youth experience consistency and structure, therapeutic programming remains meaningful, and departments work together toward common treatment goals.

We aren't simply looking for someone to manage schedules.

We're looking for someone who can develop people, strengthen programming, build a healthy team culture, and help create an environment where both our youth and our staff can succeed.

About Perimeter Behavioral of the Ozarks

Perimeter Behavioral of the Ozarks provides residential behavioral health treatment to youth who need a structured and supportive environment to address complex emotional and behavioral needs.

Our multidisciplinary teams work together to provide compassionate, individualized care while helping youth build the skills they need to achieve greater stability and successfully transition to their next level of care.

If you are ready to bring your leadership experience to a role where you can see the impact of your work every day, we would love to hear from you.

Apply today and help us continue building a strong team and a therapeutic environment where meaningful change can happen.

Perimeter Healthcare is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace for all employees.
