title: Superintendent
description:
Superintendent

Job Summary
The Superintendent role is an integral part of the executive team, ensuring that KIPP DC's academic and school performance strategy translates from vision to results across all 22 schools through systems-level leadership, rigorous accountability, and trusted relationships with school communities. The starting salary range for this role is $244,025-$269,712.This is a full-time, fully in-person role based at our KIPP DC’s headquarters office with an immediate start date.


About KIPP DC

For 25 years, KIPP DC has partnered with students, families, and the community to create joyful, academically excellent schools across the nation’s capital. Today, our network of 22 schools educate more than 7,500 students in grades PreK3-12, supported by 1,500 dedicated teachers, leaders, and staff.

Our work is grounded in five pillars–Academic Excellence, Joy & Sense of Belonging, Highly Effective Teachers and Leaders, Safe, Structured, and Nurturing Learning Environments, and Commitment to College Readiness–which ensure every student is equipped with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to pursue success in college, careers, and beyond. Our schools combine high expectations with joyful, affirming environments that nurture academic success and personal growth for students and staff alike.

As part of the national KIPP network, we share best practices and innovations while maintaining deep roots in Washington, D.C. Together, we strive toward a future without limits for our students, alumni, and community.


About the Team

The executive team is KIPP DC's senior leadership body, composed of the school system's functional leaders who drive strategic direction, operational performance, and organizational health.

The Superintendent sits on the executive team as a cabinet-level peer to the President & Chief Operating Officer and the Head of Strategy, Impact, and Transformation, providing systems-level leadership for academic and school performance across all 22 schools. This work — instructional strategy, school leadership, and everything that shapes what students learn and experience — is carried out through the teams of the Chief Academic Officer and the Chief of Schools, both of whom report to the Superintendent. The Superintendent is responsible for system-level coherence, prioritization, and cross-functional alignment across both teams.


About the Role

The Superintendent serves as KIPP DC's senior executive accountable for the coherence of academic strategy and school leadership across all 22 schools. This is a rare opportunity for a systems-level leader to guide a school system with 25 years of legacy and impact through a consequential academic transformation, with a focus on preparing all students to pursue the paths they choose — college, career, and beyond.


Location and Type of Work

Fully on-site (5 days per week onsite)

As a headquarters team that is focused on being responsive to our schools and meeting the needs of our students and families, we approach our work in a way that reflects these priorities. Schools operate in person and our students and families rely on us for in-person support which requires this position to be fully on-site. This role is currently required to be on-site or in schools during regular work hours.



Responsibilities
The percentages for each key responsibility are estimates, and other duties may be assigned. Flexibility and responsiveness are encouraged to accommodate organizational needs.

Lead academic and school performance transformation (35%)

  • Shape the school system's academic vision for students within the direction set by the multiyear strategic plan, leading the integration of academic strategy and school leadership into a single, coherent academic and school performance strategy.
  • Monitor academic and school performance across all 22 schools on a regular cadence, using that visibility to inform enterprise-level decisions and priorities.
  • Hold academic and school-level work coherent with the school system's broader strategic commitments, surfacing risks and bringing timely, clear-eyed recommendations to the CEO before they compound.
  • Push the school system to innovate where innovation is needed to deliver on its commitments to students, bringing new academic and school-level approaches into the strategy where they are warranted.
  • Serve as a cabinet-level peer to the President & Chief Operating Officer (COO) and the Head of Strategy, Impact, and Transformation, participating fully in shared enterprise work on behalf of the school system's academic and school performance.
  • Partner with executive leaders across the school system, understanding how their work affects academic and school performance and elevating what students and schools need from them, so the academic and school performance strategy is properly resourced and represented.
Lead and develop portfolio leaders (25%)
  • Set clear expectations for the Chief Academic Officer (CAO) and Chief of Schools (COS), and hold each accountable for leading their team’s day-to-day work and the outcomes their team produces.
  • Ensure the CAO and COS each operate at the right altitude: each manages their own portfolio with appropriate independence, while the Superintendent maintains the cross-functional coordination and enterprise orientation the transformation requires.
  • Lead and coach the CAO and COS, sharpening their systems-level leadership and building the capacity each needs to translate the academic and school performance strategy into excellent execution as the school system's transformation deepens.
  • Ensure the CAO and COS each build a strong talent bench within their own portfolio. Provide additional support when capability gaps require enterprise-level structural adjustment across the academics and schools portfolio.
Ensure internal and external accountability for academic excellence (25%)
  • Hold the school system accountable for delivering on its academic and school performance commitments to students, naming gaps directly and ensuring they are addressed, while identifying and scaling what is genuinely driving strong outcomes.
  • Oversee the school system's progress toward the academic and school-level standards required for charter renewal and regulatory compliance, including under applicable school performance frameworks. Hold the CAO and COS accountable for the strategies that meet or exceed those standards.
  • Serve as the primary liaison to the board's School & Community Affairs committee, giving the committee the information and access it needs to fulfill its oversight of academic and school performance.
  • Serve as the school system's point of decision and escalation for academic and school-level matters requiring enterprise-level resolution, ensuring the school system responds with clarity and speed.

Build and steward relationships in service of the portfolio (15%)

  • Maintain a visible and consistent presence across school communities and at key school and community moments, building trust with families and communities and ensuring firsthand observation from schools informs how the academic and school performance strategy is refined.
  • Engage regularly with school leaders through purpose-built structures, gathering a firsthand read on whether academic and school systems are functioning as intended.
  • Represent the school system's academic and school performance work with external stakeholders, including DC PCSB and OSSE, in coordination with the CEO and Chief External Affairs Officer as appropriate.
  • Serve as one of the school system's primary points of contact within the broader KIPP network, engaging in network-level convenings and peer learning communities and keeping the school system's academic and school-level work aligned with national priorities.
  • Build relationships with peer leaders and external organizations, in and outside the KIPP network, whose expertise and perspective strengthen the school system's academic and school-level work.

Requirements & Preferences

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required
  • 15+ years of school system experience required, including significant leadership experience in a complex, multi-function organization
  • 5+ years of experience in a central office or headquarters leadership role within a multi-site school system, leading work that spans schools
  • Demonstrated experience managing across functions and through multi-layered teams, with a track record of developing and holding senior leaders accountable for results
  • Proven ability to lead and manage organizational change effectively to drive student outcomes
  • Excellent internal and external communication skills and a demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across an organization, within communities, and with a board of directors

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's Degree in education-field
  • 15+ years experience in urban schools, including experience working in or alongside K-12 school systems at a similar scale and complexity
  • Experience managing large multi-layer teams in or supporting schools
  • Deep knowledge of and commitment to equity to drive student outcomes and achieve academic excellence
  • Experience with special education and/or multilingual education
  • School leadership experience
  • Strong cultural competency skills, including ability to communicate, work effectively, cultivate relationships with a diverse set of stakeholders
  • Passion for education reform and the belief that every child can succeed
  • Unquestioned integrity and commitment to KIPP DC’s mission and to advancing its antiracist ambition through their work with staff, students, alumni, and families

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to travel across and between campuses and schools
  • Flexibility to work outside normal business hours or weekends in the event of a school or system crisis.


Demonstrated Excellence in the Following Areas:

  • Commitment to Students and Schools: Demonstrates commitment to education reform, believing in every child's potential for success and prioritizing students, schools, and the essential role of families.
  • Strategic Thinking and Problem Solving: Finds creative solutions to challenges that achieve broader goals of team and organization.
  • Project Management: Sets a high bar for own work and supports others to achieve desired team outcomes.
  • Communications and Influence: Demonstrates adept communication skills and influence to advance work by adjusting content and style.
  • Teamwork: Contributes to a supportive team culture, fostering diverse work styles and maintaining a high performance standard.
  • Trust and Collaboration: Establishes and nurtures effective relationships with a diverse set of stakeholders to support the best outcomes for our work.
  • Cultural Humility: Advances KIPP DC’s commitment to anti-racism by creating a diverse, equitable, and inclusive environment for all stakeholders.
  • Continuous Learning: Commits to continuous learning through feedback, self reflection, humility, and action.

Benefits & Compensation

KIPP DC offers an extremely competitive compensation and benefits package:

  • The anticipated starting salary range for this position is $244,025-$269,712. At KIPP DC we strive for clarity, equity, and to be highly competitive. When determining salaries we look at benchmarks in the education and non-profit sector.
  • KIPP DC offers a robust benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurances; various voluntary benefits; and employer paid benefits such as short term disability, long term disability, life insurance, and a membership to One Medical.
  • KIPP DC also offers a 403(b) retirement account with a 3% employer contribution and a 3% match with vesting after three years.

Equal Employment Opportunity Employer

KIPP DC Public Schools does not discriminate against, or tolerate discrimination against, employees or applicants for employment on any legally-recognized basis or protected class including, but not limited to, actual or perceived race, color, national origin, immigration status (except as necessary to comply with federal, DC, state, or local law), religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, gender (including gender identity or expression), marital status (including domestic partnership status), genetic information, political affiliation, pregnancy, family responsibilities, personal appearance, veteran status, uniform service member status, status of being unemployed, status of victim a survivor of domestic violence, sexual offense or stalking, matriculation or any other protected class under federal, state, DC, or local law.

title: Embroidery Development Specialist
description:
At Weezie, we make towels and gifts worth celebrating, and we're on a mission to bring delight to life's moments, big and small. Embroidery and customization sit at the heart of that experience, and we're looking for an Embroidery Development Specialist to lead the development behind it, from concept through a ready-to-produce design. This person will own development across embroidery, appliqué, and custom logos, and will be the go-to expert making sure design intent can actually be brought to life in our production environment. This is a role that spans the artistry and execution of personalization. Based in Atlanta, this role splits time between our HQ/Design studio and our Austell production location, and sits within our Product Development and Design department, reporting to our Senior Designer.

It's an exciting time to join Weezie, a two-time Inc. 5000 honoree (2024 and 2025). You'll be stepping in at a pivotal inflection point as we scale toward our next major milestones.

What You'll Do

  • Drive the development of embroidery, appliqué, custom logo, icons, and customization capabilities, translating original design intent into production-ready, manufacturable designs across our product portfolio
  • Own design specifications, including sizing, placement, character counts, stitch types, densities, and paths, so each design executes as intended
  • Train to become our expert in our embroidery software and design programs: handle digitization and template creation, manage the upfront development process with software and digitizing partners, and serve as our design-side expert on font/template management and launch prep
  • Serve as our design-for-manufacturing expert, reviewing new designs and logos against production capabilities and run rate, flagging adjustments before they reach the production floor, and building mockups, stitch-outs, and customer and photoshoot samples to the highest standards for approval before launch
  • Develop custom logo and corporate gifting requests from concept through client-approved, production-ready file, in partnership with Business Development
  • Collaborate with Design and Fulfillment on a continuous improvement program for post-launch customization quality, assisting in diagnosing and troubleshooting root-cause issues in templates, digitization, or specs.
  • Test and evaluate new substrates, product placements, equipment, and customization methods to expand our capabilities, and maintain organized file systems, version control, and documentation for production files

Who You Are

  • Hands-on embroidery design and execution experience in a commercial environment
  • Experience with embroidery and/or digitization software, with a strong aptitude to become an expert in our internal design and production system, including template creation and setup.
  • Strong design eye combined with technical know-how, able to take a creative concept and figure out how to actually bring it to life
  • Comfortable assessing designs against machine capability, and flagging adjustments early
  • Strong understanding of stitch types, underlay, density, pull compensation, sequencing, hooping/clamping, and stabilizers.
  • Broad understanding of different substrates and materials and how they interact in the embroidery process.
  • Strong cross-functional communicator, able to liaise effectively with Design, Ops, and Web
  • Interest in R&D (testing new substrates, equipment, or customization methods)
  • Attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple projects and workstreams simultaneously.
  • Familiarity with Tajima embroidery machines and Pulse digitizing software is a plus.

title: Financial Audit Intern- Local Government Audit, West TN- Summer 2027
description:
Financial Audit Intern—Local Government Audit, West
Summer 2027: June 1 - August 6

About Our Program
The Comptroller of the Treasury's Audit Internship Program is a 10-week paid educational and experiential learning opportunity offering undergraduate students a chance to witness and participate in the audit operations of the office. Interns will spend the summer building skills through their assignment to an active audit, audit-specific training, and professional development training. Interns will also have opportunities to build relationships with each other through shared experiences.

Intern responsibilities may include learning to examine and review records, reports, financial statements, and management practices for local government entities and other organizations receiving public funds. Interns may have the opportunity to evaluate the following: fairness of financial statement presentation; the adequacy of internal controls; the efficiency and effectiveness of an entity's operations and systems; and compliance with laws, regulations, contracts, and grant agreements.

Our summer internship program is designed to be both professionally and academically beneficial. Interns gain hands‑on experience while participating in meaningful professional development activities such as Business Etiquette Day, a full‑day session focused on professionalism, emotional intelligence, and understanding one’s professional brand, complete with an etiquette lunch led by staff. Interns also enjoy engaging activities like speed networking with full‑time employees, a guided tour of the Tennessee Capitol to explore the state’s history, and weekly cohort check‑ins to foster connection and collaboration. The cohort experience culminates in a final presentation showcasing what interns have learned and contributed during their time with the Office.

Location
This Local Government Audit internship opportunity will be based out of the West Tennessee Region. Depending on the audit assignment, interns may have the opportunity for limited travel to counties across the West, Tennessee Region during the summer.

​
Who We're Looking For
We are seeking students who are rising juniors, seniors, or enrolled in graduate accounting programs and are interested in applying their classroom knowledge to governmental auditing. To qualify for the internship program, applicants should have successfully completed at least 6 credit hours of accounting coursework. Preference will be given to students who have completed intermediate or advanced accounting classes.

Successful interns are those who are adaptable, able to think critically, work well both individually and as part of a team, and are willing to learn and grow. Candidates should exhibit strong interpersonal, verbal communication, organizational, and writing skills. Interns are expected to apply their classroom knowledge to meaningful audit work.


About Our Office
The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury is responsible for the audit of state and local governmental entities and participates in the general financial and administrative management and oversight of state government. In the Comptroller’s Office, we strive to deliver on our mission to make government work better. Through dedicated hard work and commitment, every Comptroller’s Office employee accepts personal responsibility to accomplish our mission and uphold it.

Compensation
Interns are paid $24 per hour via a third-party company. Travel is required for Local Government Audit Interns but is generally confined to same-day commutes to and from a job site. Overnight stays are required for intern events, typically 3 per summer. Overnight hotel stay(s) and related expenses are reimbursed.

Equal Opportunity Employer

It is the Comptroller’s policy to provide an environment free of discrimination and harassment of an individual because of that person’s race, color, national origin, age (40 and over), sex, sexual orientation, transgender and gender identity status, pregnancy, religion, creed, disability, veteran’s status, or any other category protected by state and/or federal civil rights laws.
​
​​NOTICE: This position requires a criminal background check. Therefore, you may be required to provide information about your criminal history in order to be considered for this position.​

title: Sales Engineer
description:
Sales Engineer

Skills: Relationship Building, Communication skills, Blasting experience, product finishing experience, surface preperation, Manufacturing processes, Industry trends, written skills, travel to assigned territory, CRM Systems, microsoft office

Experience level: All Experience Level
Experience required: 2 Years
Education level: High school or equivalent
Relocation assistance: No

Candidates need to have experience working for a finishing company, job shop, or manufacturing operation with finishing processes. Former Warehouse Supervisor, Production Supervisor, Operations Supervisor, or similar role with customer interaction responsibilities.

Sales Engineer

Territory: Pittsburgh, PA / Eastern Ohio Region

Position Summary

Our is seeking a motivated, customer-focused Sales Engineer to develop and grow sales within the Pittsburgh and Eastern Ohio manufacturing market. This role is ideal for an individual with hands-on industrial finishing experience who understands the challenges faced by manufacturing companies and finishing operations.

The ideal candidate will have experience in abrasive blasting, vibratory finishing, surface preparation, industrial finishing equipment, or related manufacturing processes. We are particularly interested in candidates who have worked in a manufacturing environment with an in-house finishing department, finishing company, equipment sales organization, or have held leadership positions such as Warehouse Supervisor, Operations Supervisor, or Production Supervisor with direct exposure to finishing processes.

This is a sales position requiring strong technical aptitude, excellent communication skills, and the ability to build long-term customer relationships.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop new business opportunities throughout the Pittsburgh and Eastern Ohio territory.
  • Identify customer manufacturing challenges and recommend appropriate finishing solutions, equipment, and process improvements.
  • Conduct customer visits, facility walk-throughs, equipment demonstrations, and technical presentations.
  • Establish strong relationships with manufacturing engineers, plant managers, operations managers, production supervisors, and purchasing personnel.
  • Generate quotes, proposals, and technical recommendations.
  • Manage sales activities through CRM and other technology tools.
  • Coordinate with internal teams to ensure successful project implementation and customer satisfaction.
  • Attend trade shows, industry events, and customer demonstrations as needed.
  • Stay current on industry trends, finishing technologies, and competitive offerings.

Required Qualifications

2+ years of experience in industrial manufacturing, finishing operations, equipment sales, or related industries.

Direct experience with one or more of the following:

Abrasive blasting equipment and processes

Vibratory finishing systems

Surface preparation

Deburring and polishing operations

Metal finishing processes

Industrial finishing equipment

Experience working within a manufacturing facility that includes a finishing department.

Strong mechanical and technical aptitude.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Comfortable using CRM systems, Microsoft Office Suite, and other sales technology tools.

Ability to travel throughout the assigned territory.

Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working for a finishing company, job shop, or manufacturing operation with finishing processes.

Former Warehouse Supervisor, Production Supervisor, Operations Supervisor, or similar role with customer interaction responsibilities.

Knowledge of process improvement, production efficiency, and manufacturing workflows.

Established relationships within the regional manufacturing community.

Technical or engineering-related education, training, or certifications.

title: Software Engineer II - CTJ - Poly
description:

Security represents the most critical priorities for our customers in a world awash in digital threats, regulatory scrutiny, and estate complexity. We want to reshape security and empower every user, customer, and developer with a security cloud that protects them with end to end, simplified solutions. The Microsoft Security organization accelerates Microsoft’s mission and bold ambitions to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers’ heterogeneous environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate. Are you interested in working for on cutting-edge cloud security products? Look no further than the Microsoft Defender engineering team. You will be building and delivering cloud solutions to meet the scale that few companies in the industry are required to support. Leveraging state-of-the-art technologies, you will be instrumental in delivering holistic protection within government environments. The Microsoft Defender team is responsible for delivering a constantly evolving set of services and solutions to meet the challenging landscape of our ever-evolving attackers.


This is a combined DevOps team which provides leadership, direction, and accountability for cloud design, service architecture, engineering infrastructure, and data platform development. We are currently looking for Software Engineer II to join the team. You will help conduct business reviews and operate our production services. Collaboration skills will be required to work closely with other engineering teams to ensure services and systems are highly stable, meet performance Service level agreements (SLA), and meet the expectations of internal and external customers and users.


Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others andcollaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

title: Job Coach
description:
Job Coach / Employment Specialist – Part-Time

Location: Staunton, Virginia
Service Area: Staunton and surrounding Augusta County communities
Pay: $21.00–$22.00 per hour, based on experience
Hours: Up to 29 hours per week, with the potential to transition to full-time
Schedule: Predominantly daytime hours, Monday through Friday
Work Setting: Community-based with regular local travel
Mileage: Reimbursement for approved work-related travel

Help People Build Careers and Greater Independence

RISE Services is hiring a compassionate, dependable, and resourceful Job Coach / Employment Specialist to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain meaningful employment.

In this community-based role, you will meet participants at employer worksites and other locations throughout Staunton and surrounding Augusta County communities. You will help participants explore career interests, search and apply for jobs, prepare for interviews, learn workplace responsibilities, communicate with employers, and develop the skills needed for long-term employment success.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. We welcome applicants with relevant experience in disability services, human services, education, behavioral health, workforce development, direct support, career coaching, case management, retail supervision, customer service, or other positions involving teaching, mentoring, or helping others succeed.

Training is provided.

Schedule and Hours

This position offers up to 29 hours per week. Most services in the Staunton area are provided during daytime hours, Monday through Friday.

Weekend work is occasionally needed to provide coverage when another employee is unavailable, but this is not a regularly scheduled weekend position.

Weekly schedules may include:

  • On-site job coaching

  • Job searching and completing applications

  • Resume and interview preparation

  • Employer outreach

  • Employment-readiness activities

  • Community-based participant meetings

  • Progress notes and required documentation

When a participant is not working their full number of authorized service hours, the Job Coach may provide other approved employment services, including job searching, completing applications, developing resumes, preparing for interviews, contacting employers, and teaching workplace-readiness skills.

Employees who want additional hours may have the opportunity to transition to full-time as caseloads and service needs grow. Full-time hours are not guaranteed and depend on participant referrals, scheduling needs, employee availability, and satisfactory job performance.

What You’ll Do

Job Coaching and Workplace Support

  • Provide individualized coaching at employer worksites and in community settings.

  • Help participants learn job duties, workplace routines, safety procedures, and employer expectations.

  • Teach workplace communication, professional behavior, time management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Help participants communicate effectively with supervisors and coworkers.

  • Develop natural workplace supports that promote greater independence.

  • Monitor participant progress and adjust coaching strategies as participants develop new skills.

  • Provide ongoing support to promote successful employment retention.

Job Search and Career Preparation

  • Help participants identify their strengths, interests, abilities, support needs, and employment goals.

  • Assist participants with resumes, applications, job searches, and interview preparation.

  • Conduct mock interviews and employment-readiness activities.

  • Identify opportunities that match each participant’s interests, abilities, experience, and goals.

  • Coordinate interviews, hiring activities, and onboarding support.

  • Help participants understand workplace expectations and identify reasonable accommodations when appropriate.

Employer and Community Engagement

  • Build professional relationships with employers throughout Staunton and Augusta County.

  • Contact businesses to identify potential employment opportunities.

  • Educate employers about inclusive hiring and available workplace supports.

  • Communicate with participants, families, employers, vocational rehabilitation counselors, support coordinators, schools, and community partners.

  • Attend hiring events, team meetings, training, and other scheduled activities.

Documentation and Service Coordination

  • Complete accurate progress notes and service documentation within required deadlines.

  • Maintain participant records according to funding-source and organizational requirements.

  • Track job searches, applications, interviews, placements, wages, scheduled hours, and employment retention.

  • Communicate participant progress, concerns, scheduling changes, and service needs to the appropriate supervisor.

  • Participate in service-planning and team-coordination activities.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree is not required.

  • Relevant experience supporting individuals with disabilities or others who experience barriers to employment is preferred.

  • Experience in teaching, coaching, mentoring, customer service, supervision, human services, behavioral health, workforce development, or a related field may also be considered.

  • Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

  • Ability to work independently and make responsible decisions in community settings.

  • Ability to maintain a consistent schedule and complete documentation on time.

  • Basic computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.

  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

  • Ability and willingness to travel locally and transport participants when required.

  • Ability to satisfy applicable background-screening and employment requirements.

Preferred but Not Required

  • Supported Employment, Individual Supported Employment, job-coaching, or job-development experience.

title: Program Billing Specialist
description:

The Program Billing Specialist coordinates timely billing and collection of Residential
Family Support, Department of Children and Families and CBC contracts, as well as Social Security Benefits for the youth in care, as well as Medicaid services to our youth in care and ensure reconciliation of accounts receivable by ledgers for these services. title: Production Test Technician
description:
Rantec is hiring an Electronics Test Technician.

Come join our team! Based in Los Osos, California, located along California's scenic Central Pacific coastline, Rantec offers many outstanding benefits, the following are a few:

  • Competitive wages
  • Great benefits - i.e. Medical (PPO, HSA), Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Accounts

  • Peer-to-Peer recognition and Years of Service Awards.
  • We have every other Friday off as we are on the 9/80 schedule
  • Free catered lunch on the Friday/payday that we work. Voluntary overtime hours available.

Rantec is located in Los Osos, California is an upper-tier designer and manufacturer of power supplies for the military and aerospace markets. We are an engineering-based company, with expertise in all aspects of power supply design, manufacturing and test.

Position Summary

The Production Test team at Rantec is tasked with keeping product flowing from Manufacturing to the customer while catching items that do not meet customer specifications or Rantec standards for quality. It is when product fails a test or fails in operation that the Test Technician steps to the front. As a Test Technician, you will use your extensive skills in power conversion electronics and test processes to determine the cause of the failure and identify any consequential failures that must be corrected.

Rantec employs extensive automated test systems, but not all product can use these, and it take sophisticated skills to complete these tests accurately and consistently. The Test Technician will perform manual or complex tests on low volume high value product in an efficient manner. You will have the opportunity to expand your skill set through formal training and through hands-on experience with other Test Technicians and Electrical Engineers.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities, including but, are not limited to the following:

Troubleshoot failed power supplies and components

  • Review test reports of failed power supplies
  • Use a combination of automated and manual test processes to isolate the problem to a board or module
  • Identify the failure whether a bad or incorrect component
  • Identify any likely secondary damage
  • Document, report, and track failure modes
  • Report any trends noticed to the Test and Manufacturing Engineering teams

Conduct high-touch or complex test processes

  • Conduct manual tests on legacy or low volume product where there are no automated tests
  • Work with Test Engineering on first time run-throughs for new products, test fixtures, or processes
  • Provide constructive feedback to Test Engineering on new processes and test documentation
  • Conduct incoming material tests for non-standard or complex parts
  • Assist the Test Supervisor and Director of Test in scheduling resources
  • Provide additional Production Test coverage in times of high demand
  • Report to Test Engineering any test systems that are not performing correctly or are providing suspicious results
  • Work with other Test Technicians to ensure the Production Test and ESS areas remain clean and organized
  • Work with Account Management to organize and prioritize testing of customer returned material
  • Provide feedback to Engineering and Test Engineering on the testability of new product designs
  • Assist the Test Supervisor in training new Test Technicians
  • Ability to work flexible hours and/or different shifts, if needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Education and Experience

  • Associates Degree or equivalent in Electronics Technology, BSEE preferred.
  • 3-5 years in electrical assembly.
  • Experience using basic and advanced electronic measurement tools and equipment.
  • Ability to read and understand mechanical drawings and electrical schematics.
  • Experience with the MS Office suite (Excel, Word).
  • Ability to read and complete documented processes independently
  • Soldering (IPC J-STD-001 certification) preferred.
  • Electronics inspection (IPC A-610 certification) preferred.

Salary Range: $25.15 - $43.75 Hourly

title: IT GRC Analyst Level II
description:
Position Overview

The IT GRC Analyst (CMMC Control Specialist) is responsible for the daily monitoring, operational testing, and ongoing compliance analysis of the organization’s cybersecurity controls. Rather than developing high-level enterprise security policies, this operational role focuses on hands-on control execution, reviewing technical logs, verifying evidence, and authoring, maintaining, and updating granular Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). This position ensures that hybrid IT environments, cloud enclaves, and technical infrastructure continuously satisfy CMMC Level 2 and NIST SP 800-171 requirements through standardized, repeatable processes.Key Responsibilities


SOP Development, Maintenance & Operationalization:

  • Draft, review, and continuously refine detailed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that translate complex NIST SP 800-171 controls into step-by-step technical workflows for IT staff.
  • Audit operational practices regularly to ensure procedural alignment with active SOPs, updating documentation whenever technical environments or baseline configurations evolve.
  • Maintain the centralized repository of GRC SOPs, work instructions, and execution templates, ensuring version control and strict alignment with the enterprise System Security Plan (SSP).
  • Partner with System Administrators and IT Operations to convert POA&M remediation outcomes into formalized, repeatable SOPs to prevent recurring compliance gaps.


Daily Control Monitoring & Evidence Analysis

  • Perform daily, weekly, and monthly operational reviews of technical controls across all 14 NIST SP 800-171 practice domains (e.g., auditing SIEM logs, validating MFA enforcement, and reviewing access requests) in accordance with established SOPs.
  • Collect, inspect, and archive technical artifacts and evidence (configuration baselines, backup logs, patch records) to maintain continuous audit readiness.
  • Identify, document, and report control drift or non-compliance issues across hybrid Active Directory, cloud environments (GCC High/Azure), and virtualization platforms.
  • Execute recurring internal control tests to verify that technical safeguards operate as documented in the SSP and procedural guidelines.

Risk Tracking & POA&M Execution

  • Track and validate the daily progress of remediation items listed on the active Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M).
  • Collaborate directly with System Administrators and IT Operations to test and verify fixed items before closing out open POA&M entries.
  • Monitor daily CUI flow paths and enclave access logs to verify that Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) boundary controls remain strictly enforced.
  • Conduct routine vendor risk checks, verifying that subcontractors maintain active compliance with DFARS 252.204-7012 / 7020 flow-down requirements.

Audit Support & Reporting

  • Analyze compliance data to support regular SPRS score updates and internal readiness reporting.
  • Serve as the primary hands-on evidence and procedural coordinator during internal compliance reviews, DIBCAC audits, and external C3PAO assessments.
  • Generate weekly operational risk metrics, process execution logs, and gap analysis reports for the IT Security Manager.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Experience: 2–4+ years of hands-on experience performing IT compliance monitoring, internal auditing, procedural documentation, or security control testing in a DoD/DFARS environment.
  • Documentation & SOP Skills: Proven ability to author clear, step-by-step technical Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), system administration guides, and audit-ready control execution logs.
  • Framework Knowledge: Direct experience monitoring and analyzing controls under NIST SP 800-171, CMMC Level 2, and DFARS 252.204-7012.
  • Technical Familiarity: Practical experience inspecting control evidence within Active Directory / Entra ID, Microsoft 365 / GCC High, firewalls, SIEM platforms, and hypervisors.
  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or equivalent practical technical experience.

Preferred Certifications

  • CMMC / Compliance: CCP (CMMC Certified Professional) or CISA.
  • General Security: Security+, Network+, or SSCP.

What You Need to be Successful…

  • 10+ years in solution design, pre-sales consulting, or operations advisory in insurance or BPO.

  • Familiarity with AI, automation, and agentic workflow concepts in insurance operations.

Your Compensation…
Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of the total compensation package that also includes annual bonus eligibility, benefits, and other opportunities at ReSource Pro. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, geography, and balancing internal equity relative to other ReSource Pro employees. The salary range may vary based on experience and on the specific geographic location in which the candidate resides.
Your Benefits & Perks…

Your Interview Process…
To be considered for this position, please submit your application. If you meet the qualifications for the role, a member of our Talent Acquisition team will be in touch to schedule an interview via zoom. The standard interview process includes:

About ReSource Pro:

Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

ReSource Pro provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

title: Senior Program Manager
description:
Position Overview

Our client is seeking an experienced Program Manager to provide overall leadership, management, administration, staffing, quality oversight, and financial execution for a large-scale federal IT support contract serving the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO).

The Program Manager will oversee the USPTO Service Desk, Advanced Problem Resolution (APR), USPTO Contact Center (UCC), Executive Support, Equipment Request Fulfillment (ERF), and Knowledge Management functions. This individual will ensure successful contract performance, customer satisfaction, and compliance with contractual requirements, service-level agreements (SLAs), security standards, staffing commitments, quality-management processes, transition requirements, and continuity-of-operations plans.

The Program Manager will serve as the contractor’s principal point of contact for USPTO leadership, including the Contracting Officer (CO), Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), Service Desk Operations Division leadership, Product Owners, and other Government stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Contract Management and Leadership

  • Direct and manage all contract operations across Service Desk, APR, UCC, Executive Support, ERF, and Knowledge Management functions.

  • Serve as the contractor’s authorized representative with authority to commit corporate resources and make binding operational decisions.

  • Provide executive leadership and guidance to team leads, supervisors, managers, and support personnel.

  • Ensure all contractual requirements, performance objectives, deliverables, and staffing commitments are achieved.

  • Lead contract kick-off activities, transition execution, operational governance meetings, and program reviews.

  • Maintain effective communication with USPTO stakeholders and senior leadership.

  • Identify and mitigate contractual, operational, staffing, financial, and performance risks.

Program and Workforce Oversight

  • Manage staffing, recruitment, retention, workforce planning, and succession-planning activities.

  • Ensure all key personnel and staffing requirements are filled within Performance Work Statement timelines.

  • Monitor operational performance across all functional areas.

  • Evaluate staffing forecasts, workload trends, ticket volumes, and call volumes to ensure SLA achievement.

  • Approve and oversee surge-support activities during major incidents, deployments, releases, and other operational events.

  • Coordinate contractor operations across primary and alternate Continuity of Operations locations.

  • Lead geographically dispersed teams operating in onsite, remote, and hybrid environments.

Customer Experience and SLA Management

  • Ensure achievement of all contractual SLAs and performance objectives.

  • Analyze operational metrics, customer-satisfaction data, quality reviews, and trend reports.

  • Develop and implement corrective-action plans when service levels fall below performance standards.

  • Lead continuous-service-improvement initiatives across all supported functions.

  • Champion customer-focused service delivery and operational excellence.

  • Review and resolve customer complaints, escalations, major incidents, and recurring operational issues.

  • Work with Government stakeholders to improve service quality, responsiveness, and end-user satisfaction.

Financial and Business Management

  • Manage contract funding utilization, labor allocation, staffing forecasts, and operational expenditures.

  • Align program resources with contractual priorities and workload requirements.

  • Support purchasing plans and resource requirements.

  • Review subcontractor performance and contractual compliance.

  • Monitor financial and operational performance to support successful contract execution.

  • Provide program status reports to company leadership and USPTO stakeholders.

Quality Management

  • Oversee implementation and execution of the Quality Control Plan.

  • Ensure quality reviews, ticket audits, call evaluations, and process assessments are performed consistently.

  • Establish performance-improvement initiatives based on metrics and trend-analysis findings.

  • Ensure compliance with standard operating procedures, knowledge-management requirements, and IT service-management best practices.

  • Promote measurable continuous improvement throughout the program lifecycle.

  • Maintain accountability for service quality across prime and subcontractor personnel.

Security and Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with USPTO cybersecurity requirements, Authorization to Operate requirements, security policies, and applicable federal regulations.

  • Support continuity of operations, disaster recovery, risk management, and contingency-planning activities.

  • Oversee implementation of security-awareness, privacy, and regulatory-compliance requirements.

  • Ensure contractor facilities maintain required operational and security standards.

  • Coordinate responses to audits, inspections, assessments, and compliance reviews.

  • Promote compliance with applicable NIST, FISMA, privacy, and federal IT security requirements.

Reporting and Governance

  • Review and approve monthly, quarterly, and annual status reports.

  • Oversee quality reports, trend-analysis reports, performance dashboards, and other contractual deliverables.

  • Conduct Program Management Reviews and operational governance meetings.

  • Participate in stakeholder meetings, executive briefings, and performance reviews.

  • Provide strategic recommendations for operational enhancements and emerging-technology adoption.

  • Ensure all Government reporting is accurate, complete, and delivered on time.

Innovation and Emerging Technology

  • Partner with USPTO leadership to identify opportunities for operational improvement.

  • Promote the responsible adoption of AI-enabled capabilities, including virtual agents, service-request summarization, automated knowledge management, and workflow optimization.

  • Lead innovation initiatives that improve efficiency, customer experience, resiliency, and service quality.

  • Evaluate emerging technologies for their potential to enhance federal IT service delivery.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, Management, or a related discipline.

  • Additional relevant experience may be substituted for education on a year-for-year basis, consistent with contractual guidance.

Experience

  • At least 15 years of progressively responsible experience managing large-scale IT operations, service desk, help desk, contact center, or end-user support environments.

  • At least 10 years of experience leading large teams supporting enterprise IT operations.

  • Experience managing multifunctional organizations that support service desk, contact center, account management, technical support, executive support, and related functions.

  • Demonstrated experience managing federal government contracts or similarly regulated operating environments.

  • Proven success leading geographically distributed operations and hybrid workforces.

  • Experience managing operational performance within an SLA-driven service-delivery model.

  • Strong experience with workforce management, resource planning, operational metrics, and service-delivery optimization.

  • Experience managing continuity of operations and disaster-recovery programs.

  • Knowledge of cybersecurity, NIST, FISMA, and federal IT compliance frameworks.

  • Strong executive communication, briefing, and stakeholder-management skills.

Certification

  • ITIL certification or equivalent demonstrated IT service-management experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Project Management Professional (PMP).

  • HDI Support Center Director.

  • HDI Support Center Manager.

  • Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or higher.

  • Certified ScrumMaster (CSM).

  • Expert knowledge of ITIL-based service-management principles.

  • Experience with ServiceNow, Salesforce, or similar enterprise service-management platforms.

  • Experience supporting large federal agencies and mission-critical IT environments.

  • Experience overseeing subcontractors and managing performance across multiple organizations.

  • Experience implementing service automation, AI-enabled support capabilities, or digital-transformation initiatives.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Ability to lead large, geographically dispersed teams while maintaining exceptional customer satisfaction.

  • Strong understanding of enterprise service desk, contact center, incident management, problem management, and knowledge-management operations.

  • Ability to interpret contractual requirements and translate them into measurable operational objectives.

  • Strong financial, organizational, analytical, and decision-making abilities.

  • Ability to communicate complex operational and technical matters to senior executives and Government stakeholders.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, mission-critical environment.

  • Strong commitment to accountability, service quality, continuous improvement, and customer-focused delivery.

title: Business Strategy Associate
description:
DEKA Research & Development is seeking a Business Strategy Associate to help shape the commercial story behind emerging technologies and new product opportunities.

Working closely with leadership, this individual will evaluate markets and competitors, help identify potential partners, and develop the strategic materials that inform major business decisions — including investment decks, business plans, market analyses, and commercialization strategies.

This is a role with broad exposure across product strategy, commercialization, partnerships, and new business development. It is well suited for a recent MBA graduate or early-career candidate with strong experience in consulting, strategy, finance, venture, or business development who is looking for meaningful ownership early in their career.

How You Will Make an Impact as a Business Strategy Associate:
  • Help develop the strategic and commercial case for new products and technologies, from early concept through business proposal.
  • Research markets, competitors, customers, and industry dynamics to assess opportunities and inform strategy.
  • Distill complex research into clear insights, recommendations, and executive-level materials.
  • Identify potential strategic partners, customers, investors, and other collaborators.
  • Assist with the development of outreach strategies and materials and help lead early conversations with prospective partners.
  • Support relationship-building with external organizations and manage follow-up on key opportunities.
  • Build investment decks, strategic presentations, and other materials used in high-level internal and external discussions.
  • Draft key components of business plans, including market opportunity, competitive positioning, business model, and go-to-market strategy.
  • Build and refine financial models evaluating revenue potential, costs, economics, and business scenarios.
  • Help drive strategic initiatives forward by managing priorities, follow-up, and next steps across multiple stakeholders.
Skills You Will Need to Be Successful:
  • Recent MBA graduate with experience through internships or prior roles in strategy, consulting, finance, business development, or a related field; or a bachelor’s degree with 1–3 years of relevant experience.
  • Strong analytical skills and demonstrated experience conducting market, competitive, and industry research.
  • Ability to synthesize complex information and develop a clear, well-supported point of view.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Experience developing high-quality executive presentations, analyses, briefings, or business cases.
  • Strong financial and quantitative skills, including comfort building and interpreting Excel-based business models.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Exceptional organization, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
  • High initiative, ownership, and follow-through, with the ability to independently drive work from question to recommendation to execution.
  • Comfort working directly with senior leaders and engaging external partners and stakeholders.
  • Impeccable judgment and discretion when handling confidential information.
  • Adaptability and enthusiasm for tackling new, ambiguous, or rapidly evolving problems.
  • Genuine interest in technology, engineering, innovation, and bringing new products to market.
  • Must be able to work on-site at DEKA five days per week and respond to occasional time-sensitive requests outside standard business hours.

About DEKA:

One hour from the beach, Boston, and the mountains, the historic Amoskeag Millyard once housed the largest textile mills in the world. It is now home to DEKA Research and Development, where we are taking the same innovation and cutting-edge technology into the modern age.

Behind DEKA’s brick walls sits a team of professionals who strive to make a difference every day through thoughtful engineering, design, and manufacturing. Here at DEKA, some of the most innovative and life-changing products of our time are created, and new ideas are always welcome and explored.

title: ONLINE Career Growth | Leadership Development
description:
Remote Career Growth Consultant | Client Benefits & Leadership Development

Company: AO – American Income Division of Globe Life
Work Arrangement: 100% Remote | U.S. Residents Only
Schedule: Flexible | Work From Home
Experience: Entry Level Welcome | No Insurance Experience Required
Compensation: Commission-Based | Weekly Pay | Performance Incentives
Career Track: Client Services | Sales | Leadership Development

Build More Than a Job—Build a Future

Are you looking for more than your next paycheck? Do you want a career where your effort, professional development, and performance can create opportunities for greater income and advancement?

AO is seeking motivated, growth-minded professionals to join our expanding virtual team as Remote Career Growth Consultants.

In this role, you'll work with individuals and families who have requested information about available benefits, helping them understand their options, identify their needs, and make informed financial protection decisions.

This opportunity combines client service, relationship building, benefits education, consultative insurance sales, and leadership development in a fully remote environment.

No previous insurance experience is required.

We value communication skills, professionalism, coachability, work ethic, and a willingness to grow. Comprehensive training, licensing guidance, mentorship, and ongoing professional development are provided.

✓ 100% Remote / Work From Home
✓ Flexible Scheduling
✓ Qualified Client Opportunities Provided
✓ No Lead Purchasing Required
✓ No Traditional Cold Calling
✓ Weekly Commission-Based Pay + Performance Bonuses
✓ Renewal & Residual Income Opportunities
✓ Comprehensive Training & Mentorship
✓ Performance-Based Leadership Advancement

About the Opportunity

As a Remote Career Growth Consultant, you'll begin by learning how to provide an exceptional client experience while developing valuable communication, business, and relationship-management skills.

You'll meet virtually with clients, learn about their needs, explain available life, accident, and supplemental health insurance options, and assist eligible clients through the enrollment process.

As you demonstrate consistency and strong performance, you'll have opportunities to develop additional skills in mentorship, coaching, team development, and leadership.

Our approach is centered on education, relationships, service, and trust—not high-pressure sales tactics.

What You'll Do

🤝 Client Service & Relationship Building

  • Meet virtually with clients through scheduled Zoom and phone appointments

  • Connect with individuals and families who have requested benefit information

  • Ask questions to understand each client's needs and priorities

  • Build trust through professional and personalized communication

  • Answer client questions clearly and accurately

  • Provide ongoing follow-up and client service

  • Build long-term relationships beyond the initial appointment

  • Maintain accurate digital records and documentation

🛡️ Benefits Education & Enrollment

Once properly licensed, you'll:

  • Explain available life, accident, and supplemental health insurance options

  • Help clients understand coverage features and benefit choices

  • Identify individual and family financial protection priorities

  • Provide needs-based recommendations

  • Guide clients through applications and enrollment

  • Assist with required documentation

  • Help ensure clients understand the coverage they select

  • Provide continued service after enrollment

📞 Qualified Client Opportunities – No Traditional Cold Calling

Spend your time helping people who are interested in learning more about available benefits.

Representatives connect with qualified client opportunities, including individuals and families who have requested information.

This allows you to focus on:

  • Scheduled client consultations

  • Benefits education

  • Needs-based conversations

  • Enrollment assistance

  • Relationship building

  • Follow-up and ongoing service

No lead purchasing is required.

🏡 100% Remote Work

Build your career from home while remaining connected to clients, mentors, teammates, and leadership.

You'll have access to:

  • Virtual client appointments

  • Remote training and coaching

  • Online team meetings

  • Modern digital business systems

  • Collaborative virtual support

  • No daily commute

Remote work also requires self-motivation, organization, accountability, and consistent follow-through.

⏰ Flexible Scheduling

Enjoy greater control over your schedule while maintaining the consistency and availability necessary to serve clients and achieve your professional goals.

This opportunity can provide greater flexibility than a traditional office environment while still rewarding individuals who approach their career with discipline, structure, and accountability.

💰 Weekly Performance-Based Compensation

This is a commission-based independent contractor opportunity—not an hourly or salaried position.

Compensation opportunities may include:

  • Weekly commission payments

  • Performance-based bonuses

  • Renewal and residual income opportunities

  • Leadership incentives as applicable

  • Recognition programs

  • Additional performance rewards

There is no predetermined cap on commission-based production; however, compensation is directly tied to individual activity, production, consistency, and results.

Individual earnings vary, and no specific income level is guaranteed.

📚 Comprehensive Training & Mentorship

No Industry Experience? No Problem.

We provide structured training and ongoing professional development designed to help motivated individuals learn the business and build confidence.

Training may include:

  • Structured virtual onboarding

  • Product and benefits education

  • Client-service development

  • Consultative sales training

  • Virtual presentation skills

  • Enrollment systems and procedures

  • Communication and relationship-building development

  • Weekly virtual coaching

  • One-on-one mentorship

  • Leadership development

  • Ongoing professional education

You bring the motivation and willingness to learn. We'll provide the training, mentorship, systems, and support to help you develop.

🎓 Licensing Guidance & Support

You do not need to already hold an insurance license to apply.

Because this opportunity involves discussing and enrolling clients in insurance products, representatives must obtain the appropriate state Life & Health Insurance License before performing activities requiring licensure.

Licensing guidance and support are provided.

📈 Your Career & Leadership Growth Path

At AO, your professional development doesn't stop after onboarding.

As you gain experience and demonstrate strong performance, you'll have opportunities to:

  • Strengthen communication and presentation skills

  • Develop advanced client relationship skills

  • Receive one-on-one mentorship from experienced leaders

  • Learn coaching and team-development fundamentals

  • Participate in leadership development

  • Mentor and support newer representatives

  • Develop business-building and organizational skills

  • Pursue additional leadership and management responsibilities

A potential development path may include:

Career Growth Consultant → Mentor/Trainer → Team Leader → Management → Advanced Leadership

Advancement is based on performance, consistency, initiative, professional development, and demonstrated leadership ability—not simply tenure.

Leadership positions are earned through performance and development and are not guaranteed.

❤️ Benefits & Professional Resources

Qualifying representatives may have access to:

  • Medical reimbursement program

  • Company-supported life insurance

  • Accidental Death Benefit coverage

  • Renewal and residual income opportunities

  • Leadership development programs

  • Professional coaching and mentorship

  • Virtual business technology and resources

  • Professional conferences and development events

Eligibility requirements and qualification periods may apply.

✈️ Recognition & Performance Incentives

Strong performance may also qualify representatives for opportunities such as:

  • Company-sponsored incentive travel

  • Leadership conferences

  • Professional development events

  • Performance contests

  • Recognition programs and awards

  • Team experiences

  • Additional advancement opportunities

Who We're Looking For

You may be a strong fit if you demonstrate:

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills

  • Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building abilities

  • Positive, professional attitude

  • Growth-oriented mindset

  • Self-motivation and personal accountability

  • Goal-oriented approach to work

  • Strong organization and time-management skills

  • Dependable follow-through

  • Ability to work independently from home

  • Comfort using Zoom and virtual technology

  • Ability to collaborate within a remote team

  • Coachability and openness to feedback

  • Professionalism and integrity

  • Desire for continuous personal and professional development

Potential Matters More Than Industry Experience

We're looking for people who are willing to learn, apply coaching, stay consistent, and grow.

Experience That Transfers Well

Previous insurance experience is not required.

Experience in these areas may transfer well:

Customer Service • Client Relations • Sales • Healthcare • Hospitality • Retail • Education • Administrative Support • Banking • Financial Services • Account Management • Recruiting • Call Centers • Military Service • Leadership or Management

Recent graduates and career changers are encouraged to apply.

Minimum Requirements

Applicants must:

  • Be at least 18 years of age

  • Be legally authorized to work in the United States

  • Be physically located within the United States

  • Have access to a reliable computer or laptop

  • Maintain reliable high-speed internet

  • Have webcam and microphone capability

  • Maintain a quiet, professional workspace

  • Be comfortable communicating with clients through Zoom and phone

  • Be comfortable learning web-based technology and business systems

  • Be willing to complete required training and professional development

  • Be willing and able to obtain the appropriate state Life & Health Insurance License

Virtual Interview Process

Qualified applicants will first complete a brief career overview covering:

  • Position responsibilities

  • Client opportunities

  • Commission-based compensation

  • Licensing requirements

  • Training and mentorship

  • Benefits and incentives

  • Career growth and leadership advancement

Candidates interested in continuing will then have the opportunity to participate in a live Zoom interview with our hiring team.

All interviews are conducted virtually.

Ready to Build More Than a Job?

If you're looking for a 100% remote career where you can help families, develop valuable professional skills, build long-term client relationships, and create greater earning and leadership opportunities through your performance, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply today to be considered for our Remote Career Growth Consultant opportunity with AO.

Learn Continuously. Serve With Purpose. Grow Through Performance. Build Your Future With AO. 🚀

title: Community Health Administration Coordinator (English/Spanish)
description:
Community Health Administration Coordinator English/Spanish (Contract)

Los Angeles, CA

$23 - $27 /hour

Schedule: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday

Employment Type: Contract 9 months

Travel: Up to 75% across multiple clinic sites in the Los Angeles area (mileage/travel reimbursed from designated home base location)

title: License Owner / Operator, Charlotte
description:

title: Entry Level Interior Designer

title: Ground Handler

title: Hard Top Cut & Cap
description:
Hard Top Cut & Cap – Lamination Department

Department: Lamination
Company: Sea Fox Boat Company
Reports To: Small Parts Lamination Manager
Position Type: Full-Time

Position Summary

The Hard Top Cut & Cap team member is responsible for cutting, trimming, preparing, and capping fiberglass hard tops according to Sea Fox quality and production standards. This position requires attention to detail, safe operation of cutting and grinding equipment, and the ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced boat manufacturing environment.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Cut and trim fiberglass hard tops according to established specifications and cut lines.

  • Use grinders, saws, routers, and other pneumatic or power tools safely and effectively.

  • Remove excess fiberglass and material from molded hard tops.

  • Grind and prepare edges and surfaces for the capping process.

  • Fit, bond, and cap hard top components to ensure proper alignment and structural integrity.

  • Apply fiberglass, resin, adhesives, putty, or other materials as required during the capping process.

  • Inspect completed work for proper fit, finish, dimensions, and overall quality.

  • Identify and correct minor fiberglass defects when necessary.

  • Follow established work instructions, production procedures, and quality standards.

  • Meet daily production goals while maintaining workmanship standards.

  • Properly handle and maintain tools, equipment, molds, and materials.

  • Follow all PPE requirements and safety procedures when working with fiberglass, resin, chemicals, and power tools.

  • Maintain a clean and organized work area throughout the shift.

  • Properly dispose of fiberglass waste, resin materials, and other production debris.

  • Communicate quality, material, equipment, or safety concerns to the Lamination Supervisor.

  • Assist other members of the Lamination Department as production needs require.

  • Perform other duties assigned by management.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Previous fiberglass, lamination, boat manufacturing, construction, or similar manufacturing experience preferred.

  • Experience using grinders, saws, routers, sanders, and pneumatic tools preferred.

  • Ability to read and follow work instructions and production specifications.

  • Strong attention to detail and quality.

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a production team.

  • Dependable attendance and ability to maintain expected production pace.

  • Willingness to learn Sea Fox manufacturing and quality standards.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand and work for extended periods.

  • Ability to regularly bend, reach, kneel, climb, push, and pull.

  • Ability to lift and/or move materials and components as required by the position.

  • Ability to work around fiberglass dust, resin, adhesives, chemicals, noise, and manufacturing equipment while wearing required PPE.

  • Ability to wear safety glasses, gloves, hearing protection, respirators, and other required protective equipment.

title: Clinical Development Trainer (LVN)
description:
Under the direct supervision of the Associate Director of Clinical Services, the Trainer, Clinical Development (LVN) performs a variety of tasks to ensure TVHC’s Medical Assistants (MA), Licensed Vocational Nurses (LVN), and Registered Nurses (RN) receive proper and consistent training across all clinical departments.


The Trainer performs full Licensed Vocational Nurse responsibilities as part of hands-on training for new hires and provides one-on-one instruction to ensure clinical competencies are met. The Trainer also coordinates and facilitates training for Registered Nurses, ensuring RN-specific competencies are delivered by an appropriately licensed designee.


Schedule: This is a full-time position, working 40 hours per week, typically Monday through Friday, with occasional Saturday hours.


About TVHC: Tiburcio Vasquez Health Center is a nonprofit community health center dedicated to promoting the health and well-being of our community by providing accessible, high-quality care through the integration of primary care, dental care, WIC support, mental health counseling, community health education, and more.


Benefits: We offer excellent benefits, including: medical (100% paid co-payments, premiums, etc.), dental, vision (including dependent and domestic partner coverage), generous paid leave benefits including holidays, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement plans with an Employer match, tuition reimbursement, monthly treats, pet insurance, and more.


Compensation: $38.71 - $42.30 per hour, depending on experience.


This position is represented by SEIU, with compensation and benefits determined by the terms of the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA). Salary is based on the wage scales outlined in the agreement. Beyond base pay, TVHC provides a comprehensive compensation package that supports the health, wealth, and career development of our employees.


Responsibilities:

  • Trains new and current MAs and LVNs on required clinical competencies, including clinical workflows, CLIA/lab procedures, vaccine administration, infection prevention, and use of TVHC systems.
  • Coordinates and facilitates training for RNs ensuring RN-specific competencies are provided and validated by an appropriately licensed designee. Provides instruction to RNs on shared clinical workflows, infection prevention, systems, and other cross-functional areas within LVN scope.
  • Performs all Medical Assistant and Licensed Vocational Nurse responsibilities utilizing best practice standards and promoting TVHC’s Service Excellence Standards.
  • Creates and develops training materials, which may include SOPs, workflows, presentations, and procedures.
  • Identifies learning and reinforcement needs for adult learners and provides additional support and follow-up education as needed.
  • Supports MAs, LVNs, and RNs in registering for and maintaining access to required systems (e.g., EZIZ, CAIR, Epic) and monitors compliance to ensure accounts remain active and up to date.
  • Partners with clinic leadership to support clinical workflows, quality initiatives, and new product or equipment implementation.
  • Assists with quality control, quality assurance, safety, and infection control practices to ensure compliance with internal and external regulations.
  • Facilitates end of training loop closure and handoff to Operational leadership.
  • Provides mentoring, assessment, and feedback to trainees regarding performance as part of the educational process.
  • Stays current with evidence-based practices, regulatory requirements, and emerging trends in clinical education and Medical Assistant and nursing support training.
  • Serves as an Epic “superuser,” providing EHR orientation, ongoing individual support, and refreshers for clinical staff in collaboration with IT/IS. Assists in the design and delivery of EHR workflows and related training materials.
  • Acts as a resource for clinical staff to answer questions, provide coaching, and assess performance in the execution of job duties.
  • Creates new hire orientation schedules in collaboration with Operational leadership.
  • Ensures all Medical Assistants, Licensed Vocational Nurses, and Registered Nurses are trained, signed off, and current with all competency and compliance requirements according to scope.
  • Provides back-up support to clinical staff as needed, ensuring all duties performed are within LVN scope.
