title: Security Manager
company: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
description:
About Us: The Griffin Museum of Science and Industry, Chicago is the largest and most interactive science museum in the Western Hemisphere. Chicago’s Museum of Science and Industry (MSI) expose guests of all ages to awe-inspiring exhibitions that spark curiosity and bring science to life. MSI’s mission – to inspire the inventive genius in everyone – is realized through its world-class exhibitions and engaging guest experiences. The Museum of Science and Industry provide programs and experiences that deepen the engagement of students and teachers in science and science-related disciplines, with a vision to inspire and motivate our children to achieve their full potential in the fields of science, technology, engineering and math.

We offer a creative, collaborative, and innovative environment for our employees. Our employees get great perks such as: benefits starting day one of your employment, free admission to MSI for family and friends, free admission to other museums, free parking in MSI’s garage and more! If you are equally passionate about our vision and want to be surrounded by a team of dynamic, smart and innovative people, the Museum of Science and Industry is the right place for you!

The Security Manager is responsible for overseeing the safety and security operations of the Kenneth C. Griffin Museum of Science and Industry, including the management of a contract security provider. This position ensures the protection of Museum staff, visitors, assets, and facilities while maintaining compliance with relevant regulations and standards. This role will assist in developing, implementing, and monitoring security policies, procedures, and systems to ensure a secure environment.

Responsibilities

Security Operations Management:
  • Assist to develop and implement comprehensive security plans, policies, and procedures.
  • Conduct regular risk assessments and recommend improvements to mitigate risks.
  • Monitor security systems, including surveillance cameras, access control, and alarm systems, ensuring they are operational and effective.
  • Prepare and file safety, criminal, incident, and other department reports.
  • Participate in setting and achieving short-term and long-term goals for the Security Department

Contract Security Provider Oversight:
  • Act as the primary point of contact for the contract security provider.
  • Review and approve schedules, ensuring appropriate staffing levels are maintained.
  • Monitor performance and compliance of the contract security team with organizational policies and contractual obligations.
  • Conduct regular audits and evaluations of contract security personnel.
Incident/Emergency Management:
  • Respond to and manage security incidents, including theft, vandalism, trespassing, and emergencies.
  • Conduct investigations and prepare detailed incident reports.
  • Coordinate with law enforcement and emergency services as necessary.
  • Assist in overseeing the emergency preparedness and recovery plans, operations, and operations.
  • Participate in all disaster preparedness activities, assist in coordinating emergency drills, manage, and coordinate central dispatch and communications in time of disaster and implement the emergency action plan/disaster plan.
  • Assist in periodic inspection program of facilities to assure compliance with applicable fire, safety, security codes and regulations.
  • Assist in coordinating emergency response activities, including emergencies involving medical situations, active threats, civil unrest etc. Ensure Museum is prepared for emergency responses including maintaining current emergency action plan, emergency boxes, and first aid kits.
Training and Awareness:
  • Develop and conduct security training programs for Museum staff and contract security personnel.
  • Promote a culture of security awareness across the organization.
Compliance and Reporting:
  • Ensure compliance with applicable local, state, and federal regulations.
  • Maintain records of security activities, including incident reports, audits, and training sessions.
  • Prepare and present regular security reports to senior management.
Collaboration:
  • Work closely with other departments to ensure alignment of security measures with organizational goals.
  • Participate in cross-functional teams to address security-related challenges and projects
  • Other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, security management, or a related field (preferred).
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in security management or a related role.
  • Proven experience managing contract security providers.
  • Strong knowledge of security systems, technologies, and best practices.
  • Excellent leadership, verbal, written, and electronic communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to handle stressful situations and make sound decisions under pressure.
  • Certifications such as Certified Protection Professional (CPP) or Physical Security Professional (PSP) are a plus.
  • Skill in project and time management with minimum supervision.
  • Ability to work cooperatively within a team environment and maintain effective working relationships.
  • Ability to interpret appropriate laws and regulations; administer security policies and activities; formulate procedures.
  • Knowledge of investigative techniques and principles and procedures of record keeping and report writing
  • Knowledge of procedures of psychology and crowd control and emergency evacuation, and investigative techniques and practices
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise judgement and diplomacy in dealing with sensitive issues such as confidential matters that involve staff and visitors involved in incidents or activities.
  • Ability to deliver a high level of customer service for staff and visitors.
  • Skill in verbal de-escalation in crisis and conflict resolution
  • Language:
    • Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
    • Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.
    • Ability to speak effectively before groups of employees of the organization.
  • Mathematical:
    • Ability to calculate basic figures and amounts such as percentages, area, etc.
  • Reasoning:
    • Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists.
    • Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, or schedule form.
  • Physical:
    • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel & talk or hear, stand, sit, walk, and reach with hands & arms.
    • The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance; kneel or crouch; taste or smell.
    • The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
    • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close, distance, color & peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Work Environment:
    • The employee is occasionally exposed to wet and/or humid conditions; high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals; outside weather conditions; extreme cold; extreme heat; and vibration.
    • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

The salary for this position is $70,000.

title: Job Coach
description:
Job Coach / Employment Specialist – Part-Time

Location: Rehoboth Beach, Delaware
Service Area: Rehoboth Beach and surrounding Sussex County communities
Pay: $22.00 per hour
Hours: Up to 29 hours per week, with the potential to transition to full-time
Schedule: Predominantly daytime hours, Monday through Friday
Work Setting: Community-based with regular local travel
Mileage: Reimbursement for approved work-related travel

Help People Build Careers and Greater Independence

RISE Services is hiring a compassionate, dependable, and resourceful Job Coach / Employment Specialist to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain meaningful employment.

In this community-based role, you will meet participants at employer worksites and other locations throughout Rehoboth Beach and surrounding Sussex County communities. You will help participants explore career interests, search and apply for jobs, prepare for interviews, learn workplace responsibilities, communicate with employers, and develop the skills needed for long-term employment success.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. We welcome applicants with relevant experience in disability services, human services, education, behavioral health, workforce development, direct support, career coaching, case management, retail supervision, hospitality, customer service, or other positions involving teaching, mentoring, or helping others succeed.

Training is provided.

Schedule and Hours

This position offers up to 29 hours per week. Most services are provided during daytime hours, Monday through Friday.

Weekend work is occasionally needed to provide coverage when another employee is unavailable, but this is not a regularly scheduled weekend position.

Weekly schedules may include:

  • On-site job coaching

  • Job searching and completing applications

  • Resume and interview preparation

  • Employer outreach

  • Employment-readiness activities

  • Community-based participant meetings

  • Progress notes and required documentation

When a participant is not working their full number of authorized service hours, the Job Coach may provide other approved employment services, including job searching, completing applications, developing resumes, preparing for interviews, contacting employers, and teaching workplace-readiness skills.

Employees who want additional hours may have the opportunity to transition to full-time as caseloads and service needs grow. Full-time hours are not guaranteed and depend on participant referrals, scheduling needs, employee availability, and satisfactory job performance.

What You’ll Do

Job Coaching and Workplace Support

  • Provide individualized coaching at employer worksites and in community settings.

  • Help participants learn job duties, workplace routines, safety procedures, and employer expectations.

  • Teach workplace communication, professional behavior, time management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Help participants communicate effectively with supervisors and coworkers.

  • Develop natural workplace supports that promote greater independence.

  • Monitor participant progress and adjust coaching strategies as participants develop new skills.

  • Provide ongoing support to promote successful employment retention.

Job Search and Career Preparation

  • Help participants identify their strengths, interests, abilities, support needs, and employment goals.

  • Assist with resumes, applications, job searches, and interview preparation.

  • Conduct mock interviews and employment-readiness activities.

  • Identify opportunities that match each participant’s interests, abilities, experience, and goals.

  • Coordinate interviews, hiring activities, and onboarding support.

  • Help participants understand workplace expectations and identify reasonable accommodations when appropriate.

Employer and Community Engagement

  • Build professional relationships with employers throughout Rehoboth Beach and Sussex County.

  • Contact businesses to identify potential employment opportunities.

  • Educate employers about inclusive hiring and available workplace supports.

  • Communicate with participants, families, employers, vocational rehabilitation counselors, schools, and community partners.

  • Attend hiring events, team meetings, training, and other scheduled activities.

Documentation and Service Coordination

  • Complete accurate progress notes and service documentation within required deadlines.

  • Maintain participant records according to funding-source and organizational requirements.

  • Track job searches, applications, interviews, placements, wages, scheduled hours, and employment retention.

  • Communicate participant progress, concerns, and scheduling changes to the appropriate supervisor.

  • Participate in service-planning and team-coordination activities.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree is not required.

  • Relevant experience supporting individuals with disabilities or others who experience barriers to employment is preferred.

  • Experience in teaching, coaching, mentoring, customer service, hospitality, supervision, human services, behavioral health, workforce development, or a related field may also be considered.

  • Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

  • Ability to work independently and make responsible decisions in community settings.

  • Ability to maintain a consistent schedule and complete documentation on time.

  • Basic computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.

  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

  • Ability and willingness to travel locally and transport participants when required.

  • Ability to satisfy applicable background-screening and employment requirements.

Preferred but Not Required

  • Supported Employment, job-coaching, or job-development experience.

  • Experience supporting individuals with intellectual, developmental, behavioral, or other disabilities.

  • Knowledge of vocational rehabilitation or disability-employment services.

  • Understanding of the Americans with Disabilities Act and reasonable workplace accommodations.

  • Experience working with employers, schools, vocational rehabilitation counselors, or community organizations.

  • CESP, ACRE, DSP, or another employment-support credential.

Who Will Succeed in This Position?

You may be a strong fit if you are:

  • Compassionate, patient, dependable, and encouraging.

  • Comfortable working at employer locations and throughout the community.

  • Able to teach and motivate participants while promoting independence.

  • Professional and confident when communicating with employers and community partners.

  • Resourceful and willing to find solutions when challenges arise.

  • Organized and able to manage appointments, follow-ups, and documentation.

  • Flexible when participant or employer schedules change.

  • Comfortable working independently without constant direct supervision.

Why Join RISE Services?

  • Make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals with disabilities.

  • Help people build careers, confidence, and greater independence.

  • Work predominantly during weekday daytime hours.

  • Receive mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel.

  • Participate in paid training and professional development.

  • Build experience in human services, disability services, workforce development, and career coaching.

  • Access potential opportunities for additional hours and advancement.

  • Join a collaborative, growing, and mission-driven organization.

Benefits

Part-time employees may be eligible for:

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Employee Tenure Bonus Program

  • Mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel

  • Paid training and professional development

Employees who transition to an eligible full-time position may also receive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays

  • Short-term disability insurance

  • Life insurance

  • Long-term care option

Benefit eligibility requirements apply.

Important Work-Setting Information

This is a community-based position, not a remote or traditional office-based role. Services are provided at employer worksites and other community locations throughout Rehoboth Beach and surrounding Sussex County communities.

Applicants must have reliable transportation and be comfortable driving between community locations. Transporting participants may be required as part of the position.

Equal Opportunity Employer

RISE Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We recruit, hire, train, compensate, and promote employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Apply Today

If you enjoy teaching, encouraging others, solving problems, and helping people accomplish meaningful goals, apply for the Part-Time Job Coach / Employment Specialist position with RISE Services.

A bachelor’s degree and previous job-coaching experience are not required. Relevant experience, dependability, professionalism, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to helping others succeed are strongly valued.

title: Corporate Controller
description:
Job Purpose Summary:
Reporting directly to executive leadership, the Controller serves as the strategic financial steward for Kenson Plastics, responsible for directing all accounting operations, financial reporting, internal controls, and compliance frameworks. This is not a maintenance role. We are looking for a creative, visionary accountant who sees extraordinary long-term opportunity in a growing environment where the systems aren't entirely built yet.

If you are an architect of process who wants to lay the permanent financial foundation, build the infrastructure from the ground up, and turn a blank slate into a high-performance engine, this is your platform. You will combine meticulous transactional oversight with advanced data analytics, transforming complex financial insights into actionable intelligence that empowers management to drive precision manufacturing excellence and sustainable business growth.

This is a hybrid role with 4 days/week onsite at our Beaver Falls facility.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Accounting Operations Oversight: Lead and direct end-to-end accounting functions, including general ledger maintenance, accounts payable/receivable, and payroll processing, while supervising and mentoring the accounting team.
  • Internal Controls + Asset Protection: Design, implement, and continuously improve robust internal control frameworks to safeguard company assets and ensure operational integrity.
  • Financial Reporting + GAAP Compliance: Prepare and deliver accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in strict compliance with U.S. GAAP.
  • Month and Year End Close Management: Drive efficient, timely month-end and year-end close processes to maintain accurate financial records and seamless reporting schedules.
  • Job Costing + Cost Modeling: Develop, refine, and maintain precise product cost models for manufactured parts using real-time and historical production data.
  • Production Variance Analysis: Partner with operations leadership to analyze manufacturing metrics, cost drivers, efficiencies, and production variances to support profitability.
  • Audit Coordination: Serve as the primary liaison for external auditors, leading the successful coordination and execution of annual financial audits.
  • Tax + Regulatory Compliance: Manage and coordinate all required federal, state, and local tax filings to ensure full regulatory compliance.
  • Special Projects: Perform all other duties and special projects as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
  • Technical Accounting + GAAP: Advanced knowledge of U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), general ledger management, financial reporting, and end-to-end accounting operations (AP/AR, payroll).
  • Cost Accounting + Modeling: Proven ability to develop, refine, and maintain complex job costing models for a manufacturing environment, utilizing both real-time and historical production data.
  • Analytical + Operational Partnership: Strong capability to analyze production metrics, cost drivers, efficiencies, and variances, partnering with operations and executive leadership to drive strategic decision-making.
  • Internal Controls: Deep understanding of internal control frameworks, asset protection principles, and federal, state, and local tax and regulatory requirements.
  • Leadership + Supervision: Excellent interpersonal and team management skills with the ability to mentor, supervise, and develop accounting personnel.
  • Systems + Data Proficiency: Advanced proficiency in ERP systems, general ledger software, and advanced data analytics tools, including minimally Microsoft Excel.

Education and Experience Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a closely related business field required.
    • CPA designation or Master’s degree in Accounting/MBA is highly preferred.
  • Minimum of 7 years of progressive accounting experience required, with at least 3 years in a Controller, Assistant Controller, or finance/accounting management role required.
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience within a manufacturing environment within accounting, specifically handling job costing and operational variance analysis required.
  • Proven track record managing full-cycle month-end closes, external audits, and tax compliance required.
  • Demonstrated experience leading external audit coordination, serving as the primary liaison for financial auditors.

title: Data Management Maturity & Governance Lead
description:

Location: Lahore / Karachi / Islamabad, Pakistan
Job Type: Full-Time

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced Data Management Maturity & Governance Lead to lead data governance and data management maturity initiatives across the organization. The role will focus on data management maturity assessments, governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, gap assessments, remediation, evidence management, and compliance readiness.

The ideal candidate will have strong experience in enterprise data governance and the ability to translate data management requirements into practical policies, processes, controls, and implementation plans.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and coordinate data management maturity and governance initiatives.
  • Assess existing data management capabilities against defined maturity requirements and assessment criteria.
  • Conduct data management maturity and gap assessments and identify improvement opportunities.
  • Develop, review, and maintain data management policies, standards, procedures, frameworks, and guidelines.
  • Define and implement data governance controls, processes, roles, and responsibilities.
  • Coordinate with business and technical stakeholders to implement required data management and governance practices.
  • Develop and maintain remediation plans for identified governance and maturity gaps.
  • Track remediation actions, ownership, timelines, dependencies, and closure status.
  • Define, collect, validate, organize, and maintain evidence and supporting documentation for maturity and governance requirements.
  • Ensure policies, procedures, controls, and supporting evidence are aligned with applicable assessment requirements.

title: Physical Therapist (PT) – Mobile/Home-Based Care
description:
Overview

We are seeking a skilled, compassionate, and dependable Physical Therapist (PT) to provide high-quality physical therapy services to patients in their homes throughout the Austin, TX region.

The Physical Therapist will travel to patients' homes to perform comprehensive evaluations, develop individualized plans of care, provide skilled therapeutic interventions, monitor patient progress, and educate patients and caregivers on strategies to improve mobility, function, safety, and independence.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working independently in a home-based environment, has strong clinical judgment and communication skills, and is passionate about delivering patient-centered care.

This is a 1099 independent contractor position.

Duties and Responsibilities

· Travel to patients' homes throughout the assigned service area to provide physical therapy services.

· Perform comprehensive physical therapy evaluations in the patient's home environment.

· Assess strength, range of motion, balance, gait, mobility, coordination, endurance, pain, functional limitations, and ability to safely perform activities of daily living.

· Evaluate the patient's home environment and identify potential safety and fall risks that may impact mobility and independence.

· Develop individualized plans of care based on evaluation findings, physician orders/referrals, patient needs, clinical judgment, and functional goals.

· Establish measurable short-term and long-term functional goals.

· Provide skilled physical therapy interventions appropriate to the patient's diagnosis and functional limitations, including:

o Therapeutic exercises

o Therapeutic activities

o Neuromuscular re-education

o Gait and mobility training

o Balance and coordination training

o Functional strengthening

o Manual therapy when clinically appropriate

o Transfer training

o Fall prevention and safety training

· Train patients in the safe use of assistive devices such as walkers, canes, and other mobility equipment.

· Develop and instruct patients in individualized home exercise programs.

· Educate patients and caregivers regarding diagnosis, treatment, exercises, mobility, safety, fall prevention, and strategies to promote independence.

· Monitor patient response to treatment and make appropriate clinical modifications to the plan of care.

· Perform reassessments and communicate changes in patient condition or functional status as appropriate.

· Coordinate care with physicians, nurses, caregivers, physical therapist assistants, occupational therapists, and other healthcare professionals.

· Communicate effectively with referring providers regarding patient progress, concerns, and recommendations.

· Complete accurate, timely, and thorough documentation for evaluations, daily treatment visits, reassessments, progress reports, and discharge summaries.

· Maintain compliance with applicable federal and state regulations, professional standards, payer requirements, and company policies.

· Recognize changes in patient condition that may require physician notification, additional medical evaluation, or modification of treatment.

· Maintain patient confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries at all times.

· Provide compassionate, respectful, and professional care to patients and their families in the home setting.

Requirements

· Current and valid Texas Physical Therapist license in good standing.

· Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapy program.

· Strong knowledge of anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, and rehabilitation principles.

· Strong clinical reasoning and patient assessment skills.

· Ability to independently perform comprehensive PT evaluations and develop appropriate plans of care.

· Experience treating patients with orthopedic, musculoskeletal, neurological, balance, gait, weakness, mobility, and/or functional limitations preferred.

· Strong knowledge of therapeutic exercise, gait training, balance training, functional mobility, neuromuscular re-education, and fall prevention.

· Excellent patient assessment and acute/chronic pain management skills.

· Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

· Ability to work independently and effectively manage a mobile patient caseload.

· Must be punctual, dependable, organized, and professional.

· Comfortable entering and providing care in patients' homes and working with patients and caregivers in a home-based environment.

· Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required.

· Ability to travel throughout the assigned service area.

· CPR/BLS certification preferred or required according to company policy.

· Previous home health, mobile therapy, outpatient, orthopedic, neurological, geriatric, or community-based experience is preferred.

Mobile/Home-Based Care Expectations

Because this position involves providing care in patients' homes, the Physical Therapist must be able to:

· Arrive at scheduled visits within the expected timeframe.

· Manage travel time and maintain an efficient daily schedule.

· Carry and transport necessary clinical equipment and supplies.

· Adapt treatment approaches to different home environments and available space.

· Maintain a safe and professional environment during every patient visit.

· Communicate promptly regarding cancellations, scheduling changes, or patient concerns.

· Respect patients' homes, privacy, routines, and individual preferences.

· Demonstrate sound clinical judgment when working independently in the community.

Documentation and Compliance

The Physical Therapist is responsible for completing all required clinical documentation accurately and within established timeframes, including:

· Initial evaluations

· Treatment notes

· Reassessments

· Progress reports

· Recertifications, when applicable

· Discharge documentation

· Home exercise programs

· Communication with referring providers

· Other documentation required by the organization, payer, or applicable regulations

Job Type

Full-time – 1099 Independent Contractor

Pay Structure (1099)

· Guaranteed base pay: $1,080 per week

· Base compensation is calculated at $45 per patient visit, based on a minimum of 6 patient visits per day.

· $45 per additional patient visit for visits beyond the daily base of 6.

· Compensation is subject to the terms of the independent contractor agreement.

Schedule

4/10 Schedule

· Four 10-hour workdays per week

· Typical start time: 7:30 AM–8:30 AM, depending on patient scheduling and geographic coverage.

· Daily schedule may vary based on patient locations, visit duration, and patient needs.

Work Location

Mobile/Home-Based – Austin, TX Region

The Physical Therapist will travel to assigned patients' homes throughout the designated service area.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a clinically confident, compassionate, and self-motivated Physical Therapist who enjoys working one-on-one with patients and families. The successful candidate will be comfortable making clinical decisions independently, adapting treatment to the patient's home environment, and providing high-quality care while maintaining excellent documentation and communication.

This position is an excellent opportunity for a Physical Therapist who values autonomy, flexibility, meaningful patient relationships, and community-based care

title: Civic Awards Advisory Committee - Closing November 6, 2026
description:
The Municipality of Port Hope’s boards and committees are the heart of local community involvement. As a member, you'll have the opportunity to shape the future of Port Hope and contribute to the betterment of our community. No matter what your passion is, there's a place for you to make a difference.

Municipal boards and committees are essential components of local government dedicated to addressing specific community needs. Comprising of appointed or elected members, these bodies serve as advisory committees, focusing on a variety of community services. Municipal boards and committees play a vital role in promoting effective local governance. Get involved today and be part of the change you want to see in your town. Your voice matters, and together, we can make a difference!

The Municipality is recruiting for the Civic Awards Advisory Committee. See below for details.

Remuneration
Please note that no remuneration is provided to members of the Civic Awards Advisory Committee, as service on the Committee is voluntary.

About
Join the Civic Awards Advisory Committee to play an integral role in planning the annual Civic Awards Ceremony and advising Council on the administration of the Civic Awards Program, including providing recommendations to Council on the selected nominees to be awarded a Civic Award in accordance with the Civic Awards Program Criteria.

If you are dedicated to recognizing the impactful contributions and inspiring achievements of individuals and groups that bring honour and enrichment to the Municipality of Port Hope, we encourage you to apply for a position on the Civic Awards Advisory Committee.

Mandate
The Civic Awards Program celebrates nominees worthy of recognition for exceptional contributions and/or achievements bringing honour and/or enrichment to the Municipality of Port Hope. The mandate of the Committee is as follows:

Promotion and Nomination
  • To encourage and reward achievements and volunteerism within the Municipality;
  • Increase awareness about the Civic Awards program and recipient contributions and achievements while promoting and soliciting nominees for civic recognition;
  • To ensure nominations and award selection is completed in a fair and consistent manner; in order to help preserve the integrity of the Civic Awards Program over the long term;
  • To collaborate with Municipal staff and Council to host a successful program, annually;
  • Comply with Municipal branding requirements and review annually as it relates specifically to the function of the Civic Awards program.
Administration of the Civic Awards Program
  • Collaborate and assist municipal staff in the planning and execution of the annual Civic Awards Program and ceremony;
  • Managing tracking of each year’s award recipients and their nominations to prevent duplication of awards;
  • Ensure that each recipient receives a duly inscribed award;
  • Ensure that the Outstanding Citizen and Outstanding Youth award recipients’ names are displayed for public viewing in Town Hall;
  • Create and alter, from time to time, a nomination form that is readily available to the public;
  • Submit budget requests through the Local Boards and Committees Budget submission for the Civic Awards Night event that reflects the event’s operating and capital needs, in keeping with budget directions and timelines;
  • Administer the council approved communication plan funded through the Civic Awards Annual Budget Allocation.
  • To evaluate the Municipality’s recognition program once each Council term, including available input from Civic Awards Advisory Committee volunteers who have contributed over the previous four (4) years.
  • To review and recommend award categories and criteria for Council’s consideration and required amendments to the Civic Awards Nomination Criteria Policy.
Submit an Application
Please submit your cover letter and resume online at www.porthope.ca/careers by November 6, 2026. We are looking to fill one vacancy.

Recruitment Process

The Municipality of Port Hope is a progressive employer who believes a diverse and inclusive workplace strengthens the team and fosters an environment where everyone feels as though they belong and their dignity, beliefs and identity are respected.

We are committed to creating and sustaining an environment that provides a supportive workplace and equal opportunity for all employees. Accommodations can be requested throughout the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act.

Applications will be reviewed, and interviews may be scheduled prior to the job posting closing date. All applicants will receive an automated email confirming the submission of their application, but only those candidates selected for an interview will be further contacted by Human Resources.

Personal information is collected under the authority of the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act and the Municipal Act, as amended.

description:
Weekend Sign Installer

Are you looking for a flexible way to earn extra income on the weekends—and potentially grow it into your own small business? This position is a remote opportunity. Applicant should live in or near the zip-code listed.
Earn $70–$125 per weekend to start, with the opportunity to grow to $250–$350+ per weekend as you take on additional routes. Our Average Installer makes approximately $300 per weekend.
Weekend Directional Service is seeking reliable independent contractors to place and pick up temporary directional signs. This is a simple, independent role that can be completed in just a few hours each weekend.

What You’ll Do
  • Place signs between Friday 5:00 PM – Saturday 10:00 AM
  • Pick up signs between Sunday 6:00 PM – Monday 8:00 AM
  • Follow provided Google Maps routes and/or placement lists
  • Complete routes in any order within the allowed time windows
  • Store signs safely between weekends
  • Use your own vehicle to complete local routes
Most routes consist of 30–60 signs and typically take 45 minutes to 1.5 hours once you’re familiar with the area.
Why This Opportunity Works
  • Flexible schedule that fits around other commitments
  • Consistent weekend work available
  • Independent, low-stress work environment
  • Opportunity to grow earnings by taking on more routes
This role is ideal for rideshare drivers, delivery drivers, students, retirees, veterans, or anyone looking for reliable supplemental income.
Pay & Perks
  • $70–$125 per weekend to start
  • Opportunity to earn $200–$300+ per weekend as you grow
  • Signing Bonus
  • Direct deposit, paid bi-weekly
  • Training provided (video + support from managers)
When routes are completed consistently and correctly, we expand services—giving you access to more work and higher earnings.
Requirements
  • Valid driver’s license
  • Current auto insurance
  • Reliable vehicle with space for 30–60 signs
  • Smartphone (iPhone or Android, ~4 years old or newer)
  • Ability to lift and place signs outdoors in various weather conditions
  • Ability to hammer stakes 6–8 inches into the ground as needed
  • Dependability to complete routes within required time windows
Independent Contractor Notice
This is a 1099 independent contractor position. Contractors are not employees of Weekend Directional Services.
  • You are responsible for your own fuel, expenses, taxes, and insurance
  • You choose how to complete your route within the time windows
  • No benefits or guaranteed hours are provided
  • You may accept or decline routes, but must complete any route you commit to

Apply Now
We have immediate openings in multiple areas and are looking for dependable individuals ready to get started.

title: Subcontract Administrator
description:
Subcontract Administrator

Job Summary:
The Subcontract Administrator will create and review industry subcontract agreements. The duties will include negotiating terms and conditions with each party, analyzing potential risks involved with subcontract clauses, helping vendors, employees and leadership better understand and comply with the requirements. The Subcontract Administrator will manage the process for contractual documents proceeding efficiently through review and approval processes with the goal of maximizing financial and operational performance and minimizing risk.

Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Review and/or prepare subcontracts, contracts, agreements, amendments, change orders, business proposals, non-disclosure agreements, rental agreements and other contractual documents.

  • Take sufficient steps to identify project risks

  • Liaise with and support the Project Managers to ensure the project is executed in compliance with terms and conditions

  • Participate in the development of new business proposals, ensuring compliance with terms and conditions.

  • Ensure compliance with the company’s policies, standards, and procedures

  • Prepare and review subcontracts in cooperation with Supply Chain and Procurement, insuring flow down of requirements

  • Prepare monthly project reports and make presentations at meetings

  • Support negotiations of claims, manage contractual changes and resolve disputes or conflict resolution with Contractors and Customers

  • Assess and prepare claims from suppliers

  • Manage contract closeout procedures

  • Confer with counsel and leadership on items out of the ordinary or carrying significant risk

  • Support supply chain in supplier and vendor certification and compliance

  • Assist in debriefings, resolving disputes, claims, litigation and settlements

  • Ensure completeness of contract files and records.

Required Qualifications and Skills:

  • BA/BS degree in contract management, business management, procurement, law or a related field preferred

  • A minimum of 5 years’ experience in any combination of the following areas: contracts, subcontracts or purchasing.

  • US Citizenship Required

  • Demonstrated experience in Project Subcontract Administration required

  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret contractual and legal documents, financial reports and technical documents

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Must possess excellent organizational skills, problem solving, and decision-making skills.

  • A working knowledge of federal government procurement procedures

  • Good understanding of Federal Acquisition Regulations, industrial standard operating procedures (SOPs) and occupational, industrial regulations and law

  • Ability to maintain integrity and confidentiality while working with purchasing information and other pertinent, sensitive information.

  • Excellent computer skills is a must, including a variety of software applications; tracking/scheduling software and Microsoft Products

  • Time management, organization, and problem-solving skills

  • Detail oriented

Desired Qualifications and Skills:

  • Certified Professional Contract Manager (CPCM) certification desired

  • Knowledge of operations, program management, project management, product development, and procurement desired

  • Expertise working with cross-functional teams

  • Experience in aerospace preferred

  • Preferred familiar with ISO9001/AS9100

  • Advanced understanding of purchasing and supply chain procedures

Comprehensive Benefits & Perks:

title: Social Services Director
description:
Healthcare, Dental, Vision

Paid Time Off

Excellent Pay

Your Job

The Social Services Director will be responsible for planning, developing, organizing, evaluating and directing the overall operation of the Social Services department in accordance with the National Association of Social Workers (NASW) Code of Ethics and in compliance with Federal, State, and Local guidelines and regulations, company policies and procedures, and governing agencies. Responsible for fostering a climate, policies and routines that enable residents to maximize their individuality, independence and dignity. This climate should provide residents with the highest practical level of physical, mental and psychosocial well-being and quality of life. Responsible for identifying psychosocial, mental and emotional needs along with providing, developing, and/or aiding in the access of services to meet those needs.

Qualifications

• One year of supervisory social work experience in a healthcare setting working directly with geriatric individuals.

• Minimum of 2 years of nursing experience in a Skilled Nursing Facility preferred.

Principal Responsibilities

• Plans, organizes, implements, evaluates, and directs a comprehensive Social Services program.

• Assist the Social Service Consultant in the planning, developing, organizing, implementing, evaluating, and directing of the social service programs of the facility; Participates in reviewing and setting policies concerning resident care and quality of life; Participates in developing facility social work policies.

• Prepares Social Services department for annual survey.

• Works with Social Services staff, interdisciplinary team, and administration to promote and protect resident rights and the psychological well-being of all residents/residents. Prevents and addresses resident/resident abuse as mandated by law and professional licensure.

• Completes social history and psychosocial assessment for each resident that identifies social, emotional, and psychological needs; Completed relevant parts of the minimum data set (MDS); Utilizes the minimum data set to guide the care plan.

• Maintains accurate and timely documentation which complies with federal/state regulations, The Company Corporate policy, and specific center practices, including, but not limited to, Advanced Directives, Minimum Data Set, Social Service History and Assessment, Raps, Care Plans, Social Service Progress Notes, Behavior Tracking, monitoring of cognitive and psychosocial changes, PASARR and Discharge Planning documentation, and psych services.

• Supports each resident’s/resident’s right to self-determination; Documents resident/resident refusal of services offered; Informs resident/resident of any therapeutic alternatives to the refused service; Involves others, as appropriate, to help educate the resident/resident about the alternatives.

• Participates in the development of a written, interdisciplinary plan of care for each resident that identifies the psychosocial needs/issues of the resident, the goals to be accomplished for those needs/issues, and the appropriate social worker interventions.

• Ensures or provides therapeutic interventions to assist residents in coping with their transition and adjustment to a long-term care facility, including their social, emotional, and psychological needs.

• Ensures or provides support and education to residents/family members/significant others to assist in their understanding of placement and facility issues in addition to referring them to the appropriate social service agencies when the facility does not provide the needed services.

• Coordinates the resident discharge planning process and make referrals for appropriate home care services prior to the resident’s return to the community.

• As part of interdisciplinary care team, identifies discharge teaching needs; Communicates with center team members the estimated discharge date and updating Point Click Care; Makes referrals as needed for post discharge care to appropriate agencies and suppliers.

• Initiates and participates in completion of Discharge Transition Plan & Discharge packet materials and orienting the resident/resident and family around the process.

• Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or assigned at any time with or without notice.

title: DoW Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM)
description:
Tetrad Digital Integrity (TDI) is a leading-edge cybersecurity firm with a mission to safeguard and protect our customers from increasing threats and vulnerabilities in this digital age.

TDI is seeking a Risk Management Framework (RMF) subject matter experts as Information Systems Security Managers to support cloud-based and Artificial Intelligence (AI) integrated systems. We are looking for candidates who have demonstrated experience building and maintaining RMF packages from development and through sustainment, are technically sharp, and ready to work in a fast-paced environment on some of the nations most advanced systems. We need experts who can support ATO efforts and turn DoW Component RMF, NIST 800-53, and Cloud SRG guidance into clear, defensible deliverables. These roles require in-depth knowledge of DoW requirements and the ability to independently lead and support complex systems integrating cloud IaaS/SaaS, custom applications and AI. if you’re eager to build credibility fast, experience cutting edge technology, leading artificial intelligence models, and make a visible impact on mission systems—including cloud-native, containerized workloads—you’ll fit right in.
The position is remote requiring a Secret or Top-secret, active clearance.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Lead and support RMF execution and customer coordination in an IL 5/6 environment
  • Provide expert guidance on DoW cloud security policies, NIST SP 800-53 controls, CNSS policies, and DoW-specific frameworks such as Cloud Computing SRG and AI-specific guidance.
  • Conduct security architecture reviews and security engineering analysis for cloud-native and containerized workloads.
  • Evaluate security controls associated with Kubernetes, Docker, and container orchestration platforms within cloud infrastructure.
  • Assess security risks related to generative AI components, including large language models (LLMs) and AI/ML workloads, ensuring responsible and compliant use.
  • Develop and maintain System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and related RMF documentation.
  • Perform threat modeling, vulnerability assessments, and risk analysis tailored to cloud environments and AI technologies.
  • Interface with system architects, developers, and DevSecOps teams to integrate security throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC).
  • Support security control assessments (SCAs) and coordinate with third-party assessors.
  • Monitor, track, and report on security compliance posture through Continuous Monitoring (ConMon) processes.
  • Minimal travel will be required.
QUALIFICATIONS:
  • Active Secret or Top-secret security clearance.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or Information Technology, and 8+ years of cybersecurity experience, including demonstrated experience supporting Risk Management Framework (RMF) activities for Department of War (DoW) systems.
  • Security certifications such as Certified Information System Security Professional (CISSP) and/or Certified Information System Manager (CISM).
  • Practical knowledge and application of concepts with cloud platforms. Experience with AWS, Azure and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including IAM, VPC, Kubernetes, and security-related services are preferable.
  • Strong knowledge of containerized environments (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) and container security best practices.
  • Familiarity with Generative AI technologies, including LLMs and AI/ML security considerations.
  • Deep understanding of NIST SP 800-53, DoD RMF, FedRAMP, and other relevant cybersecurity frameworks.
  • Experience with security risk assessments in DoW environments.
PAY RANGE:
The anticipated salary range for this position is $150,000 - $180,000. This range is a good-faith estimate and not a guarantee of compensation. Final compensation will be based on factors including experience, education, skills, geographic location, internal equity, market data and applicable contract requirements, and may fall outside the posted range.

TDI does business with the federal government, which restricts employment to individuals who are either US citizens or lawful permanent residents of the United States.

“TDI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made based on individual qualifications, merit, and business needs. We do not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin, in accordance with applicable federal laws.”

  • Ability to hear bells, alarms, whistles, etc.
  • Employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
Work Environment: While performing the duties of this job, the employee regularly works on-site at the hydroelectric facility work site where there is exposure to moving mechanical parts; high precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; outside weather conditions and risk of electrical shock. The noise in these work environments is usually moderate to very loud.

JOB TITLE: SUD Counselor I

Who are we?
Horizon Services, Inc. (HSI) is a nonprofit established in 1974 with the goal of reducing substance use-related challenges for people from all walks of life, including those from some of the most disenfranchised and marginalized communities. Providing exceptional services to our diverse community. We are proud to support Behavioral Health Services Department (BHSD) clients in their preferred languages, ensuring accessibility and inclusivity for all.
We practice our values of Integrity, Compassion, Respect, and Professionalism to provide residential treatment, withdrawal management, and sobering programs to support the well-being of women, men, youth, LGBTQ, and BIPOC clients to live healthy, fulfilling and constructive lives. How can you make a difference in people’s lives?

We are seeking a SUD Counselor I who is passionate about serving diverse communities. Bilingual candidates fluent in one or more of BHSD’s threshold languages—Chinese, Spanish, Tagalog, or Vietnamese—are eligible for an additional incentive.


This position is responsible for collaborating with the Program Manager or Director of Outpatient and Prevention Programs on creating a welcoming atmosphere for incoming clients, monitoring and preparing them for continued treatment in the broader system of care. The position will perform intakes/admissions, treatment plans, monitoring of client’s progress, maintaining documentation per organization’s guidelines, discharges and resources to assist the client in finding appropriate ongoing services as well as overseeing the activities of other staff and provide guidance when needed.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities

  • Perform client admissions, transfers, assessments, referrals, and discharges daily

  • Maintain a positive, welcoming approach with all incoming and present clients at the Detoxification Center
  • Provide ASAM screening and assessment at intake
  • Ensure daily census requirements are being met as directed by manager by ensuring that appointments are scheduled quickly and with minimal delay from treatment request to first appointment
  • Perform initial screening/assessment, recovery and treatment planning/problem list and individual check-in with clients to ensure goals are being achieved
  • Provide daily recovery plan meeting with clients to update Detoxification and referral progress.
  • Reconcile daily logs, rosters, and other census information to ensure daily census accuracy
  • Develop initial ongoing ASAM-informed referral and discharge planning with clients
  • Meet weekly for group clinical supervision
  • Inputs data into HSI’s Electronic Health Record System (EHR) and/or the EHR platform of the County funder
  • Maintain appropriate records in the EHR
  • Daily monitoring and maintenance of client EHR for errors, correcting and updating
  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships with all staff members and community organizations
  • Coordinate with program Case Manager to ensure referral mechanisms are properly engaged to maximize post-discharge treatment
  • Maintain attendance and punctuality to perform duties as scheduled
  • Attend all staff meetings and required agency meetings unless excused
  • Responsible for always maintaining a clean environment
  • Responsible for informing Program Manager or Director of Outpatient and Prevention Programs of perceived household, environmental, participant, and personal needs when appropriate
  • Maintain a basic knowledge of medications used by clients
  • Drive program vehicle when necessary
  • Confer with staff and other individuals in agency regarding participants
  • Perform any other duties as assigned
  • Performs vitals sign patient self-monitoring tasks as needed to ensure clients fall within established safe stabilization guidelines, if applicable at program site.
  • Performs withdrawal assessment scoring duties to ensure clients fall within established safe stabilization guidelines, if applicable at program site.
  • Responsible for supervising meal preparation and, when necessary, preparing and serving meals
  • Adheres to confidentiality requirements as governed by HIPAA and 42 CFR

Success Competencies for the Position

  • Client Focus – Gains insight into client needs, quickly establishes rapport and relationships using evidence based practices, provides compassionate and empathic client care to all program participants
  • Problem Solving – uses logic and methods to solve difficult problems with effective solutions…looks beyond the obvious and doesn’t stop at the first answer.
  • Being Resilient- Rebounds from setbacks faced in a high stress environment. Handles and manages crises effectively. Maintains stability when faced with conflict.
  • Interpersonal Communication- delivers effective communication with a wide range of audiences. Addresses miscommunication quickly and appropriately. Convey information clearly.

Functional/Technical Skills and Knowledge
Technical Training or Knowledge

  • Certification or registration with either Substance Use state certifying body in California (CAADE/CCAPP/CADTP),
  • Excellent computer skills, knowledge of data capture and data input into Electronic Health Records.
  • Knowledge of alcohol and drug addiction (substance use disorder)
  • Knowledge of social model detox concepts
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills

Experience

  • Experience working with customers or clients that feel overwhelmed or in a crisis (crisis intervention).
  • Experience working with diverse populations and cultures
  • Experience working with customers or clients with co-occurring disorders and disabilities

Qualifications

  • Certification or registration with either Substance Use state certifying body in California (CAADE/CCAPP/CADTP)
  • Preferred: Bilingual in English, Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese, or Tagalog

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Note: Please use the percentage time spent in these requirements. Other duties
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

title: Technical Client Service Specialist
description:
Your future is bright at AGAT


AGAT Laboratories is seeking a Technical Client Services Specialist to join our Environmental Division in Calgary.

This is not a traditional customer service position – it is an opportunity for a technically minded, ambitious individual to become an important link between our clients and our laboratory operations. You will work directly with clients, understand their analytical needs, coordinate with our scientific and operational teams, solve problems and help ensure an exceptional client experience. We are looking for someone who wants to build a career—not simply fill a position. For this opportunity, we are seeking someone who can combine technical aptitude with exceptional people skills.

The Opportunity:
As a Technical Client Services Specialist, you will develop a strong understanding of environmental laboratory services while building relationships with clients and working closely with AGAT's laboratory professionals.

You will take ownership of the client experience from sample submission through analysis, reporting and final delivery. This position offers exposure to laboratory operations, technical services and client management and provides an opportunity to develop broader responsibilities as your knowledge and capabilities grow.

For an individual with initiative, strong communication skills and an interest in science, this can be the beginning of a rewarding long-term career with AGAT. Above all, you will help deliver AGAT's commitment to Service Beyond Analysis.

What you will be doing:
  • Serve as a primary point of contact and trusted resource for Environmental clients.
  • Build and maintain strong client relationships through face-to-face meetings, telephone conversations and ongoing communication.
  • Develop an understanding of each client's business, analytical requirements and expectations.
  • Act as the link between clients and AGAT's laboratory and operational teams.
  • Take ownership of client projects and help ensure commitments are met.
  • Monitor projects and work orders as they progress through the laboratory.
  • Proactively communicate project status, laboratory updates and potential turnaround-time delays.
  • Coordinate with laboratory and operational teams regarding client projects, technical questions and reanalysis requirements.
  • Communicate sample integrity concerns and work with clients and laboratory personnel toward appropriate solutions.
  • Ensure accurate and timely delivery of sample receipt notifications, certificates of analysis, reports, exports and invoices.
  • Identify opportunities to improve analytical packages, reporting formats and the overall client experience.
  • Maintain accurate client information and special instructions within AGAT's systems.
  • Participate in ongoing technical, client-service and professional development.

Who we are looking for:

  • A diploma or degree in Science, Environmental Science, Chemistry or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of client-facing experience is preferred.
  • Minimum one to two years of laboratory or customer service expeirence.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Confidence communicating directly with clients and technical professionals.
  • The ability to develop relationships and earn the trust of clients and colleagues.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to quality.
  • Initiative, curiosity and strong problem-solving ability.
  • The confidence to take ownership of an issue and follow it through to resolution.
  • The ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment while managing competing priorities.
  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office. Experience with Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) or reporting systems is an asset.
  • A collaborative approach and genuine desire to learn and develop.

Who We Are:

AGAT Laboratories is a premier full-service laboratory operating at the cutting edge of science and innovation across North America. Our expertise spans geochemistry, biochemistry, chemistry, microbiology, geology, and engineering, enabling us to deliver comprehensive analytical solutions. These services drive progress in industries such as Mining, Environmental, Energy, Transportation, Industrial, Agri-Food, and Life Sciences.

We pride ourselves on our state-of-the-art technology, diverse expertise, and commitment to providing precise, timely, and reliable results. Beyond our technical excellence, AGAT Laboratories believes in the power of strong client relationships, fostering trust and collaboration to ensure mutual success.

Our Commitment to Community and Philanthropy:

At AGAT, we strive not only to advance science but also to make a positive impact in our communities. The AGAT Foundation is at the heart of our philanthropic efforts, supporting initiatives that improve education, environmental stewardship, and community well-being.

Through partnerships with local organizations, volunteer activities, and donations, the AGAT Foundation champions programs that inspire future generations, promote sustainable practices, and provide support to those in need. Whether funding scholarships, participating in environmental cleanups, or supporting health and wellness initiatives, AGAT is deeply invested in giving back.

Our work extends beyond the laboratory—we’re committed to creating a brighter future for our employees, clients, and the communities we serve.

Join AGAT Laboratories to be part of an organization that values not just scientific innovation but also meaningful connections and lasting contributions to society.

Inclusion and Diversity:

AGAT Laboratories is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. If you require accommodation during any stage of the recruitment process, please inform us confidentially, and we will work to meet your needs.
Thank You for Your Interest:

We appreciate the time and effort of every applicant. Only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

title: Senior Accessibility Subject Matter Expert
description:
At Team Carney, we believe that true performance acceleration happens at the intersection of innovative learning and deep strategic expertise. Since 1994, our mission has been to provide top-tier training, learning, and human capital solutions that empower Federal Government agencies to meet their critical mandates. We are seeking a highly experienced Senior Accessibility Subject Matter Expert to support our federal client.

This position is contingent on contract award.

Work Schedule and Location

  • Employment Status: Full-Time

  • Location: This position is fully remote, based out of Fredericksburg, VA.

Who You Are & What You’ll Do

The Senior Accessibility Subject Matter Expert will serve as a senior strategic and technical authority for Section 508 compliance, accessibility governance, and Information and Communications Technology (ICT) quality assurance.

In this full-time role, you will perform high-level Section 508 testing of web content and electronic documents using Department of Homeland Security (DHS) approved assessment methods, conduct quality control reviews of test results completed by HQ 508 Program Trusted Testers, and provide end-to-end document remediation. Beyond testing and remediation, you will guide ICT project and acquisition efforts by evaluating Accessibility Conformance Reports (ACRs) / Voluntary Product Accessibility Templates (VPATs), advising project teams and senior management on accessibility risks throughout the System Development Lifecycle (SDLC), and serving as an operational back-up to the Government Section 508 Program.

What You Bring to the Table - Requirements

  • Certifications:

    • Active DHS Trusted Tester Version 5.0 (or later) Certification required.

    • Active IAAP Certified Professional in Accessibility Core Competencies (CPACC) Certification required.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.

  • Technical Experience:

    • 7+ years of overall experience working in Information and Communications Technology (ICT) environments.

    • 2+ years of dedicated experience testing web electronic content and applications for conformance to Section 508 Standards.

    • 2+ years of dedicated experience testing and remediating electronic documents and forms (e.g., Microsoft Office Suite, Adobe PDF) to Section 508 standards.

    • 3+ years of experience supporting ICT project and acquisition efforts by integrating Section 508 requirements across defined lifecycle stages.

  • Core Capabilities:

    • Quality Control & Review: Proven ability to conduct thorough quality checks and peer reviews of Section 508 test results submitted by HQ 508 Program Trusted Testers.

    • SDLC & Governance Advisory: Extensive experience advising project teams and senior leadership on Section 508 compliance, accessibility risk assessment, and technical remediation strategies throughout the system development lifecycle.

    • Acquisition & VPAT/ACR Evaluation: Technical expertise responding to complex accessibility inquiries during vendor product evaluations, including analyzing ACRs and VPATs.

    • Testing & Document Remediation: Advanced capability in developing accessibility test plans, interpreting test outputs, and performing hands-on remediation of complex electronic documents and forms using Federal CIO Council Community of Practice endorsed tests.

    • Programmatic Support: Ability to act as a reliable back-up to the Government Section 508 Program office as needed.

Why Join Team Carney?

When you join Team Carney, you join a legacy of excellence. We focus on our people because when we make a positive impact on the lives of our employees, they are able to make a positive impact on our clients. We offer a full suite of competitive benefits, including:

  • Health & Wellness: Multiple medical, dental, and vision insurance options (BCBS CareFirst), health spending accounts (HSA), and flexible spending accounts (FSA).

  • Financial Security: 401(k) retirement plan with company match, plus Carney-paid life and disability insurance.

  • Work-Life Harmony: Generous Paid Time Off (PTO), 11 paid holidays, and 6 weeks of paid parental leave.

  • Professional & Personal Growth: Annual tuition assistance (up to $5,000) and student loan repayment.

  • Get Out and Learn: Up to $200 annually to learn almost anything (from pottery to coding!).

  • Get Out and Run: Up to $200 annually to participate in fitness and active lifestyle events.

  • Continuous Development: Ad hoc training and ongoing professional development access.

title: Construction Inspector
description:
KDG Construction Consulting is seeking a highly motivated Construction Inspector to provide quality assurance and construction inspection services for large-scale building and infrastructure projects. This position supports inspection activities across multiple construction projects, with a primary focus on civil construction and infrastructure disciplines. The ideal candidate will possess extensive experience performing construction inspections on heavy civil, roadway, structural, and public works projects, a strong understanding of applicable construction standards and specifications, and the ability to effectively coordinate with contractors, engineers, inspectors, and project stakeholders in a fast-paced construction environment.

Key Responsibilities:
• Perform comprehensive daily inspections of civil construction activities to ensure compliance with applicable standards, contract documents, plans, specifications, and project requirements.
• Review and interpret construction drawings, specifications, contract documents, submittals, Requests for Information (RFIs), and change orders.
• Prepare detailed daily inspection reports documenting construction activities, progress, deficiencies, safety concerns, and corrective actions, clearly identifying the WHO, WHAT, WHEN, WHERE, and HOW of work performed.
• Perform inspections of major reinforced concrete structures, including pile foundations, roadways, bridges, and related structural elements.
• Conduct inspections for the installation of sanitary sewer systems and storm drain systems, including related structures, in accordance with applicable City and County standards.
• Perform inspections of utility infrastructure, including underground utilities and related civil construction.
• Perform inspections for the installation of street lighting and traffic signal systems in accordance with applicable plans, specifications, and requirements.
• Apply knowledge of applicable City, County, and Caltrans Standard Plans and Specifications and the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (Greenbook).
• Ensure compliance with multi-phased, site-specific traffic control plans, with a strong emphasis on pedestrian safety and routing.
• Apply and enforce applicable Cal-OSHA, contractor, and project-specific safety requirements.
• Track and document time-and-material work, field changes, installed quantities, and other construction activities as assigned.
• Assist in reviewing and validating contractor monthly progress payment requests based on completed and approved work and schedules of values.
• Utilize electronic equipment and project management systems to review construction plans and contract documents and maintain inspection records and project documentation.
• Coordinate with project managers, contractors, engineers, consultants, testing agencies, and other project stakeholders to resolve field issues and maintain construction quality.
• Perform additional project-related duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:
• High school diploma or equivalent.
• Current Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS) Deputy Inspector License in either Grading or Post-Tensioning (Pre-Stressed).
• Minimum of five (5) years of experience performing inspection of Caltrans bridge, roadway, and structure projects, or a minimum of ten (10) years of experience as a Superintendent on Caltrans bridge, roadway, and structures projects.
• Minimum of ten (10) years of experience in public works field inspection, with a focus on heavy civil and roadway construction, or a minimum of ten (10) years of experience as a Superintendent on Caltrans bridge, roadway, and structures projects.
• Proven expertise in the installation and inspection of sewer and storm drain systems, utility infrastructure, and traffic control measures.
• Strong working knowledge of City of Los Angeles, County of Los Angeles, and Caltrans standards, standard plans, and specifications.
• Cal-OSHA 30-Hour training completed within the last four (4) years prior to assignment/start date.
• Ability to work effectively and communicate professionally in a team-oriented environment.
• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
• Ability to work flexible schedules, including day, swing, night, weekend, holiday, and overtime shifts as required.
• Ability to walk long distances, navigate active construction sites, climb stairs and ladders, and access construction areas as required by project activities and applicable safety procedures.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Outlook, Adobe Acrobat Pro, Bluebeam, PM Web, ProCore, and similar construction project management and document control systems.
• Strong ability to review and utilize electronic contract documents, including drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, and change orders.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
• Strong organizational, documentation, and time management skills.
• Ability to maintain effective working relationships with contractors, consultants, clients, inspectors, engineers, and project stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Current Caltrans test method certifications in the 100, 200, 300, and 500 series.
• Experience inspecting major reinforced concrete structures, including pile foundations, roadways, bridges, and related structural elements.
• Experience inspecting sanitary sewer systems, storm drain systems, utility infrastructure, traffic control measures, street lighting, and traffic signal systems.
• Experience applying City of Los Angeles, County of Los Angeles, and Caltrans Standard Plans and Specifications and the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (Greenbook).
• Experience with contractor monthly progress payment requests, schedules of values, and installed quantity verification.
• Experience with comprehensive daily inspection reporting and construction documentation.
• Experience coordinating inspections with contractors, engineers, consultants, testing agencies, and other project stakeholders.
• Strong understanding of construction quality assurance practices, inspection procedures, and compliance requirements.
• Experience utilizing PM Web, ProCore, Bluebeam, or similar project management and document control software.
• Experience performing construction inspection across multiple phases of civil and infrastructure projects.

Anticipated Salary Range: $140,000.00 – $160,000.00 per year

title: AI Engineer with TS/SCI Clearance & Full Scope Polygraph - Hybrid role in Annapolis Junction
description:
An active Top Secret/SCI Clearance with a Full Scope Polygraph is required.

This is a hybrid schedule with up to 3 days/week remote and 2 days/week onsite in Annapolis Junction, MD.

We have an immediate need for an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Engineer to support the development and sustainment of mission-focused AI capabilities. The AI Engineer will work closely with system and software engineers to design, prototype, and integrate AI-enabled capabilities into existing software architectures. This role centers on applying existing large language models (LLMs) to real mission workflows rather than training new models. The AI Engineer will build agentic solutions, systems of coordinated AI agents and prompts, that automate tasks currently performed manually, streamline authoring and reporting workflows, and enhance the overall effectiveness of intelligence operations.

Responsibilities

• Agentic Solution Design & Development: Lead the design and development of AI-driven solutions from conception to deployment, building multi-agent workflows in which coordinated agents and prompts work together to produce outputs supporting reporting and dissemination. This includes prototyping, writing production-quality code, and maintaining deployed AI capabilities.

• LLM Integration: Integrate existing foundation models into existing software architectures via APIs and orchestration frameworks, selecting the right model and approach for each task rather than building models from scratch.

• Prompt Engineering & Workflow Automation: Design, test, and refine prompts and agent instructions to reliably automate manual tasks, and decompose complex mission workflows into discrete steps an agent pipeline can execute.

• Evaluation & Reliability: Develop robust testing, evaluation, and validation strategies for AI-generated outputs, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and appropriate handling of edge cases before outputs reach analysts and reports.

• Collaboration & Communication: Serve as a key technical liaison, collaborating with cross-functional teams including system engineers, software developers, and domain experts. Effectively present and articulate recommended AI approaches, discussing the tradeoffs and implications of different implementations with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Continuous Improvement: Stay current with the rapidly evolving LLM and agentic AI landscape (new models, orchestration frameworks, and tooling), continuously identifying practical opportunities to apply emerging capabilities to the system.

Required Technical Skills

• Strong Python development skills, with experience writing production-quality, maintainable code

• Hands-on experience building applications on top of existing LLMs (e.g., via APIs for commercial or self-hosted models)

• Experience designing multi-agent or multi-step AI workflows, including prompt chaining, tool use, and agent orchestration (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom frameworks)

• Strong prompt engineering skills and experience evaluating/validating LLM outputs

• Experience integrating AI capabilities into existing software architectures (RESTful APIs, microservices)

• Experience with the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud computing platform

Desired Technical Skills

• Experience with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines and vector databases

• Familiarity with LLM observability and evaluation tooling

• Experience conducting exploratory data analysis on structured and unstructured datasets to prepare inputs for AI workflows

• Familiarity with MLOps/LLMOps practices for deploying and monitoring AI capabilities at scale

• Familiarity with domain knowledge surrounding government agency reporting and dissemination policies
