title: Physical Therapist (PT) – Mobile/Home-Based Care
description:
Overview

We are seeking a skilled, compassionate, and dependable Physical Therapist (PT) to provide high-quality physical therapy services to patients in their homes throughout the Dallas, TX region.

The Physical Therapist will travel to patients' homes to perform comprehensive evaluations, develop individualized plans of care, provide skilled therapeutic interventions, monitor patient progress, and educate patients and caregivers on strategies to improve mobility, function, safety, and independence.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working independently in a home-based environment, has strong clinical judgment and communication skills, and is passionate about delivering patient-centered care.

This is a 1099 independent contractor position.

Duties and Responsibilities

· Travel to patients' homes throughout the assigned service area to provide physical therapy services.

· Perform comprehensive physical therapy evaluations in the patient's home environment.

· Assess strength, range of motion, balance, gait, mobility, coordination, endurance, pain, functional limitations, and ability to safely perform activities of daily living.

· Evaluate the patient's home environment and identify potential safety and fall risks that may impact mobility and independence.

· Develop individualized plans of care based on evaluation findings, physician orders/referrals, patient needs, clinical judgment, and functional goals.

· Establish measurable short-term and long-term functional goals.

· Provide skilled physical therapy interventions appropriate to the patient's diagnosis and functional limitations, including:

o Therapeutic exercises

o Therapeutic activities

o Neuromuscular re-education

o Gait and mobility training

o Balance and coordination training

o Functional strengthening

o Manual therapy when clinically appropriate

o Transfer training

o Fall prevention and safety training

· Train patients in the safe use of assistive devices such as walkers, canes, and other mobility equipment.

· Develop and instruct patients in individualized home exercise programs.

· Educate patients and caregivers regarding diagnosis, treatment, exercises, mobility, safety, fall prevention, and strategies to promote independence.

· Monitor patient response to treatment and make appropriate clinical modifications to the plan of care.

· Perform reassessments and communicate changes in patient condition or functional status as appropriate.

· Coordinate care with physicians, nurses, caregivers, physical therapist assistants, occupational therapists, and other healthcare professionals.

· Communicate effectively with referring providers regarding patient progress, concerns, and recommendations.

· Complete accurate, timely, and thorough documentation for evaluations, daily treatment visits, reassessments, progress reports, and discharge summaries.

· Maintain compliance with applicable federal and state regulations, professional standards, payer requirements, and company policies.

· Recognize changes in patient condition that may require physician notification, additional medical evaluation, or modification of treatment.

· Maintain patient confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries at all times.

· Provide compassionate, respectful, and professional care to patients and their families in the home setting.

Requirements

· Current and valid Texas Physical Therapist license in good standing.

· Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapy program.

· Strong knowledge of anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, and rehabilitation principles.

· Strong clinical reasoning and patient assessment skills.

· Ability to independently perform comprehensive PT evaluations and develop appropriate plans of care.

· Experience treating patients with orthopedic, musculoskeletal, neurological, balance, gait, weakness, mobility, and/or functional limitations preferred.

· Strong knowledge of therapeutic exercise, gait training, balance training, functional mobility, neuromuscular re-education, and fall prevention.

· Excellent patient assessment and acute/chronic pain management skills.

· Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

· Ability to work independently and effectively manage a mobile patient caseload.

· Must be punctual, dependable, organized, and professional.

· Comfortable entering and providing care in patients' homes and working with patients and caregivers in a home-based environment.

· Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required.

· Ability to travel throughout the assigned service area.

· CPR/BLS certification preferred or required according to company policy.

· Previous home health, mobile therapy, outpatient, orthopedic, neurological, geriatric, or community-based experience is preferred.

Mobile/Home-Based Care Expectations

Because this position involves providing care in patients' homes, the Physical Therapist must be able to:

· Arrive at scheduled visits within the expected timeframe.

· Manage travel time and maintain an efficient daily schedule.

· Carry and transport necessary clinical equipment and supplies.

· Adapt treatment approaches to different home environments and available space.

· Maintain a safe and professional environment during every patient visit.

· Communicate promptly regarding cancellations, scheduling changes, or patient concerns.

· Respect patients' homes, privacy, routines, and individual preferences.

· Demonstrate sound clinical judgment when working independently in the community.

Documentation and Compliance

The Physical Therapist is responsible for completing all required clinical documentation accurately and within established timeframes, including:

· Initial evaluations

· Treatment notes

· Reassessments

· Progress reports

· Recertifications, when applicable

· Discharge documentation

· Home exercise programs

· Communication with referring providers

· Other documentation required by the organization, payer, or applicable regulations

Job Type

Full-time – 1099 Independent Contractor

Pay Structure (1099)

· Guaranteed base pay: $1,080 per week

· Base compensation is calculated at $45 per patient visit, based on a minimum of 6 patient visits per day.

· $45 per additional patient visit for visits beyond the daily base of 6.

· Compensation is subject to the terms of the independent contractor agreement.

Schedule

4/10 Schedule

· Four 10-hour workdays per week

· Typical start time: 7:30 AM–8:30 AM, depending on patient scheduling and geographic coverage.

· Daily schedule may vary based on patient locations, visit duration, and patient needs.

Work Location

Mobile/Home-Based – Dallas, TX Region

The Physical Therapist will travel to assigned patients' homes throughout the designated service area.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a clinically confident, compassionate, and self-motivated Physical Therapist who enjoys working one-on-one with patients and families. The successful candidate will be comfortable making clinical decisions independently, adapting treatment to the patient's home environment, and providing high-quality care while maintaining excellent documentation and communication.

This position is an excellent opportunity for a Physical Therapist who values autonomy, flexibility, meaningful patient relationships, and community-based care

description:

title: Legal Intern

location: Administration, Central Office, Rapid City, SD, US
description:
SUMMER INTERNSHIP

Position Title: Legal Intern

Reports To: General Counsel or Designee

Job Summary:

The Summer Legal Intern supports the legal, compliance, governance, and policy functions of a tribal health organization operating under a 638 framework. This paid internship is designed for a qualified first- or second-year American Indian/Alaska Native law student with a demonstrated interest in healthcare law, Federal Indian law, tribal governance, and self-determination.

The Summer Legal Intern will gain practical experience through legal research, writing, policy analysis, contract review support, and special projects related to tribal health operations. The intern will have an opportunity to learn about the legal and regulatory environment affecting tribal health organizations, including Public Law 93-638, tribal sovereignty, healthcare operations, compliance, employment matters, governance, and related legal issues.

This position offers meaningful exposure to mission-driven legal work that supports tribal communities, health equity, and organizational excellence.

Essential Functions:

The following functions are fundamental to the position and are required of all incumbents, with or without reasonable accommodation. These functions define the role and are not an exhaustive list of all duties.

• Conducts legal research and analysis on matters related to healthcare law, Federal Indian law, tribal sovereignty, Public Law 93-638, employment law, privacy, compliance, governance, and administrative law.

• Assists in drafting legal memoranda, briefing materials, summaries, correspondence, and issue analyses for leadership and internal stakeholders.

• Supports review of policies, procedures, contracts, agreements, and other organizational documents for legal and operational consistency.

• Assists with research and project work involving tribal health systems, self-governance, self-determination, and regulatory compliance.

• Organizes and summarizes legal and regulatory information in a clear, practical format for operational use.

• Participates in meetings with legal, executive, compliance, operational, and departmental leaders as appropriate.

• Assists with special projects involving governance, risk management, workforce issues, healthcare operations, and strategic initiatives.

• Maintains confidentiality of sensitive legal, personnel, operational, and organizational information.

• Supports the development of legal resource materials, templates, trackers, and internal guidance documents.

• Performs other related duties as assigned in support of organizational operations and internship learning objectives.

Physical and Environment Requirements

This position requires the ability to perform the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. Physical demands and work environment may include:

• Primarily sedentary work is performed in an office or administrative setting.

• Requires the ability to sit for extended periods and regularly use standard office equipment such as a computer, keyboard, telephone, and copier.

• Occasional standing, walking, bending, and reaching may be required.

• Ability to lift and carry office materials or supplies up to 25 pounds occasionally.

• Requires manual dexterity and visual acuity for computer use and document review.

• Must be able to read, write, speak, and hear.

• Work is performed primarily in an indoor office or administrative environment.

• The environment involves everyday risks or discomforts that require normal safety precautions typical of office settings, including proper use of office equipment and awareness of trips, falls, and fire regulations.

• The work area is adequately lighted, heated, and ventilated.

• Minimal exposure to hazardous conditions; no routine exposure to clinical, field, or high risk environments.

• Occasional attendance at meetings, training sessions, or events may require travel within the organization's facilities.

Education/Experience/Certificates/Credentials

Minimum Qualifications

• Current first-year or second-year law student in good standing at an accredited law school.

• American Indian or Alaska Native student preferred and/or eligible for Native preference consideration consistent with applicable law and organizational policy.

• Demonstrated interest in healthcare law, Federal Indian law, tribal law, 638/self-governance issues, public service, or related legal fields.

• Strong legal research, writing, and analytical skills.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion with sensitive information.

• Ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with supervisors and internal stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

• Lived, academic, or professional experience related to tribal communities, tribal governance, Indian health systems, or Native-serving institutions.

• Prior coursework or experience in Indian law, administrative law, health law, employment law, or public policy.

• Experience with legal research platforms such as Westlaw or Lexis.

• Interest in long-term work supporting tribal organizations, public health, or Native communities.

The GPTLHB is a tribal organization which follows tribal preference laws. It is our policy to give preference

to qualified Indian/Tribal candidates over qualified non-native candidates in hiring decisions, if all other

qualifications are equal.

Employment is contingent upon the outcome of all required criminal background checks and drug test.

Compliance with our Employee Health Procedure is a condition of employment. You are required to

agree that you will comply with all job-related employee health screening and immunizations prior

to your first day of employment. Jobs require that you have documentation that you have

completed the following immunizations prior to your first day of employment: MMR (Measles,

Mumps and Rubella, Varicella (Chicken Pox), Hepatitis B, Influenza, T-dap (Tetanus - Diphtheria -

Pertussis), and COVID-19 vaccination is required.

title: Job Coach
description:
Job Coach / Employment Specialist – Part-Time

Location: Georgetown, Delaware
Service Area: Georgetown and surrounding Sussex County communities
Pay: $22.00 per hour
Hours: Up to 29 hours per week, with the potential to transition to full-time
Schedule: Predominantly daytime hours, Monday through Friday
Work Setting: Community-based with regular local travel
Mileage: Reimbursement for approved work-related travel

Help People Build Careers and Greater Independence

RISE Services is hiring a compassionate, dependable, and resourceful Job Coach / Employment Specialist to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain meaningful employment.

In this community-based role, you will meet participants at employer worksites and other locations throughout Georgetown and surrounding Sussex County communities. You will help participants explore career interests, search and apply for jobs, prepare for interviews, learn workplace responsibilities, communicate with employers, and develop the skills needed for long-term employment success.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. We welcome applicants with relevant experience in disability services, human services, education, behavioral health, workforce development, direct support, career coaching, case management, retail supervision, hospitality, customer service, or other positions involving teaching, mentoring, or helping others succeed.

Training is provided.

Schedule and Hours

This position offers up to 29 hours per week. Most services in the Georgetown area are provided during daytime hours, Monday through Friday.

Weekend work is occasionally needed to provide coverage when another employee is unavailable, but this is not a regularly scheduled weekend position.

Weekly schedules may include:

  • On-site job coaching

  • Job searching and completing applications

  • Resume and interview preparation

  • Employer outreach

  • Employment-readiness activities

  • Community-based participant meetings

  • Progress notes and required documentation

When a participant is not working their full number of authorized service hours, the Job Coach may provide other approved employment services, including job searching, completing applications, developing resumes, preparing for interviews, contacting employers, and teaching workplace-readiness skills.

Employees who want additional hours may have the opportunity to transition to full-time as caseloads and service needs grow. Full-time hours are not guaranteed and depend on participant referrals, scheduling needs, employee availability, and satisfactory job performance.

What You’ll Do

Job Coaching and Workplace Support

  • Provide individualized coaching at employer worksites and in community settings.

  • Help participants learn job duties, workplace routines, safety procedures, and employer expectations.

  • Teach workplace communication, professional behavior, time management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Help participants communicate effectively with supervisors and coworkers.

  • Develop natural workplace supports that promote greater independence.

  • Monitor participant progress and adjust coaching strategies as participants develop new skills.

  • Provide ongoing support to promote successful employment retention.

Job Search and Career Preparation

  • Help participants identify their strengths, interests, abilities, support needs, and employment goals.

  • Assist with resumes, applications, job searches, and interview preparation.

  • Conduct mock interviews and employment-readiness activities.

  • Identify employment opportunities that match each participant’s interests, abilities, experience, and goals.

  • Coordinate interviews, hiring activities, and onboarding support.

  • Help participants understand workplace expectations and identify reasonable accommodations when appropriate.

Employer and Community Engagement

  • Build professional relationships with employers throughout Georgetown and Sussex County.

  • Contact businesses to identify potential employment opportunities.

  • Educate employers about inclusive hiring and available workplace supports.

  • Communicate with participants, families, employers, vocational rehabilitation counselors, schools, and community partners.

  • Attend hiring events, team meetings, training, and other scheduled activities.

Documentation and Service Coordination

  • Complete accurate progress notes and service documentation within required deadlines.

  • Maintain participant records according to funding-source and organizational requirements.

  • Track job searches, applications, interviews, placements, wages, scheduled hours, and employment retention.

  • Communicate participant progress, concerns, scheduling changes, and service needs to the appropriate supervisor.

  • Participate in service-planning and team-coordination activities.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree is not required.

  • Relevant experience supporting individuals with disabilities or others who experience barriers to employment is preferred.

  • Experience in teaching, coaching, mentoring, customer service, hospitality, supervision, human services, behavioral health, workforce development, or a related field may also be considered.

  • Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

  • Ability to work independently and make responsible decisions in community settings.

  • Ability to maintain a consistent schedule and complete documentation on time.

  • Basic computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.

  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

  • Ability and willingness to travel locally and transport participants when required.

  • Ability to satisfy applicable background-screening and employment requirements.

Preferred but Not Required

  • Supported Employment, job-coaching, or job-development experience.

  • Experience supporting individuals with intellectual, developmental, behavioral, or other disabilities.

  • Knowledge of vocational rehabilitation or disability-employment services.

  • Understanding of the Americans with Disabilities Act and reasonable workplace accommodations.

  • Experience working with employers, schools, vocational rehabilitation counselors, or community organizations.

  • CESP, ACRE, DSP, or another employment-support credential.

Who Will Succeed in This Position?

You may be a strong fit if you are:

  • Compassionate, patient, dependable, and encouraging.

  • Comfortable working at employer locations and throughout the community.

  • Able to teach and motivate participants while promoting independence.

  • Professional and confident when communicating with employers and community partners.

  • Resourceful and willing to find solutions when challenges arise.

  • Organized and able to manage appointments, follow-ups, and documentation.

  • Flexible when participant or employer schedules change.

  • Comfortable working independently without constant direct supervision.

Why Join RISE Services?

  • Make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals with disabilities.

  • Help people build careers, confidence, and greater independence.

  • Work predominantly during weekday daytime hours.

  • Receive mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel.

  • Participate in paid training and professional development.

  • Build experience in human services, disability services, workforce development, and career coaching.

  • Access potential opportunities for additional hours and advancement.

  • Join a collaborative, growing, and mission-driven organization.

Benefits

Part-time employees may be eligible for:

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Employee Tenure Bonus Program

  • Mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel

  • Paid training and professional development

Employees who transition to an eligible full-time position may also receive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays

  • Short-term disability insurance

  • Life insurance

  • Long-term care option

Benefit eligibility requirements apply.

Important Work-Setting Information

This is a community-based position, not a remote or traditional office-based role. Services are provided at employer worksites and other community locations throughout Georgetown and surrounding Sussex County communities.

Applicants must have reliable transportation and be comfortable driving between community locations. Transporting participants may be required as part of the position.

Equal Opportunity Employer

RISE Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We recruit, hire, train, compensate, and promote employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Apply Today

● Energy & Enthusiasm

● Solution-oriented

● Highly Collaborative Team Player

● Self-Motivated

Creative Freedom to cultivate your own unique program at a partner school from design to inception.

title: State Partnerships Lead – Eviction Data Response Network
description:
About: Housing instability in the U.S. has reached historic levels. Across most metropolitan regions, housing costs have risen far faster than incomes, leaving millions of families cost-burdened and economically precarious. The country faces an estimated shortage of more than four million homes, while homelessness continues to rise, and more than 10 million Americans face eviction each year. The impacts of this crisis are deeply unequal. Black and Latino households—especially families with young children—face disproportionately high rates of eviction and housing instability, and the racial homeownership gap is the largest since the Fair Housing Act was passed in 1968.

The U.S. does not lack ideas for solving this problem—it lacks a coordinated capacity to identify the most promising solutions, refine them through implementation and public debate, and drive their adoption at scale. New America’s Future of Land and Housing program is building that capacity. We operate at the intersection of research, policy, and implementation—clarifying ideas through research and convening power, supporting local leaders to test and refine them on the ground, and translating field-based lessons into broader systems and policy change.

Primary Function: This position primarily supports the Eviction Data Response Network (EDRN), a groundbreaking initiative to create the country’s first large-scale eviction data infrastructure and use that data to keep more families stably housed. EDRN supports 11 state-level partners with technical assistance, financial support, and peer-to-peer learning to:

  • Build durable eviction data pipelines that provide reliable, comprehensive, and regularly updated data on evictions statewide; and
  • Stand up multi-sector problem-solving teams that use that data to craft policy and practice interventions that measurably reduce evictions.

This position will serve as the primary liaison between New America’s FLH team and six state-level teams – Colorado, Georgia, Indiana, Maryland, Pennsylvania, and Maryland – as they work to accomplish these goals.

The ideal candidate is passionate about implementation of large scale change efforts, particularly for housing stability, with experience in coaching partners and supporting learning networks. Familiarity with court eviction data, eviction processes and housing stability are preferred. The candidate should be a self-starter and a good multi-tasker, and capable of working in a fast paced environment on a small, agile team, acting as a primary liaison between the state stakeholders in the EDRN and our team. title: Vice President of Development
description:
“Every person deserves compassion, dignity, and the safety of a place to call home.”

Homelessness is the largest social and public health crisis in California. Illumination Health + Home is a growing non-profit organization dedicated towards disrupting the cycle of homelessness by providing targeted, interdisciplinary services in our recuperative care centers, emergency shelters, housing services and children's and family programs. IH+H currently has 13+ facilities with 22+ micro-communities scattered across Orange County, Los Angeles County and the Inland Empire.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a strategic, hands-on Vice President of Development to lead and grow our philanthropic revenue while building a high-performing, mission-driven team. Reporting to the CEO and serving on the executive leadership team, you will shape and execute a multi-year fundraising strategy spanning major gifts, individual giving, corporate and foundation partnerships, special events, Board engagement, and campaign development.

This is a leadership role for a fundraiser who loves both the work and the people. You will set strategy and lead a team, while personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major donors and philanthropic partners.

The pay range for this position is $155,000 - $175,000 annually, depending on experience.

What you'll do

Fundraising Strategy & Revenue Growth

  • Develop and execute a three-year comprehensive fundraising strategy aligned with organizational priorities, with annual goals by revenue stream and quarterly revenue, pipeline, and activity targets.

  • Maintain a fundraising pipeline sufficient to support 2–3 times the annual major-gift and institutional goals, and identify opportunities to diversify revenue and grow unrestricted support.

  • Monitor performance and provide the CEO and Board with regular reports on revenue, pipeline, projections, and progress, partnering with Finance on accurate forecasts.


Major Gifts & Individual Philanthropy

  • Build and personally manage a portfolio of high-capacity donors, developing individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies.

  • Personally lead or participate in five-, six-, and seven-figure solicitations, and grow the number and value of major gifts.

  • Develop compelling cases for support, and partner with the CEO and Board to identify and engage high-capacity individuals and community influencers.

  • Build and deepen relationships with corporations, foundations, and institutional partners, moving funders from transactional grants toward strategic, multi-year partnerships.


Corporate, Foundation & Board Engagement

  • Build and deepen relationships with corporations, foundations, and institutional partners, moving funders from transactional grants toward strategic, multi-year partnerships.

  • Partner with the CEO and Board to maximize their effectiveness as ambassadors and fundraisers, setting clear annual engagement expectations and providing tools, coaching, and meeting preparation.

  • Create opportunities for Board members to leverage their networks to expand the donor base.


Donor Stewardship & Campaigns

  • Design and lead a comprehensive stewardship strategy, with a goal of increasing donor retention by at least 5% in the first year.

  • Drive donor upgrades, recurring and multi-year giving, and re-engagement of lapsed donors, ensuring donors receive timely, meaningful communication about their impact.

  • Assess organizational readiness for future capital and transformational campaigns, completing a campaign readiness assessment within the first six months.


Team Leadership & Operations

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of seven, setting clear goals and expectations and fostering a culture that is collaborative, supportive, accountable, and donor-centered.

  • Lead with kindness, humility, professionalism, and respect while maintaining high standards, and encourage collaboration across Finance, Programs, Marketing, and Executive Leadership.

  • Ensure the CRM is fully utilized for fundraising management, with standardized dashboards, reliable monthly and quarterly forecasting, and accurate reporting in partnership with Finance.


What you'll bring

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.

  • 8–10+ years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising experience, including leading development functions and managing fundraising professionals.

  • Demonstrated success securing major gifts, ideally at the five-, six-, and seven-figure levels.

  • Proven ability to build fundraising strategies that produce measurable revenue growth.

  • Experience across major gifts, individual giving, corporate and foundation relations, events, stewardship, and campaign planning.

  • Skilled at partnering with CEOs, Boards, major donors, and community leaders.

  • Experience with CRM systems, pipeline development, forecasting, and metrics-driven management.

  • Strong financial acumen and excellent communication and relationship-building skills.

  • Experience in healthcare, homelessness, housing, or human services preferred.

  • Meaningful connections within Orange County and/or Southern California a plus.


Who you are

You are an entrepreneurial, relationship-oriented fundraising leader who pairs a strong track record of results with genuine care for people. You lead with kindness, humility, and accountability, you are comfortable rolling up your sleeves alongside your team, and you bring energy, creativity, and a genuine commitment to our mission.

Benefits

  • Medical Insurance funded up to 91% by Illumination Foundation (Kaiser and Blue Shield), depending on the plan
  • Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Life, AD&D and LTD Insurance funded 100% by Illumination Foundation
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Professional Development Reimbursement
  • 401K with Company Matching
  • 15 days vacation PTO/year
  • 6 days sick PTO/year
  • 10 days holiday PTO/year
  • Potential eligibility for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSFL) for federally qualified loans

title: Software Engineer II - Fundamentals
description:
Overview

The Windows + Devices Fundamentals team improves the reliability, performance, battery life, and sustainability of Windows devices. We define and measure the health of the Windows ecosystem by transforming device telemetry and diagnostic signals into actionable insights and engineering improvements.

We are seeking a Software Engineer II to build data-driven solutions that reveal how Windows devices behave at enterprise scale in commercial landscape. You will develop metrics, analytics, and system improvements that help teams detect regressions, prioritize investments, and deliver measurable gains in Windows Fundamentals.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Define meaningful Windows Fundamentals metrics and success criteria for reliability, performance, battery life, and sustainability.
  • Analyze fleet telemetry, diagnostic signals, and traces to identify trends, anomalies, regressions, and customer impact.
  • Build reliable data pipelines, queries, dashboards, and automated analyses that make device-health insights timely and actionable.
  • Investigate metric movements using statistical methods, experimentation, debugging, and performance-analysis tools.
  • Design, implement, and test well-scoped operating-system or analytics improvements that address identified opportunities.
  • Evaluate data quality, establish baselines, quantify tradeoffs, and validate outcomes against measurable goals.
  • Collaborate with Windows engineering, data science, security, servicing, Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), support, and enterprise partner teams to drive Fundamentals improvements.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python.
    • OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical discipline and 3+ years of software engineering experience – or equivalent practical experience.
  • 1+ years of experience in software engineering, systems analysis, debugging, performance engineering, data engineering, or related work.
  • Experience analyzing telemetry or operational data to diagnose system behavior and improve reliability, performance, efficiency, or security.
  • Experience developing, testing, and delivering reliable production software, data pipelines, metrics, or analytics.
  • Solid programming, debugging, data-analysis, and problem-solving skills; ability to independently execute well-scoped work and use evidence to guide decisions.
  • Experience with operating systems, system-level development, performance engineering, data engineering, or large-scale analytics.
  • Knowledge of Windows internals, reliability engineering, performance analysis, or power efficiency.
  • Experience defining KPIs, establishing baselines, investigating regressions, and communicating insights through dashboards or technical reports.
  • Experience with Kusto, Azure data platforms, fleet telemetry, statistical analysis, experimentation, anomaly detection, or machine learning.

title: Maintenance Director
description:

Ensure the facility is well-maintained in a safe and comfortable manner.

A. Role Responsibilities – Job Knowledge/Duties:

1. Manages the operations of the Maintenance Department by adhering to proper staffing and scheduling of personnel

2. Inspect storage rooms, work rooms, utility/janitorial closets, etc for upkeep and supply control

3. Participates in facility surveys made by authorized governmental agencies

4. Ensures that outside services are properly completed/supervised in accordance with contracts/work orders

5. Assists in establishing a preventative maintenance program

6. Meets with maintenance personnel on a regular basis and solicit advice from inter-department supervisors concerning the operation of the maintenance department, assist in identifying and correcting problem areas and /or improvement of services

7. Assists in identifying, evaluating, and classifying routine and job related maintenance functions to ensure that tasks involving the potential exposure to blood/body fluids are properly identified and recorded

8. Makes daily rounds to assure that maintenance personnel are performing required duties and assure that appropriate maintenance procedures are being rendered to meet the needs of the facility

9. Maintains fire alarm and other fire protection and preventive systems

10. Completes carpentry and other building repairs within the scope of expertise

11. Maintains heating and cooling systems

12. Makes some electrical and plumbing repair within scope of expertise

13. Monitors, maintains, and records inventory and orders supplies as needed, ensures supplies are available

14. Heads snow and ice removal for the sidewalks

15. When required, is on call seven days a week, 24 hours a day for emergencies

16. Other duties as required by the Administrator

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE:

1. Must possess, as a minimum, a high school education or its equivalent

2. Must have, as a minimum, one year experience in a supervisory capacity, in a maintenance related position

3. Must have a valid driver’s license

4. Must be able to withstand inside and outside environmental conditions, extreme heat, freezing conditions, and a noisy, dirty, dusty, or greasy work environment at times

5. Must be knowledgeable of boilers, compressors, generators, etc., as well as various mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems

6. Must be knowledgeable in building codes and safety regulations

title: Manufacturing Technician 1
description:
Bring Your Skills to Biotechnology as a Manufacturing Technician!

The Manufacturing Technician I accurately follows written Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to perform a variety of molecular biology techniques which support the manufacture of molecular controls. Manufacturing Technicians are expected to have excellent laboratory dexterity, be proficient with micropipettes, aseptic techniques, molecular biology techniques and in the use of associated laboratory equipment. This individual is well-organized, enjoys detailed work, works with limited supervision by the Manager of Manufacturing Operations and may be called upon to assist with troubleshooting manufacturing processes and products.

What You Will Get to Do
  • Accurately and reproducibly performs a variety of molecular biology techniques that support the manufacture of molecular controls
  • Follows aseptic techniques and current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP)
  • Works with a variety of chemistries, labware and laboratory equipment including performing work in BSLII hoods
  • Precisely delivers small volumes using micropipettes
  • Performs in-process QC on manufacturing components and products (pH, spectrometry, and electrophoresis). Accurately documents all results
  • Assists other manufacturing personnel in the manufacture of products
  • Assists with troubleshooting of processes and products as needed
  • May participate in modifying / improving existing MMQCI products and processes
  • Performs routine laboratory tasks including inventory, ordering, and maintaining organization
  • Follows MMQCI’s quality systems based on cGMP and International Organization for Standardization (ISO) regulatory requirements. Accurately documents work and keeps detailed records
  • Contributes to laboratory support tasks such as routine cleaning of laboratory and equipment and general housekeeping duties

Required Skills & Experience
  • B.A., B.S. in Biology/Biotech/Life Sciences, or an A.S degree with 2 years relevant hands-on manufacturing experience or similar laboratory function
  • Experience working with DNA and RNA molecular biology techniques (PCR, spectrometry, and gel electrophoresis experience is highly desired)
  • Ability to read, comprehend and accurately follow SOPs quickly with attention to detail
  • Requires fine and gross motor skills, ability to work with various sizes of labware including the ability to firmly grasp
  • Able to visually inspect product and perform visual inspections of gels
  • Able to work under a BSLII hood for multiple hours in a row
  • Able to follow aseptic and contamination control techniques including working in an environmentally controlled facility that has gowning requirements
  • Able to work with hazardous materials such as acids
  • Highly organized with the ability to perform precise, detail-oriented work in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines and shifting priorities
  • Good communication skills, written and oral, and excellent computer skill
  • Must be able to stand for several hours and lift approximately 30 lbs
Preferred
  • Experience in an industrial environment following cGMP and/or ISO is preferred

Why You’ll Love Working Here
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a growing diagnostic company
  • Collaborative, mission-driven team environment
  • Competitive compensation and benefits

Benefits We Offer
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan
  • Company profit sharing program
  • Paid time off: including vacation, holidays, and sick leave
  • Paid Parental Leave Program
The pay range for this position is $19.23 to $36.06/hour

Get to know the MMQCI team!
https://www.mmqci.com/about/employee-spotlight/employee-spotlight.html

Maine Molecular Quality Controls, Inc. (MMQCI) designs, develops, manufactures, and sells unique quality control products used by hospital laboratories and manufacturers to monitor the accuracy of tests for genetic, oncologic, and infectious diseases. MMQCI has proprietary technologies to stabilize DNA and RNA for use as quality controls and continues to pursue the discovery of novel techniques useful for the development of new quality control products.

MMQCI is conveniently located in beautiful southern coastal Maine, minutes from the Maine Turnpike, Portland International Jetport, and less than 2 hours from Boston. description:
Job Summary

The EHR IT Support Specialist provides technical support for OCHIN Epic and associated clinical technologies by ensuring end-user devices, infrastructure, system access, connectivity, and peripheral equipment are properly deployed, maintained, and supported. This position serves as a key liaison between Information Technology, clinical operations, and end users to ensure reliable access to healthcare technology systems. The EHR IT Support Specialist supports implementation, optimization, troubleshooting, information security, and ongoing operational readiness activities that promote effective, secure, and efficient healthcare delivery.

Essential Functions

The following functions are fundamental to the position and are required of all incumbents, with or without reasonable accommodation. These functions define the role and are not an exhaustive list of all duties.

  • Deploys, configures, maintains, and supports workstations, laptops, tablets, mobile devices, and other equipment required for OCHIN Epic and related clinical applications.
  • Coordinates equipment readiness, including inventory, staging, testing, deployment, replacement, and lifecycle management.
  • Provides end-user technical support by troubleshooting hardware, software, access, connectivity, and workflow-related issues.
  • Manages user access, including provisioning, modification, deactivation, and troubleshooting in accordance with security protocols and organizational policies.
  • Supports system connectivity, interfaces, integrations, network access, wireless access, remote access, and device performance.
  • Installs, maintains, and supports printers, scanners, signature pads, label printers, badge readers, and other clinical technology peripherals.
  • Monitors, resolves, and escalates technical issues affecting clinical operations, patient care, implementation activities, or system availability.
  • Supports cybersecurity, HIPAA, privacy, information security, device management, access management, audit, and compliance activities.
  • Provides technical support for EHR implementation, upgrades, optimization, training events, go-live activities, and workstation/peripheral readiness.
  • Documents procedures, inventories, support activities, and troubleshooting solutions to support efficiency, continuity, and knowledge sharing.
  • Collaborates with IT staff, operational leaders, vendors, trainers, analysts, and end users to support technology adoption and service delivery.

Physical Requirments

  • Frequently required to sit, stand, walk, bend, stoop, reach, kneel, and climb while installing or supporting technology equipment.
  • Frequently uses hands and fingers to operate computers, tools, and technology devices.
  • Must be able to lift, carry, move, and install equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.
  • Requires close visual acuity for troubleshooting hardware, reviewing technical documentation, and working with computer systems.

Required Qualifications

Education


Associate degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Healthcare Technology, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience required.

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field preferred.


Experience


Minimum of two (2) years of experience providing technical support, help desk services, information technology operations, or infrastructure support.

Experience deploying and supporting hardware, software, user accounts, and network-connected devices.

Experience supporting healthcare technology systems, electronic health records, or clinical environments preferred.

Experience supporting OCHIN Epic or Epic environments preferred.

Post-secondary education or experience that provides the expertise required to perform the functions of the position effectively may substitute for the degree on a year-for-year basis.


Licensure and Certifications

Preferred certifications include one or more of the following:

CompTIA A+

CompTIA Network+

CompTIA Security+

Microsoft certifications

Healthcare technology or Epic-related certifications


The GPTLHB is a tribal organization that follows tribal preference laws. Our policy is to give preference to qualified Indian/Tribal candidates over a qualified non-native candidate in hiring decisions when all other qualifications are equal.


Employment is contingent upon the outcome of all required criminal background checks.

We exist to drive the success of our partners. We do this by fundamentally changing the way you transact with others. We just happen to make great payment systems. If you love helping others succeed, in a culture that celebrates perfecting your craft, consider partnering with us.

Location

PayJunction takes a Flex First approach to work environments. This means that our team members can choose to work from our Santa Barbara office or remotely from home. We ensure that everyone has the resources and equipment to work where they feel most productive. We trust our teams to make the best decision for their work environment. All PayJunction employees must reside in one of the following states: CA, IL, TX, MN, CO, GA, CT, NY or MA.

Mission

Our mission at PayJunction's Product Department is to drive relentless innovation and deliver customer-centric payment solutions. Through in-depth research, collaboration, and a deep understanding of market and user needs, we continuously challenge the status quo. We strive not only to meet industry standards but to set them, ensuring every transaction is efficient, transparent, and built on trust, all while delivering unparalleled value to our clients and partners.

Vision

To lead the frontier of payment innovation, continuously challenging and reshaping industry norms. We envision a future where our disruptive solutions not only redefine transaction experiences but also set the global standard for what's next in payment technology.

Responsibilities

  • Own the product vision, strategy, and quarterly roadmap for the Payment Experience domain. Articulate where we are going, why, in what order, and what we are choosing not to do.
  • Own the full payment experience lifecycle across the domain — VT, surcharging, tender types, and login/security. Each payment service has a defined adoption target, merchant-facing education or configuration strategy, and post-ship validation.
  • Drive surcharge enrollment growth as the domain’s clearest revenue lever. Navigate state legality, card-brand rules, and merchant-facing constraints to design enrollment strategies that are compliant and effective.
  • Manage tender-type adoption and expansion. Own the BNPL (Sunbit) partnership, ACH, Apple Pay, and future payment methods. Drive merchant-facing education and activation to increase adoption rates.
  • Build and maintain the product backlog with strategic intent. Prioritize based on business value, cost of delay, and merchant impact. Maintain 2–4 sprints of ready work at all times.
  • Conduct product discovery before committing major work. Talk to merchants, listen to support calls, analyze usage patterns, review competitive payment experiences. Validate before building.
  • Navigate regulated payments constraints as first-class design inputs. Treat card-brand rules, PCI scope, state surcharge regulations, and Nacha/ACH rules as product problems to solve, not checkboxes to clear.
  • Write benefit hypotheses for major initiatives and validate outcomes post-ship. Own the full cycle: discover, plan, build, ship, measure, learn.
  • Collaborate with engineering during sprint planning, refinement, and execution. Be available, be clear, and treat developers as partners in building the right thing.
  • Communicate proactively with stakeholders. Send monthly domain updates. Surface trade-offs and sequencing changes before people have to ask.
  • Triage all incoming requests in the domain. Accept, defer, decline, or route. Every request gets a visible disposition within 10 business days.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience as a Product Manager or in a similar product leadership role
  • 3+ years working with Agile/Scrum teams, driving (not just participating in) sprint planning, refinement, and backlog health
  • Direct experience in payments, acceptance, or processing (gateway, acquirer, processor, or merchant-facing payment product) - must understand authorization, capture, settlement, interchange, and funding at a product-decision level
  • Proven track record of navigating regulated payments constraints (surcharge legality, card-brand rules, PCI, Nacha/ACH, state regulations) as product design inputs
  • Proven track record of outcome-focused delivery with measurable business impact — revenue lift, adoption rate improvement, retention contribution, or deal-enablement tied to products owned
  • Experience owning merchant-facing or SMB-facing product experiences where the end user is a business operator managing daily payment workflows
  • Experience with B2B SaaS product management - understands SaaS delivery, multi-tenant considerations, and merchant lifecycle
  • Experience with BNPL, alternative tender types, or payment method expansion preferred
  • Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, and product intake/discovery tools preferred
  • Product management certifications (CSPO, PSPO, or equivalent) preferred
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, or a related field preferred

About PayJunction

Founded in 2000 by three UCSB graduates, PayJunction has grown from a bootstrapped startup to a recognized and respected leader in the payments industry. PayJunction processes more than $12 billion dollars annually for thousands of businesses with solutions that make it easy to accept credit and debit card payments in-store, online, and on-the-go.

Our people-first culture values long-term relationships over short-term profits. Honesty and integrity are part of every interaction with partners, customers and employees. We foster a collaborative work environment, where creative ideas are welcomed, teams are inspired, and success is celebrated. PayJunction is a place where you can find experienced mentors and supportive friends who are committed to your growth.

Total Rewards Benefits

Office Environment

title: Performance Audit Intern- Summer 2027
description:
Performance Audit Intern
Summer 2027: June 1 - August 6

About Our Program
The Comptroller of the Treasury's Audit Internship Program is a 10-week paid educational and experiential learning opportunity that offers undergraduate students a chance to observe and actively participate in the office's audit operations. Interns will spend the summer building skills through their active audit experience and audit-specific training. Interns will also have opportunities to build relationships with each other through shared experiences.

The Performance Audit Intern will have the opportunity to actively participate in an audit of a state government entity receiving public funds and will be part of an audit team that evaluates management’s mission and operational practices by conducting management interviews and reviewing management’s records and reports. Interns may also have the opportunity to evaluate the following: the design, implementation, and effectiveness of management’s internal controls; the efficiency and effectiveness of an entity's operations and systems; and compliance with laws, regulations, contracts, and grant agreements. At the end of the 10-week internship program, Performance Audit Interns will have gained experience in making government work better by determining whether the state entity met the mission and goals that it was created to accomplish.

Our summer internship program is designed to be both professionally and academically beneficial. Interns gain hands‑on experience while participating in meaningful professional development activities such as Business Etiquette Day, a full‑day session focused on professionalism, emotional intelligence, and understanding one’s professional brand, complete with an etiquette lunch led by staff. Interns also enjoy engaging activities like speed networking with full‑time employees, a guided tour of the Tennessee Capitol to explore the state’s history, and weekly cohort check‑ins to foster connection and collaboration. The cohort experience culminates in a final presentation showcasing what interns have learned and contributed during their time with the Office.

Location
Performance audit internship opportunities are based out of Nashville, Tennessee. Depending on the audit assignment, interns may have the opportunity for limited travel during the summer. Typical travel opportunities are in the Nashville area; however, some may allow for travel to other parts of Tennessee.

Who We're Looking For
We are seeking students who are rising juniors, seniors, or enrolled in graduate accounting programs and are interested in applying their classroom knowledge to governmental auditing. To qualify for the internship program, applicants should have successfully completed at least 6 credit hours of accounting coursework. Preference will be given to students who have completed intermediate or advanced accounting classes.

Successful interns are those who are adaptable, able to think critically, work well both individually and as part of a team, and are willing to learn and grow. Candidates should exhibit strong interpersonal, verbal communication, organizational, and writing skills. Interns are expected to apply their classroom knowledge to meaningful audit work.

We are looking for a professional to join our team who will commit to delivering exceptional work that helps us make government work better. Learn more about us at and by watching a video about what it's like to be a Performance Auditor!

About Our Office
The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury is responsible for the audit of state and local governmental entities and participates in the general financial and administrative management and oversight of state government. In the Comptroller’s Office, we strive to deliver on our mission to make government work better. Through dedicated hard work and commitment, every Comptroller’s Office employee accepts personal responsibility to accomplish our mission and uphold it.

Compensation
Interns are paid $24 per hour via a third-party company. This position may require in-state day travel to audit sites. Audit-related travel will be reimbursed.

Equal Opportunity Employer
Pursuant to the Comptroller of the Treasury’s Workplace Discrimination and Harassment policy, the Office is firmly committed to the principle of fair and equal employment opportunities for its citizens and strives to protect the rights and opportunities of all people to seek, obtain, and hold employment without being subjected to illegal discrimination and harassment in the workplace. It is the Comptroller’s policy to provide an environment free of discrimination and harassment of an individual because of that person’s race, color, national origin, age (40 and over), sex, sexual orientation, transgender and gender identity status, pregnancy, religion, creed, disability, veteran’s status, or any other category protected by state and/or federal civil rights laws.
​
​​NOTICE: This position requires a criminal background check. Therefore, you may be required to provide information about your criminal history in order to be considered for this position.

Texting TOS and Privacy Policy:

Message type: informational; you will receive text messages regarding your application and potentially regarding interview scheduling. You can cancel the SMS service at any time. Just text "STOP" to the short code. After you send the SMS message "STOP" to us, we will send you an SMS message to confirm that you have been unsubscribed. After this, you will no longer receive SMS messages from us. If you want to join again, just sign up as you did the first time and we will start sending SMS messages to you again. If you are experiencing issues with the messaging program, you can reply with the keyword HELP for more assistance, or you can get help directly at ig.askhr@cot.tn.gov. Message frequency will vary depending on the application process.

Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. Msg & data rates may apply. If you have any questions about your text plan or data plan, it is best to contact your wireless provider. If you have any questions regarding privacy, please read our privacy policy below.

title: Senior Environmental Planner / Project Manager
description:
About Us
We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 600+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Our mission is to deliver practical, science-based environmental and planning solutions that support communities, infrastructure, and natural systems.

As a people-centric organization, we value collaboration, fairness, and transparency, and are committed to fostering a workplace that supports both personal and professional growth while offering robust career opportunities. We are especially proud of our recent Great Place To Work® certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team member experiences.

About The Role
We are seeking a Senior Environmental Planner / Project Manager to join our Environmental Planning team and support environmental review for a diverse range of public- and private-sector projects throughout California.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys managing the preparation of clear, defensible environmental documents, leading projects and technical assignments, and providing trusted guidance to clients. The successful candidate will manage small-to-moderate projects or components of larger efforts while remaining engaged in technical work and supporting junior staff.

How We Collaborate
This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.

Eligible office locations for this role include Monterey, Oakland, and Sacramento.

What You’ll Do
Environmental Review and Technical Work
  • Manage the preparation and review of CEQA and NEPA documents, including streamlining and exemption documentation, Initial Studies/Mitigated Negative Declarations, Environmental Impact Reports, Environmental Assessments, and Environmental Impact Statements
  • Direct project research and analysis, evaluate environmental impacts, develop mitigation measures, and clearly communicate findings in defensible documents
  • Coordinate technical specialists and oversee document production and QA/QC to maintain quality and meet project schedules and budgets
  • Lead agency consultations and technical or regulatory discussions supporting environmental permitting and compliance
  • Prepare and present materials for agency staff, decision-making bodies, community members, and other stakeholders
Project Management and Client Support
  • Manage small-to-moderate projects or components of larger efforts, including scopes, schedules, budgets, and deliverables
  • Serve as a trusted day-to-day advisor to clients, providing responsive communication and identifying project risks and regulatory considerations
  • Direct and coordinate project team members, technical specialists, and subcontractors
  • Provide guidance and mentorship to junior staff on CEQA, NEPA, technical writing, and environmental planning practices
Business Development
  • Support client outreach and proposal development by contributing CEQA and NEPA expertise, scopes, schedules, and cost estimates

What You’ll Bring
  • B.A./B.S. in Environmental Science/ Studies, Urban/Regional Planning, or a related field; an advanced degree is a plus
  • 5+ years of relevant environmental planning and review experience in California, with increasing responsibility for technical work, project management, and client support
  • Experience managing CEQA and/or NEPA documents and independently drafting, reviewing, and synthesizing technical information
  • Established knowledge of CEQA and NEPA processes and the judgment to lead technical discussions and advise clients on related regulatory and permitting requirements
  • Experience managing project scopes, schedules, budgets, and deliverables
  • Excellent writing, presentation, and communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with clients, agencies, and multidisciplinary teams
  • Sound judgment, initiative, and a practical, results-oriented approach to problem-solving
  • Ability to travel occasionally as project needs require

Nice to Have
  • Experience working in a California environmental consulting environment
  • Experience leading complex or high-profile CEQA or NEPA documents
  • Experience supporting projects across multiple sectors, such as transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, government, or private development

Investing in You
The base salary range for this full-time position is $95,000–$120,000, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards Package designed to support employee well-being, growth, and financial security. Our benefits are designed to offer flexibility and choice, including health coverage options, employer-sponsored insurance, retirement benefits, generous time off, and programs that support learning, growth, and community engagement.

Explore more about our culture, benefits, and life at Rincon on our Culture and Benefits page.

Additional Employment Information
Individuals offered employment must successfully complete a pre-employment drug screening as a condition of employment. Additionally, those hired who may be assigned to federal projects will be subject to further drug testing, including screening for cannabinoids (THC/marijuana), in compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 and other applicable federal regulations, which take precedence over California state and local laws.

Rincon Consultants does not accept unsolicited applicant/candidate resumes from search firm recruiters and/or temporary agencies that do not have a signed contract and specified work order with Rincon Consultants. Further, such resumes received will be deemed the sole property of Rincon Consultants and no fees will be paid in the event Rincon Consultants subsequently hires such individual. Rincon Consultants is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law.
