title: Entry - Level Member Specialist | Work From Home
description:
Remote Member Specialist | Work From Home

AO Globe Life | 100% Remote | U.S. Applicants | Training & Mentorship | Performance-Based Income

Empower Members. Protect Families. Build Legacies.

Are you looking for a fully remote career where you can help families make important financial-protection decisions while building your own long-term professional and financial future?

AO Globe Life is seeking motivated, service-focused professionals to join our growing virtual team as Remote Insurance & Member Benefits Specialists.

You'll work directly with eligible members and families who have requested information about available benefits, helping them understand their options, select appropriate protection, and receive ongoing service throughout the life of their policies.

No previous insurance experience is required. We provide training, mentorship, licensing guidance, and ongoing professional development for motivated individuals ready to learn.

✓ 100% Remote / Work From Home
✓ Qualified Member Opportunities Provided
✓ No Traditional Cold Calling
✓ Weekly Commission-Based Pay
✓ Uncapped Earning Potential
✓ Performance Bonuses & Incentives
✓ Renewal & Residual Income Opportunities
✓ Training & One-on-One Mentorship
✓ Leadership & Management Advancement

About AO Globe Life

AO operates within the American Income Division of Globe Life, serving working families through life, accident, and supplemental health insurance solutions.

Our organization has a longstanding history of serving labor union members, veterans, credit union members, associations, and their families, with a focus on personalized service and long-term relationships.

Our mission is simple:

Protect Every Child. Serve All Working People.

Our virtual business model combines modern technology with ongoing training, mentorship, and professional development, allowing representatives to build their careers from home.

What You'll Do

As a Remote Insurance & Member Benefits Specialist, you'll combine customer service, benefits education, relationship management, and consultative insurance sales.

🤝 Connect With Members

  • Meet with members virtually through Zoom and phone appointments

  • Connect with individuals who have requested information about available benefits

  • Ask questions to understand each family's needs, priorities, and financial-protection goals

  • Build professional relationships based on trust, service, and consistent communication

🛡️ Educate & Recommend Solutions

  • Explain available life, accident, and supplemental health insurance options

  • Help members understand coverage features and available choices

  • Assess individual needs and recommend appropriate solutions

  • Answer questions clearly and professionally

  • Guide eligible members through applications and enrollment

  • Complete required documentation accurately

❤️ Provide Long-Term Member Service

Your relationship with members doesn't end after enrollment.

You'll also:

  • Conduct policy reviews

  • Assist with beneficiary updates

  • Answer policy and coverage questions

  • Provide appropriate claims-related assistance

  • Follow up with members regarding changing needs

  • Maintain accurate digital client records

  • Deliver responsive, professional service

  • Follow applicable company procedures, state regulations, and ethical standards

📞 Qualified Member Opportunities — No Traditional Cold Calling

Instead of purchasing leads or relying primarily on traditional cold prospecting, representatives have access to qualified member opportunities.

You'll connect with individuals who have requested information regarding available programs and benefits, allowing you to focus on:

Understanding Needs → Educating Members → Recommending Solutions → Enrollment → Long-Term Service

There is no requirement to purchase leads.

💰 Weekly Performance-Based Compensation

This is a commission-based opportunity rather than a guaranteed hourly or salaried customer-service position.

Compensation opportunities may include:

  • Weekly commission payments

  • Uncapped personal production potential

  • Performance-based bonuses

  • Renewal income

  • Long-term residual income opportunities

  • Leadership compensation as you advance

  • Additional achievement and performance incentives

High-performing representatives may build six-figure annual income potential, but earnings are not guaranteed and vary based on individual activity, production, consistency, and results.

🎓 No Insurance Experience? Training Is Provided.

We value communication skills, professionalism, work ethic, coachability, and motivation more than previous industry experience.

Training and development may include:

  • Virtual onboarding

  • State insurance licensing guidance

  • Product and benefits education

  • Client-service training

  • Consultative sales development

  • Virtual presentation skills

  • Enrollment systems and procedures

  • Compliance education

  • One-on-one mentorship

  • Weekly coaching and development

  • Leadership training

  • Ongoing professional education

Representatives must obtain the appropriate state Life & Health Insurance License before conducting activities that require licensing.

🏠 Build Your Career From Home

This opportunity operates in a virtual environment, including:

  • Zoom client consultations

  • Phone communication

  • Online training

  • Digital enrollment systems

  • Virtual coaching and mentorship

  • Remote team meetings

  • Online professional-development programs

You'll have the independence of working remotely while remaining connected to a team focused on accountability, development, service, and performance.

❤️ Benefits & Professional Support

Qualifying representatives may have access to:

  • Medical insurance reimbursement opportunities

  • Company-supported life insurance

  • Accidental Death Benefit coverage

  • OPEIU Local 277 representation where applicable

  • Renewal and residual income opportunities

  • Professional coaching and mentorship

  • Leadership-development programs

  • Virtual business technology and resources

Eligibility and qualification requirements may apply.

🏆 Recognition & Performance Incentives

Strong performance may also provide opportunities to qualify for:

  • Company-sponsored incentive travel

  • Leadership conferences and conventions

  • Performance bonuses

  • Achievement awards

  • Recognition programs

  • Team events

  • Advanced leadership-development opportunities

📈 Career & Leadership Advancement

For individuals interested in building beyond an individual producer role, AO provides opportunities for continued professional and leadership development.

Potential growth may include:

Benefits Specialist → Trainer/Mentor → Team Leader → Management → Advanced Leadership

Advancement is based on performance, consistency, professional development, and demonstrated leadership ability—not simply tenure.

Who We're Looking For

Successful candidates typically demonstrate:

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Strong customer-service and relationship-building abilities

  • Active listening and problem-solving skills

  • Professionalism and attention to detail

  • Self-motivation and personal accountability

  • Strong organization and time-management skills

  • Goal-oriented and performance-driven mindset

  • Confidence working independently

  • Comfort using computers and virtual communication technology

  • Ability to learn and adapt quickly

  • Coachability and willingness to implement feedback

  • Commitment to ethical, client-focused service

Experience in customer service, sales, banking, financial services, healthcare, hospitality, retail, education, administration, military service, call centers, account management, or client relations can transfer well to this opportunity.

Previous insurance experience is helpful but not required.

Minimum Requirements

Applicants must:

  • Be at least 18 years of age

  • Be physically located within the United States

  • Be legally authorized to work in the United States

  • Have a reliable computer or laptop

  • Maintain reliable high-speed internet

  • Have webcam and microphone capability

  • Maintain a quiet, professional workspace

  • Be comfortable conducting business through Zoom and phone

  • Be willing to complete required training

  • Be willing and able to obtain the appropriate state Life & Health Insurance License

💻 Virtual Interview Process

Qualified applicants will receive information explaining the career opportunity, compensation structure, licensing requirements, training program, member process, and advancement opportunities.

Candidates interested in continuing will then have the opportunity to participate in a live virtual interview through Zoom with our hiring team.

Ready to Empower Members & Build Your Future?

If you're looking for a 100% remote career where you can serve working families, develop valuable professional skills, build long-term client relationships, and create opportunities for financial and leadership growth, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply today with your updated resume to be considered for our Remote Insurance & Member Benefits Specialist opportunity with AO Globe Life.

Empower Members. Protect Families. Build Legacies. Build Your Future. 🚀

title: IT Support Analyst
description:
Position: IT Support Analyst
Classification: Full-time, Non-Exempt
Reports to: IT Portfolio, Change and Training Manager
Company: DePelchin Family Services
Location: Houston, TX

Position Description:
The IT Support Analyst provides day-to-day support to the Information Technology department's project, change management, and service management functions. This position assists with tracking and updating project tasks in a work management platform, supports the intake, triage, and processing of requests through the change management queue, and helps administer and maintains the service management platform. The IT Support Analyst also provides general IT customer/software support, helping ensure requests, incidents, and changes are documented, routed, and resolved in a timely and organized manner.

Primary Responsibilities:
  • Assist with maintaining and updating project tasks, timelines, and statuses in Asana in coordination with the IT Portfolio, Change and Training Manager and project leads.
  • Support the intake, documentation, and tracking of items in the IT change management queue, helping ensure changes are properly logged, categorized, and routed for approval.
  • Assist with scheduling and coordinating change advisory board (CAB) meetings, including preparing agendas, tracking action items, and documenting outcomes.
  • Help administer and maintain FreshService, including ticket queue monitoring, workflow/automation configuration support, category and form maintenance, and basic reporting.
  • Provide first- and second-level IT customer support, including troubleshooting hardware, software, and application issues and escalating complex issues as needed.
  • Monitor and help manage the IT service desk ticket queue to ensure requests and incidents are acknowledged, assigned, and resolved within service level targets.
  • Assist with documenting IT processes, procedures, and knowledge base articles to support the service desk and end users.
  • Support training coordination efforts, including scheduling sessions, maintaining training materials, and tracking staff completion records.
  • Help generate reports and dashboards related to project status, change activity, and service desk performance for IT leadership.
  • Assist with software and application support tasks, including basic configuration, user access requests, and coordination with vendors as needed.
  • Participate in continuous improvement efforts for IT project management, change management, and service management processes.
  • Maintain confidentiality and follow agency policies regarding data security, HIPAA, and CJIS requirements when handling systems and information.
Required Qualifications:
  • Associates degree, preferably in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related field. Relevant experience/certifications may be considered in lieu of formal education
  • Minimum one (1) year experience in an IT customer support, help desk, or software/application support role.
  • Experience providing end-user technical support in a professional office environment.
Preferred Qualifications:
  • CompTIA A+, ITIL Foundation, or similar IT support/service management certifications a plus
  • Experience using or supporting project/work management tools (e.g., Asana, or similar) preferred.
  • Experience using IT service management platforms (e.g., FreshService, ServiceNow, or similar) preferred.
  • Familiarity with IT change management concepts, workflows, and processes a plus.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
  • Basic understanding of IT service management concepts, including incident, request, and change management.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams) or similar software.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to track multiple tasks, requests, and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical staff.
  • Strong customer service orientation and a professional, patient approach to supporting end users.
  • Ability to learn new software applications and systems quickly.
  • Attention to detail and accuracy in documentation and data entry.
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team.
Work Conditions:
  • Environment: Office
  • Range of Schedule: Mon – Fri, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Occasional flexibility required to support IT projects, changes, or issues outside normal hours.
  • Travel: Occasional

DePelchin is Proud to be an Equal Opportunity Workplace.

DePelchin is committed to selecting and employing the best and most qualified person available for each job opening without unlawful discrimination of any kind. Additionally, DePelchin is committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity), marital or parental status, veteran status, religion, national origin, age, disability, family medical history, genetic information, or political affiliation.

title: Director, Industry - Tribeca
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
Tribeca is seeking a strategic, entrepreneurial, and deeply networked Director of Industry to take ownership of the industry program at one of the world's preeminent festivals for the business of film and storytelling. This is a newly created, full-time leadership position — reporting directly to the Festival Director — with a clear mandate for growth: to expand Tribeca's role as a destination for discovery, sales, and deal-making, and to build an industry program that matches the ambition, scale, and influence of the Festival itself. Reflecting Tribeca's interdisciplinary identity, this mandate also extends to adjacent creative industries beyond film.

The Director of Industry will own the strategic vision, revenue growth, and full lifecycle of industry engagement — from year-round relationship cultivation and business development to delegate experience on the ground during the Festival. Throughout this role, references to sales agents, distributors, buyers, financiers, producers' reps, and similar industry constituencies refer to the business and market side of the Festival — professionals who attend Tribeca for accreditation, deal-making, and market purposes — as distinct from the filmmakers, talent, and creative relationships managed through Programming. In addition to accreditation and credentialing, this role owns Tribeca's existing industry-facing programs, including the Creators' Market and Storytelling Summit, leading their growth plans and working closely with Programming on their curation and execution. They will build and lead a team, set department goals and budget priorities, and serve as Tribeca's primary industry ambassador to this business-side industry community across the global festival and market landscape. This role also acts as a key strategic partner to Programming, Partnerships, Marketing, and Operations, ensuring industry considerations are embedded across the Festival's broader vision.

ABOUT YOU
You are a seasoned industry leader with a deep and active rolodex of sales agents, distributors (domestic and international), buyers, financiers, and producers' reps, and a track record of converting those relationships into measurable program growth. You understand the businesses and goals of every industry constituency at a festival — and can speak persuasively and credibly with them about a festival's slate and value proposition. You are as comfortable setting multi-year strategy and owning a budget as you are working a market floor or trouble-shooting a delegate's issue in real time. You bring a builder's mindset: proactive, entrepreneurial, and energized by the challenge of scaling a program and a team. Above all, you are a diplomatic, positive, and decisive leader who keeps Tribeca's mission — connecting filmmakers and creators with the people who can bring their work to a wider audience — at the center of everything you do.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Strategy & Vision
• Own and continually evolve Tribeca's long-term industry strategy, in partnership with the Festival Director, strengthening the Festival's position within the global marketplace ecosystem alongside other major festivals and markets (e.g., Sundance, Berlinale/EFM, Cannes Marché du Film, TIFF, SXSW, and AFM).
• Set annual goals and KPIs for industry attendance, accreditation/badge revenue, sales activity, and deal-making outcomes, and report progress to senior leadership.
• Identify, pilot, and scale new industry programs and revenue-generating programs beyond the Festival's existing offerings (e.g., unscripted/nonfiction sales initiatives, emerging media and technology partners, international co-production forums).
• Develop a strategy to grow Tribeca's relevance and industry presence beyond film, reflecting the Festival's interdisciplinary identity — identifying and cultivating new creative industries such as gaming, podcasts/audio, digital and online creators, and television/episodic.
• Serve as a strategic advisor to the Festival Director and senior leadership on industry trends, market shifts, and competitive positioning.
Year-Round Cultivation & Relationship Management (Business-Side Industry)
• Build, maintain, and expand relationships with sales agents, distributors, buyers, streamers, financiers, and producers' reps on a year-round basis — not solely in the lead-up to the Festival.
• Lead personalized outreach and cultivation of past, current, and prospective industry delegates, with a focus on expanding and diversifying the industry base year over year.
• Represent Tribeca at other major festivals, markets, and industry events throughout the year to cultivate relationships, gather market intelligence, and promote Tribeca's line-up and programs.
• Serve as the primary, senior point of contact for industry partners, including major sales agencies, studios, and distributors representing films in the Festival.
Business Development & Revenue Growth
• Own the industry growth targets and budget, including accreditation/credential revenue and related industry revenue streams.
• Design and execute strategies to grow paid industry attendance and market participation, including new packages, tiers, or offerings for buyers and sellers.
• Track, analyze, and report on industry program performance and revenue to the Festival Director and organizational leadership.
Industry Programs: Creators' Market & Storytelling Summit
• Own strategic and operational oversight of Tribeca's existing industry-facing programs, including the Creators' Market and Storytelling Summit, in addition to accreditation and credentialing.
• Lead multi-year growth plans for both programs, including targets for participation, attendance, and revenue, and present progress against those plans to the Festival Director and senior leadership.
• Work closely with Programming on the curatorial direction, session/track design, speaker and participant selection, and overall programming of the Creators' Market and Storytelling Summit.
• Identify opportunities to expand or evolve these programs — new tracks, formats, or partner categories — in response to industry trends and Festival growth goals.
Programming & Slate Support
• Partner closely with Programming on slate strategy, buyer/distributor previews, premiere status, and rights considerations for films in the Festival.
• Oversee the creation of market-facing materials, including slate documents, buyer decks, and premiere/availability information.
• Coordinate slate overview calls and screening schedules between the Programming team and buyers/distributors.
Team Leadership & Department Management
• Build, hire, train, and manage a year-round and seasonal Industry team, including managers and coordinators.
• Establish department structure, workflows, onboarding, and training to support a growing industry program.
• Set performance goals for direct reports and manage staff performance, development, and accountability.
• Own the Industry department's operating budget and staffing plan.
Festival Execution
• Own the end-to-end industry delegate experience at the Festival — registration, credentialing, the Industry Concierge desk, hospitality, and off-boarding.
• Design and host dedicated networking and social programming for industry delegates (e.g., mixers, receptions, breakfasts, and lounges) to drive cultivation and repeat attendance.
• Serve as the primary escalation point for issues affecting industry delegates during the Festival.
• Oversee P&I (press and industry) screening reporting, attendance tracking, and delegate communications during the Festival.
• Attend Festival events, screenings, and market functions as Tribeca's senior industry representative.
Cross-Departmental & Organizational Leadership
• Serve as a member of Festival leadership, representing Industry in cross-departmental planning and organization-wide strategy.
• Partner closely with Marketing, Partnerships/Sponsorship, Communications, Box Office, and Operations to align industry initiatives — including sponsorship and brand-partner opportunities tied to the industry program — with broader Festival goals.
• Act as the primary liaison between the Industry department and internal stakeholders, ensuring timely, accurate information flow in both directions.

QUALIFICATIONS
• 15 years of progressive experience with sales agents, distributors, or buyers in a film festival, market, or industry organization setting, including experience in a senior or leadership capacity.
• A deep, active rolodex of industry contacts spanning domestic and international distributors, sales agents, producers, and financiers.
• Demonstrated success building, scaling, or growing an industry, market, or business development program, including revenue accountability.
• Experience building, managing, and developing a team, and owning a departmental budget.
• Excellent executive communication and external representation skills; comfort serving as the public face of a program to senior industry stakeholders.
• In-depth, current knowledge of the global film industry, sales and distribution landscape, and international festival/market ecosystem.
• Strategic sensibility, with the ability to balance long-term vision with hands-on, detail-oriented execution.
• Ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
• Curiosity about and familiarity with adjacent creative industries beyond film, and an interest in identifying where Tribeca can build new relevance and relationships, is a strong plus.

Salary Range $125,000 -150,000

title: Associate Editor - Romance
description:
Sourcebooks is revolutionizing romance publishing—and we’re looking for an Associate Editor to help us take our authors and their stories to the next level.

As one of the fastest-growing publishers in the industry, Sourcebooks has built a market-leading, author-first approach that delivers unforgettable stories to devoted readers. If you are a passionate, hands-on editor with experience in shaping commercially successful fiction—and you love romance—this is an incredible opportunity to work closely with bestselling and breakout authors to craft books that readers can’t put down.

In this role you will acquire, edit, and manage your own list of adult romance authors while providing essential editorial and publishing support to senior staff. This is a hands-on role for a self-sufficient, commercially minded editor who is ready to build a list, champion authors, and help shape the future of a dynamic imprint. The ideal candidate has a deep, current understanding of the romance market as well as a strong sense of what readers are excited to discover next. You’ll evaluate submissions, develop projects from acquisition through publication, collaborate across departments, and build lasting relationships with authors and agents. You’ll also support senior editors with precision, initiative, and good judgment, helping keep a fast-moving list on track. If you’re a deeply engaged, perceptive romance reader, an entrepreneurial editor, and someone eager to make a meaningful mark on the genre, we’d love to hear from you.

This is an exempt, salary position with a salary range of $55,000 - $65,000. We determine starting pay based on a thorough evaluation of job-related factors, including geographic location, market conditions, relevant experience, training, and education. This process ensures a fair and competitive salary that aligns with both the company and the candidate’s qualifications.

The location for this position can be hybrid or remote in New York or Naperville, Illinois or remote based in any of the following states: Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, Washington D.C. and Wisconsin. This role includes some travel, including occasional meetings at the home office in Naperville, IL.

What You'll Do:
  • Build and develop a romance list by identifying, evaluating, and soliciting manuscripts in priority categories and areas of opportunity.
  • Monitor the romance marketplace, reader trends, competitive titles, and industry developments to identify acquisition and positioning opportunities.
  • Present potential acquisitions at editorial and acquisitions meetings; recommend projects, recruit authors, evaluate proposals, and participate in contract negotiations with authors and agents under Associate Editorial Director guidance.
  • Develop acquired manuscripts for content, structure, voice, commercial appeal, and market positioning; assist senior editors with early editorial reads of key titles as assigned.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with author and agent partners.
  • Collaborate closely with marketing, publicity, sales, and design to identify opportunities and ensure that each title is positioned effectively for its intended audience.
  • Maintain accurate editorial schedules and serve as a proactive point of contact for authors, agents, and internal stakeholders to keep projects moving on time.
  • Support senior editors with editorial preparation, launch materials, acquisitions materials, and other high-priority projects as assigned. Tasks will include conducting development first reads, assisting with list management, and completing editorial and administrative tasks as assigned.
  • Manage general editorial and administrative responsibilities as needed, including correspondence, shipping, copyediting and proofreading corrections, and other tasks necessary to support a successful publishing program.
What You Bring:
  • 3–5 years of publishing experience, with significant experience in romance editorial. Direct experience with evaluating submissions, making acquisition recommendations, and acquiring romance fiction.
  • Be a self-starter. Exhibit initiative, leadership, and a strong curiosity about what’s next in book and product development.
  • A willingness to play well with others. Seriously, we’re a hard-working team who also happen to be pretty nice.
  • The ability to juggle and coordinate at great speed. We want a clear communicator who is detail-oriented, organized and can keep short- and long-term projects on schedule while following through on deadlines.
  • Comfort speaking in front of groups and building strong relationships across teams and with external partners.
  • A positive, collaborative spirit; we’re a “yes, AND!” kind of team.
  • Strong editorial judgment, commercial instincts, and the ability to articulate why a project will appeal to romance readers.
  • A voracious reading habit in adult romance, with strong familiarity with traditional and indie authors, tropes, trends, and community conversations.
Why Sourcebooks?
Sourcebooks is a thriving entrepreneurial publisher driven by our mission to change lives through books. The fifth-largest publisher in the U.S. by print units sold, we bring extraordinary authors to readers in dynamic, data-driven ways, leading to hundreds of national and international bestsellers. Our insight-driven approach has earned us recognition from Fast Company as a Most Innovative Company, a Best Workplace for Innovators, a Most Loved Workplace by Newsweek, a Best Workplace by Inc., and Publishers Weekly’s nod as “the most successful self-made publisher operating in the 21st century.” Story by story, book by book, we have changed more than 300 million lives. Join us as we change 300 million more!

Ready to Apply:

Please submit your resume, salary requirements, and cover letter detailing your relevant experience and interest in this role. Applications without a cover letter will not be considered. Show us your passion and creativity — we’re looking for someone who’s as enthusiastic about this opportunity as we are!

Full-time employees are eligible for our comprehensive benefits program. Our range of benefits include, but are not limited to, Medical/Prescription drug insurance, Dental, Vision, Health Care, Dependent Care, Flexible Spending Account, Health Savings Account 401(k), Short and Long-Term Disability Insurance, Life/AD&D Insurance, & generous paid time off.

Sourcebooks values the array of talents and perspectives that a diverse workforce brings. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status.

title: Assistant Conservator for East Asian Works of Art on Paper
description:
We Are Committed to an Inclusive Workplace

At the Philadelphia Museum of Art, we actively seek to employ a diverse group of people who embody our organizational values. We welcome and encourage individuals of all backgrounds to apply, especially those from marginalized and underrepresented groups in the museum field, who are inspired by our shared purpose and enjoy working collaboratively with others.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship or immigration status, color, disability, ethnicity, familial status, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected status.

How You Will Contribute

The Philadelphia Museum of Art seeks to hire an Assistant Conservator for East Asian Works of Art on Paper for a two-year term. Working closely with the museum’s Senior Conservator of Works of Art on Paper in our state-of-the art paper conservation laboratory, the Assistant Conservator will study the scope and materiality of the museum’s Asian Art works on paper, evaluate strategies for conserving works in specific media, and perform conservation examinations and treatments. This growing and important collection comprises 9,400 objects of which 1,000 are East Asian hanging scrolls, handscrolls, album leaves, and folding screens and 6,100 Chinese and Japanese woodblock prints. The Assistant Conservator will serve as an integral member of the museum’s conservation staff and participate in activities relating to exhibitions, installations, loans, preventive care of the permanent collections, and professional and public engagement, gaining a broad range of knowledge, skills, and techniques to launch their career in this specialized field.


Specifically, you will:
  • Examine, conduct research, and perform conservation treatment on a broad range of Asian works of art on paper
  • Coordinate and assist consulting Asian Conservation specialists as they are contracted for treatment or remounting projects
  • Assess the condition of works requested for loan or being considered for acquisition, and document the condition of incoming or outgoing loans
  • Participate and support preventative conservation initiatives for the care of Asian art on paper in the galleries and in storage
  • Advise on housing, installation, storage, handling, packing, and transport of works of art
  • Collaborate with conservation scientists in chemical and instrumental analysis and characterization of materials of works of art
  • Conduct microfadometry analysis of light sensitive works of art using a Fotonowy Automated Fadeometer
  • Serve as a liaison with conservation studios and material researchers in Asia on matters pertaining to the conservation of the museum’s collection
  • Work with Asian Art curatorial staff and consulting specialists to identify and plan, and prioritize Asian Art preservation projects
  • Represent the museum’s Conservation Division in a range of institutional initiatives and functions, as well as in professional and public engagement

Your background and experience include:
  • Academic credentials from a recognized conservation training program and a minimum of 2 years specialized experience beyond the degree in the study, care, and treatment of works of art on paper.
  • Proven ability to plan and execute a variety of complex conservation treatments
  • Preliminary experience and training in the conservation of Asian works of art on paper (e.g., internships, fellowships, intensive trainings, etc.)
  • Experience/interest in microfadometry analysis of works of art on paper
  • Demonstrated visual, manual, and scholarly aptitudes. Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Familiarity with Asian art, languages, and cultures
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively


Position and Compensation Details
  • The salary for this position is $64,000.
  • This position is Full-Time, Exempt, and 35 hours per week.
  • This position is part of the AFSCME Local 397 bargaining unit.
  • This position reports to he Charles K. Williams, II, Senior Conservator of Works of Art on Paper
  • This is a 2 year term position.
  • Physical requirements:
    • Able to remain stationary for extended periods of time, to utilize computers and other office equipment required of this job, to perform physically administrative duties in a typical interior office environment, gallery, or exhibit space, and to access most public and staff areas of the museum campus
  • Background check required after a conditional job offer is made. Consideration of the background check will be tailored to the requirements of the job.


Institutional Requirements
  • Upholds the professional standards of the field, always acts in a manner that is consistent with the best interests of the museum and protects and enhances its reputation and standing within the community of museums.
  • Adheres to the museum’s code of ethics and Employee Handbook and avoids any real or perceived conflicts of interest.
  • Shows respect for co-workers and visitors and an understanding of and appreciation for the diversity of the museum’s staff, volunteers, and audiences.
  • Maintains confidentiality.
  • Adheres to all museum protocols, procedures, rules, and policies.


Application Timeline

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage candidates to apply early as the position will close once we have a robust applicant pool or a candidate has been selected.

Application Procedures:

• Cover letter
• Curriculum vitae
• Examination and treatment reports (including photographic documentation) for two works of art (no more than 10MB); or a link to documents
• Contact information (phone number and email) for three professional references familiar with the candidate’s work


What We Offer

Our employees are at the center of the museum. As an employee, you will have access to numerous museum perks including, but not limited to:
  • Free general admission to the museum for you and your immediate family
  • Discounted guest tickets for admission
  • Discounts on gift memberships
  • Special staff tours and presentations from our curatorial and conservation teams
  • Discounts at the museum restaurant, museum cafés, and museum retail and online stores

We offer a comprehensive benefits package for employees including:
  • Medical, dental, and vision benefits
  • Fully paid short-term disability insurance, long-term disability insurance, and life insurance
  • Health savings or flexible spending account program
  • Retirement savings program with museum match
  • Paid vacation, personal days, sick days, and holidays

*Eligibility for certain benefits is based on a variety of factors including the employee’s regular schedule and tenure.

Be careful of Recruitment Scams: Fraudsters or employment scammers often pose as legitimate recruiters, employers, recruitment consultants or job placement firms, advertising false job opportunities through email, text messages and WhatsApp messages. They aim to cheat jobseekers out of money or to steal personal information.

To help you look out for potential recruitment scams, here are some Red Flags:

  • Upfront Payment Requests: Deloitte will never ask for any upfront payment for background checks, job training, or supplies.
  • Requests for Personal Information: Be wary if you are asked for sensitive personal information, especially early in the recruitment process and without a clear need for it. Fraudulent links or contractual documents may require the provision of sensitive personal data or copy documents (e.g., government issued numbers or identity documents, passports or passport numbers, bank account statements or numbers, parent’s data) that may be used for identity fraud. Do not provide or send any of these documents or data. Please note we will never ask for photographs at any stage of the recruitment process.
  • Unprofessional Communication: Scammers may communicate in an unprofessional manner. Their messages may be filled with poor grammar and spelling errors. The look and feel may not be consistent with the Deloitte corporate brand.

If you're unsure, make direct contact with Deloitte using our official contact details. Be careful not to use any contact details provided in the suspicious job advertisement or email.

We actively support the inclusion of people with disabilities and embrace neurodiversity in the workplace. We recognise and value the unique strengths that neurodivergent individuals bring, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive.

title: Senior Program Coordinator – Clean Cities and Clean Vehicles
description:

The Houston-Galveston Area Council is one of the largest regional planning commissions in the country with a diverse service area of 13 counties and more than 7 million people. We are the pulse of our region, addressing issues that cross city limits and county lines every single day.

We make decisions that affect our transportation system, ensure the safety and well-being of our seniors, connect people to jobs, help families recover from natural disasters, preserve water quality for our children, and so much more. title: Financial Audit Intern- Local Government Audit, Middle TN- Summer 2027
description:
​Local Government Audit Intern, Middle
Summer 2027: June 1 - August 6

About Our Program
The Comptroller of the Treasury's Audit Internship Program is a 10-week paid educational and experiential learning opportunity offering undergraduate students a chance to witness and participate in the audit operations of the office. Interns will spend the summer building skills through their assignment to an active audit, audit-specific training, and professional development training. Interns will also have opportunities to build relationships with each other through shared experiences.

Intern responsibilities may include learning to examine and review records, reports, financial statements, and management practices for local government entities and other organizations receiving public funds. Interns may have the opportunity to evaluate the following: fairness of financial statement presentation; the adequacy of internal controls; the efficiency and effectiveness of an entity's operations and systems; and compliance with laws, regulations, contracts, and grant agreements.

Our summer internship program is designed to be both professionally and academically beneficial. Interns gain hands‑on experience while participating in meaningful professional development activities such as Business Etiquette Day, a full‑day session focused on professionalism, emotional intelligence, and understanding one’s professional brand, complete with an etiquette lunch led by staff. Interns also enjoy engaging activities like speed networking with full‑time employees, a guided tour of the Tennessee Capitol to explore the state’s history, and weekly cohort check‑ins to foster connection and collaboration. The cohort experience culminates in a final presentation showcasing what interns have learned and contributed during their time with the Office.

Location
This Local Government Audit internship opportunity will be based out of the Middle Tennessee Region. Depending on the audit assignment, interns may have the opportunity for limited travel to counties across the Middle Tennessee Region during the summer.
​
Who We're Looking For
We are seeking students who are rising juniors, seniors, or enrolled in graduate accounting programs and are interested in applying their classroom knowledge to governmental auditing. To qualify for the internship program, applicants should have successfully completed at least 6 credit hours of accounting coursework. Preference will be given to students who have completed intermediate or advanced accounting classes.

Successful interns are those who are adaptable, able to think critically, work well both individually and as part of a team, and are willing to learn and grow. Candidates should exhibit strong interpersonal, verbal communication, organizational, and writing skills. Interns are expected to apply their classroom knowledge to meaningful audit work.

About Our Office
The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury is responsible for the audit of state and local governmental entities and participates in the general financial and administrative management and oversight of state government. In the Comptroller’s Office, we strive to deliver on our mission to make government work better. Through dedicated hard work and commitment, every Comptroller’s Office employee accepts personal responsibility to accomplish our mission and uphold it.

Compensation
Interns are paid $24 per hour via a third-party company. Travel is required for Local Government Audit Interns but is generally confined to same-day commutes to and from a job site. Overnight stays are required for intern events, typically 3 per summer. Overnight hotel stay(s) and related expenses are reimbursed.

Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Document Specialist & Training Specialist (Document Remediation)
description:
At Team Carney, we believe that true performance acceleration happens at the intersection of innovative learning and deep strategic expertise. Since 1994, our mission has been to provide top-tier training, learning, and human capital solutions that empower Federal Government agencies to meet their critical mandates. We are seeking a dedicated Document Specialist & Training Specialist (Document Remediation) to support our federal client.

This position is contingent on contract award.

Work Schedule and Location

  • Employment Status: Full-Time

  • Location: This position is fully remote within the U.S.

Who You Are & What You’ll Do

The Document Specialist & Training Specialist (Document Remediation) will combine hands-on technical document accessibility remediation with instructor-led training delivery to ensure federal digital content meets strict Section 508 accessibility standards.

In this full-time role, you will perform technical evaluation and remediation of electronic documents and forms across Microsoft Office and Adobe PDF formats using tests endorsed by the Federal CIO Council Community of Practice. In addition to direct remediation work, you will design, create, and facilitate instructor-led training sessions to educate government personnel on document accessibility standards, evaluation methodologies, and remediation techniques. You will also assist the government in making multimedia content fully Section 508 compliant.

What You Bring to the Table - Requirements

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.

  • Experience:

    • 2+ years of dedicated experience evaluating and remediating electronic documents and forms (including Microsoft Office Suite and Adobe PDF) for Section 508 compliance.

    • Proven experience creating and delivering instructor-led training materials and conducting training sessions on document accessibility.

  • Standards Knowledge: Broad knowledge and practical understanding of Accessibility Tests for Documents endorsed by the Federal CIO Council Community of Practice and Revised Section 508 Standards.

  • Core Capabilities:

    • Document & Form Remediation: Skilled in evaluating, remediating, and validating complex electronic documents, PDFs, fillable forms, spreadsheets, and presentations to ensure full accessibility.

    • Instructional Delivery: Demonstrated ability to provide clear verbal and written instruction and conduct engaging instructor-led training on document accessibility and remediation techniques.

    • Multimedia Compliance: Ability to assist the government in making multimedia content, digital assets, and video materials Section 508 compliant (including captioning, transcripts, and audio descriptions).

    • Communication: Excellent technical writing and oral presentation skills to translate accessibility standards into clear, actionable training content for government personnel.

Why Join Team Carney?

When you join Team Carney, you join a legacy of excellence. We focus on our people because when we make a positive impact on the lives of our employees, they are able to make a positive impact on our clients. We offer a full suite of competitive benefits, including:

  • Health & Wellness: Multiple medical, dental, and vision insurance options (BCBS CareFirst), health spending accounts (HSA), and flexible spending accounts (FSA).

  • Financial Security: 401(k) retirement plan with company match, plus Carney-paid life and disability insurance.

  • Work-Life Harmony: Generous Paid Time Off (PTO), 11 paid holidays, and 6 weeks of paid parental leave.

  • Professional & Personal Growth: Annual tuition assistance (up to $5,000) and student loan repayment.

  • Get Out and Learn: Up to $200 annually to learn almost anything (from pottery to coding!).

  • Get Out and Run: Up to $200 annually to participate in fitness and active lifestyle events.

  • Continuous Development: Ad hoc training and ongoing professional development access.

title: Job Coach
description:

Location: Bridgewater, Virginia

Hours: Up to 29 hours per week, with the potential to transition to full-time

Help People Build Careers and Greater Independence

RISE Services is hiring a compassionate, dependable, and resourceful Job Coach / Employment Specialist to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain meaningful employment.

In this community-based role, you will meet participants at employer worksites and other locations throughout Bridgewater, Harrisonburg, and surrounding Rockingham County communities. You will help participants explore employment interests, search and apply for jobs, prepare for interviews, learn workplace responsibilities, communicate with employers, and develop the skills needed for long-term employment success.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. We welcome applicants with relevant experience in disability services, human services, education, behavioral health, workforce development, direct support, career coaching, case management, retail supervision, customer service, or other positions involving teaching, mentoring, or helping others succeed.

Training is provided.

Schedule and Hours

This position offers up to 29 hours per week. Most services are provided during daytime hours, Monday through Friday.

Weekend work is occasionally needed to provide coverage when another employee is unavailable, but this is not a regularly scheduled weekend position.

Weekly schedules may include:

  • On-site job coaching

  • Job searching and completing applications

  • Resume and interview preparation

  • Employer outreach

  • Employment-readiness activities

  • Community-based participant meetings

  • Progress notes and required documentation

When a participant is not working their full number of authorized service hours, the Job Coach may provide other approved employment services, including job searching, completing applications, developing resumes, preparing for interviews, contacting employers, and teaching workplace-readiness skills.

Employees who want additional hours may have the opportunity to transition to full-time as caseloads and service needs grow. Full-time hours are not guaranteed and depend on participant referrals, scheduling needs, employee availability, and satisfactory job performance.

What You’ll Do

Job Coaching and Workplace Support

  • Provide individualized coaching at employer worksites and in community settings.

  • Help participants learn job duties, workplace routines, safety procedures, and employer expectations.

  • Teach workplace communication, professional behavior, time management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Help participants communicate effectively with supervisors and coworkers.

  • Develop natural workplace supports that promote greater independence.

  • Monitor progress and adjust coaching strategies as participants develop new skills.

  • Provide ongoing support to promote successful job retention.

Job Search and Career Preparation

  • Help participants identify their strengths, interests, abilities, support needs, and employment goals.

  • Assist with resumes, applications, job searches, and interview preparation.

  • Conduct mock interviews and employment-readiness activities.

  • Identify opportunities that match each participant’s interests, abilities, experience, and goals.

  • Coordinate interviews, hiring activities, and onboarding support.

  • Help participants understand workplace expectations and identify reasonable accommodations when appropriate.

Employer and Community Engagement

  • Build professional relationships with employers throughout the local community.

  • Contact businesses to identify potential employment opportunities.

  • Educate employers about inclusive hiring and available workplace supports.

  • Communicate with participants, families, employers, counselors, schools, and community partners.

  • Attend hiring events, team meetings, training, and other scheduled activities.

Documentation and Service Coordination

  • Complete accurate progress notes and service documentation within required deadlines.

  • Maintain participant records according to funding-source and organizational requirements.

  • Track job searches, applications, interviews, placements, wages, scheduled hours, and employment retention.

title: Packaging Line Lead (201 B-shift)
description:
Job Summary:

The Packaging Line Lead is responsible for overseeing the setup, operation, and documentation of the packaging line to ensure efficient, compliant, and high-quality production. This role coordinates with cross-functional teams, troubleshoots equipment issues, and ensures adherence to batch production records and regulatory standards.

Key Responsibilities:

Line Preparation & Setup

  • Confirm line clearance prior to each new lot and ensure complete setup per batch production record (BPR), including filler hoses, nozzles, screens, pumps, and other components.
  • Assemble and connect equipment and filler parts, verifying proper cleaning and documentation.
  • Stage and verify labeling and packaging components, ensuring accuracy of lot numbers and expiration dates.
  • Coordinate product changeovers, including pre-staging of equipment parts and materials, disassembling equipment, cleaning per SOPs, and reassembly.

Production Monitoring & Troubleshooting

  • Monitor equipment performance throughout production, ensuring operational criteria (e.g., filler speed, mixing speeds, sealing temperatures, portable tank condition) meet BPR specifications.
  • Ensure continuous supply of containers and closures in coordination with Material Handlers.
  • Collaborate with Maintenance, QA, and Supervisors to identify and resolve process issues, documenting all occurrences in the Packaging Record.
  • Work with QA to verify fill volume/weight and make necessary adjustments to meet lot specifications.
  • Operation of packaging equipment as part of the line crew

Documentation & Compliance

  • Accurately complete all required documentation in the Packaging Records and associated logbooks.
  • Perform SAP transactions related to packaging runs.
  • Review batch records and line logbooks to ensure proper documentation and compliance with SOPs and regulatory standards.
  • Ensure changeover activities and time are accurately recorded in appropriate systems.

Leadership & Coordination

  • Organize and direct the work of Packaging Personnel on assigned lines/shifts, provide guidance, answering questions, providing clear and concise communication, demonstrating conflict resolution abilities and conducting training as needed.
  • Communicate effectively with other departments regarding labeling, packaging components, equipment status, and production challenges.
  • Interface with QA, Validation, and Maintenance to ensure line readiness and timely completion of preventive maintenance procedures.
  • Demonstrate Empathetic understanding, effective listening and have ability to provide constructive feedback.

Quality & Safety

  • Monitor cleanliness and orderliness of work areas, ensuring compliance with safety, GMP, and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure all operations follow company policies, procedures, and applicable State, Federal, and Local laws.
  • Identify opportunities and challenges related to compliance with Quality / EH&S and escalate for proactive elimination of risks.

Required Skills/Abilities:

  • Must be able to speak and read in English.
  • Ability to perform basic Math computations.
  • Follows verbal and written directions.
  • Communicates clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing.
  • Establishes and maintains cooperative working relationships with others.

Education and Experience:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent
  • Experience in Manufacturing processes and equipment procedures.
  • 2-5 years of experience in pharmaceutical, medical device, and/or food manufacturing
  • Knowledge of Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP’s).
  • Familiarity with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and other regulatory requirements.
  • Understanding of SOP’s, equipment and safety practices.

Physical Requirements/ Working Conditions:

Employees in this position are subject to extended periods of sitting, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, bending, vision monitoring, lifting equipment or materials up to 30 pounds.

  • Support reconstruction of exercise events.
  • Support doctrine / Tactics, Techniques and Procedures (TTP) validation and product modifications.

• Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or other regulated industries.

Ericsson Enterprise Wireless Solutions, Inc. seeks a Developer (Senior Software Development Engineer) in Boise, ID, or various unanticipated worksites throughout the U.S., responsible for designing and developing SaaS applications for private 5G networks; building event-driven microservices in Golang using GCP Pub/Sub; architecting highly available and scalable cloud-based backend services; developing RESTful APIs; and integrating monitoring, analytics, and messaging platforms across multi-cloud environments.

What you will do:

Design and develop SaaS applications using event-driven microservices architectures for private 5G networks. Use PostgreSQL for event sourcing and analytics, persisting event logs, metadata, and state changes.   • High School Diploma or GED required.

Experience
  • Prior experience in a retail/boutique store dealing with high-end goods, and clientele-oriented sales.
  • Ideally has a cultivated and established clientele following
  • Experience working in retail environment(s) with 7 days a week operation, which require open scheduling availability based on business needs.

COMPETENCIES REQUIRED

  • Candidates must also be outgoing, energetic, professional and good representatives of our brand and be able to emanate the James Perse brand lifestyle.
  • Strong interpersonal and communications skills both verbal and written.
  • Strong independent work ethic, excellent time management skills, and high level of integrity.
  • Composure: Ability to handle customer interactions and potential issues or concerns courteously and professionally.

PAY TRANSPARENCY

This position pays $20.00 per hour plus commission on personal net sales.

JAMES PERSE was founded over 20 years ago in Los Angeles, California by its eponymous designer. James’ signature design philosophy and aesthetic – the pairing of elegance and sophistication with simplicity and comfort – is borne from his passion for minimalist architecture and (as a Los Angeles native) his intimate familiarity with west coast indoor / outdoor living and the casual clothing inspired by it. This approach has been applied to each step in developing the JAMES PERSE brand, which has become synonymous with Southern California life and style.

At the Company’s inception, James’ mission was to bring an elevated look and feel to unique baseball caps and basic tees. Two decades later, the Company has expanded to producing full lines of its famously soft and meticulously constructed modern classics for men and women, as well as home furnishings, accessories, and limited edition goods. Our collections are sold in over 40 JAMES PERSE boutiques, as well as in fine department and specialty stores around the world.

title: Physical Therapist (PT) – Mobile/Home-Based Care
description:
Overview

We are seeking a skilled, compassionate, and dependable Physical Therapist (PT) to provide high-quality physical therapy services to patients in their homes throughout the Tucson region.

The Physical Therapist will travel to patients' homes to perform comprehensive evaluations, develop individualized plans of care, provide skilled therapeutic interventions, monitor patient progress, and educate patients and caregivers on strategies to improve mobility, function, safety, and independence.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working independently in a home-based environment, has strong clinical judgment and communication skills, and is passionate about delivering patient-centered care.

This is a 1099 independent contractor position.

Duties and Responsibilities

· Travel to patients' homes throughout the assigned service area to provide physical therapy services.

· Perform comprehensive physical therapy evaluations in the patient's home environment.

· Assess strength, range of motion, balance, gait, mobility, coordination, endurance, pain, functional limitations, and ability to safely perform activities of daily living.

· Evaluate the patient's home environment and identify potential safety and fall risks that may impact mobility and independence.

· Develop individualized plans of care based on evaluation findings, physician orders/referrals, patient needs, clinical judgment, and functional goals.

· Establish measurable short-term and long-term functional goals.

· Provide skilled physical therapy interventions appropriate to the patient's diagnosis and functional limitations, including:

o Therapeutic exercises

o Therapeutic activities

o Neuromuscular re-education

o Gait and mobility training

o Balance and coordination training

o Functional strengthening

o Manual therapy when clinically appropriate

o Transfer training

o Fall prevention and safety training

· Train patients in the safe use of assistive devices such as walkers, canes, and other mobility equipment.

· Develop and instruct patients in individualized home exercise programs.

· Educate patients and caregivers regarding diagnosis, treatment, exercises, mobility, safety, fall prevention, and strategies to promote independence.

· Monitor patient response to treatment and make appropriate clinical modifications to the plan of care.

· Perform reassessments and communicate changes in patient condition or functional status as appropriate.

· Coordinate care with physicians, nurses, caregivers, physical therapist assistants, occupational therapists, and other healthcare professionals.

· Communicate effectively with referring providers regarding patient progress, concerns, and recommendations.

· Complete accurate, timely, and thorough documentation for evaluations, daily treatment visits, reassessments, progress reports, and discharge summaries.

· Maintain compliance with applicable federal and state regulations, professional standards, payer requirements, and company policies.

· Recognize changes in patient condition that may require physician notification, additional medical evaluation, or modification of treatment.

· Maintain patient confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries at all times.

· Provide compassionate, respectful, and professional care to patients and their families in the home setting.

Requirements

· Current and valid Texas Physical Therapist license in good standing.

· Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapy program.

· Strong knowledge of anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, and rehabilitation principles.

· Strong clinical reasoning and patient assessment skills.

· Ability to independently perform comprehensive PT evaluations and develop appropriate plans of care.

· Experience treating patients with orthopedic, musculoskeletal, neurological, balance, gait, weakness, mobility, and/or functional limitations preferred.

· Strong knowledge of therapeutic exercise, gait training, balance training, functional mobility, neuromuscular re-education, and fall prevention.

· Excellent patient assessment and acute/chronic pain management skills.

· Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

· Ability to work independently and effectively manage a mobile patient caseload.

· Must be punctual, dependable, organized, and professional.

· Comfortable entering and providing care in patients' homes and working with patients and caregivers in a home-based environment.

· Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required.

· Ability to travel throughout the assigned service area.

· CPR/BLS certification preferred or required according to company policy.

· Previous home health, mobile therapy, outpatient, orthopedic, neurological, geriatric, or community-based experience is preferred.

Mobile/Home-Based Care Expectations

Because this position involves providing care in patients' homes, the Physical Therapist must be able to:

· Arrive at scheduled visits within the expected timeframe.

· Manage travel time and maintain an efficient daily schedule.

· Carry and transport necessary clinical equipment and supplies.

· Adapt treatment approaches to different home environments and available space.

· Maintain a safe and professional environment during every patient visit.

· Communicate promptly regarding cancellations, scheduling changes, or patient concerns.

· Respect patients' homes, privacy, routines, and individual preferences.

· Demonstrate sound clinical judgment when working independently in the community.

Documentation and Compliance

The Physical Therapist is responsible for completing all required clinical documentation accurately and within established timeframes, including:

· Initial evaluations

· Treatment notes

· Reassessments

· Progress reports

· Recertifications, when applicable

· Discharge documentation

· Home exercise programs

· Communication with referring providers

· Other documentation required by the organization, payer, or applicable regulations

Job Type

Full-time – 1099 Independent Contractor

Pay Structure (1099)

· Guaranteed base pay: $1,080 per week

· Base compensation is calculated at $45 per patient visit, based on a minimum of 6 patient visits per day.

· $45 per additional patient visit for visits beyond the daily base of 6.

· Compensation is subject to the terms of the independent contractor agreement.

Schedule

4/10 Schedule

· Four 10-hour workdays per week

· Typical start time: 7:30 AM–8:30 AM, depending on patient scheduling and geographic coverage.

· Daily schedule may vary based on patient locations, visit duration, and patient needs.

Work Location

Mobile/Home-Based – Tucson Region

The Physical Therapist will travel to assigned patients' homes throughout the designated service area.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a clinically confident, compassionate, and self-motivated Physical Therapist who enjoys working one-on-one with patients and families. The successful candidate will be comfortable making clinical decisions independently, adapting treatment to the patient's home environment, and providing high-quality care while maintaining excellent documentation and communication.

This position is an excellent opportunity for a Physical Therapist who values autonomy, flexibility, meaningful patient relationships, and community-based care

title: ESP Field Service Supervisor
description:

title: Job Coach
description:
Job Coach / Employment Specialist – Part-Time

Location: Frederick, Maryland
Service Area: Frederick and surrounding Frederick County communities
Pay: $21.00–$22.00 per hour, based on experience
Hours: Up to 29 hours per week, with the potential to transition to full-time
Schedule: Predominantly daytime hours, Monday through Friday
Work Setting: Community-based with regular local travel
Mileage: Reimbursement for approved work-related travel

Help People Build Careers and Greater Independence

RISE Services is hiring a compassionate, dependable, and resourceful Job Coach / Employment Specialist to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, obtain, and maintain meaningful employment.

In this community-based role, you will meet participants at employer worksites and other locations throughout Frederick and surrounding Frederick County communities. You will help participants explore career interests, search and apply for jobs, prepare for interviews, learn workplace responsibilities, communicate with employers, and develop the skills needed for long-term employment success.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. We welcome applicants with relevant experience in disability services, human services, education, behavioral health, workforce development, direct support, career coaching, case management, retail supervision, customer service, or other positions that involve teaching, mentoring, or helping others succeed.

Training is provided.

Schedule and Hours

This position offers up to 29 hours per week. Most services in the Frederick area are provided during daytime hours, Monday through Friday.

Weekend work is occasionally needed to provide coverage when another employee is unavailable, but this is not a regularly scheduled weekend position.

Weekly schedules may include:

  • On-site job coaching

  • Job searching and completing applications

  • Resume and interview preparation

  • Employer outreach

  • Employment-readiness activities

  • Community-based participant meetings

  • Progress notes and required documentation

When a participant is not working their full number of authorized service hours, the Job Coach may provide other approved employment services, including job searching, completing applications, developing resumes, preparing for interviews, contacting employers, and teaching workplace-readiness skills.

Employees who want additional hours may have the opportunity to transition to full-time as caseloads and service needs grow. Full-time hours are not guaranteed and depend on participant referrals, scheduling needs, employee availability, and satisfactory job performance.

What You’ll Do

Job Coaching and Workplace Support

  • Provide individualized coaching at employer worksites and in community settings.

  • Help participants learn job duties, workplace routines, safety procedures, and employer expectations.

  • Teach workplace communication, professional behavior, time management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Help participants communicate effectively with supervisors and coworkers.

  • Develop natural workplace supports that promote greater independence.

  • Monitor participant progress and adjust coaching strategies as participants develop new skills.

  • Provide ongoing support to promote successful employment retention.

Job Search and Career Preparation

  • Help participants identify their strengths, interests, abilities, support needs, and employment goals.

  • Assist participants with resumes, applications, job searches, and interview preparation.

  • Conduct mock interviews and employment-readiness activities.

  • Identify opportunities that match each participant’s interests, abilities, experience, and goals.

  • Coordinate interviews, hiring activities, and onboarding support.

  • Help participants understand workplace expectations and identify reasonable accommodations when appropriate.

Employer and Community Engagement

  • Build professional relationships with employers throughout Frederick and surrounding communities.

  • Contact businesses to identify potential employment opportunities.

  • Educate employers about inclusive hiring and available workplace supports.

  • Communicate with participants, families, employers, vocational rehabilitation counselors, schools, and community partners.

  • Attend hiring events, team meetings, training, and other scheduled activities.

Documentation and Service Coordination

  • Complete accurate progress notes and service documentation within required deadlines.

  • Maintain participant records according to funding-source and organizational requirements.

  • Track job searches, applications, interviews, placements, wages, scheduled hours, and employment retention.

  • Communicate participant progress, concerns, scheduling changes, and service needs to the appropriate supervisor.

  • Participate in service-planning and team-coordination activities.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree is not required.

  • Relevant experience supporting individuals with disabilities or others who experience barriers to employment is preferred.

  • Experience in teaching, coaching, mentoring, customer service, supervision, human services, behavioral health, workforce development, or a related field may also be considered.

  • Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

  • Ability to work independently and make responsible decisions in community settings.

  • Ability to maintain a consistent schedule and complete documentation on time.

  • Basic computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.

  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

  • Ability and willingness to travel locally and transport participants when required.

  • Ability to satisfy applicable background-screening and employment requirements.

Preferred but Not Required

  • Supported Employment, job-coaching, or job-development experience.

  • Experience supporting individuals with intellectual, developmental, behavioral, or other disabilities.

  • Knowledge of vocational rehabilitation or disability-employment services.

  • Understanding of the Americans with Disabilities Act and reasonable workplace accommodations.

  • Experience working with employers, schools, rehabilitation counselors, or community organizations.

  • CESP, ACRE, DSP, or another employment-support credential.

Who Will Succeed in This Position?

You may be a strong fit if you are:

  • Compassionate, patient, dependable, and encouraging.

  • Comfortable working at employer locations and throughout the community.

  • Able to teach and motivate participants while promoting independence.

  • Professional and confident when communicating with employers and community partners.

  • Resourceful and willing to find solutions when challenges arise.

  • Organized and able to manage appointments, follow-ups, and documentation.

  • Flexible when participant or employer schedules change.

  • Comfortable working independently without constant direct supervision.

Why Join RISE Services?

  • Make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals with disabilities.

  • Help people build careers, confidence, and greater independence.

  • Work predominantly during weekday daytime hours.

  • Receive mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel.

  • Participate in paid training and professional development.

  • Build experience in human services, disability services, workforce development, and career coaching.

  • Access potential opportunities for additional hours and advancement.

  • Join a collaborative, growing, and mission-driven organization.

Benefits

Part-time employees may be eligible for:

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Employee Tenure Bonus Program

  • Mileage reimbursement for approved work-related travel

  • Paid training and professional development

Employees who transition to an eligible full-time position may also receive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays

  • Short-term disability insurance

  • Life insurance

  • Long-term care option

Benefit eligibility requirements apply.

Important Work-Setting Information

This is a community-based position, not a remote or traditional office-based role. Services are provided at employer worksites and other community locations throughout Frederick and surrounding Frederick County communities.

Applicants must have reliable transportation and be comfortable driving between community locations. Transporting participants may be required as part of the position.

Equal Opportunity Employer

RISE Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We recruit, hire, train, compensate, and promote employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Apply Today

If you enjoy teaching, encouraging others, solving problems, and helping people accomplish meaningful goals, apply for the Part-Time Job Coach / Employment Specialist position with RISE Services.

A bachelor’s degree and previous job-coaching experience are not required. Relevant experience, dependability, professionalism, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to helping others succeed are strongly valued.
