title: AVP, AI Strategy & Transformation
description:
Job Description Summary

‎

Mosaic Health is seeking an Assistant Vice President of AI Strategy & Transformation to own the enterprise-wide AI strategy, governance, and portfolio execution across Mosaic Health, CareMore, Vera Whole Health, and Millennium. This is a high-visibility, high-accountability role at the center of one of the most consequential transformation programs in the organization's history: an enterprise AI value creation mandate for 2026-27 and a newly established three-tier governance structure built to deliver it.



The AVP, AI Strategy & Transformation serves as the primary AI strategy executive for the enterprise, partnering directly with the CIIO and enterprise IT leadership to translate AI investment into measurable clinical, operational, and financial outcomes. This leader chairs the AI Transformation Hub, serves as the AI Executive Council's Lead by owning its agenda, materials, and decision-drive alongside the Co-Chairs, owns the Horizon Framework execution discipline, drives the 90-day gate process, holds named decision rights within the Transformation Hub's authority threshold, and is the named accountability anchor for AI portfolio performance across all four business units.



This is not a research or exploratory role, and it is not a program-management role. It functions as the operating executive for enterprise AI transformation: bringing recommendations to the AI Executive Council for input and sign-off rather than simply reporting status upward, and holding direct decision rights within defined thresholds. The AVP will be expected to move the portfolio forward with speed, discipline, and business partnership: eliminating bureaucracy, enforcing fixed-fee cost discipline, and holding the organization accountable to outcomes that justify every dollar of AI investment.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise AI Strategy

  • Own and advance the enterprise AI strategy in partnership with the CIIO and enterprise IT leadership: translating the Horizon AI Framework into a prioritized, funded, and accountable initiative portfolio
  • Define the annual AI investment roadmap aligned to H1, H2, and H3 objectives; present recommendations to the AI Executive Council with clear ROI models and risk assessments
  • Ensure AI strategy is built with the business, not imposed on it, by maintaining active partnerships with clinical, financial, and operational leaders across all four BUs
  • Evaluate and recommend adoption of new AI capabilities and emerging technologies, balancing innovation appetite with fixed-fee cost discipline and enterprise standardization

Governance Execution

  • Chair the AI Transformation Hub: owning the bi-weekly cadence, initiative registry, intake discipline, and all in-threshold go/no-go decisions within the authority bands
  • Own the operating rhythm of the monthly AI Executive Council, co-chaired by the CIO and Jon Porter: setting the agenda, preparing portfolio scorecards, escalation packages, and ROI progress reports, and driving Council input and sign-off against the enterprise value creation framework
  • Enforce the 90-day gate process for all active initiatives: making scale, stop, or pivot decisions within the Transformation Hub authority threshold and escalating above-threshold decisions to the AI Executive Council with structured recommendations
  • Maintain the enterprise AI initiative registry across all four BUs; ensure every initiative has a named owner, a Horizon designation, and an active gate status
  • Manage the HIPAA/compliance gate as a mandatory stop for all initiatives touching PHI, clinical workflows, or patient data, no exceptions

Governance Effectiveness & Continuous Improvement

  • Own evaluation of how the AI governance and execution structure itself is performing, not just the initiatives running through it
  • Design and run the After Action Report (AAR) / retrospective cadence and structure across the Transformation Hub, Executive Council, and Solutions Team tiers
  • Execute that structure on a defined cadence, identify structural and process improvements, and build buy-in with the AI Executive Council before implementing changes
  • Drive improvement recommendations to resolution with measured, before/after outcomes: the governance model is expected to get faster and more effective release over release, not remain static

Portfolio Performance & ROI

  • Own delivery against the enterprise AI value creation framework for 2026: tracking initiative-level ROI, surfacing risks with 30-day advance notice to the AI Executive Council, and driving corrective action on underperforming initiatives
  • Build and maintain the enterprise AI ROI tracking framework, connecting initiative outcomes to financial, clinical, and operational metrics
  • Ensure every active initiative has a clear 90-day performance signal before any H2 or scale investment is authorized
  • Partner with Finance to validate AI ROI claims and ensure savings attributed to AI initiatives are recognized in the financial plan

Business Partnership & Cross-BU Coordination

  • Serve as the enterprise AI strategy partner to business unit leaders across CareMore, apree/Vera Whole Health, Millennium, and Mosaic Health: translating AI capabilities into domain-specific value
  • Partner with clinical, operational, and financial leaders to identify and prioritize AI use cases with the highest ROI and lowest risk profiles
  • Manage the AI Solutions Team engagement model across the Delivery tier: ensuring named reps in each BU and function are engaged, accountable, and delivering initiative-level outcomes
  • Escalate persistent Solutions Team Rep disengagement to the CIIO; coordinate interim ownership for high-ROI initiatives at risk

Vendor Strategy & Procurement Discipline

  • Evaluate AI vendor proposals and make selection recommendations for contracts within the Transformation Hub authority threshold
  • Enforce the enterprise default posture of fixed-fee, defined-scope contracting for all AI vendors; open-ended T&M arrangements require AI Executive Council approval
  • Coordinate with Procurement, Legal, and IT Security on vendor due diligence, contract terms, data use agreements, and BAA requirements
  • Maintain awareness of the AI vendor landscape across clinical AI, operational automation, ambient documentation, revenue cycle, and population health to inform the strategic roadmap

Responsible AI & Clinical Safety

  • Ensure all AI initiatives governed under the charter comply with the enterprise Responsible AI framework: clinical safety, algorithmic bias review, explainability, regulatory compliance, data minimization, and human oversight
  • Partner with Clinical Affairs and Compliance to ensure clinical AI tools complete mandatory safety assessments before go-live
  • Identify FDA SaMD-qualifying tools early and ensure regulatory counsel involvement before any clinical deployment
  • Monitor and report AI-related compliance, safety, and reputational risks to the AI Executive Council

Team Leadership & Organizational Capability

  • Lead, develop, and hold accountable the Director of Emerging Technology; set clear expectations, maintain a high standard of portfolio rigor, and create conditions for the team to execute with excellence
  • Build organizational AI fluency across the enterprise: developing training, communication, and change management approaches that accelerate adoption across clinical and business teams
  • Recruit and develop AI talent, including data scientists, AI product managers, and clinical AI specialists, as the portfolio scales from H1 pilots to H2 transformation
  • Represent Mosaic in the external AI ecosystem: vendor partnerships, industry working groups, and peer network engagement, to keep the enterprise at the frontier of healthcare AI

Qualifications

Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive experience leading large-scale business transformation, from ideation through delivery, scale, and measured results, with at least 5 years owning transformation programs with enterprise-wide, multi-entity scope
  • Proven track record taking transformation initiatives from concept to operating reality in organizations where technology, field/frontline operations, and data were central to the outcome, not purely a technology deployment
  • Demonstrated experience owning governance and prioritization discipline for a complex initiative portfolio in a regulated or compliance-intensive environment: including intake, gating, vendor selection, and resource allocation
  • Experience leading cross-functional governance bodies: committees, working groups, or enterprise boards/councils, with the ability to drive alignment, decisions, and resolution of C-suite-level conflicts without relying on direct line authority
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver results primarily through influence and cross-functional leadership rather than positional power, operating effectively in complex, matrixed, multi-entity organizations
  • Experience in healthcare, health plan, or another highly regulated industry is a differentiator, not a requirement; genuine interest in and working familiarity with how AI applies to enterprise transformation is expected
  • Demonstrated ability to manage large, complex vendor relationships with fixed-fee commercial discipline

AI & Technology Fluency

  • Strong working knowledge of AI and ML technologies, including large language models, generative AI, predictive analytics, and NLP, with the ability to evaluate vendor claims, assess technical risk, and guide build vs. buy decisions
  • Familiarity with healthcare AI platforms and vendors relevant to Mosaic's portfolio (ambient clinical documentation, clinical decision support, care management AI, revenue cycle automation)
  • Understanding of data governance and data infrastructure requirements that underpin reliable AI deployment: data pipelines, model lifecycle management, monitoring, and drift detection
  • Awareness of FDA SaMD regulatory pathway and HIPAA requirements as they apply to AI tools in clinical and patient-facing contexts

Skills & Competencies

  • Executive presence: able to communicate AI strategy, risk, and portfolio performance clearly to an AI Executive Council accountable for enterprise AI value creation and to clinical, financial, and operational leaders who are not technologists
  • Governance instincts: comfortable designing and operating governance structures, not just participating in them: owns the framework, enforces the discipline, eliminates the ambiguity
  • Business partnership orientation: earns credibility with business and clinical stakeholders by delivering outcomes they can measure, not AI concepts they have to interpret
  • Commercial discipline: approaches every vendor engagement, build decision, and resource allocation with a fixed-fee, defined-ROI mindset: cost discipline is not a preference, it is the standard
  • Portfolio management: able to hold 14+ concurrent initiatives in view simultaneously: tracking status, surfacing risk, sequencing decisions, and maintaining stakeholder visibility without losing momentum
  • Change leadership: drives adoption across a complex, multi-entity organization where authority is federated and results depend on named accountability at the BU level

‎

to

Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, internal equity, and business needs.

title: Information Systems Audit Intern- Summer 2027
description:
Information Systems Audit Intern
Summer 2027: June 1 - August 6

About Our Program
The Comptroller of the Treasury's Audit Internship Program is a 10-week paid educational and experiential learning opportunity offering undergraduate students a chance to witness and participate in the audit operations of the office. Interns will spend the summer building skills through their assignment to an active audit and audit-specific training, Interns will also have opportunities to build relationships with each other through shared experiences.

Information Systems (IS) Audit Intern responsibilities may include learning to examine and review the following: the adequacy of internal controls; records; reports; financial statements; information systems; compliance with laws and regulations; and management practices for state government entities and other organizations receiving public funds. IS Audit Interns may assist in evaluating:
  • The fairness of financial statement presentation,
  • The adequacy of internal controls,
  • Data integrity for application systems,
  • Compliance with laws, regulations, contracts, and grant agreements, and/or
  • The efficiency and effectiveness of an entity’s operations.
Our summer internship program is designed to be both professionally and academically beneficial. Interns gain hands‑on experience while participating in meaningful professional development activities such as Business Etiquette Day, a full‑day session focused on professionalism, emotional intelligence, and understanding one’s professional brand, complete with an etiquette lunch led by staff. Interns also enjoy engaging activities like speed networking with full‑time employees, a guided tour of the Tennessee Capitol to explore the state’s history, and weekly cohort check‑ins to foster connection and collaboration. The cohort experience culminates in a final presentation showcasing what interns have learned and contributed during their time with the Office.


Location
Information Systems audit internship opportunities are based out of Nashville, TN. Depending on the audit assignment, interns may have the opportunity for limited travel during the summer. Typical travel opportunities are in the Nashville area; however, some may allow for travel to other parts of Tennessee.

Who We're Looking For
We are looking for rising juniors, seniors, or graduate accounting students who are interested in applying what they've learned in the classroom to governmental auditing. To be considered for the internship program, candidates should have successfully completed at least 6 hours of accounting, computer information systems, computer science, information security, data analytics, or business-related coursework.

Successful interns are those who are adaptable, able to think critically, work well both individually and as part of a team, and are willing to learn and grow. Candidates should exhibit strong interpersonal, verbal communication, organizational, and writing skills. Interns are expected to apply their classroom knowledge to meaningful audit work.

About Our Office
The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury is responsible for the audit of state and local governmental entities and participates in the general financial and administrative management and oversight of state government. In the Comptroller’s Office, we strive to deliver on our mission to make government work better. Through dedicated hard work and commitment, every Comptroller’s Office employee accepts personal responsibility to accomplish our mission and uphold it.

Compensation
Interns are paid $24 per hour via a third-party company. Audit-related travel will be reimbursed.

It is the Comptroller’s policy to provide an environment free of discrimination and harassment of an individual because of that person’s race, color, national origin, age (40 and over), sex, sexual orientation, transgender and gender identity status, pregnancy, religion, creed, disability, veteran’s status, or any other category protected by state and/or federal civil rights laws.

title: Project Manager I
description:

title: Medical Laboratory Technician
company: Great Plains Tribal Leaders Health Board
location: Laboratory, Oyate Health Center, Rapid City, SD, US
description:
Medical.Laboratory.Technician.fy26.docx

Position Title: Medical Laboratory Technician

Division: OHC

Reports To: Lab Manager

Direct Reports: N/A

Job Summary:

This position is responsible for performing Hematology, Chemistry, Serology, Urinalysis, and Microbiology, and microscopic tests to obtain data for use in diagnosis and treatment of diseases for Oyate Health Center (OHC) patients. Rotating shifts, with occasional weekends and holidays.

The following functions are fundamental to the position and are required of all incumbents, with or without reasonable accommodation. These functions define the role and are not an exhaustive list of all duties.

  • Performs tests in the fields of microbiology, chemistry, hematology, serology, and urinalysis.
  • Conducts analyses of body fluids and/or tissue to determine presence of normal and abnormal components.
  • Prepares reagents and primary reference materials.
  • Performs non-routine and specialized test procedures using manual and/or instrumental techniques in accordance with established protocols.
  • Recognizes and reacts to indicators of instrument and reagent malfunctions; locates and implements corrections.
  • Obtains analytical data, converts to proper units for reporting, and correlates data to verify results.
  • Prepares patient laboratory reports and provides to appropriate individuals.
  • Performs manual differentials.
  • Analyzes test results and enters findings in computer.
  • Performs routine preventative maintenance on assigned instruments and equipment according to established schedule and procedure.
  • Verifies instrument functioning by checking and calibrating specific lab instruments and documents data.
  • Records on instrument logs any repairs, replacement, and maintenance needed of equipment; identifies the cause of common problems and makes simple repairs.
  • Conducts quality control procedures on equipment, reagents, and products. Maintains proper records for quality controls reports.
  • Performs phlebotomy duties to obtain blood samples.
  • Maintain effective, collaborative interdepartmental and external relations.
  • Must comply with federal laws and regulations as required by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).
  • Knowledge of federal, state, local, and accrediting agency regulations affecting areas of responsibility (CAP, CLIA, HIPAA).
  • Performs related duties.
  • Performs the core responsibilities of the position accurately, timely, and in accordance with established standards.
  • Maintains regular and reliable attendance consistent with the position’s schedule and operational needs.
  • Communicates effectively with internal and external stakeholders as required by the role.
  • Adheres to all applicable policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
  • Utilizes required systems, tools, and technology necessary to perform the job.

This position requires the ability to perform the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. Physical demands and work environment may include:

  • Sitting, standing, walking, lifting, or other job-related activities.
  • Office, clinical, community-based, or remote work environments.

Education/Experience:

  • Associate degree from a Medical Laboratory Technician Program.

  • Valid certification by a recognized certifying agency (ASCP, AMT) within six months of hire.

  • License not required by South Dakota.

  • Basic Life Support (BLS) certification is required or must be obtained within ninety (90) days of employment.

  • Must successfully pass a criminal and background check and a pre-employment drug screen.

The GPTLHB is a tribal organization that follows tribal preference laws. Our policy is to give preference to qualified Indian/Tribal candidates over qualified non-native candidates in hiring decisions if all other qualifications are equal.

Employment is contingent upon the outcome of all required criminal background checks.

Compliance with our Employee Health Procedure is a condition of employment. You are required to agree that you will comply with all job-related employee health screening and immunizations prior to your first day of employment. Jobs require that you have documentation that you have completed the following immunizations prior to your first day of employment: MMR (Measles, Mumps and Rubella, Varicella (Chicken Pox), Hepatitis B, Influenza, T-dap (Tetanus - Diphtheria - Pertussis), and COVID-19 vaccination is required.

title: Responsible Content Analyst 2
description:
Overview

Microsoft is a company where passionate innovators come to collaborate, envision what can be, and take their careers further. This is a world of more possibilities, more innovation, more openness, and the sky is the limit thinking in a cloud-enabled world.

The CoreAI organization at Microsoft builds the end-to-end AI stack and is core to Azure AI innovation and differentiation, as well as all of Microsoft’s flagship products, from GitHub, to Office, Teams, and Xbox. We are the team building Responsible AI, Azure OpenAI, Model as a Service, Azure ML, Cognitive Services, and the global Azure AI infrastructure for running the largest AI workloads on the planet. We do not just value differences or different perspectives, we seek them out and invite them in so we can tap into the collective power of everyone in the company. As a result, our customers are better served. Within CoreAI, the Foundry team empowers builders around the world of all skill levels to easily create AI apps.

CoreAI RAI Ops (Responsible AI Operations) is the operational arm of CoreAI that monitors AI misuse, investigates abuse signals, reviews high risk content, manages customer notifications and appeals, supports data labeling and quality programs, and helps ensure Microsoft AI systems are deployed safely and responsibly. The team combines human review, policy enforcement, incident response, analytics, and operational tooling to identify emerging AI risks, protect customers, improve model safeguards, and scale Responsible AI governance across Microsoft AI products.

We are looking for a Responsible Content Analyst 2, Cyber-focused work may include investigating malicious or deceptive uses of AI systems, including activity intended to compromise accounts, systems, data, or safety controls.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.



Responsibilities
  • Investigate emerging abuse patterns and safety risks across Microsoft AI products, with particular emphasis on cyber-based misuse.
  • Investigate potential malicious code generation, phishing, social engineering, credential abuse, malware-related activity, reconnaissance, exploitation workflows, and attempts to circumvent safety controls.
  • Review and adjudicate user prompts, model outputs, account activity, and other available evidence using Responsible AI policies, Cyber Safety guidance, abuse taxonomies, and structured decision frameworks.
  • Distinguish benign, dual-use, harmful, and policy-violating activity in complex or ambiguous scenarios.
  • Support abuse monitoring across text, image, audio, video, multimodal, and other emerging content types and risk categories.
  • Analyze safety, abuse, quality, and operational data to identify trends, test investigative hypotheses, scope potential impact, and support evidence-based enforcement or mitigation decisions.
  • Document emerging abuse behaviors, indicators, tactics, techniques, and patterns, including cyber-related adversarial activity involving generative AI.
  • Develop, refine, and validate moderation guidelines, Cyber Safety taxonomies, classifier definitions, reviewer instructions, escalation criteria, and evaluation datasets.
  • Translate investigative findings into recommendations for improved detections, classifiers, model safeguards, policies, enforcement strategies, operational processes, and product mitigations.
  • Produce high-quality annotations, calibrations, and policy-aligned judgments that support AI training, evaluation, and safety-system improvements.
  • Lead or contribute to complex escalations, customer appeals, high-risk submissions, incidents, and priority investigations involving potential AI misuse or policy violations.
  • Analyze operational metrics, quality signals, false-positive and false-negative patterns, and investigation outcomes to improve accuracy, consistency, efficiency, and customer experience.
  • Support the onboarding and operationalization of new risk categories, AI models, safeguards, policies, and abuse-monitoring capabilities.
  • Partner with engineering, data science, policy, threat intelligence, legal, security, customer-support, and Responsible AI teams to resolve cases and strengthen protections.
  • Communicate investigative findings, trends, risks, and mitigation recommendations through clear written analyses and stakeholder briefings.
  • Perform all work in accordance with Microsoft privacy, security, compliance, wellness, and Responsible AI requirements, including the safe handling of sensitive or potentially disturbing content.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Communication, Media, Behavioral Psychology, Criminal Justice, Linguistics, Education, Business, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years relevant experience in work requiring privacy, discretion, and/or exposure to sensitive situations or content (e.g., digital safety, content review, the use and creation of content moderation tools, data annotation, paralegal, social work, law enforcement) OR High School Diploma (or local equivalent), AND 5+ years relevant experience in work requiring privacy, discretion, and/or exposure to sensitive situations or content (e.g., digital safety, content review, the use and creation of content moderation tools, data annotation, paralegal, social work, law enforcement) OR equivalent experience.

Other Requirements:

Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience conducting evidence-based investigations and making decisions using structured policies, investigative frameworks, operational procedures, or enforcement guidelines.
  • Working knowledge of cyber threats and adversary tradecraft, such as phishing, malware, credential abuse, reconnaissance, exploitation, persistence, evasion, exfiltration, indicators of compromise, and MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
  • Experience analyzing operational, investigative, or security data using query, scripting, visualization, or analytical tools such as SQL, Kusto Query Language, Python, Power BI, or comparable technologies.
  • Ability to distinguish benign, dual-use, and harmful activity while applying sound judgment in complex, sensitive, or ambiguous situations.
  • Understanding of generative AI and large language model capabilities, limitations, failure modes, and potential misuse across cyber and other Responsible AI risk areas.
  • Written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document investigations and explain technical findings, risks, and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, maintain attention to detail, and deliver consistent, high-quality work in a rapidly evolving operational environment.
  • Ability to handle sensitive or potentially disturbing content while following applicable privacy, security, compliance, wellness, and Responsible AI requirements.
  • Experience investigating cyber-based misuse, content abuse, platform abuse, fraud, policy violations, or attempts to circumvent product safety controls.
  • Experience in Responsible AI, trust and safety, content moderation, abuse prevention, security operations, threat intelligence, incident response, or customer-facing risk operations.
  • Familiarity with cyber threat frameworks, taxonomies, indicators of compromise, and threat-intelligence platforms or standards such as MITRE ATT&CK, STIX/TAXII, or MISP.
  • Experience reviewing or investigating text, image, audio, video, or multimodal content using structured policies, taxonomies, or evaluation frameworks.
  • Experience evaluating, red-teaming, or testing generative AI systems, classifiers, safety controls, or abuse-detection mechanisms.
  • Experience developing or improving operational guidelines, abuse taxonomies, reviewer instructions, escalation criteria, evaluation datasets, or quality-assurance processes.
  • Experience working with engineering, data science, policy, legal, compliance, security, threat intelligence, or customer-support teams on sensitive investigations or escalations.
  • Experience with Microsoft Azure, Power BI, Kusto Query Language, SQL, Python, incident-management systems, or comparable investigative and analytical tools.

There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $102,200 - $169,900 per year.

title: Art Director
description:
Are you driven by curiosity? The kind that makes you ask “what if we tried this?”
Hiebing is a passionate, full-service agency fueled by curiosity and collaboration. Our teams in Madison and Austin work together to craft meaningful stories for brands we love and pro bono causes we believe in.

We believe in We Before Me, where the team has your back, and a Yes And mindset, where ideas get stronger when others build on them.

As a fully integrated agency, our creative teams partner closely with strategy, media, PR, social, and production to develop ideas that move brands forward in meaningful ways.

We’re looking for a mid-level Art Director who loves developing big ideas and bringing them to life visually. Someone who enjoys the full creative process—from concepting campaign ideas with teammates to crafting thoughtful design across multiple channels.

In this role, you’ll collaborate closely with writers, strategists, producers, and creative directors to turn ideas into work that shows up across brand campaigns, digital experiences, social storytelling, video, and traditional media.

Hiebing is an agency, which means the pace is dynamic and the work is varied. This role is best suited for someone who feels energized by momentum, enjoys juggling multiple creative challenges, and thrives in a collaborative environment where strong ideas are developed through shared thinking.

If you’re curious, collaborative, and excited to build great work with a team, you’ll feel right at home here.

What you'll do
  • Develop creative concepts and design solutions across print, digital, social, video, and brand identity
  • Partner closely with copywriters and creative teammates to build campaign ideas and executions
  • Bring ideas to life through thoughtful, high-quality design and visual storytelling
  • Collaborate with strategy, media, PR, and production teams to create integrated brand experiences
  • Adapt creative thinking to evolving digital and social platforms
  • Manage multiple projects and priorities while maintaining strong creative standards
  • Present work internally and contribute to the creative development process
  • Contribute to a collaborative, positive creative culture
  • Leverage AI-enabled creative tools to explore ideas, accelerate concept development, and support creative execution, while ensuring final work reflects Hiebing's standards for strategic thinking, creativity, and craft
  • Curiosity about emerging AI-enabled creative tools and a willingness to thoughtfully incorporate them into the creative process to improve efficiency and enhance the work
What we're looking for
  • 3–6 years of experience in an agency or creative environment
  • A portfolio demonstrating conceptual thinking, strong design craft, and visual storytelling
  • Experience collaborating with copywriters, strategists, or cross-disciplinary teams to develop campaign ideas
  • Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, especially InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills
  • Curiosity, initiative, and the ability to build on others’ ideas
  • Comfort managing multiple projects in a fast-moving agency environment
  • Curiosity about AI-powered creative and production tools, and an interest in folding them into your everyday workflow
  • Ability to apply thoughtful creative judgment when using AI-enabled tools, ensuring work remains original, strategically sound, and aligned with client goals and brand standards

Portfolio required to apply.
Your portfolio should demonstrate conceptual thinking and the ability to translate ideas into compelling visual work across multiple channels. We’re especially interested in seeing work that reflects your role in developing the idea behind the work—not just the final execution.

Benefits include: Hybrid work flexibility, health + dental insurance, paid parental leave, matching 401(k) + profit sharing, a professional development fund and many more! This position is a hybrid position.

Work Environment & Eligibility
Hybrid role based in Austin, TX (in-office Monday–Wednesday; remote Thursday–Friday). Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future sponsorship.

title: Chicago Event Facilitator
description:
About Puppy Sphere:

Welcome to Puppy Sphere, we are a high-growth startup redefining the wellness category through puppy therapy! We’re on a mission to bring people together in welcoming spaces where the gentle power of puppies helps them slow down, boost their mood, and return again and again.

As North America’s original puppy yoga company, we’ve built a community of over 400,000 people, making puppy therapy part of their everyday wellbeing ritual. As an Event Facilitator, you’ll play a key role in bringing our classes to life; from setup through to breakdown, while creating a seamless, positive experience for our Puppy Sphere community and ensuring the safety and wellbeing of both people and puppies.

This is a part-time, on-site role in Chicago; and weekday availability is a necessity, weekend availability is a plus!
The rate for this role is $16.60 USD per hour.

  • Set up the studio and puppy area at the start of each shift, ensuring everything is clean, organized, and ready for guests and pups

  • Help build a strong sense of community by creating moments that keep guests coming back
  • Embrace change and support the implementation of new processes and initiatives, helping ensure they land smoothly onsite

  • Adhere to company policies, safety protocols, and animal welfare guidelines at all times

Job Requirements:

  • Experience in the service or hospitality industry is preferred
  • Availability to work weekdays (at least one day per week)
  • Availability for a minimum of 4 shifts per month
  • Additional weekend availability is a strong plus
  • A warm, engaging, and outgoing personality that helps create a welcoming and positive experience
  • Comfortable working in a fast-growing startup environment where things evolve quickly and adaptability is key.
  • Must be 18 years of age or older
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull items weighing up to 30 lbs.
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods, including throughout the duration of events.
  • Ability to bend, kneel, crouch, reach, and perform repetitive motions as required during event setup, execution, and breakdown.
  • Comfortable working with standard cleaning supplies and solutions, following proper safety and handling guidelines.
  • Ability to work in environments with moderate noise levels, animals present, and high guest interaction.
  • Bonus if you have access to a car and ability to drive.

We’re looking for someone who:

  • Goes above and beyond to create an exceptional experience
  • Is a true team player: proactive, supportive, and collaborative
  • Embodies our values in everything they do
  • Communicates clearly and confidently, with strong interpersonal and customer service skills
  • Stays organized and can multitask in a fast-paced environment
  • Is kind, thoughtful, and genuinely cares about creating a positive experience for every guest
  • Feels comfortable and confident working around puppies, and understands the importance of creating a calm, safe, and positive environment for both guests and pups

Perks:

🚀 Join a fast-growing startup with upward mobility.
🦮 Experience the happiness of working around puppies.
🧘 4 complimentary puppy yoga classes for you, family and friends.
🔖 35% discount on individual puppy yoga classes.
✨ Opportunity to work with celebrity clients and industry giants.

Puppy Sphere Values:

  • We create happiness.
  • We care.
  • We adapt.
  • We show up.
  • We raise the bar.

We’re so grateful for your interest in joining the team here at Puppy Sphere! Due to the high number of applications we receive, we may not be able to personally reach out to everyone, but please know we truly appreciate the time and effort you’ve taken to apply 🤍

title: Intelligence Analyst - Contractor
description:
Position Summary and Objective

We are seeking an experienced and proactive Intelligence Analyst to serve in a dedicated role with a specific client in the medical space. In this role, the intelligence analyst will provide incident monitoring, real-time social-media threat monitoring and analysis, and crisis communication support to ensure the safety and security of our client’s personnel, assets, and operations. The intelligence analyst will be embedded within the client organization, working closely with their corporate security team to deliver actionable intelligence and facilitate rapid response to emerging threats. This role is based in Warsaw, Poland.


Duties and Responsibilities

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide centralized monitoring of critical events (natural disasters, civil unrest, cyber threats), ensuring rapid outreach to impacted personnel and stakeholders.

  • Conduct predictive and real-time analytical assessments to identify and manage security, safety, and product-related risks; issue real-time threat alerts to support informed decision-making and incident reduction.

  • Monitor and track mission-critical operations and employee locations in real time, ensuring team safety and swift adaptation to evolving threats or logistical changes.

  • Evaluate flight patterns, hotel locations, high-risk destinations, and transportation options to provide travelers with safer choices and risk-reduction strategies.

  • Maintain meticulous data keeping for security systems maintenance, tracking all repairs and problematic devices, and escalating damaged equipment to the Systems Team through end-to-end repair completion.

  • Utilize Client-directed mass communication system and standard operating procedures to send communications to key stakeholders and impacted travelers.

title: Manufacturing Assistant
description:
Begin Your Career in Biotech with Hands-On Training

The Manufacturing Assistant provides key support to the manufacturing, production and QC teams by performing a wide variety of laboratory support tasks. The individual is a great team player with good dexterity, organization skills, and attention to detail. This position requires working in an environmentally controlled laboratory environment where personal protective equipment and good lab practices are required. This individual also enjoys assisting others, having work variety, and has a passion for organization!

Training on all aspects of position, including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), will be provided.

What You Will Get to Do
  • Works in environmentally controlled lab spaces, follows good lab practices, and appropriately uses personal protective equipment (PPE) per protocol for the specific spaces (hair net, goggles/safety glasses, facemask, lab coat, gloves and booties)
  • Routinely washes, treats, and autoclaves laboratory glassware and labware, ensuring materials are properly prepared and available to support manufacturing schedules
  • Restocks laboratory spaces with materials and cleaning supplies and prepares cleaning solutions as needed
  • Tracks expiration dates of stocked materials and removes out of date materials from labs
  • Monitors and maintains supplies needed for manufacturing, and places orders to ensure material availability
  • Ensures information is up to date in electronic inventory software (ERP)
  • Reconciles physical inventory and electronic inventory and maintains organization of lab materials
  • Assists team members with laboratory support tasks such as cleaning of lab hoods, benches, and equipment following SOPs
  • Supports ad-hoc materials/support requests to keep labs running smoothly. Understands work area needs and prioritizes requests appropriately
  • Performs routine accuracy checks of critical lab equipment following standard operating procedures
  • Performs weekly cleaning of lab spaces, equipment, and other housekeeping duties and ensures cleanings logs are up to date
  • Assists as needed with environmental monitoring of lab areas including particle counts, air sampling, and water sampling
  • Follows MMQCI’s protocols based on current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) and International Organization for Standardization (ISO) quality systems. Follows defined work procedures

Required Skills & Experience
  • High School Diploma, with an interest in working in a laboratory setting or Associate Degree in Biology, Life Sciences, or Chemistry. Prior work history that includes routine glassware washing and inventory stocking tasks preferred
  • Good communication skills, written and oral, with good computer skills
  • Able to accurately perform a wide variety of laboratory tasks quickly with attention to detail in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines and shifting priorities
  • Experience in a GMP or ISO quality system industrial environment is preferred
  • Has a passion for organization, follows instructions, and enjoys precise, detailed work
  • Strong work ethic; willingness to help the MMQCI team whenever and wherever needed, ability to multitask
  • Must be able to lift approximately 35 lbs
  • Must have manual dexterity to be able to wash and clean large laboratory glassware
  • Able to visually inspect glassware for defects and debris
  • Ability to stand for several hours
Preferred
  • Familiarity with clean room gowning procedures and working in an environmentally controlled environment is a plus
Why You’ll Love Working Here
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a growing diagnostic company
  • Collaborative, mission-driven team environment
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
Benefits We Offer
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan
  • Company profit sharing program
  • Paid time off: including vacation, holidays, and sick leave
  • Paid Parental Leave Program
The pay range for this position is $17.00 to $31.25/hour

https://www.mmqci.com/about/employee-spotlight/employee-spotlight.html

Maine Molecular Quality Controls, Inc. (MMQCI) designs, develops, manufactures, and sells unique quality control products used by hospital laboratories and manufacturers to monitor the accuracy of tests for genetic, oncologic, and infectious diseases. MMQCI has proprietary technologies to stabilize DNA and RNA for use as quality controls and continues to pursue the discovery of novel techniques useful for the development of new quality control products.

MMQCI is conveniently located in beautiful southern coastal Maine, minutes from the Maine Turnpike, Portland International Jetport, and less than 2 hours from Boston. Close by are fabulous Portland restaurants, sandy beaches, and a plentiful supply of Maine lobsters! title: Executive Director
description:
Executive Director

Brazos Valley Food Bank | Bryan, Texas

The Brazos Valley Food Bank (BVFB) is seeking an inspiring, strategic, and community-minded Executive Director to lead a highly respected regional organization into its next chapter.

This is an exciting time for BVFB. The organization has just completed and begun implementation of an ambitious three-year Strategic Plan focused on Food Access for All, Catalyzing Health, Transforming Foundational Conditions, and Mobilizing the Community.

Serving Brazos, Burleson, Grimes, Madison, Robertson, and Washington Counties, BVFB reaches more than 75,000 unique neighbors each year and distributes nearly 8 million pounds of food. Its impact is supported by a network of more than 100 community partners and innovative direct-service programs including food assistance for children and seniors, School-Based Food Pantries, Mobile Food Distributions, Home Delivery, Nutrition Education, SNAP Enrollment, Food is Medicine initiatives, and Together We Grow, a workforce-readiness and economic-mobility program.

BVFB is financially strong and well positioned for continued impact, with more than $4 million in annual cash revenue, significant food assets, a fully owned and recently upgraded 50,000-square-foot facility, a fully paid fleet and infrastructure, thousands of committed volunteers, and an engaged Board of Directors.

The Opportunity
The Executive Director provides visionary and operational leadership for the organization’s strategy, programs, operations, finances, development, advocacy, and community engagement. As the primary liaison to the Board of Directors, the ED translates strategy into action, supports effective governance, and ensures organizational accountability and sustainability. The ED also serves as BVFB’s chief culture leader, fostering a high-performing workplace grounded in adaptability, belonging, boldness, empathy, integrity, partnership, and radical hospitality.

The successful candidate will be a visible and collaborative leader who can inspire staff, engage donors and volunteers, build strong community partnerships, communicate effectively with diverse audiences, and navigate a changing food-insecurity landscape. The ED will champion strategic growth while ensuring sound financial stewardship, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, strong Board partnership, and measurable community impact.

Qualifications & Core Competencies

BVFB is seeking a leader who brings:

Experience & Education: a minimum of 10 years of senior leadership experience, preferably in the nonprofit sector, with demonstrated experience working with a Board of Directors. Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
Strategic Leadership: Proven ability to lead organizational strategy, drive execution, manage change, and foster continuous improvement based on data and community needs.
Fundraising & Financial Stewardship: Track record of supporting fundraising efforts, managing budgets, and ensuring responsible resource allocation.
Relationship & Stakeholder Engagement: Skilled in building and maintaining strong relationships with diverse stakeholders, including Board members, donors, partners, volunteers, and community leaders.
Communication & Public Presence: Exceptional written, verbal, and public speaking skills, with the ability to effectively represent and advocate for the organization.
Mission Alignment: Deep commitment to addressing food insecurity and advancing community impact.
Learning & Adaptability: Demonstrates learning agility, openness to feedback, and commitment to best practices and innovation.
Technical & Operational Acumen: Proficiency with standard business technologies and ability to navigate operational, compliance, and policy environments.
Sector Engagement: Active participation in relevant networks (e.g., Feeding America, Feeding Texas) to strengthen impact and collaboration.
Additional Requirements: Flexibility to support organizational needs (including occasional evenings/weekends and disaster response), valid driver’s license, and successful completion of background check; ability to meet the physical and travel demands of the role.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary: $100,000–$125,000

BVFB offers a competitive benefits package that includes:
  • 12 paid holidays
  • 23 days of PTO for employees with 0–2 years of service
  • Bereavement, parental, and caregiving leave, when eligible
  • In-state remote and/or hybrid work schedule, when eligible
  • HMO health insurance with 100% employer-paid health, vision, dental, and life insurance
  • Access to short- and long-term disability insurance, employee-paid
  • Workers’ compensation
  • Mileage reimbursement for work-related travel
  • 401(k) with BVFB matching employee contributions up to 3% of annual base salary after three continuous months of service
  • Paid professional development opportunities, when budgeted
Why BVFB?
This is more than an executive leadership position. It is an opportunity to guide a strong, established organization at a pivotal moment; build upon an extraordinary foundation; mobilize an entire community; and help shape a healthier, more resilient future for the Brazos Valley.
BVFB is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

First round of candidate review will be September 18. Applications submitted after that date will be considered after the first round of candidates are exhausted.

title: Education Specialist
description:
POSTING TITLE: Education Specialist
Join Our Team at ChildRoots

Are you an experienced early childhood educator and administrator looking to inspire young minds and build lasting connections? Do you believe in fostering a sense of wonder and curiosity in children while working in a supportive, co-teaching environment?

ChildRoots, a small family of locally and woman-owned childcare centers in Portland, Oregon, is seeking, a Step 10+ Education Specialist to work 5 days/40 hours per week (1.0 FTE). Since 2007, our progressive, play-based schools have focused on guiding children's social and emotional development while encouraging exploration and inquiry. Our awe-inspiring classrooms are designed to provoke curiosity, but it is our Teachers who make ChildRoots truly outstanding.

About the Role
An Education Specialist at ChildRoots works Monday through Friday, 8 hours per day, offering support, coaching, guidance, and management for teaching teams of classrooms of either infants (zero to two), toddlers (two to three) and/or preschool-age students (three and up). This role is perfect for former educators and current administrators who:
  • Value collaborative classroom environments that focus on child-led learning and inquiry.
  • Have a strong understanding of child development and pedagogy theory.
  • Are passionate about mentoring adult learners and guiding them through child development.
  • Have a strong dedication to teamwork and collaboration.
Compensation & Benefits
At ChildRoots, we value fair, predictable compensation. Education Specialists start at $33.15/hour.
And receive:
  • Standardized annual merit-based raises and annual PFA wage adjustments
  • Long-term commitment bonuses to incentivize teachers to remain with their cohort
Our comprehensive benefits package includes:
✅ Health & Vision Insurance – majority employer-paid
✅ Dental Insurance – majority employer-paid
✅ Life Insurance – 100% employer-paid
✅ 401(k) Retirement Plan – Generous company match
✅ Paid Time Off – Including holidays, a weeklong Winter Break, and professional development opportunities

Responsibilities
  • Provide care and educational support for a consistent group of children.
  • Foster a safe, engaging, and child-centered learning environment.
  • Design and implement developmentally appropriate activities.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with families, ensuring clear and supportive communication.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development, deliver coaching and training, and contribute to a positive workplace culture.
  • Manage a team of teaching staff and classrooms.
  • Track, manage, and log team progress and development.

Qualifications & Requirements
To be considered for a role at ChildRoots, applicants must:
  • Be a Step 10+ in the Oregon Registry Online (ORO) system
  • Be currently enrolled in Oregon's Central Background Registry (or begin the process and complete it upon receiving confirmation)
  • Meet the teacher-qualification criteria as outlined by the Office of Child Care requirements, which may include:
    • Previous experience in a structured childcare environment.
    • Completion of college-level courses in early childhood education-related subjects.
      • Degree in Early Childhood Education (or equivalent) preferred.
    • Complete Oregon’s Safety Set Trainings and required certifications:
      • Pediatric CPR/First Aid Course (hybrid or fully in-person)
      • Oregon Food Handler's Card (online course)
      • Introduction to Child Care Health & Safety (online course)
      • Recognizing & Reporting Child Abuse & Neglect (online course)
      • Prevention is Better than Treatment (online course)
      • Safe Sleep for Oregon's Infants (online course)
  • At least 4+ years of experience managing staff preferred.
  • At least 4+ years of experience teaching.
  • Experience with Microsoft Office applications preferred.

Our Work Culture
At ChildRoots, we believe that children are authentic, powerful individuals. Our mission is to guide their social and emotional development and to foster a sense of wonder about the world around them. We know that teaching is more than just meeting physical needs—it is about understanding each child’s unique experience and supporting them on their journey.

We also understand that a successful school depends on supported, valued educators. Our workplace culture emphasizes stability, emotional support, and a collaborative environment where every teacher is seen and appreciated.

Join Our Team!

Apply today and become a part of one of Portland’s most inspiring childcare communities!

To work with us, you must be teacher-qualified and currently enrolled in Oregon's Central Background Registry.

These easy, online trainings are required within 30 days of hire:

  • Pediatric CPR/First Aid Course
  • Oregon Food Handler's Card
  • Introduction to Child Care Health & Safety online course
  • Recognizing & Reporting Child Abuse & Neglect online course
  • Prevention is Better than Treatment online course
  • Safe Sleep for Oregon's Infants online course

The challenges of COVID reminded us how vital it is to center our employees’ well-being. We know we still have much to do to be the BEST place to work in child care in Portland, but that’s what we’re working toward.

All employees are eligible for:

  • 1-3 weeks of Paid Time Off per year, depending on how long they've been with ChildRoots.
  • 25 paid holidays and all-school days off
  • Company-provided continuing education
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan with generous company match and 100%, immediate vesting

Full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our insurance plans, including:

  • Providence Health, including vision, naturopathic, chiropractic, acupuncture, AND massage
  • Principal or Willamette Dental

We value commitment and invite you to stay with us for at least a year.

To learn more about us, explore our website, take a virtual tour of our facilities, and review our COVID-19 Health & Safety Guidelines.

We're a pro-vaccination community and require all employees and enrolled parents to be fully vaccinated against COVID. We still practice extraordinary safety protocols like daily health checks, masks, stable groups, and extra cleaning, and will do so for as long as it takes to keep our community safe.

Thank you for your consideration. We hope to hear from you!

title: Graphic Designer- LATAM Market
description:

  • Strong understanding of Brazilian and broader LATAM culture, trends, and consumer behaviour.
  • Fluency in Portuguese is highly desirable, particularly for work targeting the Brazilian market.

title: Prize Director, XPRIZE Healthspan
description:
XPRIZE Overview

XPRIZE is an established global leader in designing and executing large-scale competitions to solve humanity’s greatest challenges. As a 501(c)3, our unique model democratizes innovation by incentivizing crowd-sourced, scientifically viable solutions to create a more equitable and abundant future for all. Since our founding in 1994, we’ve launched $519 million in prize competitions that are driving more than $31 billion in social and economic impact — a 60x return on philanthropic investment. These competitions not only de-risk early-stage breakthrough ideas but also mobilize capital, talent, and momentum to accelerate solutions from concept to real-world scale.

We operate across 5 areas of impact, including:

  • Deep Tech + Exploration
  • Energy + Climate + Nature
  • Food + Water + Waste
  • Health
  • Learning + Society

Join XPRIZE to help create meaningful impact as we strive to empower humanity to achieve breakthroughs and architect a more equitable and abundant future for all.


Position Description

The XPRIZE Foundation is seeking a leader for our XPRIZE Healthspan competition. XPRIZE Healthspan is a 7-year competition that will recruit interdisciplinary teams of innovators from around the world to develop and scale integrated systems that can revolutionize health aging through the creation of innovative therapies that restore muscle, cognitive, and immune function by a minimum of 10 years and up to 20 years. The competition teams are entering Finals stage which runs from 2026-2030. Competing teams will work with XPRIZE and our established research partners to conduct randomized clinical trials in adults aged 50-90 years.

The Prize Director is responsible for overall operations and management of the Prize competition, including coordination of operations, team relations, management of major testing partners, developing partnership ecosystem and scientific expansion, marketing, contract negotiations, and budget. This person will be able to not only clearly explain the subject matter to non-technical team members, executives and clients, but importantly, is also able to represent the competition and its goals to internal and external constituencies.


Responsibilities

  • Provide leadership and managerial direction to the Prize team.
  • Execute Prize vision, strategies, and objectives.
  • Ensure timely response to changing needs, requirements, issues, and direction, keeping all constituents informed in a timely manner.
  • Oversee budget and authorization of expenditures within budgetary limits. Develop and implement cost control measures and processes.
  • Partner with recruiting and Domain Lead to secure, retain, and effectively and economically manage needed personnel, materials, and resources to manage the Prize.
  • Manage experts, other consultants, and advisors that support the Prize on a temporary and/or contract basis.
  • Monitor and report on Prize competition to constituents, including, Domain Lead, XPRIZE leadership, advisory boards, judging panels, sponsors, donors, and major testing partners, ensuring requirements are met.
  • Organize, host, and participate in large and small events - both domestic and international - during the competition, for the awarding of the Prize, and post-competition. These could include summits, investor meetings, site-visits, scientific and industry conferences, workshops, fundraising events, and award ceremonies.
  • Ensure the competition is conducted in line with XPRIZE foundation rules and processes and also in accordance with specific Prize goals.
  • Act as public face of the Prize through interviews, appearance at industry conferences, speaking engagements, blogging, and other public outreach activities.
  • Collaborate and communicate across departments; facilitate intra-team communications and meetings.
  • Oversee knowledge management systems and processes for the Prize.
  • In partnership with Marketing, help with development and execution of the marketing and public affairs strategy for the Prize, including communications, media and government relations, Prize messaging, branding and web presence.
  • Develop high-quality project plans which lay a path to reliable success.


Qualifications

  • Strong scientific background, preferably with clinical and/or research experience in biomedical sciences, biotechnology, drug development, geroscience, longevity, geriatrics, family medicine, preventive medicine, or regenerative medicine.
  • 7-10 years (inclusive of graduate and postgraduate training in relevant areas) of experience designing, managing, monitoring, and executing large complex projects, demonstrating strong attention to detail and ability to multitask.
  • Advanced degree - such as PhD, MD, DO, or similar doctorate degree - in direct field of study.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, including relationship building and collaboration within a diverse, cross-functional team and with supporting competing teams and external partners.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Record of delivering high-quality, and innovative technology-based projects.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a track record in driving success in companies or complex programs.
  • Ability to thrive and think creatively and calmly in fluid situations under deadlines.

  • Ability to travel 40% annually both domestically and internationally.

Why Work at XPRIZE:
In addition to working for a mission-driven company that catalyzes industries, pushes innovation forward, and is creating an abundant and equitable future, we offer the following benefits:

  • Quarterly company-paid All-Hands meetings in Los Angeles for frequent in-person collaboration

title: Acquisition Growth Analyst
description:
Acquisition Growth Analyst

Location: Lahore, Pakistan (onsite)
Department: Growth
Reports to: Global Growth Manager
Level: Mid-level (2 to 4 years)
Employment type: Full-time, permanent

About the role

ACE Money Transfer is a cross-border remittance business serving migrant communities across multiple send and receive corridors. Our Growth team owns how new customers find us, sign up, complete KYC, and send their first transfer.
This role sits at the centre of that. You will be the analytical owner of our customer acquisition engine, with a primary focus on our referral programme (Invite a Friend), our affiliate programmes, our associate channel, and product-led growth loops inside the app.
You will also own acquisition quality as a measurement discipline in its own right, separate from acquisition volume. Every channel will be judged not only on how many customers it delivers but on what those customers are worth: activation rate, first and repeat transaction behaviour, retention curves, corridor mix, average transaction value, and fraud or abuse rates by source.
This is not a reporting role. You will be expected to find the leaks in the acquisition funnel, design the experiments that fix them, quantify the incremental impact, and defend the numbers to senior leadership. Roughly 75% of your time sits on acquisition, activation, and referral economics. The remaining 25% supports the wider customer lifecycle, so you will see the full picture from first click to repeat sender.
If you have worked on referral programmes, affiliate programmes, viral loops, invite mechanics, onboarding funnels, or paid and organic acquisition performance in a consumer app, fintech, or marketplace environment, this role will feel familiar.

What you will own

Referral, affiliate, and viral loops (primary focus)

  • Own end-to-end performance analysis of the Invite a Friend referral programme: invite volume, invite-to-signup conversion, referred-customer activation, and referral-driven transaction volume.
  • Model and monitor referral unit economics: reward cost per acquired customer, blended and referral-specific CAC, CAC payback period, and LTV to CAC ratio by corridor.
  • Design and evaluate dual-sided incentive structures (referrer and referee rewards), including reward tiering, caps, qualification criteria, and payout triggers.
  • Measure programme virality: referral participation rate, invites per active customer, K-factor, and viral cycle time.
  • Identify and quantify referral abuse and self-referral patterns, and work with Compliance and BI to close gaps without suppressing legitimate participation.
  • Analyse affiliate programme performance by partner: traffic and sign-up volume, commission cost per acquired customer, quality of customers delivered, and payout validation against verified activity.
  • Track associate channel performance, recommend where to concentrate incentive spend, and identify which corridors the channel should expand into next based on demand signals and unit economics.

Acquisition funnel and activation

  • Analyse the full acquisition funnel: traffic and app install, sign-up, KYC and verification completion, first transaction, and second transaction.
  • Isolate drop-off points by corridor, device, channel, and customer cohort, and size the revenue opportunity behind each one.
  • Improve time-to-first-transaction and first-transaction conversion rate through funnel and onboarding recommendations.
  • Partner with Product to reduce friction in registration, verification, and first-send journeys.

Channel performance and CAC efficiency

  • Track acquisition performance by source and channel: paid media, organic, referral, affiliate, associate, and partner.
  • Build and maintain channel-level CAC, cost per activated customer, and cost per first transaction reporting.
  • Identify high-performing and underperforming acquisition sources and recommend budget and incentive reallocation.
  • Support attribution and source-of-truth alignment between marketing platforms and internal transaction data.

Experimentation

  • Design, instrument, and read out A/B tests and growth experiments across referral mechanics, onboarding, incentive levels, and in-app prompts.
  • Define hypotheses, primary metrics, sample size requirements, and test duration before launch.
  • Use holdout groups and incrementality testing to separate genuine lift from correlation, particularly on incentive-led campaigns.
  • Maintain a structured experiment repository so results, learnings, and failed tests are searchable and reusable.

Reporting and stakeholder communication

  • Deliver weekly and monthly acquisition insight: what changed in funnel conversion, referral performance, channel CAC, activation, and corridor trends, why it changed, and what to do about it.
  • Prepare executive-ready insight summaries for senior leadership: what moved, why it moved, what to do next.
  • Be explicit about data limitations, definitional caveats, and confidence levels in every number you publish.

Wider lifecycle support (secondary, approximately 25% of time)

  • Build behavioural cohorts and customer segments from transactional and engagement data.
  • Flag early churn indicators and support segmentation for retention, win-back, and reactivation campaigns.
  • Contribute to customer lifetime value modelling and repeat-transaction analysis.
  • Coordinate with relevant internal departments on campaign execution and data accuracy.

Requirements

Must have

  • 2 to 4 years of experience in customer acquisition, growth analytics, product analytics, or marketing analytics, ideally in fintech, payments, consumer apps, e-commerce, or marketplaces.
  • Hands-on acquisition funnel management: owning a funnel end to end, from traffic and sign-up through activation and first transaction.
  • Proven acquisition growth: a track record of measurable improvement in acquisition volume, conversion rate, or CAC efficiency that you can evidence and explain.
  • Advanced Excel or Google Sheets: pivot tables, lookups, cohort tables, and financial modelling of unit economics.
  • Demonstrated understanding of acquisition funnels, conversion rate optimisation, cohort analysis, retention curves, CAC, and LTV.
  • Practical experience with A/B testing and experiment design, including significance, sample sizing, and common pitfalls.
  • Ability to translate analysis into a clear recommendation and defend it to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong written and spoken English.

Strongly preferred

  • Direct experience with a referral programme, invite-a-friend mechanic, affiliate or partner programme, loyalty or rewards programme, or any incentive-led acquisition channel.
  • Experience in remittance, cross-border payments, digital wallets, neobanking, or another regulated financial product.
  • Product analytics tooling: GA4, Firebase, Amplitude, Mixpanel, CleverTap, or similar.
  • BI and visualisation tooling: Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio, or Metabase.
  • CRM and campaign platforms: Braze, CleverTap, MoEngage, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, or similar.
  • Python or R for analysis and automation.
  • Exposure to incentive fraud detection or promotional abuse analysis.

How success is measured

First 90 days
  • Full acquisition funnel mapped end to end with baseline conversion rates by corridor and channel.
  • Referral programme baseline established: participation rate, invite-to-activation conversion, cost per referred customer.
  • Internal acquisition targets adopted and owned, with a documented view of where this role adds value against each one.
  • Empirical measurement in place of how much each acquisition initiative contributes to overall acquisition, with demonstrated improvement in that contribution.
First 6 months
  • At least three referral or onboarding experiments shipped with measured, statistically defensible outcomes.
  • A documented, quantified recommendation on referral reward structure and its effect on CAC.
  • Reduction in a named acquisition funnel drop-off point, with the improvement attributable to your analysis.
Ongoing
  • Measurable improvement in referral-driven new customer volume and referral programme participation rate.
  • Improvement in blended CAC efficiency or CAC payback period.
  • Improvement in sign-up to first-transaction conversion rate.
  • Experiment throughput and quality: hypotheses tested per quarter and learnings documented.
  • Leadership reporting delivered on time, with figures that hold up under scrutiny.
